components.name: Button
components.summary: Triggers an action or navigation. The single button used everywhere in the system.
components.description:
Use `Button` for any clickable action. Variations:

- `variant`: emphasis. `default` is the primary action (at most one per view); `secondary` and `outline` for supporting actions; `soft` is a low-emphasis tinted primary (toolbars, inline "Add" actions, cards); `ghost` for dense toolbars; `link` for inline text actions; `destructive` / `success` for irreversible / confirming actions.
- `size`: density (`xs` ... `lg`); `icon*` sizes are square for icon-only buttons (ALWAYS set `aria-label`).
- `rounded`: `default` (rounded-md), `full` (pill, or a circle with `icon*` sizes), `none`.
- `block`: full-width button for forms, cards and mobile layouts.
- `iconStart` / `iconEnd` (or the `icon-start` / `icon-end` slots): icon placement around the label; while `loading` the spinner replaces the start icon.

To make a link look like a button use `as="a"` or `as-child` with a RouterLink.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual emphasis. `soft` is a tinted low-emphasis primary. Unknown values fall back to default.

props.name: size
props.description: Height/padding. `icon*` sizes are square. Unknown values fall back to md.

props.name: rounded
props.description: Corner radius: rounded-md, rounded-full (pill / circle for icon sizes) or none. Unknown values fall back to default.

props.name: block
props.description: Adds `w-full` so the button fills its container.

props.name: iconStart
props.description: Icon before the label (decorative, aria-hidden). Replaced by the spinner while `loading`. Ignored with `asChild`.

props.name: iconEnd
props.description: Icon after the label (decorative, aria-hidden). Ignored with `asChild`.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render. Non-button elements get aria-disabled instead of disabled.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).

props.name: type
props.description: Native button type. Defaults to button so it never submits forms by accident.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables interaction.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner, sets aria-busy, blocks clicks, keeps width.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: default
slots.description: Label and/or icons.

slots.name: icon-start
slots.description: Custom content before the label; overrides `iconStart`. Hidden while `loading`.

slots.name: icon-end
slots.description: Custom content after the label; overrides `iconEnd`.

Soft variant
examples.description: Low-emphasis tinted primary, good next to a `default` button or inside cards and toolbars.

examples.title: Sizes and icons
Rounded (pill)

examples.description: Pass an icon definition with `iconStart` / `iconEnd`, or use the `icon-start` / `icon-end` slots for custom content.

examples.title: Loading
examples.script:
const saving = ref(false)
function save() { saving.value = true; setTimeout(() => (saving.value = false), 1500) }
examples.code: <Button :loading="saving" :icon-start="faPlus" @click="save">Save changes</Button>

a11y: Native <button> semantics; Space/Enter activate.
Icon-only buttons need aria-label.
Icons from `iconStart` / `iconEnd` are decorative (aria-hidden); the label carries the meaning.
loading sets aria-busy and shows an indeterminate progressbar named "Loading" (so the accessible name becomes "Loading Save"); non-button elements use aria-disabled.
Target size: `xs` and `icon-xs` are 24px, `sm` 32px, `md` 36px, `lg` 44px; on coarse pointers `sm`, `md` and the icon sizes grow to 40px or 44px.

Focus uses the shared ring (`focus-visible:ring-3`) plus a transparent outline, so it is visible in forced-colors mode. Labels are `whitespace-nowrap`: keep them short or wrap the button group (`flex-wrap`) so it reflows at 320px.
requires: Throws a ContractError when a Button with `size` `icon`, `icon-xs`, `icon-sm` or `icon-lg` has no accessible name (no visible text, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`). Use IconButton for icon-only actions.
llmNotes: One `default` variant button per view; use `soft` for secondary tinted actions.
Use `rounded="full"` for pills and circular icon buttons; use `block` instead of `class="w-full"`.
Use `iconStart` / `iconEnd` for icons next to a label instead of putting an <Icon> in the default slot; icon-only buttons still need `aria-label`.
Never nest interactive elements inside a Button.
Use `as-child` with RouterLink for navigation, not onClick + router.push.
replaces: shadcn-vue Button
hand-rolled Button markup in app code

components.name: IconButton
components.summary: Square icon-only Button with a required accessible label and tooltip title.
components.description:
Use `IconButton` for toolbar and row actions that show only an icon. `label` is REQUIRED: it becomes `aria-label` and the native `title` tooltip. It composes `Button`, so `variant`, `loading`, `disabled`, `as` and `type` behave identically. Size names `xs|sm|md|lg|xl` are mapped to the square `icon-*` sizes. Defaults to the `ghost` variant.

**Sizes** (`size`): `xs` 24px, `sm` 32px, `md` 36px (44px on coarse pointers), `lg` 44px and `xl` 48px. `xs` is the smallest allowed target (24px); prefer `sm` or larger for the main action of a row. **Shape** (`shape`): `rounded` (default, rounded-md), `circle` (fully round, for floating and avatar-like actions) and `square` (no rounding, for dense toolbars). The button is always square, so a pill shape would be a circle. Unknown `size` and `shape` values fall back to `icon` (md) and `rounded`. `iconButtonVariants` returns the same classes for a plain `a` or `button`.

props.description: Accessible name: used for aria-label and title.

props.name: icon
props.description: FontAwesome icon. Omit when using the default slot.

props.name: variant
props.description: Button variant. Unknown values fall back to default (the Button rule).

props.name: size
props.description: Square size: xs 24px, sm 32px, md 36px (44px on coarse pointers), lg 44px, xl 48px; icon, icon-xs, icon-sm and icon-lg are the Button sizes. Unknown values fall back to icon.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corner shape: rounded-md, fully round or square corners. Unknown values fall back to rounded.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render.

props.name: type
props.description: Native button type.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables interaction.

props.name: loading
props.description: Replaces the icon with a spinner, sets aria-busy, blocks clicks.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: default
slots.description: Custom icon content replacing `icon`. Hidden while loading.

Loading

function run() { busy.value = true; setTimeout(() => (busy.value = false), 1500) }
examples.code: <IconButton label="Save" :icon="faPlus" variant="outline" :loading="busy" @click="run" />

examples.description: xs, sm, md, lg and xl. All are square; xs is 24px and xl is 48px.

examples.title: Shapes
examples.description: rounded (default), circle and square, with a filled and an outline variant.

a11y: `label` provides both aria-label and a visible tooltip (title) for pointer users.

Every size and shape keeps the required `label` (aria-label and title) and a target of at least 24px; `md` grows to 44px on coarse pointers and `lg` and `xl` are already 44px or more. Shape changes only the corner radius, so the focus ring and the hit area are the same.
Inherits Button semantics: Space/Enter, aria-busy while loading, disabled blocks clicks.
requires: Throws a ContractError when `label` is missing or blank.
Throws a ContractError when there is neither an `icon` nor default slot content.
llmNotes: ALWAYS provide `label`; it is required.
Use IconButton instead of Button size="icon" + manual aria-label.
Use `shape="circle"` for round actions; there is no pill shape because the button is square. Use `size="xl"` for large touch actions.
Prefer `icon` prop with a FontAwesome IconDefinition over inline SVG.
replaces: Button size="icon" with manual aria-label
ad-hoc icon-only buttons

components.name: Chip
components.summary: Compact tag that can be removable and/or selectable (toggle).
components.description:
Use `Chip` for tags, filters and selected values. `removable` adds a remove button (and Backspace/Delete on the focused chip) that emits `remove` - you remove the item from your data. `selectable` turns the label into a toggle button bound with `v-model:selected`. Do not use it for status labels with no interaction (use `Badge`).

Variations: `variant` (fixed-colour looks plus tone-aware `soft`, `solid`, `outline`), `tone` (`neutral | primary | success | warning | danger | info`, used by `soft` / `solid` / `outline`), `size` (`sm | md | lg`), `rounded` (`full` pill default, `md`, `none`), and the `selected` state for filter chips.

props.name: tone

props.name: size

props.name: rounded
props.description: Corner radius: pill (rounded-full), rounded-md or none. Unknown values fall back to full.

props.description: Chip text (default slot overrides it); also names the remove button.

props.description: Leading FontAwesome icon. Use the `leading` slot for other content.

props.name: removable
props.description: Show remove button and enable Backspace/Delete.

props.name: selectable
props.description: Render the label as a toggle button with aria-pressed.

props.name: selected
props.description: Toggle state, use `v-model:selected`. Works controlled and uncontrolled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Blocks selection, removal and keyboard shortcuts.

props.description: Element to render.

a11y: Selectable chips render a native button with aria-pressed (Tab to focus, Space/Enter to toggle).

A removable, non-selectable chip is a focusable `group` named by `label`: Backspace or Delete removes it (`aria-keyshortcuts`). The remove button has aria-label "Remove <label>" and stays out of the tab order, but screen-reader and touch users can still activate it.
The remove button is at least 24x24px (WCAG 2.5.8) even on the small chip: it extends past the chip with negative margins instead of growing it.
A selected chip adds a primary ring; the ring is also drawn in forced-colors mode through the focus outline, and `aria-pressed` carries the state so colour is not the only signal.
Disabled chips set aria-disabled and disable inner buttons.
requires: Throws a ContractError when a `removable` Chip has no non-empty `label` (it names the remove button).
Throws a ContractError when a `selectable` Chip has no text (`label` or default slot).
llmNotes: Always set `label` on removable chips so the remove button is named.
Handle `@remove` by deleting the item from your data; the chip does not hide itself.
Use `v-model:selected`, not `modelValue`.
Use `variant="soft"` + `tone` for tags, `outline` for filter chips, `solid` for strong emphasis; `tone` is ignored by the fixed-colour variants.

components.name: ShowMore
components.summary: Collapses long content to a number of lines or a height and shows a Show more toggle only when it overflows.
components.description:
Use `ShowMore` for descriptions, notes and comment bodies that can be long: show the first lines and let the reader expand the rest in place. It measures the content with a `ResizeObserver` after mount and on every resize, so the toggle appears only when something is actually clipped. Short content renders without a toggle. There is no fade or gradient. For a titled section that always has a trigger use `Collapsible` or `Accordion`; to truncate a single line with no way to expand use `Text` with `truncate`.

Variations:

- `lines` (1 to 6) clamps by line count; `maxHeight` (`xs` 64px, `sm` 96px, `md` 128px, `lg` 192px, `xl` 256px) clamps by height and wins over `lines`.
- `layout`: toggle `below` the content (default) or `inline`, beside it at the last line.
- `align`: `start`, `center` or `end` for the `below` layout (logical, so right-to-left flips it).
- `appearance`: `link` (default), `button`, `outline`. `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`.
- `moreLabel` and `lessLabel`, or the `more` and `less` slots, change the toggle text. `icon` hides the chevron.

State: `v-model:expanded` works controlled and uncontrolled. The `overflow` event reports when the collapsed content starts or stops overflowing.

The server render and the first client render are the collapsed content without a toggle; the toggle appears after mount, once the content has been measured. Nothing animates by default.

props.name: lines
props.description: Lines shown while collapsed, 1 to 6. Fractions are truncated; not a number or below 1 falls back to 3; above 6 is 6.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Clamp to a height preset (64px, 96px, 128px, 192px, 256px at the default spacing) instead of lines. Wins over `lines`. Unknown values are ignored.

props.name: layout
props.description: Toggle below the content, or beside it at its last line. Unknown values fall back to below.

props.name: align
props.description: Toggle position in the `below` layout. Unknown values fall back to start. No effect with `layout="inline"`.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Toggle look. Unknown values fall back to link.

props.name: size
props.description: Toggle size (24px, 32px, 40px minimum height; 44px on coarse pointers). Unknown values fall back to md.

props.name: moreLabel
props.description: Toggle text while collapsed. A blank value throws a ContractError unless the `more` slot is used.

props.name: lessLabel
props.description: Toggle text while expanded. A blank value throws a ContractError unless the `less` slot is used.

props.name: icon
props.description: Show a chevron that turns over when expanded.

props.name: expanded
props.description: Expanded state, bound with `v-model:expanded`. Uncontrolled when not passed.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render as the root.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.description: The content to collapse.

slots.name: more
slots.description: Toggle text while collapsed. Replaces `moreLabel`.

a11y: The toggle is a native `button` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the content element, and its visible text (`Show more` / `Show less`) is its accessible name. Enter and Space activate it.
The toggle is only rendered when the content overflows, so there is never a control that does nothing. Content that already fits has no extra tab stop.

Collapsed content is clipped, not removed: text stays in the accessibility tree, so screen readers read all of it. Links or buttons inside the clipped part stay focusable; keep interactive elements out of the part that can be hidden.
The toggle is at least 24px tall (the style packs keep this floor) and 44px on coarse pointers; focus uses the shared ring, which also shows in forced-colors mode.
No gradient fade and no height animation by default. The chevron turns only with `motion-safe:`, so reduced-motion users see it change instantly.
Logical properties only: the toggle aligns to the start or end side and flips in right-to-left text. Long words wrap (`break-words`), so the content reflows at 320px without horizontal scroll.
Focus is not moved on toggle; when the toggle disappears because the content now fits, focus returns to the page body. Keep expanded state in `v-model:expanded` if the content can change length.
requires: Throws a ContractError when `moreLabel` or `lessLabel` is blank (and the matching `more` or `less` slot is not used), because the toggle needs visible text.

components.name: AvatarGroup
components.summary: Overlapping stack of avatars with a +N overflow bubble.
components.description:
Use `AvatarGroup` to show participants, assignees or members compactly. Provide data with `items`, or compose `Avatar` children in the default slot (both can be combined; items come first). `max` limits how many avatars are shown; the rest collapse into a `+N` bubble. `size` and `shape` apply to every avatar that does not set its own.

In a stacked group it sets how far the avatars overlap (the steps follow `size`); in a spaced group it sets the gap (4px, 8px, 12px). Unknown values fall back to `stacked` and `default`.

components.name: Kbd
components.summary: Keyboard key chip (`<kbd>`) and a group that joins keys with a separator.
components.description:
Use `Kbd` to show a single key and `KbdGroup` for shortcuts made of several keys. `KbdGroup` takes either a `keys` array or `Kbd` children and can draw a `separator` (`+`, `then`) between them.

Variations:

- `variant`: `default` (muted fill with border), `outline` (border only, for use on tinted surfaces), `ghost` (no border or fill, for dense menus) and `solid` (inverted: foreground fill, background text, for tooltips and hints that need to stand out).
- `size`: `xs` (16px), `sm` (20px), `md` (24px, default), `lg` (28px). Pick the size that matches the surrounding text: `xs` or `sm` beside 12px text, `lg` beside headings.
- `KbdGroup` also takes `variant` and `size` for the chips it generates from `keys` (slotted `Kbd` children keep their own props) and `gap` (`none`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`) for the space between chips.

Keys are not interactive, so the 24px target size does not apply.

components.name: Separator
components.summary: Thin horizontal or vertical divider line, solid, dashed or dotted, optionally with a label ("or", "Today") on the line.
components.description:
Use `Separator` to split groups of content or toolbar items. It is decorative by default (role="none"); set `:decorative="false"` when the divider carries meaning for assistive tech. Vertical separators need a parent with a height (e.g. `flex items-center` with `h-5` on the separator).

**Line style** (`variant`): `solid` (default, filled `bg-border`), `dashed` and `dotted` (1px border; use for "tear-off", optional or secondary regions, receipts). Unknown values fall back to solid.

**Thickness** (`size`): `thin` (1px, default), `md` (2px) and `thick` (3px) for section breaks that need more weight. **Tone**: `default` (border colour), `muted` (half strength, for dense lists), `strong` (the form-control border colour, for dividers that must stay visible on cards) and `primary` (accent). On a labelled separator the tone also sets the text colour (`strong` is foreground, `primary` is the accent, the others stay muted). Unknown values fall back to `thin` and `default`. Thicker and toned filled lines add a border in forced-colors mode.

**Labelled** separators: pass `label="or"` or put any content in the default slot to show text on the line. `align` places it: `center` (line on both sides, default; sign-in forms, "or"), `start` (label first, line after; section headings) or `end` (line first, label last). Unknown `align` values fall back to center. Labelled separators work vertically too (the label sits between two vertical lines). Without `label`/slot the markup is a single element as before. With `asChild` the slot is the element to render and `label` is ignored.

a11y: Decorative by default (role="none") so screen readers skip the line; label text stays readable.
Use `decorative=false` when the line separates regions of a toolbar or menu: it is then a real `separator` that assistive tech can announce.

`size` and `tone` only change thickness and colour. A thicker or toned filled line adds a border in forced-colors mode, where background colours are replaced, so it stays visible. Tones use the existing border, input and primary tokens; a decorative divider needs no text contrast, a `strong` one meets 3:1 against the page and card surfaces.

The line is a 1px `border` colour fill. Forced-colors mode replaces background tokens, so a filled line also paints `forced-colors:bg-[CanvasText]` (a system colour keeps its value) and the default hairline, labelled lines included, stays visible. Dashed and dotted variants use borders, so they remain visible too.

With `decorative=false` it exposes role="separator"; vertical ones also set aria-orientation. Because separator children are presentational, `label` is also set as aria-label (slot content is not; pass aria-label yourself).

Keep `decorative` true unless the divider conveys structure.
Use `label="or"` for dividers between alternatives instead of hand-rolled flex + two hr.
Use `variant="dashed"|"dotted"` for style; do not set border classes manually.
Use `size="md"|"thick"` for section breaks and `tone="muted"` inside dense lists; do not set `h-*` or `bg-*` classes by hand.
Do not combine `label` with `asChild`.

components.name: Skeleton
components.summary: Placeholder block shown while content loads: text, circle, avatar, pill, rounded, rect and paragraph shapes with a pulse or no animation.
components.description:
Use `Skeleton` to reserve layout space while data loads. Size it with classes (`h-4 w-40`, `size-12`) and compose several to mimic the final layout. Unknown `shape` / `animation` values fall back to `rect` / `pulse`. Do not use it for in-progress actions (use `Spinner`).

**Shapes**: `text` (one text line, h-4), `circle` and `avatar` (round size-10; `avatar` never shrinks in flex rows), `rect` (default block), `rounded` (block with large radius for cards and images), `pill` (h-6 w-24 for badges, chips and buttons) and `lines` (a paragraph of `lines` text lines, the last one shorter).

**Animation**: `pulse` (default), `shimmer` (deprecated alias: it pulses, because a moving highlight needs a gradient) or `none` (static placeholder, e.g. dense tables or when many skeletons would be noisy). The pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion. The older boolean `shimmer` still works and is ignored when `animation` is set.

components.name: AspectRatio
components.summary: Keeps its content at a fixed width-to-height ratio (images, video, maps, placeholders).
components.description:
Use `AspectRatio` to reserve space for media before it loads and to crop it consistently. The outer wrapper is `width: 100%` and takes its height from `ratio`; your content fills it absolutely. Size it by placing it in a width-constrained container. `class` and attributes go on the inner content element, so `overflow-hidden rounded-lg` clips the media. Where the native `aspect-ratio` CSS fits (a plain box), a Tailwind `aspect-video` class is simpler.

**Rounded** (`rounded`): `none` (default), `md`, `lg` or `full`. A non-`none` value also sets `overflow-hidden`, so media is clipped to the corners; `full` with `:ratio="1"` is a circle. **Variant** (`variant`): `plain` (default), `bordered` (1px border) and `muted` (muted background with muted text, for placeholders and empty media; it keeps a border in forced-colors mode, where backgrounds are replaced). **Fit** (`fit`): `none` (default, nothing is applied), `cover` (crop to fill), `contain` (letterbox) and `fill` (stretch) for a direct `img` or `video` child. Unknown values fall back to the defaults. `aspectRatioVariants` returns the same classes for a plain element.

The `muted` surface uses the muted foreground on the muted background (4.5:1 in every theme) and a border in forced-colors mode. `fit` sets sizing on direct `img` and `video` children only.

components.name: ScrollArea
components.summary: Scrollable region with consistent, themed scrollbars across browsers.
components.description:
Use `ScrollArea` for bounded lists, logs, code panels and side panels where native scrollbars look inconsistent. Give it a bounded size (`h-64`, `max-h-80` via `class`, or a flex/grid parent). Native keyboard, wheel and touch scrolling are preserved, and the viewport is always keyboard focusable (reka-ui sets `tabindex="0"`). Pass `label` to name it. `type` controls when bars show: `hover` (default), `scroll`, `auto` (only when overflowing) or `always`. For horizontal overflow set `horizontal`. Use `ScrollBar` directly only when composing custom layouts inside a reka ScrollAreaRoot.

**Scrollbar thickness** (`size`): `sm` (6px), `md` (10px, default) and `lg` (16px, easier to grab). **Scrollbar look** (`variant`): `default` (transparent track, faint thumb), `track` (a visible muted track behind a solid thumb, so the scroll extent is readable) and `solid` (a solid thumb with no track, for content where the faint thumb is hard to see). When the bars appear is still `type`; `variant` and `size` only change how they look. Unknown values fall back to `md` and `default`. `scrollBarVariants` returns the bar classes for custom layouts.

a11y: Uses native scrolling inside the viewport, so wheel, touch and keyboard scrolling keep working.

Keyboard: the viewport is a Tab stop (`tabindex="0"`, set by reka-ui), so Arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home and End scroll it; the focus ring is drawn inset so the root `overflow-hidden` does not clip it.
With `label`, the focusable viewport is exposed as `role="region"` with that name; without it only the tab stop exists, so always pass `label` for content that matters.

`size` and `variant` only restyle the bars: the viewport stays the focusable, named scroller. The `track` and `solid` thumbs use the muted foreground colour (at least 4.5:1 on the background, card and muted surfaces) and a border in forced-colors mode; the default thumb is `bg-input` (the form-control border colour, 3:1 against the background and card surfaces in light and dark, about 3.1:1 and 3.4:1 measured in Chrome) and darkens to the muted foreground on hover; it is lighter than the solid thumbs but no longer a faint hint, and it is still not the only way to scroll. Use `lg` where a thicker bar is easier to grab; bars never replace the keyboard path.
Scrollbars are decorative, hidden from assistive tech by reka-ui, and have no motion beyond fade.
Responsive: size it with `w-full max-w-*` so it never forces horizontal scroll of the page at 320px.

Always pass `label` so the focusable viewport has a name.
Use `horizontal` (and `:vertical="false"` if needed) only for content wider than the area; use `w-max` on the inner row.
Use `viewport-class` for padding so scrollbars stay at the edge.
Use `variant="track"` or `"solid"` when the faint default thumb is too subtle; use `size="lg"` for touch-first panels. Do not add `::-webkit-scrollbar` CSS.
Prefer `type="auto"` or `always` on touch-first or test pages where hover is unavailable.

components.name: Link
components.summary: Inline text link with variants, safe external handling and RouterLink support.
components.description:
Use `Link` for navigation inside or between text. `external` opens a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, adds an arrow icon and an sr-only "(opens in new tab)" hint. For router navigation pass `as` (or `as-child`) with a RouterLink and give it its `to` as an attribute. For link-looking buttons use `Button variant="link"`; for button-looking links use `Button as="a"`.

Variations:

- `variant`: `default` (primary, underline on hover), `underline` (primary, always underlined), `muted`, `subtle` (foreground colour, always underlined), `plain` (inherits the surrounding text colour, always underlined, for links inside tinted or coloured text) and `destructive` (destructive colour, always underlined, for links to irreversible actions such as a delete page).
- `size`: `inherit` (default, keeps the surrounding text size), `sm` (14px), `md` (16px), `lg` (18px).

Inline links are exempt from the 24px minimum target size (WCAG 2.5.8); a standalone link in a toolbar or list should sit in a row with at least 24px of height.

components.name: Badge
components.summary: Small non-interactive label for status, counts and categories.
components.description:
Use `Badge` to label an item with a short status or category (`Beta`, `Paid`, `3 new`). It is not interactive: for removable or toggleable tags use `Chip`; for presence on an avatar use `Avatar status`.

Variations:

- `variant`: fixed-colour looks `default`, `secondary`, `outline`, `destructive`, `success`, `warning`, `info`, plus the tone-aware `soft`, `solid` and `outline`.
- `tone`: `neutral | primary | success | warning | danger | info`. Pair with `soft` (tinted, the usual choice in tables and lists), `solid` (strong, for counts and "new") or `outline` (bordered). `soft` / `solid` without a tone are neutral. Ignored by the fixed-colour variants.
- `size`: `sm` (dense tables), `md` (default), `lg`.
- `rounded`: `default` (rounded-md), `full` (pill), `none`.
- `dot`: leading status dot in the current text colour, for "Active" / "Offline" style statuses.

When using `badgeVariants` outside the component, wrap the result in `cn()` so tailwind-merge drops overridden neutral colours.

components.name: CountBadge
components.summary: Numeric count pill or small dot for unread items and pending work, with a required accessible label.
components.description:
Use `CountBadge` for a number that sits next to or on top of another element: unread messages, open tasks, items in a cart. A count of 0 renders nothing, a large count is capped (`99+`), and the visible number is hidden from assistive technology in favour of a `label` such as `3 unread messages`. For a status word (`Paid`, `Draft`) use `Badge`; for a status light without a number use `StatusDot`.

Variations:

- `tone`: `neutral | primary | success | warning | danger | info`.
- `appearance`: `solid` (default), `soft` (tinted) or `outline` (border on the page background, readable over other elements).
- `size`: `sm` 16px, `md` 20px (default), `lg` 24px tall.
- `shape`: `pill` (grows with the text), `circle` (round for one or two digits), `square` (control radius).
- `dot`: a marker without a number. With `count` it hides at 0, without `count` it always shows.
- `max` and `showZero`: the cap before `max+`, and whether `0` is rendered.

Placement: wrap the target and the badge in `CountBadgeAnchor` and put the badge in its `badge` slot. `placement` is `top-end` (default), `top-start`, `bottom-end` or `bottom-start`; start and end flip in right-to-left text. `countBadgePlacement` exposes the same classes for custom wrappers.

Bad input is handled, not thrown: a count that is not a number or is NaN or negative counts as 0, a fraction is truncated, `Infinity` shows `max+`, and an invalid `max` falls back to 99. Wrap `countBadgeVariants(...)` in `cn()` when you use it on a plain element, because a few classes override each other.

A rendered badge without `label` text throws a ContractError in strict mode. A badge that renders nothing (count 0) is not checked.
The label does not update itself: when `count` changes, pass a matching `label`. A change is not announced; for live updates keep an existing polite `role="status"` region elsewhere in the page.
Numbers use tabular figures. Tone colours are Badge token pairs covered by the contrast tests (light and dark). In forced-colors mode the border stays visible.
Placement uses logical `start` and `end` insets and flips the shift for right-to-left text. The anchor wrapper has `pointer-events-none` on the badge so clicks reach the element underneath.
The badge is small by design and is not a target. Put the interaction on the element it is attached to.

llmNotes: Always pass `label` with the full phrase a screen reader should hear ("3 unread messages"), not just the number; keep it in sync with `count`.
Do not guard with `v-if="count > 0"`: `CountBadge` already renders nothing at 0 unless `show-zero` is set.
Use `max` for a cap (`99+`); do not format the number yourself.
To attach a badge to another element use `CountBadgeAnchor` with the `badge` slot and `placement`; never position it with physical left/right classes.
Use `dot` for presence without a number and `Badge` for words. Do not signal state by colour alone: the label or neighbouring text must say it.
Use `appearance="outline"` when the badge overlaps other content so it keeps its own background.

components.name: Progress
components.summary: Horizontal progress bar with determinate and indeterminate modes, tones, sizes, a pulse animation, inside/top labels and segments.
components.description:
Use `Progress` to show how far a known task has come (`modelValue` 0..`max`) or that something is working with no known end (omit `modelValue` or pass `null`). Values are clamped: NaN and negatives become 0, values above `max` become `max`, an invalid `max` falls back to 100. Unknown `size`/`tone`/`valuePosition` values fall back to the defaults.

Variations: **size** `xs` (2px) to `xl` (20px); **tone** for meaning (primary, success, warning, danger, info, neutral); **animated** pulses the filled bar (a busy but determinate task; static under prefers-reduced-motion). `striped` is deprecated and draws nothing, because stripes need a gradient and the design system uses none; **valuePosition** `end` (percentage beside the bar, default), `inside` (percentage inside the filled bar, needs size `lg`/`xl`, clipped when the value is very small) or `top` (header row with the visible `label` on the left and the percentage on the right); **segments** splits the bar into N steps for wizards, password strength or quotas (each segment fills proportionally). For a circular meter use `ProgressRing`; for tiny inline waits use `Spinner`.

Pass `label` (aria-label) describing what is progressing; a bar without a name throws a ContractError (the rendered fallback is "Progress"). Use `aria-labelledby` to point at visible text instead.

The percentage text uses `tabular-nums`, so the digits do not jitter while the value changes. Progress updates are not announced as a live region; use a separate `role="status"` message for milestones.

The indeterminate animation is replaced by a static half-opacity bar and the pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion. In forced-colors mode (where background colours are replaced by system colours) the track gets a 1px border and the fill a 2px border, so the filled length stays readable.
Responsive: the bar is `w-full` and shrinks with its container; give it a `max-w-*` parent rather than a fixed width.

Control width with the parent (e.g. `max-w-72`); the bar fills its container by default.
Use tone="danger"/"warning" for thresholds instead of custom colours.
Use value-position="inside" only with size lg/xl; use value-position="top" when the label should be visible.
Use `segments` for discrete steps; use `animated` only while work is actually running. Do not use `striped`.

components.name: ProgressRing
components.summary: Circular SVG meter that fills clockwise from the top, with a centre label.
components.description:
Use `ProgressRing` for scores, quotas and completion where a compact circular readout fits (dashboards, cards). It is pure and stateless: the arc animates with a CSS transition when `value` changes (disabled for reduced motion). Values are sanitised: NaN and negatives become 0, values above `max` become `max`, an invalid `max` falls back to 100. For linear bars use `Progress`.

Variations:

- `size`: a number of px (default 64) or a preset: `xs` 40, `sm` 48, `md` 64, `lg` 96, `xl` 128. A preset also sets a matching thickness (4, 5, 6, 8, 10px) unless you pass `strokeWidth`.
- `variant`: `default` draws the muted track under the arc; `bare` draws the arc alone, for rings on tinted or busy surfaces.
- `shape`: the line cap of the arc, `round` (default) or `butt` (flat ends, so the arc length is exact).
- `tone`: colour of the arc.

components.name: StatusBadge
components.summary: Badge that maps a raw status string (active, pending, failed...) to a tone, with a leading dot.
components.description:
Use `StatusBadge` to display backend status values without writing a status-to-colour map in every view. Statuses are matched case-insensitively after trimming and normalising spaces and dashes to underscores, so `In Progress`, `in-progress` and `IN_PROGRESS` all match `in_progress`. Built-in groups: success (active, online, healthy, ok, success, completed, approved, ...), warning (pending, warning, degraded, queued, paused, ...), info (running, in_progress, processing, new, draft, info, ...), danger (error, failed, offline, down, rejected, critical, unhealthy, ...), anything else neutral. `null`/empty renders "Unknown". Override with `tones`, or reuse the logic with the exported `statusTone(status, overrides?)` and `statusBadgeDefaultTones`.

Variations:

- `variant`: `soft` (default: tinted success, warning and info, filled danger, secondary neutral), `outline` (bordered, tone-coloured text), `solid` (filled with the tone colour) and `plain` (tone-coloured dot and text with no border, fill or side padding, for dense tables and lists).
- `size`: `sm`, `md` (default), `lg`. The dot scales with the text (4px, 6px, 8px).

Use `StatusDot` next to text that already names the state (a table row, a list item, a header). - `tone`: `neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`.

components.name: Toggle
components.summary: Two-state button that stays pressed (bold, mute, pin). Controlled or uncontrolled.
components.description:
Use `Toggle` for an independent on/off button, typically with an icon (formatting, mute, favourite). Use `v-model` for the pressed state, or `default-pressed` when you only need an initial state. For a set of related toggles use `ToggleGroup`; for settings use `Switch` or `Checkbox`. Icon-only toggles MUST have an `aria-label`.

Variations:

- `variant`: `default` (flat), `outline` (bordered), `soft` (muted fill, primary tint when pressed) and `filled` (secondary fill, solid primary when pressed). `soft` and `filled` read as buttons without a border, for toolbars and filter rows.
- `tone`: `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info` recolours the PRESSED state: tinted for `default`, `outline` and `soft`, solid for `filled`. Unset keeps the neutral accent (primary for `soft` and `filled`).
- `size`: `xs` (28px), `sm` (32px), `md` (36px, default), `lg` (40px), `xl` (44px).
- `shape`: `rounded` (default, rounded-md), `pill`, `square`.

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.summary: Joined set of toggle buttons (default, outline or segmented look) with single or multiple selection and roving keyboard focus.
components.description:
Use `ToggleGroup` with `ToggleGroupItem` children for segmented choices (alignment, view mode, text formatting). `type="single"` keeps one value (string, pressing the active item clears it); `type="multiple"` keeps an array. `variant` and `size` are provided to every item (items can override). Unknown `variant`/`size` values fall back to `default`/`md`. For a required single choice with radio semantics prefer `RadioGroup`/`Tabs`.

**Variants**: `default` (flat joined buttons; toolbars and formatting), `outline` (bordered joined buttons; filters, alignment) and `segmented` (separate rounded items sitting on a muted track, the active one raised; view switchers like List/Grid or Day/Week/Month, best with `fullWidth`). **Sizes**: `xs` (28px) to `xl` (44px). `fullWidth` stretches the group and shares the width between items.

**Shape** (`shape`): `rounded` (default), `pill` (fully rounded ends or segments) and `square`. **Tone** (`tone`): the colour of the pressed item. `neutral` (default) keeps the accent fill; `primary`, `success`, `danger` and `info` use a solid status fill with its foreground colour. **Gap** (`gap`): `none` (default) joins the items; `sm` (4px) and `md` (8px) turn them into separate buttons. All three can be combined with every `variant`, `size` and `orientation`; items may override `shape` and `tone`. Unknown values fall back to the defaults.

components.name: Markdown
components.summary: Renders Markdown text (CommonMark plus GFM tables, task lists and strikethrough) as styled, accessible elements without v-html.
components.description:
Use `Markdown` for text you do not author element by element: README files, release notes, help text, user comments and LLM replies. The source is parsed by a small built-in parser into a tree and drawn with Vue render functions, so raw HTML in the source is shown as literal text and `v-html` is never involved. Use `Prose` when you already have trusted HTML to style, and `Heading`, `Text` and friends for hand-written pages.

Supported: ATX and setext headings, paragraphs, block quotes, ordered and bullet lists (nested, start numbers, tight and loose), task items, fenced and indented code, thematic breaks, GFM tables with alignment, link reference definitions, hard and soft breaks, emphasis, strong, strikethrough (`~~`), inline code, inline and reference links, `<url>` autolinks, bare http and https URLs, images, backslash escapes and character references (numeric plus a small named set). Not supported: raw HTML (shown as text), footnotes, math, emoji shortcodes, single-tilde strikethrough, `www.` autolinks.

Safety: link targets must be http, https, mailto, tel, a relative path or a `#fragment`; images may use http, https, relative paths and `data:image/png|jpeg|gif|webp` (never SVG). Anything else, including obfuscated `javascript:` variants, renders the label as plain text. `allowedProtocols` can only narrow the list. Input longer than `maxLength` renders as plain text and nesting beyond `maxDepth` stays literal.

Streaming: set `streaming` while text is still arriving. The whole source is parsed again on every change (the parser is linear time, a 200 KB document takes a few milliseconds), and in the last block unfinished emphasis, code spans, links, images and table rows are closed or hidden instead of showing raw syntax. Turn it off when the text is complete.

No existing app component was verified as replaced.

props.name: source
props.description: Markdown text. When omitted, the text of the default slot is used (the Vue compiler collapses whitespace in slot text, so use `source` for multi-line documents).

props.name: headingOffset
props.description: Added to every heading level, clamped to 0..5 (integers; invalid values count as 0). `3` renders `#` as h4. Levels above 6 clamp at h6.

props.name: headingIds
props.description: Give headings stable, unique slug ids (`-1`, `-2` suffix on duplicates, `section` for empty headings).

props.name: headingAnchors
props.description: Add a keyboard-focusable link named "Link to this section" beside each heading. Needs `headingIds`.

props.name: idPrefix
props.description: Prefix for heading ids (`doc` gives `doc-install`). Use it when several documents share one page.

props.name: linkTarget
props.description: Target for internal links. Only `_blank` sets the attribute.

props.name: externalTarget
props.description: Target for external (absolute http/https or protocol-relative) links. `_blank` adds `target`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and a screen-reader-only "(opens in a new tab)". External links always get `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

props.name: baseUrl
props.description: Resolves relative link and image URLs. Fragments and absolute URLs are left alone. The result is checked again.

props.name: allowedProtocols
props.description: Narrows the allowed schemes (subset of `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `tel`; images also `data`). Names outside the built-in list are ignored. An empty array allows only relative URLs and fragments.

props.name: highlight
props.description: Use CodeViewer for fences tagged json, yaml/yml, go/golang, toml, shell/sh/bash/zsh or plain/text. Other languages, and everything when false, render a plain labelled region.

props.name: codeFold

props.name: size
props.description: Body text 14px, 16px or 18px; headings scale with it.

props.name: tone
props.description: `muted` uses the muted foreground colour for body text.

props.name: inline
props.description: Parse and render only inline syntax inside a `span`: no paragraphs, headings or lists. For one-line UI strings.

props.name: streaming
props.description: The text is still arriving. Closes or hides unfinished syntax in the last block, hides a table header until its delimiter row exists, and sets `aria-busy`.

props.name: components
props.description: Custom renderers by node type: `link` (props href, title, external, target, rel; label as default slot), `image` (src, alt, title) and `code` (code, language, info, filename, closed). Each is a component or an element name and only receives checked values.

props.name: maxDepth
props.description: Maximum nesting of block quotes, lists and inline emphasis (clamped to 1..100). Deeper markers stay literal text.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Longer sources render as one unformatted plain-text paragraph.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge. The default measure is `max-w-prose`; override it with e.g. `max-w-none`.

components.name: Prose
components.summary: Wrapper that styles raw HTML content (headings, lists, links, code, tables, images) with design tokens.
components.description:
Use `Prose` around content you do not control element-by-element: rendered Markdown, CMS HTML or long-form articles. Styles apply to descendants via Tailwind arbitrary variants, so it works without any plugin. Set `measure` for a readable line length (`max-w-prose`, 65ch). For individual, hand-authored elements prefer `Heading`, `Text` and friends.

Sizes: `xs` 13px (dense help panels), `sm` 14px (app UI), `base`/`md` 16px (default reading size), `lg` 18px (articles), `xl` 20px (landing copy). Tones: `default` follows the page; `inverted` swaps foreground and background tokens for a high-contrast block in either theme; `dark` forces the dark palette for the block regardless of page theme. Both non-default tones add a padded rounded surface (override with `class`, e.g. `p-0`).

Density sets the vertical rhythm: `compact` (tight margins for help panels and changelogs), `default`, `relaxed` (generous margins and `leading-relaxed` for long-form reading). Density overrides descendant margins through tailwind-merge, so use `Prose` (or wrap `proseVariants` in `cn()`).

components.name: FormattedNumber
components.summary: A locale-aware number, percentage, currency amount, unit or compact figure rendered with Intl.NumberFormat, with tabular figures and bidi isolation.
components.description:
Use `FormattedNumber` wherever a figure is shown to people: prices, deltas, counts, durations, table cells. It wraps `Intl.NumberFormat`, accepts numbers, bigints and numeric strings (formatted exactly, no float rounding), and never throws on bad input.

The number-format "style" is the prop `format` (`decimal`, `percent`, `currency`, `unit`, `compact`), not `style`: in Vue `style` is the inline-style attribute, and a static `style="percent"` is compiled into an empty style object before the component sees it. A dynamic `:style="'percent'"` string that names one of the five formats is still accepted as an alias (for code written against the Intl option name), but write `format`. `format="compact"` is decimal style with compact notation ("1.2K"); an explicit `notation` wins over it.

`locale` defaults to `en`, not the browser locale, so server and client render identical text; pass the app locale explicitly. Safe fallbacks (nothing throws): a value that is NaN, Infinity, blank or non-numeric renders `fallback` (default `n/a`); `format="currency"` without a valid `currency`, or `format="unit"` without `unit`, renders plain decimal (and throws a ContractError in strict mode, see `requires`); a malformed `currency` code renders plain decimal; an unknown `unit` renders the plain number followed by the unit text; a malformed `locale` falls back to `en`; fraction digits are clamped to 0 to 20 and `maximumFractionDigits` is raised to `minimumFractionDigits` when smaller. `-0` is shown as `0`. A small negative that rounds to zero ("-0") needs `signDisplay="negative"`.

`tone="positive"`, `"negative"` and `"auto"` (from the sign of the value) add colour AND a visible sign (`signDisplay` defaults to `exceptZero` for them), so colour is never the only signal. Use `formatNumber(value, options)` (exported next to the component) for plain strings such as chart labels or `aria-label`s.

props.name: value
props.description: The figure. Numeric strings (`"1234.5"`, `"1e3"`) and bigints are formatted exactly. NaN, Infinity, blank and non-numeric values render `fallback`.

props.name: format
props.description: Number-format style (the Intl `style` option; named `format` because `style` is the Vue inline-style attribute). `percent` multiplies by 100 (0.25 is 25%). `currency` needs `currency`, `unit` needs `unit`. `compact` is decimal with compact notation. Unknown values fall back to `decimal`.

props.name: currency
props.description: ISO 4217 code such as `EUR` (any case). Required for `format="currency"`. A malformed code renders plain decimal.

props.name: unit
props.description: Intl sanctioned unit such as `kilometer`, `liter`, `kilometer-per-hour`. Required for `format="unit"`. An unknown unit renders the number then the unit text.

props.name: notation
props.description: Notation. Defaults to `compact` for `format="compact"`, else `standard`. Unknown values are ignored.

props.name: minimumFractionDigits
props.description: Fewest fraction digits, 0 to 20 (clamped).

props.name: maximumFractionDigits
props.description: Most fraction digits, 0 to 20 (clamped); raised to `minimumFractionDigits` when smaller.

props.name: signDisplay
props.description: When to show a sign. Defaults to `auto`, or `exceptZero` for the tones `positive`, `negative` and `auto` so the sign backs up the colour.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 tag (`de-DE`, `ar-EG`). Malformed tags fall back to `en`. Never defaults to the runtime locale, so SSR and hydration agree.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Text for an invalid value. Sets `data-invalid="true"` on the root.

props.name: tabular
props.description: Equal-width figures (`tabular-nums`) so numbers in a column line up.

props.name: isolate
props.description: Wrap the text in a `<bdi>` so a number or its sign never reorders inside right-to-left or mixed-direction text.

props.name: variant
props.description: `plain` inherits the font, `mono` uses the monospace font, `outline` draws a hairline box. Unknown values fall back to `plain`.

props.name: size
props.description: Font size; `inherit` keeps the surrounding size. Unknown values fall back to `inherit`.

props.name: tone
props.description: `muted` secondary colour. `positive` (success) and `negative` (destructive) colour the text and show a sign. `auto` picks positive, negative or default from the sign of the value. An invalid value never gets a status colour.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight. Unset inherits.

props.name: as
props.description: Root element tag (`span`, `strong`, `div`, `td`...).

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

components.name: Heading
components.summary: Semantic h1-h6 heading with independent visual size, underline/divider decoration and optional eyebrow and description.
components.description:
Use `Heading` for every title. `level` decides the semantic element (h1-h6, invalid values fall back to 2) and drives the default visual size; `size` overrides the look without changing the document outline. components.name: RelativeTime
components.summary: A `<time>` element that writes a moment as relative text ("3 minutes ago", "in 2 days") with the absolute date in the tooltip, optionally kept fresh by one shared timer.
components.description:
Use `RelativeTime` for timestamps in feeds, tables and activity lists. It renders a real `<time datetime="...">` with text from `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`, so the machine-readable value and the localised text always agree. Past and future moments both work ("3 minutes ago", "in 3 minutes"); units step from seconds through minutes, hours, days, weeks and months to years, truncating toward zero so 59 minutes never reads as an hour. Use `minUnit` and `maxUnit` to limit the units (`maxUnit="day"` gives "400 days ago").

Hydration safety: the component never reads the clock while setting up or rendering. Without `now`, the first render (server and client) is the absolute date, formatted in UTC unless `timeZone` is given, and the relative text appears right after mount. With `now` (a Date, epoch milliseconds or ISO string) the output is fully pinned and identical everywhere, which also makes tests, docs and screenshots deterministic. `locale` defaults to `en`, not the browser locale, for the same reason: pass the app locale. After mount the tooltip date uses the browser time zone unless `timeZone` is set.

Live updates: `updateInterval` (milliseconds, 250 to 2147483647, default 0 = off) refreshes the text. Every instance shares ONE module-level timer that runs at the smallest requested period and is created with the first subscriber and cleared with the last, or when the interval changes to 0. A pinned `now` disables updates. Avoid intervals below 1000 ms for lists: text only changes when a unit count changes.

Input handling: strings must be ISO 8601 (`2025-06-15`, `2025-06-15T09:30:00Z`, with an offset or a space instead of `T`); other date strings are treated as invalid because engines parse them differently. Dates and numbers outside the JavaScript Date range, NaN, Infinity, blank or non-date values render `fallback` (default "Unknown time") in a `<time>` without a `datetime` attribute and with `data-state="invalid"`. Nothing throws. `data-state` is `relative`, `absolute` (before mount without `now`) or `invalid`.

The name is `unitStyle` because `style` is the Vue inline-style attribute; it maps to the Intl `style` option. For a plain string use `formatRelative(datetime, now, options)` exported next to the component.

a11y: Renders a native `<time>` element with a machine-readable `datetime`; the visible text is the accessible name and is read as written ("3 minutes ago").
The `title` tooltip is supplemental: it is not reachable by keyboard or touch. Show the absolute date as text where it matters (receipts, audit logs).
`lang` is set to the resolved locale and `dir="auto"` lets right-to-left text such as `ar` resolve its own direction inside a left-to-right page.
Live updates replace the text in place without a live region, so screen readers are not interrupted every tick. Do not wrap the element in `aria-live`.

Tone and the dotted variant are never the only signal. Colours use `text-success`, `text-warning-foreground`, `text-destructive`, `text-info` and `text-muted-foreground`, covered by the contrast tests; the dotted underline survives forced-colors mode.
llmNotes: Always pass `now` in docs, tests and server-rendered pages that must be deterministic; without it the first render is the absolute date.
The Intl style option is the prop `unitStyle`, not `style`.
Pass `datetime` as ISO 8601 (or a Date or epoch ms); other date strings are invalid and render the fallback.
Use `updateInterval` (for example 60000) only on pages that stay open; all instances share one timer, so many rows are cheap.
Do not format times in templates with `new Date()` or `Date.now()`: it breaks hydration. Use RelativeTime.
Use `formatRelative(datetime, now, options)` for plain strings (`aria-label`, chart tooltips).

components.name: Text
components.summary: Body text with variant presets, size, tone, weight, leading, transform, wrapping, alignment and truncation or line clamping.
components.description:
Use `Text` for paragraphs, captions and inline labels instead of raw `

Variants are presets that fill only the `size` / `tone` / `weight` you leave unset: `default` plain body copy; `caption` (xs, muted) for helper text under media or inputs; `label` (sm, medium, tight leading) for form-like labels and metadata keys (render with `as="label"`/`span`); `overline` (xs, muted, medium weight, normal case) for small labels that are not headings; `mono` (sm, monospace) for IDs, hashes and numbers. Tones: `muted` secondary copy, `subtle` (same colour as `muted`; a dimmer grey cannot meet AA contrast), `foreground` to reset inside muted parents, `primary` accent, and `success`/`warning`/`danger`/`info` for status.

components.name: ConfigProvider
components.summary: Sets text direction, locale, time zone, motion override, default size and density, and translated built-in strings for everything inside it.
components.description: Wrap an app or a region once instead of passing `locale`, `size` or translated labels to every component. `dir` and `locale` are set as `dir` and `lang` on the wrapper and passed to the headless primitives (menus, tabs, sliders), which read them even in portalled content. `labels` translates the strings a component ships with, keyed `<component>.<string>`: `pagination.nav|first|previous|next|last|page|summary`, `datePicker.placeholder|clear|required|dialog`, `confirmDialog.confirm|cancel|defaultTitle|error`. Pagination, DatePicker and ConfirmDialog read them today. Precedence per value is the component prop, then the nearest provider, then the English default, so a component with no provider behaves exactly as before. Providers nest: an inner provider overrides an outer one per key and `labels` merge per key. Invalid values (an unknown `dir`, a bad locale or time zone, a label that is not a non-blank string) are ignored, and labels are always rendered as text, never as HTML. Read the merged result in your own components with `useConfig()` (a computed with `dir`, `locale`, `timeZone`, `reducedMotion`, `size`, `density`, `labels`) and give them the same translation hook with `useConfigLabels(prefix, defaults)`. `reducedMotion` is an app-level override for code that asks; CSS `motion-reduce:` rules still follow the operating system. `dir` and `lang` are attributes of the wrapper, so portalled content (dialogs, popovers) does not inherit them from the DOM: use the same `dir` on `<html>` for those, or rely on the primitives that read it from the provider. Use `asChild` to render no extra element, or `class="contents"` to keep layout unchanged.

props.name: timeZone

props.name: reducedMotion
props.description: `user` follows the operating system. The other two are exposed as `data-reduced-motion` and `useConfig().reducedMotion`; CSS media queries are not changed.

props.name: size
props.description: Default size for Pagination and DatePicker when they have no `size` of their own. Sizes a component does not support fall back to its default. Set as `data-size`.

props.name: density

props.name: labels
props.description: Translations of built-in strings keyed `<component>.<string>`. Merged per key with outer providers. Non-string, blank and unknown-key entries are ignored.

components.name: AppShell
components.summary: Application frame with header, collapsible sidebar (drawer on mobile), main content and footer slots.
components.description: Use `AppShell` as the root layout of dashboards and admin apps. Pick a `layout`: `top-nav-sidebar` (default; full-width header above sidebar and content), `sidebar-left` / `sidebar-right` (full-height sidebar, header over the content column only), `top-nav` (header and content, no sidebar) or `dual-sidebar` (`sidebar` slot on the start side plus a `sidebar-end` slot, e.g. a details panel). Sidebars render in `<aside>` landmarks with the `sidebar-*` tokens; their content is yours. From the drawer breakpoint up (`md` by default, `lg` via `drawerBreakpoint`) a sidebar is always visible and collapses to an icon rail (`railWidth` sm/md/lg, `collapseMode="rail"`) or disappears (`collapseMode="hidden"`) with `v-model:collapsed` (`v-model:collapsed-end` for the end sidebar); `sidebarWidth` sets the expanded width. Below the breakpoint the sidebar is an off-canvas drawer: hidden unless `v-model:open` (`v-model:open-end`) is true, then it is a modal dialog over the page above a backdrop that closes on click and Escape: everything behind it is `inert` (so focus cannot leave the drawer), page scrolling is locked (`lockScroll`), focus moves into the drawer and returns on close, and closes by itself when the viewport grows past the breakpoint. `contentMaxWidth` centres and constrains the page content (`sm` … `7xl`, `prose`, `full`) with responsive padding. Slot props `{ collapsed, open, toggle, sidebarId, expanded, triggerProps, collapsedEnd, openEnd, toggleEnd }` are available in every slot; `toggle` collapses on desktop and opens/closes the drawer on mobile, and `v-bind="triggerProps"` on the menu button adds `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded`. The default slot is the `<main>` content (set `:main="false"` to render a `div` when the shell is embedded in a page that already has a `main`). No extra dependencies: it is plain CSS classes plus a media query listener.

Unknown values fall back to the default. Sets `data-layout` when not default.

a11y: Sidebar is an <aside> landmark with `aria-label` (sidebarLabel); header, main and footer are native landmarks.
<main> has an id and tabindex="-1" so skip links and programmatic focus work; enable `skipLink` for a built-in skip link.

Mobile drawer: while open the sidebar is `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="true"` and its `aria-label`; the header, content and the other sidebar are `inert`, so Tab cannot leave the drawer and screen readers cannot reach the page behind it. The backdrop is aria-hidden and closes on click; Escape closes it; focus moves into the drawer on open and returns to the previously focused control on close; page scroll is locked while it is open.

Menu button: give it an `aria-label` and spread the `triggerProps` slot prop on it (`aria-controls` points at the sidebar id, `aria-expanded` follows the drawer on mobile and the collapsed state on desktop).
Responsive: below the drawer breakpoint the content column is full width (no sidebar column), so nothing scrolls horizontally at 320px; the drawer is capped to the viewport width.
Only one `<main>` per page: pass `:main="false"` when the shell is embedded.
Give each sidebar a distinct accessible name (`sidebarLabel`, `sidebarEndLabel`) when there are two.
With `layout="sidebar-right"` or `dual-sidebar` the end sidebar comes after the main content in the DOM, which is its reading and tab order.
Collapsing only changes width; make sure collapsed sidebar items keep accessible names (aria-label on icon-only links).
requires: Throws a ContractError when a rendered sidebar has a blank `sidebarLabel` (or `sidebarEndLabel` for the end sidebar).
Throws a ContractError when `skipLink` is set and `mainId` or `skipLinkLabel` is blank.
Throws a ContractError when `main` is false and the page has no `<main>` (or `role="main"`) landmark elsewhere.
llmNotes: Sidebar content is the consumer's; AppShell only provides the frame, width, drawer behaviour and tokens.
Bind both v-model:collapsed and v-model:open if you need to persist state; otherwise they work uncontrolled.
Use the slot prop `toggle` for the hamburger button (`toggleEnd` for the end sidebar).
Choose layout by structure: top-nav-sidebar (header over everything), sidebar-left/right (full-height sidebar), top-nav (no sidebar), dual-sidebar (two sidebars; use the sidebar-end slot).
Use contentMaxWidth instead of wrapping the default slot in a Container; use drawerBreakpoint="lg" for dense sidebars that need more room.
Do not mix collapsed with `open`: collapsed is desktop-only (rail/hidden), open is the mobile drawer.
Pair with PageHeader inside the default slot for page titles.

components.description: Use `CenteredLayout` for pages with a single focused task: login, sign-up, password reset, 404, onboarding. components.name: PageHeader
components.summary: Page title block with description, breadcrumb, back link, tabs, actions, centered / compact / hero variants and optional sticky mode.
components.description: Put one `PageHeader` at the top of every page view. The title renders in an `h1` (change with `titleAs`), the description below it, a `breadcrumb` slot above, and `actions` on the right (stacked below on small screens). Set `sticky` to pin it to the top of the scroll container with an opaque background and bottom border. Variants: `default` (heading left, actions right), `centered` (everything centred, e.g. marketing and empty states; `align="center"` centres any variant), `compact` (tighter spacing and a smaller title for dense or nested pages) and `hero` (banner with a flat `background`: `muted`, `primary` or an `image` via `backgroundImage`, plus a `background` slot for custom art). Add a back link with `backHref` (or the `back` slot for a router link) and sub-navigation with the `tabs` slot. For app-wide top bars use the `header` slot of AppShell instead.

components.name: ResizablePanels
components.summary: Two or more panels separated by draggable, keyboard-accessible handles; sizes are percentages that always add up to 100.
components.description: Use `ResizablePanels` for IDE-style layouts: a file tree next to an editor, a master/detail view, a console under a preview. Put `ResizablePanel` and `ResizableHandle` as alternating direct children (panel, handle, panel, ...). Sizes are percentages with `defaultSize` / `minSize` / `maxSize` per panel; they are always normalised to sum 100 and clamped, whatever you pass (NaN, negative, sums other than 100). Bind `v-model:sizes` to read or control the layout, or set `storageKey` to remember it in localStorage. A panel can be `collapsible`. Dragging uses pointer events (mouse, touch and pen); the handle is a focusable `separator` with arrow-key, Shift, Home / End and Enter support. For a fixed, non-resizable split use `SplitLayout`. The root fills its parent (`h-full w-full`): give it a height with `class`. For an exact server-rendered first paint give every panel a `defaultSize`; sizes are finalised right after mount.

parts.name: ResizablePanel
parts.description: A sized region. Direct child of `ResizablePanels`; its content scrolls / clips independently (`overflow-hidden` by default, override with `class`).

props.name: defaultSize
props.description: Initial size in percent. Missing or invalid values (NaN, negative) share the remaining space equally.

props.name: minSize
props.description: Minimum size in percent.

props.name: maxSize
props.description: Maximum size in percent (never below minSize).

props.name: collapsible
props.description: Collapses to `collapsedSize` when dragged below half of `minSize`, or with Enter on an adjacent handle. Sets `data-collapsed`.

props.name: collapsedSize
props.description: Size in percent while collapsed (0 .. minSize).

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last; wins over internal classes.

parts.name: ResizableHandle
parts.description: The draggable divider (`role="separator"`) between two panels. Exposes `aria-valuenow` (size of the preceding panel), `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`.

props.name: variant
props.description: `line` = hairline with a wide hit area; `bar` = thicker muted track.

props.name: size
props.description: Visible thickness. `line`: sm and md 1px, lg 2px. `bar`: sm 4px, md 8px, lg 12px. The 24px hit area never changes. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the separator. Required: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` must say which panels it resizes.

props.name: grip
props.description: Show a small grip in the middle. The default slot replaces it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable this handle only: leaves the tab order, gets `aria-disabled`, ignores pointer and keys.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last; wins over internal classes.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` lays panels in a row (the handles are vertical bars); `vertical` stacks them. Unknown values fall back to horizontal.

props.name: sizes
props.description: Controlled sizes in percent (`v-model:sizes`), one per panel in DOM order. Ignored while its length differs from the panel count; normalised and clamped.

props.name: storageKey
props.description: localStorage key. Layout is restored after mount and saved after each completed resize. Missing / throwing storage and corrupt JSON are ignored.

props.name: step
props.description: Arrow-key step in percent. Invalid values fall back to 5.

props.name: largeStep
props.description: Step in percent while Shift is held. Invalid values fall back to 20.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable every handle.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes (e.g. `h-64`).

a11y: Each handle is `role="separator"` with `tabindex="0"`, `aria-orientation` (a horizontal row of panels has VERTICAL separators), `aria-valuenow` (size % of the preceding panel), `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`.

Keyboard: Arrow keys along the layout axis resize by `step` (Shift = `largeStep`); Home / End jump to the smallest / largest size reachable; Enter toggles a collapsible neighbour. Arrows flip in right-to-left containers.
Always give handles an `aria-label` that says what they resize (the `label` prop; default "Resize panels"). Disabled handles leave the tab order and set `aria-disabled`.
Pointer target: the 1px line handle has a 24px-wide invisible hit area (WCAG 2.5.8); the keyboard alternative to dragging is the Arrow/Home/End map above (WCAG 2.5.7).

Focus shows as a ring-coloured handle plus a transparent outline, so it is visible in forced-colors mode. The `line` handle fills with `CanvasText` there (hover, focus and drag included) and the `bar` handle draws a border, because forced-colors mode drops background tokens; the idle outline that `outline-hidden` would add is removed so the divider stays a clean line. Panels stay side by side at every width; give the root a sensible `min-w-0` parent so it does not overflow at 320px.

Handle `size` changes the visible thickness only: the 24px hit area, keyboard map and `aria-value*` attributes are identical at every size. Prefer `lg` when the divider is the main control of the layout.
Handle transitions and hover colours respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
requires: Throws a ContractError when ResizablePanels has no ResizablePanel, starts or ends with a ResizableHandle, or has two panels or two handles in a row.
Throws a ContractError when a ResizableHandle has none of `label`, `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`.
Throws a ContractError when a ResizablePanel or ResizableHandle is used outside ResizablePanels.
llmNotes: Children of ResizablePanels must alternate ResizablePanel, ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel ...; never put two handles in a row.
Give ResizablePanels an explicit height (`class="h-64"`) or a sized parent; the root is `h-full w-full`.
Sizes are percentages summing to 100; do not compute pixel widths yourself.
Use `v-model:sizes` with an array whose length equals the panel count, or `storage-key` for persistence; not both.
Add `aria-label` to every ResizableHandle.
For a static split use SplitLayout instead.

components.name: SplitLayout
components.summary: Two-pane layout (start / end) with ratio presets, fixed-width pane and responsive stacking.
components.description: Use `SplitLayout` for master/detail views, settings with a side panel, or content next to a preview. Choose a `ratio` preset (`1:1`, `1:2`, `2:1`, `1:3`, `3:1` as start:end; the older `equal`, `1/3`, `2/3` still work as aliases of `1:1`, `1:2`, `2:1`) or pin one pane to a CSS length with `fixed-start` / `fixed-end` + `fixedWidth`. Below the `stackBelow` breakpoint the panes stack vertically. Use `sticky="start"` or `"end"` to keep one pane (filters, summary, table of contents) in view while the other scrolls, and `reverseOnMobile` to show the end pane first when stacked (e.g. a summary above the form). Panes do not scroll by themselves; add `overflow-auto` and a height via `class` on the content you slot in. For resizable panes use a dedicated Resizable component.

props.name: ratio
props.description: Column split, start:end. `1:1` = `equal`; `1:2` = `1/3` (start gets a third); `2:1` = `2/3` (start gets two thirds); `1:3` and `3:1` quarter splits. Unknown values fall back to equal.

props.name: fixedWidth
props.description: CSS length of the fixed pane, set through the `--split-fixed` CSS variable. Only used by fixed-start / fixed-end.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description: Breakpoint below which the panes stack vertically.

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between panes.

props.name: divider
props.description: Border between the panes (horizontal when stacked, vertical when side by side).

props.name: sticky
props.description: Makes that pane sticky (self-start, top = stickyOffset) once side by side. Unknown values are ignored. Sets `data-sticky`.

props.name: stickyOffset
props.description: CSS length for the sticky pane top offset, set through the `--split-sticky-top` CSS variable. Empty values fall back to 1rem.

props.name: reverseOnMobile
props.description: While stacked, show the end pane first (max-md:order-first / max-lg:order-first). DOM order is unchanged. Sets `data-reverse-mobile`.

props.name: as
props.description: Root element.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: start
slots.description: First pane (left in LTR).

slots.name: end
slots.description: Second pane (right in LTR).

a11y: Presentational grid; DOM order (start, then end) is the reading and tab order, including when stacked. With `reverseOnMobile` the visual order differs from the DOM order, so only use it when both orders make sense.
Use `as` with a landmark (`section`) and aria-label when a pane is a distinct region.

Responsive: panes stack in one column below `stackBelow` (`md` by default, 768px; `lg` = 1024px) and both panes have `min-w-0`, so nothing overflows at 320px. A scrolling container around a sticky pane must be focusable and labelled (see the live example).
Ratios and the fixed width are applied through CSS variables (`--split-cols`, `--split-fixed`) so they follow the same breakpoint as the stack.
llmNotes: Slots are named `start` and `end`.
The ratio, fixedWidth and stickyOffset are applied as CSS variables (the only inline styles); pass any valid CSS length.
Prefer a:b ratios (`1:2`, `2:1`) in new code; `1/3` and `2/3` are legacy aliases.
Use sticky + stickyOffset for side summaries/filters; the sticky pane sticks to the nearest scroll container and only once side by side.
reverseOnMobile changes visual order only; keep the important pane first in the DOM for screen readers.
Panes use min-w-0 so wide content does not overflow; set overflow on your own content.

components.name: Affix
components.summary: Pins content with `position: sticky` and reports whether it is currently stuck.
components.description: Wrap a toolbar, table of contents or summary card in `Affix` so it stays visible while the page (or a scroll container, via `root`) scrolls. Positioning is pure CSS (`sticky` plus an inline `top` / `bottom` from `offsetTop` / `offsetBottom` in px); an `IntersectionObserver` watching a 1px sentinel placed next to the content drives the `change` event, the `data-stuck` attribute and the `stuck` slot prop (a scroll-listener fallback is used when IntersectionObserver is unavailable). The `variant` prop adds a shadow or border only while stuck. Sticky only works while the nearest scrolling ancestor and the parent are taller than the content: do not put `overflow: hidden` on ancestors. The sentinel is a zero-net-height inline-block sibling next to the content, so avoid parents that add `gap` between children. For two-column layouts use `SplitLayout` with `sticky`.

props.name: offsetTop
props.description: Pixels from the top of the scroll container where the content sticks. Defaults to 0 unless only `offsetBottom` is given. Non-finite values are ignored; negative values are allowed.

props.name: offsetBottom
props.description: Pixels from the bottom edge (pins to the bottom). Drives stuck detection only when `offsetTop` is not set; both are applied inline when both are set.

props.name: zIndex
props.description: A number or any CSS value such as `var(--z-overlay)`. Invalid values fall back to the `--z-sticky` token.

props.name: variant
props.description: Look while stuck: `elevated` adds background + shadow, `bordered` background + edge border. Unknown values fall back to plain.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Render as a normal block: not sticky, no observer, never stuck.

props.name: root
props.description: Scroll container as an element or CSS selector. `null` or not found = the viewport.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge (e.g. `z-10`, `bg-card`); wins over internal classes.

slots.name: default
slots.description: The pinned content.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The stuck state flipped. Not emitted for the initial not-stuck state.
