a11y: Affix adds no role or label of its own: put landmarks (`role="toolbar"`, `<nav aria-label>`) on the content or pass `aria-*` attributes, which fall through to the pinned element.
The sentinel is `aria-hidden` and not focusable. Stuck styling never hides content; ensure the pinned element does not cover focused elements below it (use scroll-padding on the container).
Transitions are disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

When `root` is a scrolling box, that box must itself be keyboard reachable: give it `tabindex="0"`, `role="region"` and an `aria-label` (the live example does), or axe reports scrollable-region-focusable.

The `elevated` variant also gets the opaque `bg-background`, and a border in forced-colors mode (shadows disappear there), so stuck content is distinguishable from the scrolled content without relying on the shadow alone.
requires: Throws a ContractError when `root` is a selector that matches no element (or is not a valid selector), because the Affix would silently watch the viewport.
llmNotes: Use `offset-top` / `offset-bottom` numbers (px), not inline style, for the sticky distance.
Use `z-index` with a CSS variable such as `var(--z-overlay)` rather than magic numbers when layering.
Sticky fails if an ancestor has overflow hidden/auto without a height; point `root` at the real scroll container.
Attributes (id, aria-label, data-*) land on the pinned element, not on a wrapper; the component renders a sentinel sibling before/after it.

components.name: InfiniteScroll
components.summary: Fires `load` when the end of a list scrolls into view; handles loading, end-of-list and error-with-retry states.
components.description: Wrap the items of a feed, table or list in `InfiniteScroll`. A hidden sentinel after the content is watched with `IntersectionObserver` (with a scroll-listener fallback when it is unavailable); when it comes within `rootMargin` of the viewport (or of your scroll container via `root`) the component emits `load` once. Set `loading` synchronously in your handler and clear it when the page arrived: the sentinel is re-checked after every loading cycle, so a still-visible sentinel loads the next page. Set `finished` when no more data exists and `error` to show a retry affordance. Do not use it for page-numbered data (use pagination) or for rendering thousands of rows (pair it with VirtualList).

props.name: loading
props.description: A page is being fetched: shows the loading slot and blocks `load`. Set it synchronously inside `@load`.

props.name: finished
props.description: No more data: shows the end slot and stops observing.

props.name: error
props.description: Last fetch failed: shows the error slot with a retry button and stops auto-loading. A string is used as the message.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Pause loading (no observer, no `load`).

props.name: root
props.description: Scroll container as an element or CSS selector (resolved after mount). `null` or not found = the viewport.

props.name: rootMargin
props.description: IntersectionObserver rootMargin: how early `load` fires. Invalid values fall back to the scroll-listener path.

props.name: variant
props.description: Footer density for the loading, end and error blocks. `default`: py-4, error message above the retry button. `compact`: py-2, message and retry on one wrapping row. Sets `data-variant` when not default. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: size
props.description: Footer text and spinner size: sm text-xs with a 12px spinner, md text-sm with 16px, lg text-base with 20px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: default
slots.description: The loaded items.

slots.name: loading
slots.description: Shown while `loading` (default: spinner + "Loading…").

slots.name: end
slots.description: Shown when `finished` (default: "No more results.").

slots.name: error
slots.description: Shown when `error` (default: message + "Try again" button). Call `retry` to emit `retry` + `load`.

emits.name: load
emits.description: Fetch the next page. Emitted once per intersection; never while `loading`, `finished`, `error` or `disabled`.

emits.name: retry
emits.description: The retry button was used; `load` follows immediately.

components.name: Grid
components.summary: CSS grid with 1-12 columns, per-breakpoint column counts and a gap scale.
components.description: Use `Grid` for card galleries, stat rows and form layouts. Set `cols` for the base (mobile) count and `sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl` to change it from that breakpoint upwards (mobile-first). All class names come from fixed maps so Tailwind generates them. Invalid column numbers fall back to 1 (base) or are ignored (breakpoints). For content-driven grids set `minItemWidth` (e.g. `16rem`): the grid fits as many columns as possible, each at least that wide (`repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 16rem), 1fr))`), so no breakpoints are needed. Add `autoFill` to keep empty tracks. `gapSm` / `gapMd` / `gapLg` grow the gap responsively. `variant` draws each direct child as a `bordered` or `card` cell and `layout` sets emphasis: `lead` makes the first item span the whole row, `feature` makes it span 2 columns and 2 rows from `md` up (use at least 3 columns from `md`). For other span control apply your own classes on the children.

props.name: xl

props.name: gap

props.name: gapSm
props.description: Gap from the `sm` breakpoint up (sm:gap-*). Invalid values are ignored.

props.name: gapMd
props.description: Gap from the `md` breakpoint up (md:gap-*). Invalid values are ignored.

props.name: gapLg
props.description: Gap from the `lg` breakpoint up (lg:gap-*). Invalid values are ignored.

props.name: minItemWidth
props.description: Auto-fit mode: columns are at least this wide and as many as fit. Number = px, string = CSS length (`16rem`, `240px`, `20ch`, `30%`). Set through the `--grid-min` CSS variable; replaces base `cols`; breakpoint props (`sm`/`md`/...) still override it. Invalid values are ignored.

props.name: autoFill
props.description: With `minItemWidth`: use `auto-fill` (keeps empty tracks) instead of `auto-fit` (collapses empty tracks so items stretch).

props.name: gapY

props.name: variant

components.summary: Flex container that lays children out in a row or column with consistent gaps.
components.description: Use `Stack` for one-dimensional layout with a gap scale instead of `flex flex-col gap-4` snippets. `HStack` (row, vertically centred) and `VStack` (column) are thin wrappers that preset `direction`. components.name: StyleScope
components.summary: Applies one style pack (density, corners, depth, type) to everything inside it.
components.description: A style pack restyles the whole system by overriding tokens (`--spacing`, `--radius`, shadows, text sizes, fonts, borders), so every component follows without changing its markup. `StyleScope` sets `data-style` on a wrapper, which lets one page mix looks: a dense `workbench` data panel next to the core `quiet` marketing page, or an `editorial` article inside an app. The pack CSS must be imported once (`@perfect-design/ui/packs.css` or a single `@perfect-design/ui/packs/<name>.css`). To switch the whole app, use `useThemeStore().setStyle()` or `StylePicker`, which set `data-style` on `<html>`. The packs are: `quiet` (core), `workbench` (dense, hairlines), `tactile` (raised surfaces), `editorial` (serif, square, reading-first), `raw` (hard shadows, ink borders), `contrast` (7:1 text, bold focus) and `terminal` (mono, dense). Each one is justified in DESIGN.md.

components.summary: Boolean (or indeterminate) checkbox with optional label and description, sizes, tones, shapes, invalid state and Field wiring.

For a bordered or filled tile around the choice use `CheckboxCard`; `Checkbox` has no `variant` because the card components already cover that look. Use `Switch` for settings that apply immediately, `RadioGroup` when exactly one option can be chosen. The model is `true | false | 'indeterminate'`; clicking an indeterminate box turns it on. components.description: Use `CheckboxCard` when a boolean (or multi-select) choice deserves more room than a plain `Checkbox`: plan add-ons, notification channels, feature toggles with an explanation. Use `RadioCard` when exactly one option can be chosen, and `Checkbox` for compact lists. Any extra attribute (`aria-label`, `id`, `data-*`, listeners) is forwarded to the native input, not the label root.

a11y: The native `<input type="checkbox">` carries the semantics (role checkbox, checked state, form submission); it is visually hidden but focusable and the whole card is its label.
Space toggles when focused; `:focus-visible` shows a ring on the card via `has-focus-visible`.
The input is `aria-labelledby` the title and `aria-describedby` the description when present. With no title, pass `aria-label` (forwarded to the input).

`CheckboxCardGroup` has `role="group"`: give it `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`, or wrap it in a `Field`, whose label then names the group through `aria-labelledby` (hint and error go to `aria-describedby`). `aria-invalid` is not allowed on a group, so the invalid state is on each card input.

Tones and the stacked layout change only classes: the native input, its name and description wiring and the keyboard behaviour are identical. The check mark in the indicator carries the state, the tone colour is an addition.
Forced-colors mode: the focus ring becomes an outline, the checked card gets a system-colour border and the indicator a system-colour fill, and an invalid card a dashed border.
The check indicator is `aria-hidden`; state is exposed through the native `checked` property and `data-state`.
requires: Throws a ContractError when a `CheckboxCard` has no accessible name: no title, description or slot text, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (an icon alone does not count).
Throws a ContractError when `CheckboxCardGroup` has no accessible name: no `Field` label, `Fieldset` legend, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
Throws a ContractError when a `CheckboxCard` inside a `CheckboxCardGroup` has a missing or empty `value`, or a `value` another card in the group already uses.
llmNotes: Use CheckboxCard for rich multi-select options; use Checkbox for plain compact ones.
Always set `value` on each card inside CheckboxCardGroup; bind a string[] to the group, not to the cards.
Label the group with aria-label/aria-labelledby (or wrap in Field); pass aria-label on cards that have no title.
Extra attrs (aria-*, id, data-*) land on the native input, not on the label root; use `class` for root styling.
Use `variant` (outline|filled), `size` (sm|md|lg), `tone` (primary|success|danger|neutral|info) and `layout` (default|stacked); on the group they cascade to cards unless a card overrides.
Use `tone="danger"` for choices with a cost or risk, not for validation errors: errors use `invalid`.

components.name: MultiSelect
components.summary: Dropdown checkbox list with chips summary, search filter, select all / clear, max selections and full keyboard support.
components.description: Use `MultiSelect` when the user picks several values from a known list of 5-10 000 options and the selection should stay visible as compact chips (first `maxVisible` chips, then "+N more"). It is dependency-free: the panel is rendered inline below the trigger (absolute, `z-(--z-dropdown)`), so avoid placing it inside an `overflow-hidden` ancestor that would clip it. The model is `string[]` of option values; options are `{ value, label, disabled? }`. Use `Select` for a single value, `Combobox` for async/free-text lookups, `TagsInput` for free-form tags, `CheckboxCard` for a few rich options. Works controlled (`v-model`) and uncontrolled (`default-value`); the open state can be controlled with `v-model:open`. Extra attributes (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `data-*`) go to the trigger button; an `aria-label` is rendered as a hidden name and combined with the visible chips, so the accessible name always contains the visible text. `class` goes to the root.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: Selected option values (v-model). Omit for uncontrolled use. Non-arrays are treated as empty; duplicates and non-strings are dropped.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial selection when uncontrolled.

props.name: open
props.description: Open state (v-model:open). Omit for uncontrolled use. Never open while disabled.

props.name: options
props.type: { value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }[]
props.description: Available options. Entries without a string `value` are ignored. Disabled options cannot be toggled (a selected disabled option stays selected, also on Clear).

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Trigger text when nothing is selected.

props.name: searchable
props.description: Show the search box (case-insensitive label filter). When false the listbox takes focus and typing jumps to the first option starting with the typed text.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.description: Placeholder and accessible name of the search input.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown when no option matches or there are no options. Overridable with the `empty` slot.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum number of selected values. Remaining options become `aria-disabled`, a "n / max selected" counter replaces "Select all". Non-positive, NaN or non-numeric values mean unlimited; fractions are floored.

props.name: maxVisible
props.description: Chips shown in the trigger before the rest collapse into "+N more". 0 shows only the count; invalid values fall back to 3.

props.name: actions
props.description: Show the "Select all" (enabled, filtered options) and "Clear" actions row.

props.name: clearable
props.description: Show a clear (x) button (24px, 32px on touch devices) in the trigger while something is selected.

props.name: size
props.description: Trigger min height (28 / 32 / 36 / 40 px). Text is 16px on small screens and 14px from the `md` breakpoint (`lg` stays 16px); on touch devices the trigger is at least 44px tall.

props.name: variant
props.description: Surface of the trigger. `outline` is the bordered default, `filled` uses a muted fill, `underline` keeps a bottom rule that thickens on focus, `ghost` shows its border on hover and focus. Unknown values fall back to `outline`.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corners of the trigger. `underline` is always square-cornered. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.

props.description: Disables the trigger and blocks all changes. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.

props.name: required
props.description: Sets `aria-required` on the trigger. Also inherited from a Field.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and a destructive border. Also set by a Field with an error.

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name; one hidden input per selected value is rendered.

props.name: id
props.description: Trigger id. Falls back to the surrounding Field id, then a generated one.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the root (`data-slot="multi-select"`); use it to set the width.

a11y: The trigger is a `<button aria-haspopup="listbox" aria-expanded aria-controls>`; label it with a `Field` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (attrs go to the trigger). An author name is combined with the visible chips or placeholder through `aria-labelledby` (WCAG 2.5.3 label in name), so the trigger never has an `aria-label` that hides its visible text.

The panel contains a search input (focused on open) and a `role="listbox" aria-multiselectable` of `role="option" aria-selected` rows. The active option is announced via `aria-activedescendant` while DOM focus stays on the input (or on the listbox when `searchable=false`). The check box in each row is decorative and drawn only for selected rows, so it also shows in forced-colors mode.

`status` is never colour alone: success, warning and error draw an icon before the chevron. Success and warning also add visually hidden text ("Valid", "Warning") that the trigger references from `aria-describedby`; error sets `aria-invalid` and relies on the Field error message.

Every `variant` keeps a visible edge or fill and the focus indicator (a ring, or a thicker bottom border for `underline`); forced-colors mode draws the border of `underline` and `ghost` in system colours.
Trigger: ArrowDown / ArrowUp / Enter / Space open the panel; typing a character opens it and seeds the search.

In the panel: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the active option (skipping disabled, wrapping); Enter toggles it; Space toggles it while the search is empty (otherwise it is a normal character); Ctrl/Cmd+A selects all enabled options (unless text is typed in the search box); Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger; Tab closes. With `searchable=false`, Home/End jump and typing performs a type-ahead jump. The "Select all" and "Clear" buttons are for pointer use (`tabindex=-1`); Ctrl/Cmd+A is the keyboard equivalent of "Select all".

A visually hidden `role="status"` region announces the filtered option count ("3 options available") and the empty message while searching. Disabled and limit-blocked options are `aria-disabled`; the "n / max selected" counter is `aria-live="polite"` and uses tabular numbers.

Target sizes: the clear button is 24px (32px on touch devices), action buttons are at least 24px, options and the search input are 44px tall on touch devices. The trigger and search input use 16px text on small screens so iOS does not zoom.

Focus and the active option keep an outline in forced-colors mode; chips get a border. The trigger text wraps and the panel is at least 12rem wide, so nothing overflows at 320px. Layout uses logical properties (RTL safe). Animations respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Clicking outside or moving focus outside closes the panel.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the trigger has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (the chips and the placeholder do not count).
Throws a ContractError when an option `value` is missing, not a string, empty or used twice.
llmNotes: Bind a string[] with v-model; options are { value, label, disabled? } with unique string values.
Always give the trigger an accessible name: wrap in Field, or pass aria-label (it lands on the trigger button). The chips and placeholder do not count; without a name it raises a ContractError.
Use `max` to cap selections (it hides Select all); use `max-visible` to control chip overflow.
Set width with `class` on the root (e.g. class="w-72"); the panel matches the trigger width (min 12rem).
The panel is inline (not portalled): do not place it inside overflow-hidden containers.
Look props are `variant`, `shape`, `status` and `size`. `status="error"` already sets aria-invalid; still show a visible error message in a Field.
Use Select for a single value; use name="field" to submit one hidden input per selected value.

components.description: Use `RadioCard` + `RadioCardGroup` when exactly one option can be chosen and each option needs a title, description or icon: billing plans, shipping methods, deployment targets. Native radios are visually hidden (sr-only) so form submission and screen readers behave natively, while the group adds roving keyboard navigation (arrows move focus AND selection, Home/End jump, disabled cards are skipped). Use `RadioGroup` for compact radios, `SegmentedControl` for short inline switches, `CheckboxCard` for multiple selection. Extra attributes (`aria-label`, `id`, `data-*`) are forwarded to the native input; use `class` for the card root.

Throws a ContractError when a `RadioGroupItem` has a missing or empty `value`.
Throws a ContractError when a `RadioGroupItem` has no accessible name: no `label` prop, default slot text, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
llmNotes: Always pair RadioGroup with a visible Field label or `aria-label`.
Set `size`, `tone` and `label-position` once on the group; override on an item only when one option must differ. Use `description` on an item for helper text (needs a label).
Item `value` must be a non-empty string; put the label on the item (`label` prop), not outside it.
Use `v-model` on the group, never on items. 2-6 options only; otherwise use Select.

components.name: SegmentedControl
components.summary: Compact single choice (view switcher, range picker) built on a radiogroup, in pill, underline, outline or filled looks, horizontal or vertical.
components.description: Use `SegmentedControl` to switch between 2-5 mutually exclusive, short options that change how content is shown (List / Grid, Day / Week / Month). It looks like tabs but is a form control: it holds a value and does not own panels. Use `Tabs` for content navigation, `RadioGroup` for form answers that need descriptions, `Select` for long lists. Options come from the `options` array; override item content with the `option` slot. Works controlled (`v-model`) and uncontrolled (`default-value`).

props.name: options
props.type: Array<{ value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean; icon?: IconDefinition }>
props.description: Segments. `value` must be a non-empty string; `icon` is a FontAwesome IconDefinition shown before the label.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: v-model: the selected option value. Uncontrolled when omitted.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value when uncontrolled.

props.name: size
props.description: Segment height. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: variant
props.description: `pill`: muted tray with a raised selected chip. `underline`: a rule with a marker under (or, vertical, beside) the selected segment. `outline`: bordered tray with a bordered selection. `filled`: muted tray with a solid selection. Unknown values fall back to `pill`.

props.name: tone
props.description: Colour of the selected segment. `default` keeps the neutral look of the variant (raised chip, or foreground ink). In `pill` and `filled` a tone fills the selected segment with that colour; in `underline` and `outline` it colours the marker or border. `neutral` is foreground on background. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `vertical` stacks the segments in a column, left-aligned, and switches the arrow keys to Up and Down. Sets `aria-orientation`. Unknown values fall back to horizontal.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretch to the container width. Horizontal segments share the width equally; vertical segments keep their height.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every segment. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets `aria-invalid="true"` on the group. Also set by a Field with an error.

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name; hidden inputs are rendered when inside a `<form>`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the root; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: option
slots.description: Replaces the content (icon + label) of each segment.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Emitted when the user selects a segment.

const range = ref('week')
const options = [{ value: 'day', label: 'Day' }, { value: 'week', label: 'Week' }, { value: 'month', label: 'Month' }]

a11y: Root is `role="radiogroup"` with `role="radio"` segments and `aria-checked`. Name it with `aria-label`, or put it in a Field: the Field label then names it through `aria-labelledby`.

Keyboard: roving tabindex, so Tab enters once; the arrow keys of the control axis move focus and select (Left and Right when horizontal, Up and Down when `orientation="vertical"`, which is also announced as `aria-orientation`); Home and End move focus to the ends; disabled segments are skipped.
Icon-only segments still need a `label` (it is the accessible name); icons are decorative (`aria-hidden`).
The selected segment is also marked in forced-colors mode (system colours); invalid draws a dashed border. Segments are 24px or taller (36px on touch pointers).

Roles, names and keyboard behaviour are the same in every `variant` and `tone`: the selected segment carries `aria-checked` and `data-state="checked"`, and each variant marks it with a fill, border or underline, not colour alone. In forced-colors mode every variant uses the system highlight for the selected segment.
Responsive: the control wraps onto more rows instead of overflowing at 320px.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the control has no accessible name: no `Field` label, `Fieldset` legend, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
Throws a ContractError when an option has no text `label` (an icon alone does not count; with the `option` slot the slot must supply text).
Throws a ContractError when an option `value` is missing, empty or used twice.
llmNotes: Use for 2-5 short options that change presentation; use Tabs when each option owns a content panel.
Always label the control (`aria-label` or Field). Every option needs a text `label`.
Pass `options` as data and bind with `v-model`; never nest your own radio markup.

Pick `variant` for the look (pill, underline, outline, filled), `tone` for the selected colour (default is neutral) and `orientation="vertical"` for a column; use `segmentedControlVariants` / `segmentedControlItemVariants` to style custom elements the same way.
replaces: shadcn-vue ToggleGroup (type single) used as a segmented switch

components.name: Switch
components.summary: On/off toggle for settings that take effect immediately, with optional label and description, sizes, tones and on/off icons.
components.description: Use `Switch` for binary settings that apply right away (notifications, dark mode, feature flags). Use `Checkbox` when the choice is submitted later with a form or when several can be selected from a list. Give it a name with the `label` prop (or slot), which renders a `<label>` beside the switch, or place it in a `Field` (`orientation="horizontal"` is the idiomatic row layout), or set `aria-label`. `description` adds helper text under the label, `labelPosition="start"` moves the label before the switch, `tone` recolours the on state and `showIcons` draws a check or cross on the thumb. Works controlled (`v-model`) and uncontrolled (`default-value`).

props.name: modelValue
props.description: v-model value. Uncontrolled when omitted; `null` renders as off.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial state when uncontrolled.

props.name: size
props.description: Track and thumb size (28x16 / 36x20 / 44x24 px); the hit area is always at least 24px tall. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: tone
props.description: Colour of the on track. The off track is the same for every tone and the thumb always moves, so the state never rests on colour. Unknown values fall back to `primary`.

props.name: showIcons
props.description: Draws a check on the thumb when on and a cross when off. The glyphs are decorative (`aria-hidden`); the name and `aria-checked` carry the state for assistive technology.

props.name: onLabel
props.description: Short text inside the track while on (for example "On"). Decorative and `aria-hidden`: the accessible name stays the label and the state stays `aria-checked`. The track widens to hold it (56px at `md`, 64px at `lg`) and the off track becomes muted with an input border, so the text uses the tested tone-foreground and muted-foreground pairs. `sm` ignores it. About three characters fit; longer text is clipped.

props.name: offLabel
props.description: Short text inside the track while off (for example "Off"). Same rules as `onLabel`. Either one can be used alone; the track still widens.

props.name: label
props.description: Text rendered in a `<label for>` beside the switch. Use the `label` slot for rich content. Without a label the switch renders as the bare control, as before.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text under the label, referenced from the switch through `aria-describedby` (merged with Field hint and error ids). Shown only together with a label. Use the `description` slot for rich content.

props.name: labelPosition
props.description: Side of the label in reading order. `start` puts it before the switch and flips in right-to-left layouts. Only has an effect when a label is shown.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the switch. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.

props.name: required
props.description: Sets `aria-required`. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Also set by a Field with an error.

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name; a hidden input is rendered when inside a `<form>`.

props.name: value
props.description: Value submitted with the form when on.

props.name: id
props.description: Control id. Falls back to the surrounding Field id, then (with a label) a generated one. The label `for` always matches.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the track (`data-slot="switch"`); wins over internal classes.

slots.name: label
slots.description: Rich label content; replaces the `label` prop text.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Rich helper text under the label; replaces the `description` prop. Needs a label to be shown.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Emitted when the user toggles the switch.

examples.title: On and off icons
examples.description: `showIcons` draws a check when on and a cross when off, in every size and tone.

examples.title: On and off text
examples.description: `onLabel` and `offLabel` print a short word inside the track (md and lg). They are decorative: the name is the label, the state is `aria-checked`.

examples.title: Right to left
examples.description: The thumb and the text follow the reading direction. Sample content.

examples.title: Label, description and label position
examples.description: The `label` prop renders a `<label for>`; `description` is announced with the switch. Use `label-position="start"` for settings lists that read label first.

examples.title: Settings rows in a Field
examples.script:
const email = ref(true)
const sms = ref(false)

a11y: Button with `role="switch"` and `aria-checked`; Space and Enter toggle it, Tab moves on.

The switch itself has no text: name it with `label` (a `<label for>` beside it), a Field label (`for`/`id` wiring) or `aria-label`. The state is the on or off value, not colour: the thumb also moves, and `showIcons` adds a check or cross.

`description` is a `

` whose id is added to `aria-describedby` after any Field hint and error ids and an explicit `aria-describedby`; it is rendered only with a label. `labelPosition` changes visual order only; the switch stays first in the DOM, so reading and tab order are unchanged.

`onLabel` / `offLabel` text is `aria-hidden`, so it never changes the accessible name; the state is still `aria-checked` and the thumb position. In forced-colors mode the text takes the system text colour on the system track. The thumb and text mirror in right-to-left layouts (the checked thumb moves towards the end side).
Tones change colour only. Role, name and keyboard are identical for every variation; in forced-colors mode the track, thumb, border and glyphs use system colours and the thumb still moves.
Inside a Field it receives `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and disabled state automatically.

Hit area is at least 24px tall through an invisible ::after (about 44px on touch pointers). Forced-colors mode uses system colours for the track, thumb and border; motion is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the switch has no accessible name: no `label` (prop or slot), `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
llmNotes: Always label a Switch: pass `label`, or wrap in `Field` (prefer `orientation="horizontal"`), or pass `aria-label`.
Use `description` for helper text (it needs a label) and `label-position="start"` to put the label first.
Use `tone` (primary, success, danger, neutral, info) for the on colour and `show-icons` when the state must not rely on position and colour alone; do not recolour with classes.
Use `v-model` with a boolean. Use Switch for immediate effects, Checkbox for deferred form values.
Do not put text inside the Switch; it renders only the track and thumb (and an optional icon).
replaces: shadcn-vue Switch
hand-rolled Switch markup in app code

components.name: ColorPicker
components.summary: Swatch palette plus validated hex input; emits normalised lowercase hex colours.
components.description: Use `ColorPicker` to choose a brand, label or tag colour from a configurable palette, with a hex field for custom values. It has no canvas or hue slider. The model is a lowercase `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa` string (or `null`). Typed values accept `#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb` and `#rrggbbaa` with or without `#`, in any case, and are normalised before emitting. An unparsable hex marks the input `aria-invalid`, shows a message and is NOT emitted; blur reverts the text to the last valid value. Clearing the input emits `null`. For a native OS picker use `<input type="color">`.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: Hex colour. Normalised for display; invalid strings render as none. Uncontrolled when omitted.

props.name: swatches
props.description: Palette of hex colours. Entries are normalised; invalid ones are dropped and duplicates collapsed. Pass `[]` for hex input only.

props.name: showInput
props.description: Show the preview chip and hex text field.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables swatches and input. Also inherited from a Field.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Shows the value but blocks every change; the input snaps back.

props.name: required
props.description: Native required on the hex input. Also inherited from a Field.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets `aria-invalid` on the hex input. Typing an unparsable hex sets it temporarily as well.

props.name: size
props.description: Swatch and input size (24 / 32 / 40 px swatches). Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: shape
props.description: Outline of every swatch and of the preview chip. The checked ring and the forced-colors outline follow the shape. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.

props.name: layout
props.description: `stacked` puts the hex field under the swatches. `inline` puts both on one wrapping row (up to `max-w-lg`). `compact` is the same row with a tighter swatch gap, a fixed narrow field and `max-w-md`. The DOM and tab order never change. Unknown values fall back to `stacked`.

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name of the hex input.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Hex input placeholder.

props.name: swatchesLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the swatch radiogroup.

props.name: inputLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the hex input. Dropped when a surrounding Field label names the input, so the visible label stays the name.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Normalised lowercase hex (`#rrggbb` / `#rrggbbaa`) on swatch pick or valid input; `null` when the input is emptied. Never emitted for invalid text or unchanged values.

a11y: Swatches are `role="radio"` buttons inside a `role="radiogroup"` named by `swatchesLabel`; each is labelled with its hex value. The checked (or first) swatch is the only tab stop.

Keyboard: ArrowRight/ArrowDown select the next swatch, ArrowLeft/ArrowUp the previous one (wrapping, flipped in right-to-left layouts), Home/End the first and last. Space selects the focused swatch. Focus and selection move together, as in a native radio group.
`readonly` sets `aria-readonly` on the radiogroup (the only role of the pair that allows it) and `disabled` sets `disabled` on each swatch.

The hex input is named by `inputLabel`, or by the Field label when inside a `Field`. While the text cannot be parsed it sets `aria-invalid` and a polite `role="status"` message linked with `aria-describedby`. The preview chip is decorative.

Selection is never conveyed by colour alone: the checked swatch gets a ring, `aria-checked`, and an outline in forced-colors mode (swatch colours are kept with `forced-color-adjust: none`). Keyboard focus on the checked swatch widens its ring from 2px to 4px, so focus stays visible on the one tab stop.

Shape and layout are presentation only: the swatches stay `role="radio"` buttons named by their hex value, the DOM order (swatches, preview, input) does not change, and the checked swatch keeps its ring and forced-colors outline in every shape.
Responsive: swatches wrap, grow to 44px on coarse pointers, and the hex input uses 16px text on mobile with a 44px minimum height on touch. The picker is `max-w-xs` and `w-full`, so it fits 320px.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the hex input has no name (`inputLabel` blank and no `Field` label) or the swatch group has none (`swatchesLabel` blank).
llmNotes: Model is a lowercase hex string or null; never pass colour names or rgb().
Pass `swatches` as hex strings; use `[]` to offer only the text input.
Use `shape` ("circle" for tags and avatars, "square" for brand tiles) and `layout` ("inline" or "compact" in toolbars and table cells); they never change behaviour.
Do not rely on an event for invalid text: invalid hex is intentionally not emitted.
replaces: custom colour swatch pickers

components.name: Rating
components.summary: Rating input from 0 to N icons (star, heart, circle) with half or quarter steps, tones, keyboard support and slider semantics.
components.description: Use `Rating` to collect or display a score such as product reviews or quality marks. The value is a number from `0` to `max`; `0` means "no rating". Enable `allowHalf` for 0.5 steps (the left half of a star selects the half value), `clearable` to let a second click on the current value reset it, and `readonly` to display a score. Stars are inline SVG drawn with design tokens: empty stars are outlines, filled stars are solid with an ink outline, so the value does not depend on colour. For a small fixed set of labelled options prefer `SegmentedControl` or `RadioGroup`; for continuous values use `Slider`. Out-of-range, NaN or fractional values are clamped/snapped rather than rejected.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: v-model rating. `0`/`null` = none. Clamped to `0..max`, snapped to whole (or half) steps; NaN becomes 0. Uncontrolled when omitted.

props.name: max
props.description: Number of stars. Floored; values below 1 or non-finite fall back to 5; capped at 100.

props.name: allowHalf
props.description: Allow 0.5 steps (pointer position on the star and keyboard). Shorthand for `precision` 0.5; `precision` wins when both are set.

props.name: precision
props.description: Smallest selectable step. Arrow keys move by it, the pointer position inside an icon snaps to it (the first quarter is 0.25, the first half 0.5), and incoming values are snapped to it. Page keys always move by one whole icon. Other numbers fall back to `allowHalf`.

props.name: icon
props.description: Glyph that is repeated `max` times. A name selects a built-in shape; an icon definition (`{ icon: [width, height, , , path] }`) draws that icon, outlined when empty and solid when filled. Unknown names and malformed definitions fall back to the star. Icons are decorative.

props.name: tone
props.description: Fill colour of the active part. Empty icons stay outlines and the filled ones keep an ink outline, so the value never relies on colour. Unknown values fall back to `warning`.

props.name: clearable
props.description: Clicking the star (or half) that already holds the value resets to 0.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Displays the value; no hover, click or key changes. Stays focusable and sets `aria-readonly`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Blocks interaction, removes from tab order, dims. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and the destructive ring. Also set by a Field with an error.

props.name: required
props.description: Inherited from a surrounding Field. `aria-required` is not valid on `role="slider"`, so it is not rendered; mark the requirement in the Field label.

props.name: size
props.description: Icon size (16 / 20 / 28 px glyph, plus 4px padding per side so every star is at least 24px; 44px on coarse pointers).

props.name: name
props.description: Renders a hidden input with the numeric value for native form posts.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Emitted when the rating changes (click, or Arrow, Page and Home/End keys). Not emitted when the value stays the same.

examples.code: Value: {{ score }}

examples.description: Star (default), heart and circle. Pass an icon definition for any other shape.
examples.script: const love = ref(3)

a11y: Root has `role="slider"` with `aria-valuemin=0`, `aria-valuemax=max`, `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext` ("3 out of 5"). Stars are `aria-hidden`.

Keyboard: ArrowRight/ArrowUp add one `precision` step (1, 0.5 or 0.25), ArrowLeft/ArrowDown remove one, PageUp/PageDown +/-1, Home = 0, End = max. Left and Right swap in right-to-left layouts. The announced value text is the number ("2.25 out of 5") at every precision.

The name comes from the surrounding Field label (wired with `aria-labelledby`, because `label for` cannot name a slider), or from your own `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`. With none of these it throws a ContractError: the fallback name "Rating" does not say what is rated.
`readonly` keeps focus and announces `aria-readonly`; `disabled` sets `aria-disabled` and leaves the tab order. `aria-required` is not rendered because `slider` does not support it.
Targets: every star is at least 24px square and 44px on coarse pointers. The group wraps instead of overflowing at 320px.

Filled and empty icons differ by shape (outline versus solid) for every `icon` and `tone`, so the value survives forced-colors mode and colour-blindness. The icons are `aria-hidden`; the single slider carries the name and value.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the slider has no accessible name beyond the fallback "Rating": no `Field` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
llmNotes: Give Rating an `aria-label` or wrap it in Field with a label; without either it throws a ContractError.
Use `v-model` with a number; 0 means no rating. Use `readonly` to display averages (with `allow-half` for x.5).
Do not import star icons; Rating draws its own SVG glyphs from tokens. Use `icon="heart"` or `icon="circle"`, or pass an icon definition for another shape.
Use `precision` (1, 0.5, 0.25) for fractional input and `allow-half` only as shorthand; use `tone` for colour and keep `readonly` for averages.
Keep `max` small (<= 10); it is capped at 100.
replaces: custom star rating widgets

components.name: Calendar
components.summary: Accessible month grid with single, range or multiple day selection, min/max/disabled dates, locale names and full keyboard navigation.
components.description: Use `Calendar` to show a month (or two) inline and let people pick days. It is the engine behind `DatePicker` and `DateRangePicker`; use those when the calendar should live in a dropdown attached to a field, and `DateInput` when a native date field is enough. The value depends on `mode`: `Date | null` for `single`, `{ start, end } | null` for `range` (a reversed range is normalised so `start <= end`), `Date[]` for `multiple` (sorted, de-duplicated). Emitted dates are at local midnight. Wrong shapes and invalid dates are treated as "nothing selected". In `range` mode the first click only sets an anchor (shown highlighted, with hover preview); `update:modelValue` fires when the second click completes the range. All date maths is native `Date`/`Intl` and DST/leap-year safe (it works on calendar days, never on 24h offsets).

props.name: modelValue
props.type: Date | { start: Date; end: Date } | Date[] | null
props.description: v-model. Shape follows `mode`. Uncontrolled when omitted.

props.name: mode
props.description: Selection model. Unknown values behave as `single`.

props.name: month
props.description: Visible (first) month; any day inside it. Pair with `@update:month` to control navigation. Invalid dates are ignored.

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest selectable day (inclusive). Swapped with `max` if reversed.

props.name: max
props.description: Latest selectable day (inclusive).

props.name: isDateDisabled
props.description: Predicate; return true to disable a day (weekends, holidays, booked days). Receives a Date at local midnight.

props.name: weekStart
props.description: First weekday, 0 = Sunday .. 6 = Saturday. Default comes from the locale (Intl.Locale week info), else Sunday. Invalid values use the default.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 tag used for month, weekday and day names/numerals. Unknown tags fall back to the runtime default.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description: Months shown at once (side by side, or stacked with `orientation="vertical"`). Any value other than 2 or 3 renders one month.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout of several months: `horizontal` wraps them side by side, `vertical` stacks them. Unknown values fall back to `horizontal`.

props.name: shape

a11y: Each month is a `role="grid"` named by its visible month heading (`aria-labelledby`, or `aria-label` when `showHeading` is off). Weekday headers are `columnheader`s with the full weekday name as label. Days are buttons inside `gridcell`s that carry `aria-selected`; each day has a full-date `aria-label` (it contains the visible day number) and `aria-current="date"` marks today.
Roving tabindex: exactly one day is tabbable (selected day, else today); Tab leaves the grid. Previous and next month buttons come first in the tab order.

Keyboard: ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move one day (mirrored on a right-to-left page), ArrowUp/ArrowDown one week, Home/End the start/end of the week, PageUp/PageDown one month, Shift+PageUp/PageDown one year, Enter or Space select, Escape cancels an in-progress range. Moving past a month edge scrolls the view and keeps focus on the same day.

One persistent visually hidden `role="status"` region announces the new month(s) after every navigation and the range start prompt after the first range click. The month heading is not a live region because it is re-created on navigation.
Disabled days use `aria-disabled` (not `disabled`) so keyboard users can still move across them. `readonly` sets `aria-readonly` on the grid.

Selected days, range ends and in-between days get a border in forced-colors mode; today is bold and underlined, so no state relies on colour alone. Cells are 24, 28, 36 or 44px (`size`), always at least 24px; `lg` drops to 36px below the `sm` breakpoint so one month fits 320px. Several months wrap onto separate rows when there is no room, or stack with `orientation="vertical"`. Week numbers are `rowheader` cells named "Week N" (translate `weekLabel`); they are not focusable and not part of the roving tabindex.
Translate `prevLabel`, `nextLabel` and `rangeStartMessage`, and pass `locale` so names are localised.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the previous or next month button has no name, that is when `prevLabel` or `nextLabel` is blank.
llmNotes: Use `mode="range"` with `v-model="{start,end}|null"`; `mode="multiple"` with a `Date[]`; default `single` with `Date | null`.
Never mutate the model in place; replace it (or use v-model).
Use `min`/`max`/`isDateDisabled` for restrictions, not CSS.
Put a Calendar in a dropdown with `DatePicker`/`DateRangePicker`, not by hand.
Dates are local calendar days; do not compare with `===`, compare `toDateString()` or use the exported `calendarIsSameDay`.

components.name: TimeRangePicker
components.summary: Pick a time window from presets (last 15 minutes to 30 days, today, yesterday) or a custom from and to, as a popover, an inline panel or a segmented row, in an explicit time zone.
components.description: Use `TimeRangePicker` where the question is "which window of time": dashboards, logs, audit trails, exports. Use `DateRangePicker` when only whole days matter, and `DatePicker` for one date. v-model is `{ from, to }` as ISO 8601 strings, always emitted in UTC (`2024-05-01T10:00:00.000Z`) with `from <= to`. Incoming strings may carry an offset (`+02:00`); one without an offset is read as UTC. An end that is not a valid date makes the whole value count as empty. **Presets resolve when you choose them.** `last-15-minutes` to `last-30-days` end at the current time and are exact elapsed lengths (a "day" is 24 hours). `today` runs from the start of the day in `timeZone` to now; `yesterday` is the whole previous day in `timeZone` (23 or 25 hours across a daylight saving change). The component emits concrete from and to strings, never a relative expression, so a saved value always means the same window. Pass `now` to fix the clock in tests, demos and server-rendered pages. **Time zones.** `timeZone` is an IANA name (`Europe/Warsaw`) and defaults to `UTC`. It decides which day "today" is, how the value is displayed (with a short zone name after the end), and how typed dates and times are read. It never changes the emitted value, which is always UTC. An unknown name shows UTC (and throws a ContractError in strict mode). Only `Intl` is used. A wall time that does not exist (a spring forward gap, or the skipped Samoa day of 2011-12-30) moves forward; a wall time that happens twice (fall back) is read as its first occurrence; the fields then show the time that was stored. **Custom range.** The `custom` preset shows a calendar plus a date and a time field for each end, a note naming the zone, and an Apply button. The range is only emitted when it is valid: Apply with a start after the end, a missing end, or a time outside `min` and `max` shows the reason as visible text with an icon and does not emit. Times have minute precision. `variant` picks the layout: `popover` (trigger and dropdown, the default), `inline` (a bordered panel that is always open) or `segmented` (a row of presets as one radio group with the custom fields below). `class` goes on the root; extra attributes go to the trigger (`popover`) or to the group root (`inline`, `segmented`).

props.name: modelValue
props.description: v-model. ISO 8601 strings, emitted as UTC. Strings without an offset are UTC. Wrong shapes and invalid dates count as empty. Uncontrolled when omitted.

props.name: now
props.description: The current time used to resolve relative presets and to bound them by `min`/`max`. A `Date`, milliseconds or an ISO string. Defaults to the clock at the moment of selection; an invalid value falls back to the clock.

props.name: timeZone
props.description: IANA zone for display, typed times and the day boundaries of `today` and `yesterday`. Unknown names show UTC.

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest allowed instant (inclusive). A preset or a custom range that starts earlier is disabled or rejected. Swapped with `max` when reversed.

props.name: max
props.description: Latest allowed instant (inclusive).

props.name: presets
props.description: Ids to show, in order: `last-15-minutes`, `last-30-minutes`, `last-1-hour`, `last-6-hours`, `last-24-hours`, `last-7-days`, `last-30-days`, `today`, `yesterday`, `custom`. Default: all. Without `custom` there are no from/to fields. Unknown ids are ignored (and throw in strict mode).

props.name: presetLabels
props.description: Visible text per preset id, to translate or reword. A blank text keeps the default.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale for the displayed value and the calendar.

props.name: format
props.description: How each end is displayed (the zone is always `timeZone`). The default is the medium date with hours and minutes, and a short zone name after the end. Invalid combinations fall back to the default.

props.name: variant
props.description: Layout. `popover` is a trigger with a dropdown, `inline` a bordered panel that is always open, `segmented` a row of presets with the custom fields below. Unknown values fall back to `popover`.

props.name: size
props.description: Height of the trigger and the fields: `xs` 28px, `sm` 32px, `md` 36px, `lg` 44px. The segmented row maps `xs` to `sm`. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corners of the trigger and the fields. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.

props.name: status
props.description: Status colour plus an icon. `success` and `warning` add hidden text, `error` sets `aria-invalid`. An invalid range sets `error` by itself and shows its message as visible text. In `inline` it colours the panel border. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: statusLabel
props.description: Hidden text of the success and warning icons. Defaults to the English text (translate it).

props.name: align
props.description: Which trigger edge the dropdown aligns to (`popover`).

props.name: showCalendar
props.description: Show the range calendar beside the fields (`popover` and `inline`). The `segmented` variant never shows it.

props.name: hour12
props.description: Show the 12-hour clock with an AM/PM segment in the time fields. The value stays 24 hour.

props.name: messages
props.type: { incomplete?: string; order?: string; min?: string; max?: string }
props.description: Texts of the validation errors. `{min}` and `{max}` are replaced with the limit formatted in the zone. Blank or non-string entries keep the default.

props.name: clearable
props.description: Show a clear button while a range is set (`popover` only; hidden when disabled or readonly).

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every control. Also inherited from a surrounding Field. Closes an open dropdown.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Shows the range; nothing can be opened, chosen, typed or cleared.

props.name: required
props.description: Adds a visually hidden `requiredLabel` to the description (`aria-required` is not allowed on a button or a group). Also inherited from a surrounding Field.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and destructive styling regardless of the range. Also set by a Field with an error.

props.name: open
props.description: v-model:open. Controls the dropdown of the `popover` variant; uncontrolled when omitted.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown while no range is set.

props.name: presetsLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the presets group. Translate it.

props.name: fromLabel
props.description: Legend of the start fields and the first word of their names (`From date`, `From time`).

props.name: toLabel
props.description: Legend of the end fields and the first word of their names.

props.name: dateLabel
props.description: Last word of the name of each date input.

props.name: timeLabel
props.description: Last word of the name of each time input.

props.name: applyLabel
props.description: Text of the button that applies the custom range.

props.name: zoneLabel
props.description: Visible note above Apply naming the zone. `{zone}` is replaced with the resolved zone name.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: aria-label of the clear button.

props.name: requiredLabel
props.description: Visually hidden description announced while `required` (translate it).

props.name: dialogLabel
props.description: aria-label of the dropdown dialog (`popover`).

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the root with tailwind-merge.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: A preset was chosen, a valid custom range was applied, or the value was cleared (null). Not emitted for an invalid draft.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: The dropdown asked to open or close (`popover`).

emits.name: select
emits.payload: [selection: { preset: TimeRangePresetId; value: { from: string; to: string } }]
emits.description: Which preset (or `custom`) produced the value just emitted. Use it to remember that a window was relative.

emits.name: validate
emits.payload: [result: { valid: boolean; reason: "incomplete" | "order" | "min" | "max" | null; message: string | null; from: string | null; to: string | null }]
emits.description: The custom fields were edited or applied: whether the draft is valid and why not.

emits.name: invalid
emits.payload: [result: { valid: boolean; reason: string | null; message: string | null; from: string | null; to: string | null }]
emits.description: Only when the custom draft is not valid and its message is shown.

a11y: `popover`: the trigger is a button with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` (while open). Its name is the label source (`Field` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`) followed by the visible range, so the visible text is part of the name. Enter, Space or a click toggles the dropdown, ArrowDown opens it with focus on the chosen (or first enabled) preset, Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger, and Tab out of it closes it.

`inline` and `segmented` render a `role="group"` named by `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or the surrounding `Field` label. `segmented` presets are one `radiogroup`: arrow keys move focus and choose, as in any radio group.

Presets are a `role="group"` named by `presetsLabel`; each is a real button (32px, 44px on touch) with `aria-pressed` for the chosen one and `disabled` when its range leaves `min` or `max`. The pressed state also has heavier text and a forced-colors border.

Each end is a `fieldset` with a visible legend. The date input is named `From date`, the time input `From time` (same for the end), so the visible legend is contained in the name. Enter in a date or time field applies the range; Enter on a calendar day only selects the day. Calendar keys are documented on Calendar.

Errors are visible text with an icon, in a polite `role="status"` region that exists before it has text. A range that fails also sets `aria-invalid` and the error status icon, and the trigger is described by the message. The reason is never conveyed by colour alone.
`required` is a visually hidden description (`requiredLabel`) because `aria-required` is not allowed on a button or a group. `status` adds an icon, and `success` and `warning` add hidden text.

Times are shown with a short zone name after the end, and the custom fields state the zone in text (`zoneLabel`). Relative presets are exact elapsed lengths, so a range that spans a daylight saving change is 23 or 25 wall-clock hours long for `yesterday` and the same elapsed time for `last-*`.

Responsive: field text is 16px below `md`, controls reach 44px on touch pointers, the dropdown is as wide as the trigger below `sm` (the presets and the custom fields stack) and works at 320px. Logical properties only, so right to left mirrors it. Targets stay at least 24px in the dense style packs.
requires: Throws a ContractError when nothing names the control: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at text (the range or placeholder shown does not count).
Throws a ContractError when `presetsLabel`, `fromLabel`, `toLabel` or `applyLabel` is blank, when `dialogLabel` is blank, or when `clearLabel` is blank while `clearable` is set.
Throws a ContractError when `timeZone` is not a zone name that `Intl` accepts (it shows UTC until fixed).
Throws a ContractError when an entry of `presets` is not one of the documented ids.
llmNotes: Use `v-model` with `{ from: string, to: string } | null`; both are UTC ISO strings and `from <= to`. Never put a relative expression such as "now-15m" in the model: presets resolve to concrete strings when chosen.
Always set `timeZone` when the audience is not in UTC (it defaults to UTC); it changes display, typed times and the day of `today`/`yesterday`, never the emitted value.
Pass `now` in tests, stories and server-rendered pages so presets are deterministic.
Always label it: wrap in `Field` with a label, or set `aria-label`. Use `variant="inline"` or `"segmented"` when the choice should stay visible.
Use `select` to learn which preset produced the value (store the preset id to refresh a relative window later); use `min`/`max` to bound it.
Use `DateRangePicker` for whole days and `DatePicker` for one date.
replaces: hand-rolled quick range dropdown with a custom range form

components.name: Field
components.summary: Form-field wrapper: label, control, hint and error with automatic id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid wiring.
components.description: Wrap one form control in `Field`. It generates an id (or uses `id`), renders a `Label` with `for`, a hint and an error message, and provides a context that `Input`, `Textarea`, `PasswordInput`, `SearchInput` and other form controls read to set `id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `required` and `disabled`. Use `orientation="horizontal"` for checkbox/switch rows. Group several fields with `FieldGroup` / `Fieldset`. Custom controls can opt in with `useFieldControl()` exported from the package. When a control fails a native constraint (`required`, `pattern`, `minlength`) after the user has interacted with it, the browser message is shown as the error, so the message, `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` appear together.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text. Use the `label` slot for rich content.

props.name: hint
props.description: Helper text under the control; referenced by aria-describedby.

props.description: Mark invalid without a message.

props.description: Shows the required indicator and sets `required` on the control.

props.description: Disables the control and dims the label.

props.name: id
props.description: Control id. Generated with `useId()` when omitted.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Label above the control, or beside it.

props.name: hintPlacement
props.description: `above` puts the hint between the label and the control. Ignored when horizontal. Both placements are linked by `aria-describedby`.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size of the label, hint and error (12px, 14px, 16px) and the gap between them. Pair it with the same `size` on the control. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

a11y: The `<label for>` matches the control id. Group controls (RadioGroup, SegmentedControl, CheckboxCardGroup, RadioCardGroup) are named through `aria-labelledby` pointing at the label, because a `for` attribute cannot label a `div`.

The hint and the error are referenced by `aria-describedby`; the error is referenced only while it exists. `aria-invalid="true"` is set only when the field is invalid; a required control that is valid reports `aria-invalid="false"` so Firefox and Safari do not announce it as invalid on page load.

The error text sits in one polite live region that is always in the page. An error that appears or changes after the user leaves a field is announced; an error already present at load is not. After a failed submit, move focus to the first invalid field so its error is read through `aria-describedby`.
Required is exposed by the native `required` attribute on the control plus a visible asterisk (decorative, `aria-hidden`).
Browser constraint failures are surfaced only after interaction (`:user-invalid`), never while typing in a pristine field.
Controls that ignore the context (third-party inputs) need `:id` bound manually. The error is never colour-only: it is text.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the Field wraps a control that has no accessible name and the Field has no `label` (prop or slot) and no `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`.
Throws a ContractError when the Field has a label and wraps a native input, textarea or select whose `id` differs from the id the label points at (pass that id to `Field` instead of the control).
llmNotes: Wrap every form control in `Field`; one control per Field.
Show errors through the `error` prop, not custom markup. Do not validate on every keystroke; validate on blur or submit.
Native `required`, `pattern` and `minlength` messages are shown automatically after interaction; `error` overrides them.
Use `orientation="horizontal"` for Checkbox/Switch rows.
For several related controls (radio set, date range) use `Fieldset` with a legend instead.
replaces: hand-rolled Field markup in app code

a11y: Renders a native `<label>`: clicking it focuses or activates the control through `for`, and the text becomes the control name.
The required asterisk is `aria-hidden`; the native `required` attribute on the control is what assistive tech announces.
`for` only labels labelable elements (input, select, textarea, button). For a radio group or other `div` widget use `aria-labelledby` pointing at the label `id` (Field does this).
`muted` uses the muted-foreground colour, which meets 4.5:1 on the page and card backgrounds; every size stays real text that zooms with the page.
Text wraps (`leading-snug`) so a long label stays readable at 320px and at 200% zoom.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the label has no `for` and no control nested inside it.
Throws a ContractError when `for` does not match the id of any element in the document (the label rendered by `Field` is exempt, since it names group controls through `aria-labelledby`).
llmNotes: Prefer `Field` over bare `Label`.
Always set `for` to the control id.
Do not nest interactive controls inside Label except via `as-child` patterns.

components.name: FilterBar
components.summary: A row of applied filters as removable chips with an "Add filter" popover, "Clear all", a polite live region and URL-query helpers.
components.description: Use `FilterBar` above a table, list or board when the user narrows results by several fields at once. `v-model` is an array of `{ id, field, operator?, value, label? }`; `fields` describes what can be filtered (`text`, `number`, `select`, `multi-select`, `date`, `boolean`) and drives the field, condition and value pickers in the popover. Each applied filter is a `FilterChip` ("Status is In transit") with its own remove button; "Clear all" removes everything. Additions, removals and clearing are announced in a polite live region, and focus moves to a neighbouring chip (or "Add filter") after a removal so the keyboard user never loses their place. `variant` (`default`, `compact`, `inline`) and `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) change density and shape; the bar wraps instead of scrolling, down to 320px. `filtersToQuery` and `queryToFilters` turn the model into a plain object for the URL and back; they skip anything malformed, refuse keys like `__proto__` and never throw. The bar only edits the list: applying it to data is the app's job. Use `SearchInput` for one free-text box, `MultiSelect` for one field with many values, and `DataTable` column filters when each column already has its own control.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: Applied filters (v-model). Entries without a string `id` and `field`, with no value, or with a repeated `id` are ignored. Omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial filters when uncontrolled.

props.name: fields
props.description: What can be filtered: `{ id, label, type?, options?, operators?, placeholder?, min?, max?, step? }`. `type` defaults to `text`; `select` and `multi-select` need `options` (`{ value, label, disabled? }`); `operators` restricts the conditions to a subset of the known ids (`eq`, `neq`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `starts`, `ends`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `before`, `after`, `in`, `nin`). Fields with a blank or repeated `id` are ignored.

props.name: open
props.description: Open state of the "Add filter" popover (v-model:open). Omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: variant
props.description: `default` has 8px gaps and bordered chips with a muted fill; `compact` has 4px gaps, tighter padding and smaller corners; `inline` has flat chips with only a bottom rule and link-style buttons, for use inside a toolbar or a sentence. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size of the chips (12 / 14 / 16px) and height of the buttons (24 / 32 / 36px; 44px on touch devices). Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: clearable
props.description: Show "Clear all" while at least one filter is applied.

props.name: max
props.description: Most filters that can be applied. At the limit "Add filter" is disabled. Non-positive or non-numeric values mean unlimited; fractions are floored.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables adding, removing and clearing.

props.name: labels
props.description: Text overrides: `group`, `add`, `clear`, `field`, `operator`, `value`, `apply`, `cancel`, `remove` (uses `{filter}`), `yes`, `no`, `choose`, `valueRequired`, the live region sentences `added`, `removed` (use `{filter}`) and `cleared`, and `operators` (a map from operator id to wording). Blank or missing keys keep the English default.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the root (`data-slot="filter-bar"`, `role="group"`).

slots.name: chip
slots.description: Content of a chip, replacing the generated text. The remove button keeps naming the chip after its generated text.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: The list changed: a filter was added, removed or cleared.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: The "Add filter" popover opened or closed.

emits.name: add
emits.description: A filter was added through the popover.

emits.name: remove
emits.description: A filter was removed with its chip button.

emits.name: clear
emits.description: "Clear all" removed these filters.

parts.name: FilterChip
parts.description: One applied filter: text plus a remove button. Rendered by `FilterBar` as a list item, usable alone (for example in a summary line). Emits `remove`; Delete and Backspace on the remove button remove it too.

props.name: label
props.description: Chip text. Required (or default slot text): it also names the remove button, "Remove filter: <label>".

props.name: variant
props.description: Same looks as `FilterBar.variant`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: removable
props.description: Show the remove button.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the remove button.

props.name: removeLabel
props.description: Full accessible name of the remove button, replacing "Remove filter: <label>".

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render. `FilterBar` uses `li`.

components.description: Use `Combobox` when the user picks one value from a long list (countries, users, tags) and benefits from typing to filter. The toggle and clear buttons are pointer shortcuts: they are removed from the tab order (`tabindex=-1`), named ("Toggle options", "Clear selection") and 24px (36px on touch devices) with a focus ring. Clear is only rendered while a value exists.

components.description: Use `NativeSelect` for simple option lists where the platform picker is a feature (mobile, long lists, forms that must work without JS-heavy widgets). Provide options through the `options` array, or through the default slot with `<option>` / `<optgroup>` for grouping; both can be combined. Use `Select` for custom-styled dropdowns with rich items, `Combobox` for type-to-filter. `placeholder` renders a disabled, hidden first option with an empty value shown while nothing is selected. `class` is applied to the wrapper (use it for width such as `w-48`); every other attribute (`name`, `autocomplete`, `aria-*`) goes to the `<select>`.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: v-model value. `null`/`undefined` render as empty. Uncontrolled when omitted.

props.name: options
props.type: Array<{ value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }>
props.description: Options rendered as `<option>` before any slot content.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Disabled hidden first option (value `""`) shown while no value is selected; text is muted.

props.name: variant
props.description: Surface: muted fill (`filled`), bottom border only (`underline`, the chevron sits flush at the end), border on hover and fill on focus (`ghost`). Unknown values fall back to `outline`.

props.name: size
props.description: Height: 28, 32, 36 and 44px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corners. `pill` is fully rounded and moves the chevron in; `underline` has no corners and ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.

props.name: status
props.description: Status colour with an icon left of the chevron. `success` and `warning` add visually hidden text linked through `aria-describedby`; `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: statusLabel
props.description: Screen reader text of the `success` and `warning` status. Set it when the app is not in English.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the select. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.

props.name: required
props.description: Native required. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and destructive styling. Also set by a Field with an error.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the wrapper element; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: default
slots.description: `<option>` / `<optgroup>` elements, rendered after the `options` array.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Emitted on the native change event.

const countries = [{ value: 'pl', label: 'Poland' }, { value: 'de', label: 'Germany' }, { value: 'fr', label: 'France', disabled: true }]

    <optgroup label="Poland">
      <option value="waw">Warsaw</option>
      <option value="krk">Krakow</option>
    </optgroup>
    <optgroup label="Germany">

a11y: Status is never colour alone: an icon appears for `success`, `warning` and `error`; `success` and `warning` add screen reader text referenced by `aria-describedby`, and `error` sets `aria-invalid="true"` (pair it with a visible message in `Field`). The chevron and the status icon are decorative and ignore pointer events.
`underline` and `ghost` keep a visible focus indicator (a thicker bottom border, or a border and ring); forced-colors mode draws borders in system colours.
Native `<select>` semantics: platform picker, full keyboard (Arrow keys, type-ahead, Space or Alt+Down to open) and screen-reader support.
Inside a Field it receives `id` (label `for`), `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `required` and disabled state; otherwise give it `aria-label`.
The chevron is decorative (`aria-hidden` SVG) and ignores pointer events. Options use popover colours, so they stay readable in dark mode.
The placeholder is a disabled, hidden first option; with `required` the browser reports the empty choice as invalid after interaction.
Responsive: `w-full min-w-0`; 16px text below `md` prevents iOS focus zoom; 44px tall on touch pointers. The chevron uses `end-3`, so RTL works.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the select has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (a placeholder option does not count).
llmNotes: Use `options` for simple lists, the default slot for `<optgroup>`. Do not mix a placeholder with a pre-selected value.
Bind with `v-model`; the value is always a string.
Put width classes (`w-48`) in `class` (applied to the wrapper); pass `name`/`autocomplete` as plain attributes.
Wrap in Field with a label; never rely on the placeholder as the label.
Use `status` for validation feedback (it adds the icon) and still show the message through `Field error` or `hint`.
