components.name: Select
components.summary: Custom single-select dropdown with groups, labels, keyboard typeahead and Field wiring.
components.description: Use `Select` (compound: `Select`, `SelectTrigger`, `SelectValue`, `SelectContent`, `SelectItem`, `SelectGroup`, `SelectLabel`, `SelectSeparator`) when you need a styled, accessible dropdown for 4+ options, with grouping or rich item content. Use `NativeSelect` for the best mobile UX and simple option lists, `Combobox` when the user needs to filter a long list by typing, `RadioGroup`/`SegmentedControl` for 2-5 visible options. The model is the selected item value (string). Item values must be NON-EMPTY strings (use a `Placeholder` on `SelectValue` for the empty state, not an item with value `""`). The content is portalled, so style it through `SelectContent`'s `class`, not through the parent. Wrap in `Field` for label, hint and error; the trigger receives `id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and disabled state.

parts.name: SelectTrigger
parts.description: The button that shows the value and opens the list. Applies the shared field surface and a chevron. It carries the look props (`size`, `variant`, `shape`, `status`) because the trigger is the field surface; the `Select` root is a compound root with no element of its own. `selectTriggerVariants` returns the same classes for a plain element.

props.name: size
props.description: Height: 28px, 32px, 36px or 44px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: variant
props.description: Surface. `outline` is the bordered default, `filled` uses a muted fill, `underline` keeps a bottom rule that thickens on focus, `ghost` shows its border on hover and focus. Unknown values fall back to `outline`.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corners. `underline` is always square-cornered, so `shape` does not change it. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status. Colours the border and adds an icon before the chevron; `success` and `warning` also add hidden text that `aria-describedby` points at. `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the trigger. Also inherited from the Select root and a surrounding Field.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and destructive styling. Also set by a Field with an error.

props.name: id
props.description: Trigger id. Falls back to the surrounding Field id.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last; wins over internal classes.

parts.name: SelectValue
parts.description: Displays the selected item text or the placeholder. Place inside SelectTrigger.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown while no value is selected.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged onto the value element.

parts.name: SelectContent
parts.description: Portalled floating list with scroll buttons. Contains SelectItem/SelectGroup/SelectSeparator.

props.name: position
props.description: `popper` anchors under the trigger and matches its width; `item-aligned` overlays the selected item.

props.name: side
props.description: Preferred side (popper only).

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment against the trigger (popper only).

props.name: sideOffset
props.description: Gap in px between trigger and content (popper only).

props.name: size
props.description: Row density of every item: `sm` is compact (12px text), `md` the standard row, `lg` a roomy 16px row. A `size` on a `SelectItem` wins. Items stay 44px tall on touch devices. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the floating surface; wins over internal classes.

parts.name: SelectItem
parts.description: One option with a check indicator when selected.

props.name: value
props.description: Item value. Must be a non-empty string.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Prevents selecting this item.

props.name: textValue
props.description: Text for typeahead and the trigger display when the slot content is not plain text.

props.name: size
props.description: Row density. Defaults to the `size` of the surrounding `SelectContent`, then `md`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last; wins over internal classes.

parts.name: SelectGroup
parts.description: Groups items under a SelectLabel (`role="group"`).

props.name: class
props.description: Merged onto the group.

parts.name: SelectLabel
parts.description: Non-selectable heading for a SelectGroup.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last.

parts.name: SelectSeparator
parts.description: Thin divider between groups.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: v-model: the selected item value. Uncontrolled when omitted.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value when uncontrolled.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state (`v-model:open`).

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the trigger.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the select required for forms and `aria-required`.

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name; a hidden native select is rendered inside a `<form>`.

slots.name: default
slots.description: SelectTrigger and SelectContent.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Emitted when an item is selected.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Emitted when the list opens or closes.

<Field class="max-w-xs" label="Timezone" hint="Used for schedules." :error="tz ? '' : 'Choose a timezone'" required>

    <SelectTrigger>
      <SelectValue placeholder="Select timezone" />

    <SelectContent>

        <SelectItem value="pst">Pacific (PST)</SelectItem>

    </SelectContent>

examples.title: Sizes
Variants
examples.description: The four surfaces side by side: outline (default), filled, underline and ghost.

examples.title: Shapes
examples.description: Rounded (default), pill and square corners.

examples.title: Status
examples.description: Success, warning and error add an icon next to the chevron. Pair them with a visible message in a Field.

examples.title: Item density
examples.description: `size` on SelectContent sets the row density of every item; `size` on one SelectItem overrides it. Open each list to compare.

a11y: Trigger is a `role="combobox"` button with `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`; the list is a `role="listbox"` with `role="option"` items and `aria-selected`.
Keyboard: Enter/Space/Arrow Up/Arrow Down opens, Arrow keys move, Home/End jump, type-ahead jumps, Enter or Space selects, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
Inside a Field the trigger receives `id` (label `for`), `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` (only when invalid); without Field set `aria-label` on SelectTrigger.
Content is portalled and focus moves into the list while it is open; Tab does not leave it. Disabled items are skipped by keyboard navigation.

The trigger is 16px text on small screens (no iOS zoom) and 14px from `md` (`lg` stays 16px); trigger and items are at least 44px tall on touch devices. The content is capped to the available width and scrolls with the scroll buttons or the keyboard.

`status` is never colour alone: success, warning and error draw an icon before the chevron. Success and warning also add visually hidden text ("Valid", "Warning") that the trigger references from `aria-describedby`; error sets `aria-invalid` and relies on the Field error message.

Every `variant` keeps a visible edge or fill and the focus indicator (a ring, or a thicker bottom border for `underline`); forced-colors mode draws the border of `underline` and `ghost` in system colours.
The highlighted item keeps an outline in forced-colors mode and the selected item shows a check icon (not colour alone). Layout uses logical properties (RTL safe).
requires: Throws a ContractError when `SelectTrigger` has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (the selected value and the placeholder do not count).
Throws a ContractError when `Select` has no `SelectTrigger`, no `SelectValue` or no `SelectContent`.
Throws a ContractError when a `SelectItem` has a missing or empty `value` (the item is not rendered).
llmNotes: Always compose Select > SelectTrigger(SelectValue) + SelectContent(SelectItem...). Put `placeholder` on SelectValue.
SelectItem `value` must be a non-empty string (an empty one raises a ContractError and the item is not rendered); never use "" for "none" - use a placeholder or a "none" sentinel value.
Wrap in Field for label/error; otherwise give SelectTrigger an `aria-label`.
Style the dropdown via SelectContent `class` (it is portalled out of the parent).
Look props go on SelectTrigger (`variant`, `shape`, `status`, `size`), not on Select. `status="error"` already sets aria-invalid; still show a visible error message in a Field.
Prefer NativeSelect for simple lists or when native mobile pickers are desirable.

components.name: Slider
components.summary: Pick a number or a numeric range by dragging a thumb or using the keyboard.
components.description: Use `Slider` for approximate numeric choices where the exact value matters less than the position (volume, price range, opacity). The `v-model` is ALWAYS an array of numbers (reka-ui convention): `[40]` for one thumb, `[20, 80]` for a range, one thumb is rendered per value. Use `NumberInput` when the user must type or read an exact value. Name each thumb with `aria-label` or `thumb-labels`, or wrap the slider in a `Field` with a label.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: Controlled values, one per thumb. Always an array, even for a single thumb.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial values when uncontrolled.

props.name: min
props.description: Lowest selectable value.

props.name: max
props.description: Highest selectable value.

props.name: step
props.description: Snap increment for drag and keyboard. Fractional steps are float-safe.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout direction. Vertical needs a parent with a height, or it falls back to a minimum of 11rem. Unknown values fall back to horizontal.

props.name: size
props.description: Track thickness (4 / 6 / 10 px). The thumb is 24px in `sm` and `md` and 28px in `lg`, so the target size rule holds in every size. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: tone
props.description: Colour of the filled range and the thumb border. `neutral` uses the foreground colour. `invalid` always wins and uses the destructive colour, so an error never depends on the tone. Unknown values fall back to `primary`.

props.name: marks
props.type: boolean | number[] | Array<{ value: number; label?: string }>
props.description: Tick marks under the track (beside it when vertical). `true` marks every step, or only the two ends when there would be more than 50 intervals. Numbers mark those values; objects also print `label`. Values outside `min`..`max` and duplicates are dropped. Marks are decorative (`aria-hidden`); a thumb that sits exactly on a labelled mark announces that label as its value text.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Shows the current value in a bubble above each thumb (beside it when vertical). The bubble is decorative: the thumb already carries `aria-valuenow`. Thumbs that sit close together overlap their bubbles, so use it for single values or well separated ranges.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Formats the bubble text and sets `aria-valuetext` on the thumb, e.g. `(v) => v + '%'`. `aria-valuenow` stays the raw number.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Blocks pointer and keyboard interaction and removes thumbs from the tab order.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets aria-invalid on thumbs and applies destructive styling.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the hidden form input as required.

props.name: inverted
props.description: Flips the direction (max at the start edge).

props.name: dir
props.description: Reading direction. In `rtl` the minimum is at the right edge: thumbs, fill, marks and the value bubble mirror, and ArrowLeft moves the thumb towards the maximum. Unset follows the nearest ancestor `dir` (or the document `dir`) once mounted and tracks later changes; set it explicitly in server-rendered pages, whose first paint cannot know the ancestor. Unknown values are ignored.

props.name: minStepsBetweenThumbs
props.description: Minimum distance between range thumbs, measured in steps.

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name. Inside a native form hidden inputs `name[0]`, `name[1]`... are rendered.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name for every thumb. With several thumbs the index is appended ("Price 1 of 2").

props.name: thumbLabels
props.description: Per-thumb accessible names, e.g. `["Minimum price", "Maximum price"]`. Wins over `ariaLabel`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the root; wins over internal classes.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Fires on every change while dragging or keying.

emits.name: valueCommit
emits.description: Fires once when an interaction finishes. Use it for expensive work such as requests or filtering.

const labelled = [{ value: 0, label: 'منخفض' }, { value: 50, label: 'متوسط' }, { value: 100, label: 'مرتفع' }]

examples.title: Disabled and invalid

a11y: Each thumb is a `role="slider"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-orientation`.

Keyboard: in left-to-right, ArrowRight/ArrowUp raise the value and ArrowLeft/ArrowDown lower it by `step`; in right-to-left the arrows follow the thumb on screen, so ArrowLeft raises and ArrowRight lowers (ArrowUp/ArrowDown are unchanged). Shift+Arrow and PageUp/PageDown take larger steps, Home/End jump to the bounds. Tab moves between thumbs of a range.

Name each thumb with `aria-label` or `thumb-labels`. Inside a `Field` with a label, thumbs without their own label are named by the Field label through `aria-labelledby` (a `label for` cannot name a slider); range thumbs add reka-ui's "Minimum"/"Maximum".
Inside `Field` the first thumb receives the field id and aria-describedby; invalid sets aria-invalid on every thumb.
Targets: thumbs are 24px, and on coarse pointers the whole track area is at least 44px tall, so a tap anywhere on it moves the nearest thumb.

Marks and the value bubble are `aria-hidden` and decorative. `formatValue` and labelled marks set `aria-valuetext`; `aria-valuenow` always stays the number. Every size keeps a 24px thumb, and the bubble and marks never take pointer events.

The tone is not the only signal of state: the thumb position, the filled range length and `aria-valuenow` carry the value, and `invalid` adds `aria-invalid`. The slider follows the reading direction: `dir="rtl"` (the prop, or the nearest ancestor and then the document `dir`) puts the minimum at the right edge and mirrors the thumbs, the fill, the marks and the value bubble. `inverted` flips it again.

Forced-colors: track, range and thumb keep their token colours (`forced-color-adjust: none`) and the focus ring falls back to an outline. `disabled` dims the slider and removes the thumbs from the tab order.
requires: Throws a ContractError when a thumb has no accessible name: no `aria-label`, `thumb-labels` entry or `Field` label.
Throws a ContractError when `modelValue` or `defaultValue` is set but is not an array of numbers (use `ref([40])`, not `ref(40)`).
llmNotes: v-model is ALWAYS number[]: use `v-model="vol"` with `ref([40])`, never `ref(40)`.
Always set `aria-label` (single) or `thumb-labels` (range), or wrap in `Field` with a label; an unnamed thumb raises a ContractError.
Use @value-commit, not update:modelValue, for network requests.
Use NumberInput when users need to type an exact number.
Use `tone` for meaning (success, danger) and `size` for density; `invalid` always paints destructive, whatever the tone.
Set `dir="rtl"` (or put the slider inside a `dir="rtl"` container) on right-to-left pages; do not mirror it with CSS transforms. In server-rendered pages pass `dir` explicitly.

Use `marks` for ticks (numbers) or labelled stops (`{ value, label }`) and `show-value` with `format-value` to show units; both are decorative, so keep the value in a visible label too when it matters.

components.name: CopyField
components.summary: Read-only value (API key, URL, token) with a joined copy-to-clipboard button, copied feedback, variants, sizes, shapes and status.
components.description: Use `CopyField` to show a value the user should copy rather than type: API keys, share links, connection strings. The input selects its whole text on focus; the button copies using the async Clipboard API with an `execCommand` fallback (so it also works on plain-http origins), shows a check and "Copied" for `copiedDuring` ms and announces it through a polite live region; a failed copy shows and announces "Copy failed" the same way. `mask` hides the value but still copies the real one. Not for editable fields.

props.description: Text shown and copied.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: Alias of `value` (wins when both are set) so the field works with `v-model`. Never emits.

props.name: label

props.name: copiedLabel
props.description: Button text and live-region message in the copied state.

props.name: failedLabel
props.description: Button text and live-region message when copying fails.

props.name: copiedDuring
props.description: Milliseconds the copied state lasts. Read once when the component is created.

props.name: mask
props.description: Render the value as password dots (the real value is still copied).

props.name: iconOnly
props.description: Visually hide the button text (kept for assistive tech).

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables input and button.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets `aria-invalid`. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.

props.name: variant
props.description: Surface of the input and the joined button: muted fill (`filled`), a line with a text button (`underline`), borderless until hover with a text button (`ghost`). Unknown values fall back to `outline`.

props.name: size
props.description: Height of the input and the button: 28, 32, 36 and 44px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corners of the whole control. `pill` rounds the start of the input and the end of the button; `underline` has no corners and ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.

props.name: status
props.description: Status colour on the input and the button, with an icon at the end of the input. `success` and `warning` add visually hidden text linked through `aria-describedby`; `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: statusLabel
props.description: Screen reader text of the `success` and `warning` status. Set it when the app is not in English.

props.name: inputClass
props.description: Classes for the inner <input>.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the wrapper element.

emits.name: copy
emits.description: The value was copied.

emits.name: copy-error

examples.title: Variants, shapes and sizes
examples.description: The joined copy button follows the variant, shape and size of the input.

examples.title: Status
examples.description: The status icon sits at the end of the input, left of the button; success and warning add screen reader text.

a11y: Status is never colour alone: an icon appears for `success`, `warning` and `error`; `success` and `warning` add screen reader text referenced by `aria-describedby`, and `error` sets `aria-invalid="true"` (pair it with a visible message in `Field`). The icon is not focusable and does not cover the button.

`underline` and `ghost` keep a visible focus indicator on the input and the button (a thicker bottom border, or a border and ring); forced-colors mode draws borders in system colours. The button text and its copied and failed states are the same in every variant.
Input is `readonly` (focusable and selectable) and selects all text on focus. `autocomplete="off"` and no spellcheck.

Copy button is `type="button"` with visible text (or screen-reader-only text with `iconOnly`) that changes to the copied or failed label; icons are decorative. It is not disabled while feedback shows, so keyboard focus is kept and a failed copy can be retried.
A `role="status"` region outside the button announces "Copied" or "Copy failed" and is cleared after `copiedDuring` ms, so no stale message stays in browse mode.
Button is disabled only when the value is empty or the field is disabled. It is 36px tall (44px on touch pointers); text is 16px below `md`.
Use a descriptive `label` (for example "Copy token") when several copy buttons share a page.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the input has no accessible name: no `Field` label, `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
Throws a ContractError when the copy button has no text, that is when `label` is blank.
llmNotes: Use CopyField for read-only copyable values; use Input for editable ones.
Always label it (Field label or `aria-label`); with `icon-only` also pass a descriptive `label`.

components.name: Editable
components.summary: Inline editable text: click to edit, Enter saves, Escape cancels, blur saves (configurable).
components.description: Use `Editable` for titles, names and short notes that should look like plain text until the user wants to change them (rename a project, edit a caption). Standard attributes (`placeholder`, `name`, `autocomplete`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) fall through to the `<input>`. With `type="number"` the model is a `number` (or `""` when cleared); prefer `NumberInput` when you need clamping or steppers. `email`, `url` and `tel` inputs turn off autocorrect, autocapitalise and spellcheck. components.name: InputGroup
components.summary: Puts a prefix, a suffix or joined buttons around an Input, Textarea or NativeSelect so they share one field surface.
components.description: Use `InputGroup` with `InputGroupAddon` when a field needs fixed text ("https://", ".com", a currency sign), an icon, or an attached button ("Subscribe", "Apply"). `layout="inset"` (default) draws one surface around everything: the addons sit inside the border and the Input inside loses its own border, background and ring, so focus is shown once, on the group. `layout="joined"` keeps every child as its own control and only squares the touching edges, which suits an attached `Button` or `Select`. `variant`, `size`, `shape` and `status` take the same values as every text field. Rejected input is announced: non-numeric text restores the previous value ("Not a number, value restored") and clamping or rounding says "Adjusted to <value>".
inputmode is `decimal` (`numeric` when `precision` is 0) and enterkeyhint is `done`. Inside `Field` the input gets the id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid.
Responsive: 16px text below `md`, 44px height and stepper width on coarse pointers, tabular numerals, logical (RTL-safe) stepper borders and a forced-colors focus outline on the whole control.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the input has no accessible name: no `Field` label, `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. A wrapping `<label>` only counts without steppers, because the first button inside it is labelled instead.
Throws a ContractError when a rendered stepper has no name, that is when `decrementLabel` or `incrementLabel` is blank while `showSteppers` is on.

Give an `aria-label` or wrap in `Field` with a label.
Use `status` for validation feedback (it adds the icon) and still show the message through `Field error` or `hint`.
Use `precision` for money-like fixed decimals; use `step` for fractional increments.
Use Input (not NumberInput) for identifiers such as postcodes or phone numbers.

components.description: Use `PinInput` for OTP / verification codes and short PINs. **`v-model` is a single string** (`"123"` while typing a 6-digit code), unlike reka-ui which uses an array; the component converts internally. `complete` fires with the full joined string once every cell is filled. components.name: PromptInput
components.summary: Auto-growing message box for chat style interfaces: Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, a Stop button replaces Send while a reply is running.
components.description: Use `PromptInput` at the bottom of a conversation or a command panel where one block of text is sent at a time. It grows with its text up to `maxRows`, then scrolls. `submitOn="enter"` (default) sends on Enter and inserts a line break on Shift+Enter; `submitOn="mod-enter"` sends on Ctrl or Cmd with Enter and keeps Enter for line breaks, which suits long prompts. An Enter that confirms an IME candidate never sends. Text that is empty or only whitespace never sends; the `submit` event carries the trimmed text and the field clears afterwards unless `clearOnSubmit` is off. While `loading` the Send button becomes a Stop button (emits `stop`) and sending is blocked, but the field stays editable so the next prompt can be drafted. `maxLength` shows a `count / limit` counter in code points; typing past the limit is allowed so pasted text is not cut, but the over-limit state is shown in text and an icon, `aria-invalid` is set and sending is blocked. The component renders no `<form>` and no messages: the app owns the conversation. Use `Textarea` for ordinary form fields and `Input` for one-line text. `class` goes on the root; every other attribute reaches the `<textarea>`.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: v-model text. Uncontrolled when omitted.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Hint text while the field is empty. It is not the accessible name.

props.name: submitOn
props.description: Key that sends. `enter`: Enter sends, Shift+Enter (or Alt+Enter) adds a line. `mod-enter`: Ctrl or Cmd with Enter sends, Enter adds a line. Never sends while an IME is composing.

props.name: loading
props.description: A reply is in progress. Shows the Stop button instead of Send, sets `aria-busy` and `data-loading` on the root, and blocks sending. The field stays editable.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field and both buttons. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Blocks editing and sending. The Stop button keeps working while `loading`.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and destructive styling. Also set by a Field with an error, and by being over `maxLength`.

props.name: variant
props.description: Surface of the box. `default` is bordered, `filled` uses a muted fill, `minimal` shows its border on hover and focus. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: size
props.description: Padding, text size (14px, 14px, 16px from `md`; 16px below it) and button size (32px, 36px, 44px; 44px on touch). Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: rows
props.description: Rows shown while the text is short.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: Rows the field grows to before the text scrolls inside it.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Character limit in code points (an emoji counts as one). Adds the counter and the limit states. It is not the native `maxlength`, so typing past it is allowed.

props.name: clearOnSubmit
props.description: Empties the field after a successful submit and emits `update:modelValue` with `""`. Turn off to keep the text until the app decides.

props.name: submitLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the Send button. Set it when the app is not in English.

props.name: stopLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the Stop button.

props.name: limitNearLabel
props.description: Announced politely once when the text reaches 90% of `maxLength`.

props.name: limitOverLabel
props.description: Shown beside the counter and announced politely once when the text is over `maxLength`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last onto the root (the prompt box); wins over internal classes. Other attributes go to the `<textarea>`.

emits.name: submit
emits.description: The trimmed text. Not emitted when the text is empty or whitespace, over `maxLength`, `loading`, `disabled` or `readonly`.

An Enter that confirms an IME candidate (`isComposing`, keyCode 229) is ignored, so Japanese, Chinese and Korean input is not cut off. Tab moves from the field to the toolbar buttons.

With `maxLength` the counter is read once when the field gets focus (`aria-describedby`). A separate polite `role="status"` region stays empty until the text reaches 90% of the limit or goes over it, then says one fixed sentence, so a screen reader does not read the count on every key.

The focus ring surrounds the whole box while the field has keyboard focus; forced-colors mode draws an outline. The toolbar wraps at 320px and layout uses logical properties (RTL safe).

Use `max-length` for a limit: it allows typing past it and blocks sending. It is not the native `maxlength`.
Put the attach button in the `attach` slot and give icon-only buttons a label. Do not wrap the component in a form just to catch Enter.
Look props are `variant` and `size`; width goes in `class`, other attributes (`name`, `autofocus`, `autocomplete`) reach the textarea.

components.description: Type text and press Enter or the delimiter (comma by default) to turn it into a tag; remove tags with their delete button, or Backspace/Delete once the caret is at the start. Tags are trimmed, empty tags are ignored, duplicates (case-sensitive) are rejected and `max` limits the count. Additions, removals and rejections are spoken through a polite live region, and rejections also surface through the `duplicate` and `reject` events so you can show a visible message. `v-model` is a `string[]`. Use `Combobox` when tags must come from a fixed list, `Input` for a single value.

a11y: The text input keeps native input semantics; tags are listed before it and each remove button is named "Remove <tag>" (the button labels itself, because the library part otherwise names it with the bare tag text). Remove buttons are 24px square (36px on coarse pointers).
Additions, removals, duplicates and `max` rejections are announced through a polite `role="status"` region. After a tag is removed with its button, focus moves back to the text input.
Backspace (or ArrowLeft) at the start of an empty input highlights the last tag (aria-current); Backspace/Delete again removes it.
Inside `Field` the text input gets the field id (so the Field label names it), aria-describedby and aria-invalid; pass `aria-label` otherwise.

The field wraps tags onto new lines, is at least 44px high on coarse pointers, uses 16px text on small screens and shows a forced-colors outline while focused. The selected chip has a ring and, in forced-colors mode, an outline.

`status` is never colour alone: success, warning and error draw an icon, and success and warning add visually hidden text ("Valid", "Warning") that the text input references from `aria-describedby`. Error sets `aria-invalid` and relies on the Field error message.

Every `variant` keeps a visible edge or fill and the focus indicator on the container (a ring, or a thicker bottom border for `underline`); forced-colors mode draws the border of `underline` and `ghost` in system colours.
Enter never submits the surrounding form while text is pending.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the text input has no accessible name: no `Field` label, `for` label, `ariaLabel` or `aria-labelledby`.
llmNotes: v-model is string[]; tags are trimmed and case-sensitive unique.
Surface `reject` (reason duplicate | max) with a visible Field error. A screen reader already hears the rejection through the built-in status region.
Attributes such as id/aria-label land on the inner text input, class lands on the root.
Look props are `variant`, `shape`, `status` and `size`. `status="error"` already sets aria-invalid; still show a visible error message in a Field.
Use Combobox, not TagsInput, when values must come from a fixed set.

components.name: Textarea
components.summary: Multi-line text field with v-model, variants, sizes, shapes, status, optional autosize and character counter.
components.description: Use for free-form text longer than one line. `autosize` grows the field with its content (optionally capped by `maxRows`). `maxlength` + `showCount` renders a `n / max` counter (counts unicode code points); the counter is linked by `aria-describedby` and a polite status announces only when the limit is reached. Inside a `Field` it receives id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid automatically. `variant`, `size`, `shape` and `status` change the look; a `pill` shape is `rounded-xl` because a full pill would clip several lines, and `status` adds an icon at the top end (plus screen reader text for `success` and `warning`). `textareaVariants` gives a plain `<textarea>` the same look. Attributes (`placeholder`, `name`, `aria-*`) go to the `<textarea>`; `class` is merged onto it.

components.name: FileDropzone
components.summary: Drag-and-drop or click-to-browse file picker with type, size and count validation. Selection only, no upload.
components.description: Collects `File` objects; **it never uploads anything**. Send the `v-model` files to your own endpoint. Validation runs on drop and on pick: `accept` (native syntax: `image/*`, `.pdf`, `text/csv`), `maxSize` (bytes), `maxFiles` (with `multiple`). Accepted files go to `v-model` (always `File[]`); rejected ones are reported through `reject` (`[{ file, reason: "type" | "size" | "count" }]`) and a human-readable `error` message, which is also shown inline. In single mode a new file replaces the old one. Duplicates (same name, size and modified time) are ignored. The whole area is a native `<button>` (Enter and Space open the picker); customise its content with the default slot, which receives `{ dragging }`. `variant`, `size` and `status` change the look of the area. There is no `shape`: the area is a tall panel and a pill or square corner adds nothing to it. There is no `underline`: a bottom rule alone does not read as a place to drop files, so `solid` and `filled` cover the quieter looks.

a11y: The drop area is a native `<button type="button">`: Tab focuses it, Enter and Space open the file picker, and disabled removes it from the tab order. Clicking or pressing the button is the keyboard and touch alternative to dragging files in.

The accessible name is the visible prompt text. `ariaLabel` adds hidden text inside the button instead of replacing the name (WCAG 2.5.3 label in name). Inside a `Field`, the Field label and the prompt are combined with `aria-labelledby`.
A hidden native file input does the real work, stays out of the tab order and is `aria-hidden`.

Rejections render in a `role="alert"` paragraph, linked with `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid` on the button. Accepted and removed files are announced politely through a visually hidden `role="status"` region ("report.pdf added").
Each accepted file has a remove button named "Remove <file name>"; it is 24px square and grows to 44px on coarse pointers.
Dragging adds `data-dragging` to the root and the area and changes the text to "Drop to upload". In forced-colors mode the dragging state adds an outline, so it does not depend on colour alone.

`status` is never colour alone: success, warning and error draw an icon in the top corner, and success and warning add visually hidden text ("Valid", "Warning") outside the button that the button references from `aria-describedby` (so it does not change the accessible name). Error sets `aria-invalid` and relies on the Field error message.
Every `variant` keeps a visible edge or fill and the focus ring; `filled` and `ghost` draw a system-colour border in forced-colors mode, so the area never disappears.
Responsive: the area and file names shrink with `min-w-0` and truncate, so nothing overflows at 320px.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the drop area has no accessible name: custom slot content without text, and no `ariaLabel`, `aria-label` or `Field` label.
llmNotes: v-model is File[] (even in single mode). The component never uploads: send files yourself.
Handle `reject`/`error` or rely on the inline message; set `max-size` in BYTES.
Look props are `variant`, `size` and `status`; there is no `shape` or `underline` (see the description). `status="error"` already sets aria-invalid; still show a visible error message in a Field.
`max-files` only applies together with `multiple`.
Custom slot content must be phrasing content (spans, icons) and must not contain interactive elements: the area is itself a button.
Do not pass `aria-label` through attrs: it would replace the visible prompt in the accessible name. Use the `ariaLabel` prop.

components.name: ConfirmDialog
components.summary: Confirm / cancel dialog with destructive styling and async-aware confirm, plus a promise-based useConfirm() host.
components.description: Two ways to use it. (1) Declarative: render `<ConfirmDialog v-model:open="open" title=... @confirm="handler" />`. The handler may be async: the dialog stays open with a spinner while it runs, closes on success, and shows the error (and emits `error`) if it throws. (2) Imperative: mount `<ConfirmHost />` once (requires Pinia) and call `const { confirm } = useConfirm(); if (await confirm({ title, destructive: true })) ...`. Concurrent confirm() calls queue and resolve one at a time. Escape, outside click and the cancel button resolve `false`; while busy the dialog cannot be dismissed. `@confirm` is declared as an `onConfirm` handler prop so its returned promise can be awaited.

a11y: Built on AlertDialog (reka-ui): role="alertdialog", focus is trapped, Escape cancels, focus returns to the trigger.
Initial focus goes to Cancel, the safe action, also for non-destructive confirmations.
Clicking outside does not dismiss it: an explicit choice is required.
Title and description are wired with aria-labelledby and aria-describedby. An sr-only description is added when none is given.
While busy the confirm button exposes aria-busy, Cancel is disabled, and the dialog cannot be dismissed.
Errors from the handler render in a role="alert" paragraph.

The tone icon is decorative (aria-hidden) and the tint is a border only: the title, description and button label say what the tone says. Every size and tone keeps the Title, Description and Cancel parts.
The panel is capped at the viewport width minus 2rem and scrolls inside itself when the content is taller than the viewport.
requires: Throws a ContractError when a `ConfirmDialog` has a blank `title`, no `open` (use `v-model:open`) or no `@confirm` handler.
Throws a ContractError when `useConfirm().confirm()` is called with a blank `title` or while no `ConfirmHost` is mounted (the promise would never settle).
llmNotes: Use destructive for irreversible actions and name the action in confirmLabel.
Prefer useConfirm() + one <ConfirmHost /> for "are you sure?" checks in scripts.
Return the promise from @confirm so the dialog can show progress and errors.
Set `tone="danger"` for irreversible actions (it also styles the confirm button); use `warning`, `info` or `success` for other prompts. Keep `tone` and `title` in agreement.
Do not nest ConfirmDialog inside another dialog.
replaces: window.confirm() calls

components.name: Alert
components.summary: Inline, in-flow status message with optional icon, title, description and dismiss button.
components.description: Use `Alert` for a message that belongs to a section of the page (form-level errors, "saved" confirmations, notices above a table). Compose it with `AlertTitle` and `AlertDescription`. Tone (`variant`) and surface (`appearance`) are independent: `soft` (default, tinted) for most in-page messages, `solid` for high-emphasis notices that must not be missed, `outline` for low-key bordered notices on busy backgrounds, `minimal` for unobtrusive inline text with just an icon. `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) scales padding and type. Use `Banner` for page-wide notices, `Toast` for transient confirmations, `InlineMessage` for one line under a field and `Callout` for documentation notes.

components.name: Banner
components.summary: Full-width, page-level notice with optional sticky position, action slot and remembered dismissal.
components.description:
Use `Banner` at the very top of a page or layout for global announcements: maintenance windows, upgrade prompts, degraded service. Set `storageKey` so a dismissed banner stays dismissed across visits. Use `Alert` for messages inside the page content.

Placements: `top` (default strip at the top of a layout), `bottom` (strip at the bottom, e.g. cookie notices), `floating` (fixed, centred rounded card near the bottom of the viewport for announcements that should not shift layout) and `inline` (rounded block inside the content flow, e.g. above a table). Appearance: `solid` (filled, loud) or `soft` (tinted, calmer). Add a call to action with `actionLabel` (+ `actionHref` for a link) or the `action` slot.

props.name: variant
props.description: Solid tone. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: placement
props.description: Where the banner sits. `floating` is `position: fixed` (centred, bottom of the viewport); `inline` is a rounded in-flow block. Unknown values fall back to `top`. Non-default values add `data-placement`.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Filled tone or tinted background with a tone border. Unknown values fall back to `solid`. `soft` adds `data-appearance`.

props.name: size
props.description: Padding, gap and type scale. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Non-default values add `data-size`.

props.name: layout
props.description: `centered` centres the message and the actions (announcement strips). Unknown values fall back to `default`. Non-default values add `data-layout`.

props.name: sticky
props.description: Sticks to the top of the scroll container (z-sticky); with `placement="bottom"` it sticks to the bottom. Ignored for `floating` and `inline`.

props.name: actionLabel
props.description: Built-in call-to-action label (small outlined button, or a link with `actionHref`). Blank values render nothing. The `action` slot overrides it.

props.name: actionHref
props.description: Turns the built-in call-to-action into a link.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional leading FontAwesome icon.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Shows a dismiss button.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.description: Accessible label of the dismiss button.

props.name: storageKey
props.description: Remember dismissal in localStorage under `pd-banner:<storageKey>`; the banner is not rendered next time. Storage errors are ignored.

props.name: role
props.description: Overrides the computed role: `alert` for warning/destructive, `status` otherwise.

props.name: class

slots.name: default

slots.name: action

components.name: Callout
components.summary: Documentation-style note, tip, important, warning, caution, danger, success, quote or example block with a tinted surface and a status icon.
components.description: Use `Callout` inside long-form content (docs, articles, settings help) to highlight information. Pick the type by intent: `note` (neutral extra information), `tip` (helpful advice), `important` (must-know information), `warning` (risk of problems), `caution` and `danger` (risk of data loss or breakage; `caution` is a softer-looking icon, same tone), `success` (positive outcome or best practice), `quote` (cited text, rendered in italics) and `example` (worked sample). `appearance` sets the surface (`soft` tinted by default, `solid` filled, `outline` border only, `minimal` icon and text only) and `size` the padding and type scale (`sm`, `md`, `lg`). `dismissible` adds a close button and the `actions` slot puts buttons or links under the text. It is static content, not a status message; it does not announce itself. Use `Alert` for dynamic status messages.

props.name: type
props.description: Semantic kind; picks colour and default icon. Unknown values fall back to `note`. `data-type` reflects the resolved type.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading line. Use the `title` slot for rich content.

props.name: icon
props.description: Replaces the default icon of the type.

props.name: hideIcon
props.description: Hides the icon.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Surface, independent of `type`. `solid` fills with the type colour and its foreground; `outline` keeps a coloured border on a transparent surface; `minimal` removes border, fill and side padding. Unknown values fall back to `soft`. Non-default values add `data-appearance`.

props.name: size
props.description: Padding, gap, type scale and icon size. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Non-default values add `data-size`.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Shows a dismiss (X) button. Dismissing hides the callout and emits `dismiss` once.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the dismiss button. A blank value throws a ContractError when `dismissible`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.description: Body content (text, paragraphs, lists, code).

slots.name: title
slots.description: Rich title; overrides the `title` prop.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Buttons or links shown under the text (for example a `Button` with `size="xs"`).

emits.name: dismiss
emits.description: The dismiss button was used. Fires once; the callout then removes itself.

components.name: NotificationList
components.summary: Inbox-style list of notifications with unread dots, relative times, mark-as-read, grouping and a collapsible tail.
components.description: Use `NotificationList` for an in-app inbox, a bell dropdown or an activity panel. Each item is `{ id, title, description?, time?, read?, icon?, tone?, href?, group? }`. Times (Date, epoch ms or ISO string) render as relative text via `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` with the absolute date in the tooltip; any other string (e.g. "just now") is shown as provided and invalid values render nothing. Clicking a row marks it read and emits `select`; "Mark all as read" and per-row dismiss are built in. The list is usable uncontrolled (it updates itself and emits `update:items`) or controlled (`v-model:items` / handle `read`, `read-all`, `dismiss`). Items with a `group` are rendered under headings in order of first appearance. `maxItems` collapses the tail behind Show more; `loading` shows skeleton rows. For transient messages use `Toaster`; for page-level status use `Alert` or `Banner`.

props.name: items
props.description: Notifications (v-model:items). Every item needs a unique string or number `id` and a non-empty `title` (otherwise a ContractError; in production such entries are not shown). Never mutated.

props.name: appearance
props.description: `card` is a bordered, rounded surface. `flush` removes the border, radius and fill so the list sits inside a popover, a sheet or another card that already has one. Unknown values fall back to `card`. Non-default values add `data-appearance`.

props.name: shape

props.name: variant
props.description: Density. `compact` uses tighter rows, a smaller icon and single-line descriptions. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: loading
props.description: Show skeleton rows instead of the list and set `aria-busy`.

props.description: Skeleton rows (clamped 0-50).

props.name: maxItems

props.name: dismissible

props.name: markReadOnSelect

props.name: showMarkAll

props.name: now

a11y: The root is a labelled `region` (override with `aria-label`); each group is a `ul role="list"` of `li role="listitem"`, labelled by its heading.
Rows are native `<button>` (or `<a>` when `href` is set), so Enter and Space activate them; unread rows carry a screen-reader "Unread:" prefix in addition to the visual dot.
The unread count is an `aria-live="polite"` region and updates as items are read, dismissed or marked all read.

`appearance="flush"` removes the list border, so place it inside a container that keeps one (popover, sheet, card); rows keep their dividers. `shape` changes only the radius of the decorative icon bubble.
Dismiss buttons are labelled "Dismiss: <title>"; `loading` sets `aria-busy` and announces a status message; times use `<time datetime>` with an absolute-date tooltip.
requires: Throws a ContractError when a `NotificationList` has a blank `label`, or an item has no `id`, repeats an `id` or has a blank `title`.
llmNotes: Give every item a unique `id`; bind `v-model:items` for the simplest working inbox.
Use `time` as Date, epoch ms or ISO string; pass `now` for deterministic output.
Use `group` for headings (e.g. Today / Earlier) and `maxItems` to cap long lists.
Use `tone` + `icon` for status colour; never colour rows with hard-coded classes.
Use `appearance="flush"` inside popovers and sheets so the border is not doubled; keep `card` on the page.
Handle `select` to navigate or open details; `href` items render as real links.

components.name: AsyncBoundary
components.summary: Shows the right state for async content: loading, error with retry, empty or the content itself.
components.description: Wrap anything that is fetched. Drive it with `state` (`idle`, `loading`, `error`, `empty`, `success`) or hand it a `promise` and it follows the promise: pending is loading, rejected is the error, fulfilled is the content (or the empty state when the result has nothing in it). The built-in states are `LoadingState`, `ErrorState` and `EmptyState`; replace any of them with the `loading`, `error`, `empty` or `idle` slot. `delay` holds the loading state back so a fast load never flashes it, and `minDuration` keeps it up long enough to read. A promise that is swapped for a newer one, or that settles after the component is gone, is ignored. Use it for a region of a page. For a whole failed page use `ErrorState` with `variant="page"`; for content that only needs a skeleton while it loads, `LoadingState` alone is enough.

props.name: state
props.description: The state to show. Wins over `promise` when set. Unknown values fall back to `success`. With neither `state` nor `promise` the default slot shows.

props.name: promise
props.description: Follow a promise: pending is `loading`, rejected is `error`, fulfilled is `success` or `empty`. `null` means not started (`idle`). A newer promise replaces the old one, whose result is then ignored.

props.name: error
props.description: What went wrong: a string, an Error, an object with a `message`, a number. Rendered as plain text (never HTML), control characters removed, cut at 300 characters. Overrides the reason of a rejected promise.

props.name: variant
props.description: `default` has no surface. `card` draws a bordered surface with padding for the content. `compact` swaps in the dense forms of the built-in states: an inline loader, a single-row error, a compact empty state. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Non-default values add `data-variant`.

props.name: size
props.description: Scale of the built-in loading, error and empty states. Your own content is not affected. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Non-default values add `data-size`.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds to wait before the loading state appears. Finished content stays on screen meanwhile. A load that ends sooner never shows the loader. Negative, NaN and Infinity count as 0; the maximum is 60000.

props.name: minDuration
props.description: Milliseconds the loading state stays once it has appeared, so it does not flash. Counted from the moment it appeared. The same limits as `delay`.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: Text of the built-in loading state. Also announced when you supply your own `loading` slot.

props.name: loadingVariant
props.description: Look of the built-in loading state (the `variant` of `LoadingState`): a spinner or a skeleton that matches the content.

props.name: errorTitle
props.description: Heading of the built-in error state. Defaults to "Something went wrong".

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Your own wording for the built-in error state. The real error then moves into the collapsible technical details. Without it the error text is shown, or a generic sentence when there is none.

props.name: retryable
props.description: Show the retry button in the built-in error state. It needs an `@retry` handler.

props.name: retryLabel
props.description: Text of the retry button.

props.name: emptyTitle
props.description: Heading of the built-in empty state. Say what is empty ("No invoices yet"). Also announced when loading ends with nothing.

props.name: emptyDescription
props.description: Supporting text of the built-in empty state.

props.name: emptyIcon
props.description: Icon of the built-in empty state.

props.name: isEmpty
props.description: Decides whether a fulfilled promise value is empty. The default treats null, undefined, an empty array, a blank string and an empty Set or Map as empty. A function that throws counts as not empty.

props.name: successLabel
props.description: Announced politely when a load ends with content. An empty string turns the announcement off, for the empty state as well.

props.name: class

a11y: The root carries `aria-busy="true"` while loading, including the time before a delayed loader appears.

Announcements: the built-in loading state is a polite `role="status"` region and the built-in error state is `role="alert"` (assertive, because the person has to act). A separate visually hidden polite status region announces the end of a load ("Loaded." or the empty title), a custom `loading` slot and a custom `error` slot. Regions are siblings, never nested.
Nothing is announced on first render with finished content, and a load that ended before its `delay` produces one short announcement, not a loading and a loaded pair.

The retry button is a labelled native button with a 24px minimum target (44px on coarse pointers) and a visible focus ring. When the loader replaces the error, focus is not moved; the retry button leaves the DOM, so put your own focus management in the `retry` handler when needed.

Error text is rendered as text only, long words wrap (`break-words`), and the technical details are a labelled, focusable region. Colour is never the only signal: the error has an icon and a heading, the empty state a title.
Motion: the skeleton pulse is off under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Borders keep the card surface visible in forced-colors mode. Layout uses logical properties and wraps at 320px.
requires: Throws a ContractError when `AsyncBoundary` has no default slot (the content to show once loading succeeds).
Throws a ContractError when the retry button is on (`retryable`, the default) but there is no `@retry` handler and no `error` slot, because the button would do nothing.
llmNotes: Give the boundary one source of truth: `state` or `promise`, not both. `state` wins when both are set.
Always handle `@retry` (start the load again) or set `:retryable="false"`.
Create the promise once per load (in an event handler or a watcher). A promise created in the template runs on every render.
Use `delay` (about 200 ms) for fast endpoints and `minDuration` (about 500 ms) when a flash of loader is worse than waiting. Both default to 0.
Name what is empty in `emptyTitle` ("No invoices yet"); say what failed in `errorTitle`. Do not rely on the defaults in shipped screens.
Pass the raw error to `error`; the component shortens it and never renders HTML. Use `errorMessage` for friendlier wording.
Timers and the promise callback are cleaned up on unmount; do not add your own.

components.name: ErrorState
components.summary: Failed-load placeholder with a message, retry button and collapsible technical details.
components.description: Use `ErrorState` where content could not be loaded (a list, a page, a widget). Keep `message` short and actionable; put stacks, request ids and response bodies in `details`. The parent owns the retry logic: handle `retry` and toggle `retrying`. Variants: `default` (centred block inside a region), `card` (bordered surface), `inline` (one row for widgets, list items and table cells) and `page` (full-viewport 404/500/403/503 layout with an `h1`). Use `status` for ready-made HTTP copy (`404` and `403` hide the retry button, `500` and `503` keep it). For form-level errors use `Alert`; for one-line field errors use `InlineMessage`.

components.summary: Fixed-position, screen-reader-announced stack that renders the global toast store.
components.description: Mount `<Toaster />` ONCE near the app root (requires Pinia). Choose one of six position presets: `top-left`, `top-center`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-center`, `bottom-right` (default; also exported as `TOASTER_POSITIONS`). Top positions render the newest toast nearest the top edge, bottom positions nearest the bottom. Use `showProgress` for visible countdown bars and `hideIcons` for text-only toasts. Push from anywhere with `useToastStore()`: `push({ title, description, variant, duration, action, key })` or the shortcuts `success/error/warning/info(title, description?)`. At most 5 toasts are visible; a `key` replaces an existing toast instead of stacking. Duration 0 or Infinity makes a toast sticky. With `pauseOnHover` the stack stays visible while hovered or focused (the store timers keep running, so a toast that expired meanwhile lingers until about one second after the pointer leaves).

components.name: Tour
components.summary: Step-by-step coach marks that spotlight page elements and explain them in a positioned card.
components.description: Use `Tour` for first-run onboarding and feature announcements. Each step points at an element (`target`: CSS selector, element or getter); a spotlight dims the page around it and a card with title, description, progress and Back/Next/Skip/Finish controls is placed on the requested side, flipping and clamping to stay inside the viewport. Steps whose target element is missing or hidden show a centred card without a spotlight, so a tour never breaks when the UI changes; pass `target: null` for a step that is centred on purpose. The tour renders nothing while closed. Control it with `v-model:open` and `v-model:step`, or leave both uncontrolled and call the exposed `start()`. The overlay is teleported to `body` (disable with `:teleport="false"`). It does not lock page scroll. `variant` changes the card: `compact` tightens the padding and gap and sets the description in small text; `dots` replaces the "2 / 5" text with one dot per step (the text stays for screen readers). For a single anchored hint use `Popover`; for blocking decisions use `Dialog`.

a11y: The card is `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` (title) and `aria-describedby` (description and the progress text).
Focus moves to the card on open and on every step change, so the new step is announced. Tab and Shift+Tab are trapped inside the card and focus returns to the previously focused element on close.
Esc skips, ArrowRight goes next (Finish on the last step), ArrowLeft goes back.
With `variant="dots"` the dots are `aria-hidden` and the progress text stays in the DOM for assistive technology (the active dot is also filled, not only coloured).

The spotlight and the opaque scrim panels are `aria-hidden`. The spotlight outline stays visible in forced-colors mode. Motion is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion` and smooth scrolling falls back to instant.
The page is not scroll-locked and no body styles are touched. Listeners are removed on close and unmount. The card is capped at the viewport width minus 1rem.
requires: Throws a ContractError when a step has no `title` (or a `title` slot), when a step has no `target` (use `target: null` for a deliberately centred step), or when the tour dialog ends up without an accessible name. It is checked each time the tour opens.
llmNotes: Bind `v-model:open` (and optionally `v-model:step`); the tour renders nothing until open.

Give targets stable ids or pass a getter; a `target` that does not match an element degrades to a centred card, never an error; a step with no `target` key at all throws, so use `target: null` for a centred step.
Keep titles short and put detail in `description`; do not put interactive content in the card.
Use variant="compact" for short steps and variant="dots" for long tours where the count matters less than position; unknown size/variant values fall back to md/default.
Prefer `placement` on the step for tricky layouts; the card auto-flips and clamps to the viewport.
Tour does not lock scroll and does not block keyboard shortcuts of the page other than Esc/Arrow keys while open.

components.name: Command
components.summary: Searchable command palette: an input that filters a keyboard-navigable list of items. Inline or inside a modal `CommandDialog`.
components.description: Compose `Command` + `CommandInput` + `CommandList` (+ `CommandEmpty`, `CommandGroup`, `CommandItem`, `CommandShortcut`, `CommandSeparator`). Items are filtered as the user types: every whitespace-separated word of the search must appear (case-insensitive) in the item `value` or its `keywords`. ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the highlight (disabled items are skipped, focus stays in the input), Enter runs the highlighted item via its `select` event, and the first match is highlighted automatically while typing. Use `CommandDialog` for a global Cmd/Ctrl+K palette. Set `shouldFilter` to false to filter yourself (async/server search). `variant` sets where it sits: `palette` (default) is borderless and fills its surface (a `CommandDialog` or a popover); `inline` adds a border and a light shadow so the command list can sit in a page like a card. `size` (`sm` | `md` | `lg`) sets the height of the search row, the row padding and type, and the maximum list height; `CommandDialog` takes the same `size` and also sets its width. Defaults are unchanged. Use `DropdownMenu` for fixed action lists and `Select` or `Combobox` (forms) for picking a form value.

a11y: CommandInput is the combobox-style text field (default aria-label "Search", override it). CommandList is a named listbox (`label`, default "Results") and items are role=option. The highlighted option is exposed through aria-activedescendant.
Keyboard: type to filter. ArrowUp and ArrowDown move the highlight (disabled items are skipped, it wraps). Home and End jump. Enter selects. Esc closes a CommandDialog.

Size and variant change spacing, type and the border only. The input name, listbox name, option roles, keyboard map and live status region are the same in every combination; `lg` uses 16px input text.
Separators are decorative (hidden from assistive tech), so the listbox contains only options and groups.
A visually hidden status region reports the number of results, or "No results found.", as the search changes. CommandEmpty is the visible counterpart.
CommandDialog is a labelled modal dialog (title and description are screen-reader only).
requires: Throws a ContractError when a `Command` renders no `CommandEmpty` (it has a default message, and an empty search must be announced).
Throws a ContractError when a `CommandItem` has no `value` (or a blank one), or shares its `value` with another item in the same `Command`.
Throws a ContractError when `CommandInput` or `CommandList` has no accessible name (they default to "Search" and "Results"; blanking them throws).
Throws a ContractError when `CommandDialog` has a blank `title` (it is the screen-reader name of the dialog).
llmNotes: Run actions with @select on CommandItem (close the dialog yourself with v-model:open).
Every CommandItem needs a unique value; searchable text is the value plus keywords, not the rendered label, so use a descriptive value or add keywords.
Always render a CommandEmpty so empty results are announced.
For a global Cmd/Ctrl+K shortcut register the keydown listener in your app and toggle CommandDialog v-model:open (and remove the listener on unmount).
Use shouldFilter=false when results come from the server.

Use variant="inline" for a command list placed in a page (border and shadow); the default palette variant is for CommandDialog and popovers. size (sm, md, lg) and variant fall back to md and palette when unknown.
replaces: hand-rolled Command markup in app code

The menu opens at the pointer position. Never make it the only way to reach an action: also expose the action in a visible control (touch and keyboard users). Use `DropdownMenu` for button-triggered menus. `density` (`default` | `compact` | `comfortable`) sets the row spacing and `size` (`sm` | `md` | `lg`) sets the type scale, icon size and minimum width, exactly as on `DropdownMenu`; set them once on `ContextMenu` (or on `ContextMenuContent` to override) and every part and sub menu follows. a11y: Density and size change spacing and type only: roles, keyboard map and the 44px coarse-pointer row height are the same in every combination.
Content: role=menu. Items are menuitem, menuitemcheckbox or menuitemradio.

Keyboard: opens wherever the browser fires a contextmenu event (ContextMenu key, Shift+F10). ArrowUp and ArrowDown move (skipping disabled), Home and End jump, ArrowRight and ArrowLeft open and close sub menus, typing jumps to a matching item, Esc closes and returns focus.
Touch: long-press opens it. Always provide a visible alternative for the same actions.

The menu keeps 8px from the viewport edges (collision padding), never grows beyond the available height (it scrolls) and never exceeds the viewport width. Rows are 44px high on coarse pointers. Highlight uses system colours in forced-colors mode. RTL mirrors indicators and chevrons.

llmNotes: ContextMenuTrigger wraps the region that should react to right-click; use as="div" for block regions.
Never put an action ONLY in a context menu; mirror it in a visible control or DropdownMenu.
Run actions with @select on ContextMenuItem; call event.preventDefault() to keep the menu open.
Mark dangerous items with the destructive prop and put them last.
Set density (default, compact, comfortable) and size (sm, md, lg) once on ContextMenu; a value on ContextMenuContent overrides it. Unknown values fall back to default and md.

components.name: DropdownMenu
components.summary: Menu of actions opened from a button, with items, checkboxes, radios, groups and nested sub menus.
components.description: Compose `DropdownMenu` + `DropdownMenuTrigger` + `DropdownMenuContent` and fill it with `DropdownMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`, `DropdownMenuRadioGroup`, `DropdownMenuRadioItem`, `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuSeparator`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuSub`, `SubTrigger`, `SubContent` and `DropdownMenuShortcut`. Items fire `select` (call `event.preventDefault()` to keep the menu open). Use for lists of ACTIONS; use `Select` (forms) for choosing a value and `Popover` for arbitrary content. Density: `density="compact"` (on `DropdownMenu`, or on `DropdownMenuContent` to override) tightens every row, label, separator and the surface padding for toolbars, table row actions and dense admin UIs; it propagates to all items and sub menus through provide/inject, so you set it once. `density="comfortable"` does the opposite: roomier rows for touch-first or sparse menus. `size` (`sm` | `md` | `lg`) sets the type scale, icon size and minimum width independently of the density; `md` is the default. The default density and size are unchanged. For a right-click menu use `ContextMenu`.

components.name: ShortcutsDialog
components.summary: Help dialog that lists the keyboard shortcuts of a page, grouped, with keys drawn as Kbd chips. Opens with `?` by default.
components.description:
Use it once per page or app shell. Shortcuts come from two places: everything registered with the `useHotkeys` composable (listed automatically, grouped by `group`, with its `description`), and an optional `shortcuts` array for display-only entries such as combos the browser owns. Entries without a description are not listed.

`useHotkeys(map | array | getter, options?)` registers combos for the life of a component: `"mod+k"` (`mod` is Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere), plain keys (`"?"`, `"esc"`, `"f5"`), and sequences joined with `then` (`"g then d"`, up to 5 steps, `timeout` ms between steps, default 1000). It listens on the document, or on one element with `target`. Events that come from inputs, textareas, selects and contenteditable elements are ignored unless `allowInInputs` is set. `preventDefault` defaults to true. Invalid combos (empty, modifier-only, unknown key names, longer than 5 steps) are ignored and warned about in development. Two shortcuts that collide (same combo, or one sequence starting another) warn in development and are silent in production. Write punctuation as the character it produces (`"?"`, not `"shift+/"`). The registry is filled on mount in the browser only, so server rendering is safe. `listHotkeys()`, `useRegisteredHotkeys()`, `parseHotkey()` and `formatHotkey()` are exported for custom help screens.

Variations: `size` (`sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`) is the max width from the `sm` breakpoint up; `layout` is `list` (one column) or `columns` (two columns from `sm` up, pair with `size="lg"`); `density` is `comfortable` or `compact`; `headingLevel` sets the level of the group names (the dialog title is an h2). Open it with the `hotkey`, with a `trigger` slot, or with `v-model:open`. While it is open, other registered shortcuts still run: disable them with their `enabled` option if they would act on the page behind the dialog. Use `Command` for a searchable palette and `Dialog` for anything that is not a shortcut list.

a11y: Root has role=menubar; triggers are role=menuitem with aria-haspopup=menu and aria-expanded; content is role=menu with menuitem / menuitemcheckbox / menuitemradio rows.

Keyboard: ArrowLeft/Right move between triggers (swapped in RTL, wraps with `loop`); Enter/Space/ArrowDown open; inside a menu ArrowUp/Down move (skipping disabled), ArrowRight/Left open/close sub menus or step to the neighbouring menu, Home/End jump, type-ahead; Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.

Run actions with @select on MenubarItem; call event.preventDefault() to keep the menu open.
Use destructive on dangerous items and place them last after a MenubarSeparator.
Use MenubarCheckboxItem / MenubarRadioGroup with v-model for toggles and single choices.
Menubar is for application commands; use NavigationMenu for site links and DropdownMenu for one standalone menu.

components.name: NavigationMenu
components.summary: Site navigation bar with hover/click mega-menu panels, an optional shared viewport and an optional indicator.
components.description: Compose `NavigationMenu` > `NavigationMenuList` > `NavigationMenuItem` and give each item either a `NavigationMenuTrigger` + `NavigationMenuContent` pair (a panel with links) or a bare `NavigationMenuLink` (`variant="trigger"`) for a top-level link. By default panels render in one shared `NavigationMenuViewport` that animates its size between panels (mega menu); set `viewport=false` to position each panel under its own trigger. Add `NavigationMenuIndicator` inside the list for an arrow that follows the active trigger. Use it for a site or app header with grouped links. Use `Menubar` / `DropdownMenu` for ACTIONS, `Tabs` for in-page panels and `SidebarNav` for persistent side navigation. Built on reka-ui `NavigationMenu*`.

components.name: Pagination
components.summary: Page navigation with first/prev/next/last, sibling window and ellipses. Compact "Page X of Y" on small screens.
components.description: Give it `total` (item count) and `pageSize`; bind the 1-based page with `v-model:page`. Invalid input is sanitised: the page is clamped into range (and `update:page` re-emitted with the corrected value), a negative/NaN total means one empty page, and a pageSize below 1 falls back to 10. Below the `sm` breakpoint it shows a compact summary between prev/next; `compact` forces that everywhere. For cursor/"load more" lists use a Button instead.

a11y: `<nav aria-label="Pagination">`; the current page button has aria-current="page". Pass `labels.nav` when a page holds more than one pager.
Every button has an accessible name ("Page 3", "Next page"...); the visible number is inside it (WCAG 2.5.3). Page numbers use `tabular-nums` so the controls do not jump.

The compact summary is aria-live="polite". Edge buttons are truly disabled; when the pressed button becomes disabled (Next on the last page) focus moves to the opposite arrow instead of falling to the page.
Buttons are 32px (40px on coarse pointers) at `md`, 24px at `sm` (40px on coarse pointers) and 44px at `lg`; the row wraps at narrow widths, and arrows flip in RTL.
The `simple` variant names its buttons from their visible text ("Previous page", "Next page") and keeps the live "Page X of Y" summary; `shape` and `size` never change names or roles.

llmNotes: Use `v-model:page` with a 1-based page; pass `total` as an item count, not a page count.
Do not clamp the page yourself; the component does and re-emits.
Pass `labels` when the app is localised.

components.name: Stepper
components.summary: Shows progress through a multi-step flow, horizontal or vertical, optionally clickable.
components.description: Pass a `steps` array and the 0-based `current` index (`v-model:current`). Each step is `complete`, `current` or `upcoming` by position, or set `status` explicitly (including `error`). Unknown statuses are ignored and `current` is clamped into range. With `clickable`, steps become buttons that emit `update:current`; the Stepper only shows progress, it does not render step bodies. Use `Tabs` for peer panels and `Breadcrumb` for hierarchy.

a11y: `<ol>` with aria-label (`label`, default "Progress"); the current step has aria-current="step".
Status is announced via visually hidden text ("Completed:", "Current step:", "Error:"), so state is never colour alone: complete shows a check and error shows a cross.
Clickable steps are real buttons (Tab, Enter, Space); non-clickable steps are plain text and not focusable. Indicators are 32px, and button text aligns to the start edge for RTL.
Connectors are decorative (aria-hidden) and logical (`ms-3.75`).

Every variant keeps the same list, status text and aria-current. `dots` and `bar` markers are decorative and carry no number, so state comes from the visually hidden status text and from the check or cross (a check or cross before the title in `bar`), never from colour alone.
A horizontal stepper below the `sm` breakpoint shows only the current step title and keeps the others as visually hidden text, so it fits 320px without scrolling.

Throws a ContractError when a step has no non-empty `title` (unless the `step` slot draws the step).
Throws a ContractError when `label` is blank, because it names the list.
llmNotes: `current` is 0-based, unlike Pagination `page`.
Stepper renders progress only; render the step body yourself with v-if/v-show.
Use `status: "error"` on a step to flag validation problems.

components.description: Presentational card that starts a native HTML5 drag. On `dragstart` it writes `{ id, from }` (JSON, custom MIME type) to `dataTransfer` and marks itself `dragging`; `BoardColumn` reads that on drop. Because dragging is pointer-only, a focused card also emits `move` with a direction when you press Alt + an arrow key: apply it to your data (left/right = other column, up/down = reorder). `disabled` blocks both. The card has no drag logic beyond this and no state of its own: you keep the board data.

llmNotes: Always handle the `move` event (Alt+Arrow) in addition to the column `move`, otherwise keyboard users cannot reorder.

components.name: BoardColumn
components.summary: Kanban-style column that accepts dragged BoardCards and reports where they were dropped.
components.description: Presentational drop zone built on native HTML5 drag events. `BoardColumn` shows a title, a count badge, optional header/footer and an empty state, highlights while a card hovers over it and emits `move` with `{ cardId, from, to, index }`. It never mutates anything: you own the data and apply the move. Pair it with `BoardCard`, which is the draggable part and also provides a keyboard alternative. Cards dragged from a column know their source column automatically, so `acceptFrom` can restrict flows (for example "Done" only accepts from "In progress"). Drops of files, text or any foreign data are ignored. For sortable lists without columns use a plain list; for touch-first drag and drop add your own pointer-based layer, native HTML5 drag is mouse/desktop oriented.

props.name: id
props.description: Unique column id. Sent as `to` in `move` and provided to child cards as their `from`.

props.name: title
props.description: Column heading (also labels the group for assistive tech). Required unless the column has `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: count
props.description: Number in the badge. Defaults to the number of cards in the default slot; negative/NaN values fall back to that. Set it when the list is paginated or virtualised.

props.name: showCount
props.description: Show the count badge.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Empty-state text; override with the `empty` slot.

props.name: acceptFrom
props.description: Only accept cards coming from these column ids. Cards already in this column (reordering) are always accepted; cards of unknown origin are rejected when this is set. Empty/undefined accepts everything.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Reject every drop, never highlight, dim the column.

props.name: variant
props.description: Column surface.

props.name: size
props.description: Padding, gap and text size.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes (set the column width here, e.g. `w-72`).

slots.name: default

slots.name: footer
slots.description: Rendered below the cards (e.g. an "Add card" button). Omitted when not provided.
