components.name: BarChart
components.summary: Dependency-free SVG bar chart: grouped or stacked, vertical or horizontal, rounded or square bars, optional value labels and grid styles, with axis, legend and per-bar tooltips.
components.description: Use `BarChart` to compare values across categories. Pass `labels` (categories) and `series` (`{ name, data, tone? }`; `data[i]` belongs to `labels[i]`). The value domain always includes 0 and uses nice ticks; negative bars extend below (vertical) or left of (horizontal) the zero line. `variant="stacked"` (or the `stacked` boolean) stacks positives up and negatives down separately; `rounded`, `gap`, `size`, `showValues` and `grid` change the look without changing the data or the text alternatives. Non-finite values draw no bar and read "n/a" in the tooltip. Mismatched lengths are tolerated (category count = longest of labels and series; missing labels are empty). Crowded category labels are thinned and long ones truncated with the full text in a `<title>`; horizontal bars size their label gutter from an estimate of the rendered width of the widest label (per-glyph width classes, wide letters count more), so labels do not clip at the left edge. More than 5 series cycle through chart-1..5. For trends over time use `LineChart`; for parts of a whole use `DonutChart`. Size with `class` (`w-full`, `max-w-xl`); `width`/`height` only set the viewBox proportions.

props.name: labels
props.description: Category labels, one per group of bars.

props.name: series
props.description: One entry per series. Unnamed series get "Series N".

props.name: orientation
props.description: Bar direction. Horizontal charts list categories down the left.

props.name: variant
props.description: Series side by side (`grouped`) or stacked per category (`stacked`). When omitted, the `stacked` boolean decides.

props.name: stacked
props.description: Stack series per category instead of grouping them side by side. Same as `variant="stacked"`; `variant` wins when both are set.

props.name: rounded
props.description: Bar corner radius: `none` 0, `sm` 2px, `md` 4px, `full` a pill (half the shorter side). `auto` keeps the original look: 2px for grouped bars, square for stacked segments.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between categories: bars fill 85% (`sm`), 70% (`md`) or 50% (`lg`) of each category band.

props.name: size
props.description: Chart height when `height` is not set: 160 / 240 / 320 viewBox units.

props.name: showValues
props.description: Print the value at the end of each bar (the category total when stacked), using the axis formatter. Labels that do not fit their bar are left out; the tooltip and the hidden data table still carry every value.

props.name: grid
props.description: Gridline style: `value` lines at each tick, `dashed` dashed value lines, `full` value lines plus a separator between categories, `none` no lines. When omitted, `showGrid` decides (`value` when on).

props.name: showGrid
props.description: Gridlines at each tick.

props.name: showAxis
props.description: Value ticks, category labels and the zero baseline.

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Legend of series swatches. `auto` shows it when there is more than one series.

props.name: valueFormatter
props.description: Formats axis ticks and tooltips (default: compact on the axis, grouped numbers in tooltips).

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the chart image. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`); an auto-generated summary ("Bar chart: 3 categories, 2 series, values from 1 to 9") is only the fallback when strict mode is off.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown (as role="img") when there is nothing to plot.

props.name: width
props.description: ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px), so axis text keeps its real size at 320px.

props.name: height
props.description: ViewBox height. Overrides `size` (default height 240).

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

examples.title: Long and wide category labels
examples.description: Horizontal bars size the label gutter from the estimated width of the widest label (wide letters such as W and M count more than i or l) plus a small safety margin, capped at 40% of the chart. A label that still does not fit is cut with an ellipsis and keeps its full text in a `<title>`. Sample data.
examples.code: <BarChart orientation="horizontal" show-values label="Sample data: long and wide labels" :labels="['Warehouse Maintenance', 'MMMMWWWW', 'Mmmm Wwww Mmmm Wwww Mmmm', 'Illinois', 'ok']" :series="[{ name: 'Series', data: [14, 9, 6, 11, 3] }]" />

a11y: The chart is `<svg role="img">` with an automatic `aria-label` (category/series counts and value range); override with `label`.
Every bar has a native `<title>` tooltip: "Category, Series: value" ("n/a" for missing values).
A visually hidden data table (caption, category rows, one column per series) follows the chart, so every value is readable as text. It is cut at 200 rows.

Axis text is 12px with tabular figures and the SVG is sized to its container, so labels stay legible at 320px; the horizontal label gutter grows with the widest label (up to 40% of the width, then labels are cut with an ellipsis), so wide letters such as W and M are not clipped. Series are distinguished by legend, position and the data table, not by colour alone.
The empty state is a `role="img"` element labelled with `emptyText`.
Colour is never the only carrier: the HTML legend names every series and tooltips give exact values.

Variants change only the drawing: `variant`, `rounded`, `gap`, `size` and `grid` leave the image name, the tooltips and the hidden data table identical. `showValues` adds the values as text inside the image; gridlines are decoration inside the labelled image.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
Throws a ContractError when `labels` is not an array, `series` is not an array, or a series has no `data` array. Empty arrays are valid and show `emptyText`.
llmNotes: Use `labels` for categories and `series[].data` for values (same index); never pass objects per bar.
Use `stacked` only when series are parts of a total; otherwise group them.
Provide a `valueFormatter` for currency, percentages and units.
Only chart-N / semantic tones are available; do not pass colours. Set a `label` describing the insight.
Size with `class`, not `width`/`height` (viewBox units); pick the height with `size` (sm, md, lg).
Prefer `variant="stacked"` over the `stacked` boolean in new code. Use `showValues` for few bars; labels that do not fit are dropped, so never rely on them as the only source of values.
`rounded="full"` suits grouped bars; keep stacked segments `none` unless `gap="lg"` separates them.

components.name: BulletChart
components.summary: Bullet chart: one thin measure bar against a target marker and qualitative range bands, for one or several stacked measures.
components.description: Use `BulletChart` to compare a measure with its goal and with bands such as poor, fair and good, in the space of a single row. It replaces a gauge or a set of progress bars when several measures share one scale. Each entry of `bullets` is `{ label, value, target?, ranges?, max?, tone?, unit? }`. `ranges` are ascending upper bounds (`[50, 75, 100]`); unsorted, duplicate and non-finite bounds are cleaned up. The bands are tonal steps of the muted colour (the lowest is the darkest) and the two darkest also carry a diagonal hatch, so the bands never rely on shade alone; `showRangeLabels` prints the bounds. The target is a tick with a diamond cap: a shape, not a colour. `variant` lays the measures out as rows (`horizontal`) or columns (`vertical`); `size` sets the band thickness. With `sharedScale` (default) every measure uses one axis, so lengths compare; turn it off when the measures have different units, and each measure then fills its own scale (no common axis is drawn). A value beyond the end of the scale is clamped and marked with an arrow head; a value that is not a number is listed as "n/a" and drawn without a bar. Not for time series (use `LineChart`) or part-to-whole data (use `DonutChart`). At most 60 measures are drawn.

props.name: bullets
props.description: Measures: `{ label, value, target?, ranges?, max?, tone?, unit? }`. `ranges` are ascending upper bounds of the bands (up to 5); `max` is the upper end of that measure's scale; `unit` is appended to its value. An empty array shows `emptyText`.

props.name: variant
props.description: Rows (`horizontal`) or side-by-side columns (`vertical`). A vertical chart with many measures scrolls inside a focusable, named region.

props.name: size
props.description: Band thickness and spacing: 16, 24 or 32 px bands (vertical: 18, 26 or 35 px wide, 120, 180 or 240 px tall).

props.name: tone
props.description: Colour token of the measure bar for bullets without their own `tone`.

props.name: showTarget
props.description: Draw the target marker: a tick with a diamond cap. The table alternative always lists the target.

props.name: showValues
props.description: Print each value (with its `unit`) beside the measure.

props.name: showAxis
props.description: Draw the scale (ticks and grid lines). Only with `sharedScale`.

props.name: showRangeLabels
props.description: Print the upper bound of every range band. Adds spacing so the labels do not collide with the next measure.

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Legend for the measure, the target marker and the ranges.

props.name: sharedScale
props.description: One scale for all measures (comparable lengths, one axis). Off: each measure fills its own scale and no axis is drawn.

props.name: valueFormatter
props.description: Formats axis ticks, values, targets and range bounds. Defaults to compact numbers on the axis and grouped numbers for values.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the chart. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.

props.name: title
props.description: Visible heading text above the chart. Also names the chart when `label` is not set.

props.name: description
props.description: Visible supporting text under the title.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown when there are no measures.

props.name: width
props.description: ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px).

props.name: height
props.description: Total viewBox height. Overrides the height that follows `size` and the number of measures: bands thicken (up to twice the size) and rows spread to fill it.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

a11y: The chart is one `role="img"` SVG named by `label`, `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; an automatic summary ("Bullet chart: 3 measures") is only the fallback when strict mode is off.
A visually hidden table lists every measure with its value, target and range bounds, so no number depends on seeing the picture.

The target marker is a tick with a diamond cap (a shape). The range bands are tonal steps of the muted colour, the two darkest are hatched, and `showRangeLabels` prints their bounds: no meaning rests on colour alone. Shapes keep an outline in forced-colors mode.
Each band, bar and marker has a native tooltip (`<title>`); values and labels are 12px text with tabular figures.
The SVG fills its container (1 unit is 1 CSS px) and never widens the page; a vertical chart with many columns scrolls horizontally inside a focusable `role="region"` named like the chart.
No animation. Empty and invalid data show an inline message; NaN and Infinity never reach the SVG.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `label`, `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
Throws a ContractError when `bullets` is not an array. An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.
Throws a ContractError when a measure has no `label` text.
llmNotes: Give every BulletChart a `label` or a `title`; give every measure a `label`.
Pass `ranges` as ascending upper bounds (`[50, 75, 100]`); the lowest band is drawn darkest.
Use the same unit for all measures when `sharedScale` is on; set `sharedScale` to false for mixed units.
Use `variant="vertical"` for a few measures side by side, `horizontal` for a list.
Use `max` on a measure to fix its scale end; a larger value is clamped and marked.
Do not use a BulletChart for a time series (LineChart) or a share of a whole (DonutChart).

components.name: CalendarHeatmap
components.summary: Contribution-style calendar: one cell per day, weeks as columns and weekdays as rows, with month labels, a legend and a month table for assistive technology.
components.description: Use `CalendarHeatmap` to show activity per day over weeks or years (commits, deploys, support tickets, visits). `data` is `{ date: "YYYY-MM-DD", value }` per day; entries of the same day are summed, a date-time is read up to its date, and entries with an invalid date or a negative or non-numeric value are skipped and counted in an inline message. The range is `start` to `end`; without them it is the span of the data (at most 1830 days, the latest are kept). All date maths is UTC, and the component never reads the current date, so server and browser render the same grid. A day without an entry is drawn as an outlined "no data" cell, a day with value 0 as the faint level 0 cell, and the rest in `levels` (3 to 7) steps of the `tone` from the domain `min` (default 0) to `max` (default the largest value). Month names sit above the first week of each month (the year at the first label and every January), and Mon, Wed and Fri label the rows. The grid keeps its cell size and scrolls inside a focusable, named region instead of shrinking. For a rows-by-columns matrix of anything else use `Heatmap`.

props.name: data
props.description: `{ date, value }` per day. `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, an ISO date-time or a `Date` (its UTC date). `value` is a number >= 0. The same day is summed. An empty array with `start` and `end` draws empty days; without them it shows `emptyText`.

props.name: start
props.description: First day shown, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Default: the earliest day in `data` (or 364 days before `end`).

props.name: end
props.description: Last day shown, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Default: the latest day in `data` (or `start` when the data ends earlier).

props.name: weekStart
props.description: First row of each week column: Sunday or Monday. The Mon, Wed and Fri labels follow.

props.name: size
props.description: Cell size: 10, 12 or 16 px.

props.name: shape
props.description: Rounded squares or circles. The legend uses the same shape.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between cells: 1, 2 or 4 px.

props.name: levels
props.description: Number of intensity steps above zero, clamped to 3 to 7 (a non-number gives 5).

props.name: tone
props.description: Colour token of the intensity ramp.

props.name: min
props.description: Value where the ramp starts (default 0). Values below it are the faintest step.

props.name: max
props.description: Value of the strongest step (default: the largest value in the range). Set it to compare several calendars on one scale.

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Less ... More legend with the no-activity cell and every step.

props.name: showMonthLabels
props.description: Month names above the weeks (the year at the first label and every January).

props.name: showWeekdayLabels
props.description: Mon, Wed and Fri beside the rows.

props.name: cellTitle
props.description: Custom native tooltip per day. Receives the `YYYY-MM-DD` date and the summed value, or `null` for a day without data.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the chart. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.

props.name: title
props.description: Visible heading text above the chart. Also names the chart when `label` is not set.

props.name: description
props.description: Visible supporting text under the title.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown when there is nothing to draw: no valid data and no `start` or `end`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

examples.script: const year = Array.from({ length: 364 }, (_, i) => ({ date: new Date(Date.UTC(2025, 0, 1 + i)).toISOString().slice(0, 10), value: (i * 7 + Math.floor(i / 8) * 5) % 13 }))

components.name: DonutChart
components.summary: Dependency-free SVG donut or half donut showing parts of a whole, with a centre total and a legend of values and percentages that sits beside or under the ring.
components.description: Use `DonutChart` for a handful (2–6) of parts that add up to a meaningful total. Segments are proportional to their values; negative, NaN and Infinity values count as 0. One non-zero segment is a full ring; a zero total shows a muted ring and the centre reads "0" with the `emptyText` caption while the legend still lists every label at 0%. The centre shows the formatted total plus `centerText`; replace it with the scoped `center` slot. `variant="half"` draws a semicircle with the total in its hollow, which suits a single headline split (passed / failed) in less height; `layout` moves the legend (beside the ring, always beside, or always under it). Use `BarChart` for many categories or precise comparison.

props.name: data
props.description: Segments in draw order (clockwise from 12 o'clock). Tones cycle chart-1..5 when omitted.

props.name: size
props.description: Rendered width: 7rem / 10rem / 14rem (`size-28` / `size-40` / `size-56` for `full`).

props.name: variant
props.description: `full` is a ring, `half` a semicircle opening downwards at half the height (`h-14` / `h-20` / `h-28`), with the centre text at the bottom of its hollow.

props.name: layout
props.description: Legend placement: `auto` beside the ring and wrapping below it when narrow, `inline` always beside it (long labels truncate), `stacked` always under it at full width. Use `showLegend` to remove the legend.

props.name: thickness
props.description: Ring thickness in viewBox units (100×100 box), clamped to 2–40.

props.name: showLegend
props.description: List swatch, label, formatted value and percentage (max one decimal) per segment.

props.name: centerText
props.description: Small caption under the total in the centre.

props.name: valueFormatter
props.description: Formats the total, legend values and tooltips.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the chart image. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`); an auto-generated summary ("Donut chart: 3 segments, total 100") is only the fallback when strict mode is off.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown when `data` is empty (and as the centre caption when the total is 0).

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

slots.name: center
slots.description: Replaces the default centre content (total + caption).

Each segment has a native `<title>` tooltip "Label: value (pct%)"; the HTML legend repeats every value and percentage as real text.
The empty state is a `role="img"` element labelled with `emptyText`.

`variant` and `layout` change only the drawing and where the legend sits: the image name, the tooltips and the legend text are the same. The half ring is still one labelled image and the total stays real text in its hollow.

The ring has a fixed size (`size-28`, `size-40` or `size-56`) and the legend wraps beside or under it, so it fits a 320px screen. Values and percentages use `tabular-nums`; the legend text is the non-colour alternative to the segment colours.

components.name: FunnelChart
components.summary: Dependency-free SVG funnel chart with funnel, pyramid, bars and steps variants, vertical or horizontal layout, conversion rates, labels inside or beside the shapes and non-monotone data.
components.description: Use `FunnelChart` for a sequence of stages where each one is (usually) a subset of the one before: a sales pipeline, a sign-up flow, an order process. Pass `stages` as `{ label, value, tone? }`. `variant` picks the shape: `funnel` joins the stages into one tapering shape (the edge facing the next stage has the next value), `pyramid` is the same shape stacked the other way round (the first stage is the base), `steps` centres a rectangle per stage and `bars` aligns the rectangles to the start like a bar chart. `orientation` runs the stages top to bottom or start to end. `showConversion` prints the share of the previous stage next to each value (the first stage has none; a previous value of 0 or a missing value reads "n/a"). Text sits `beside` the shapes (a label column, or underneath when horizontal) or `inside` them; text that does not fit inside moves beside its stage. The data does not have to fall: a stage larger than the one before is drawn as it is (and its conversion is above 100%). Negative values draw no shape; missing values read "n/a". At most 50 stages are drawn; the hidden table lists up to 200. Use `BarChart` to compare unrelated categories and `Gauge` or `StatBar` for one value against a target.

props.name: stages
props.description: Stages in order. `value` sizes the shape (negative or non-finite values draw nothing and non-finite ones read "n/a"); `tone` overrides the chart `tone` for one stage. An empty array shows `emptyText`.

props.name: variant
props.description: `funnel` tapering shape, `pyramid` the same shape upside down (first stage at the base), `bars` rectangles aligned to the start (left, or bottom when horizontal), `steps` rectangles centred on the axis.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `vertical` stacks the stages top to bottom with a label column; `horizontal` runs them from start to end with text underneath each stage.

props.name: labelPlacement
props.description: `beside` prints label, value and conversion next to the shapes; `inside` prints them on a small plate inside each shape when it fits (the label moves beside the stage when it does not; when horizontal only the value and conversion go inside).

props.name: showConversion
props.description: Show the percent of the previous stage next to each value. The first stage has none. A previous value of 0 or a missing value reads "n/a".

props.name: showValues
props.description: Show the value of each stage. With it off only the label (and the conversion, if on) is printed; the values stay in the table and tooltips.

props.name: size
props.description: Height of one stage when vertical (32 / 44 / 56), height of the shapes when horizontal (96 / 144 / 200), and the spacing of the figure.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between neighbouring stages: 2, 4 or 8 viewBox units.

props.name: tone
props.description: Tone of the stages that set none.

props.name: valueFormatter
props.description: Formats values and tooltips. Defaults to compact (labels) / grouped (tooltip) numbers.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the chart image. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` names it.

props.name: title
props.description: Visible heading above the chart. It also names the chart when `label` is not set.

props.name: description
props.description: Visible description under the title. The image points to it with `aria-describedby`, next to the generated summary.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown (as role="img") when there are no stages.

props.name: loading
props.description: Show a busy placeholder (`role="status"`, `aria-busy`) with `loadingText` instead of the chart.

props.name: loadingText
props.description: Message of the loading placeholder.

props.name: width
props.description: ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px).

props.name: height
props.description: ViewBox height. Overrides the height derived from `size` and the number of stages.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element (`<figure>`).

examples.description: No stages, a loading placeholder, and stages with a missing and a negative value (they draw no shape and read "n/a" or their number).

a11y: The chart is one `<svg role="img">` named by `label` (or `title`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`) and described by the visible `description` and a generated text summary (stage count, first and last stage).

A visually hidden data table (stages as rows) lists the value, the percent of the previous stage and the percent of the first stage of every stage, so no number depends on the picture; missing rates read "n/a".

Meaning never rests on colour: every stage carries its label, and its value and conversion are text (on a plate in the page background when drawn inside a shape, so the text keeps the normal text contrast). Each shape has a native `<title>` tooltip.

The SVG is sized to its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px): text keeps its size, labels are shortened (full text in a tooltip) and horizontal labels are thinned when columns get narrow, so nothing overflows at 320px.
In forced-colors mode the shapes use the system text colour and the plates keep their border. The loading placeholder is a polite `role="status"` region marked busy; it does not animate.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
Throws a ContractError when `stages` is not an array or a stage has no `label` or no numeric `value`. An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.
llmNotes: Pass `stages` in the order of the process, each as `{ label, value }`; do not pre-compute percentages, use `showConversion`.
Set `label` (or `title`) to say what the funnel measures and use `valueFormatter` for units.
Use `variant="pyramid"` only when the first stage is the broadest and should sit at the base; for a normal funnel use `funnel`.
Use `orientation="horizontal"` for few stages (up to about 6) in wide containers; vertical for long lists and narrow screens.
Use `labelPlacement="inside"` for wide shapes; narrow stages move their text beside them automatically.
Size with `class`, `size` and `gap`, not `width` / `height`. At most 50 stages are drawn.

components.name: Heatmap
components.summary: Accessible grid heatmap (commit calendar, activity by hour) with intensity levels, labels, legend and cell tooltips.
components.description: Use `Heatmap` for a rows × columns matrix of magnitudes: activity calendars, usage by weekday/hour, correlation-style grids. It is a real `<table>`: row/column labels are `<th>`, every cell is a `<td>` with a visually hidden value and the colour in an inner span. Intensity is one of `levels` (1–5) opacity steps of the tone; `null`, NaN, missing and zero cells are the muted "empty" colour. The domain defaults to the data min/max (override with `min`/`max`). Ragged rows are padded. For long column label lists use `colLabelStep` to show every n-th label visibly. `heatLevel(value, min, max, levels)` is exported as a pure helper.

props.name: values
props.description: Rows × columns of values. Empty array → `emptyText`.

props.name: rowLabels
props.description: Row headers (`<th scope="row">`).

props.name: colLabels
props.description: Column headers (`<th scope="col">`).

props.name: tone
props.description: Colour token of the intensity ramp.

props.name: min
props.description: Domain minimum (default: smallest value in the data).

props.name: max
props.description: Domain maximum (default: largest value in the data).

props.name: levels
props.description: Number of intensity steps, clamped to 1–5.

props.name: size
props.description: Cell size: size-3 / size-4 / size-6.

props.name: shape
props.description: Cell shape: slightly rounded square, or a circle (`rounded-full`) for a dot matrix. Applies to the legend swatches too.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between cells: 1px, 2px or 4px (`border-spacing`).

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Less … More swatch legend.

props.name: colLabelStep
props.description: Show every n-th column label visibly; the others stay screen-reader only.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the region and its visually hidden table caption. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`); an auto-generated summary is only the fallback when strict mode is off.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown when there are no cells.

props.name: cellTitle
props.type: (value: number | null, rowLabel: string, colLabel: string) => string
props.description: Custom native tooltip per cell (default "Row, Col: value").

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

a11y: Native table semantics: row and column labels are `<th scope>`, cells are `<td>`; a visually hidden `<caption>` carries `label` or an automatic summary.
Each cell contains its value as visually hidden text ("no data" for empty cells), so colour is never the only carrier; the swatch has a native tooltip.

The grid sits in a focusable `role="region"` (named by `label` or the summary) that scrolls horizontally, so a wide heatmap never widens the page and keyboard users can scroll it. Text is 12px; the legend uses tabular figures.
The empty state is a `role="img"` element labelled with `emptyText`.
`shape` and `gap` change only the swatches: the table, the hidden values and the intensity steps are identical. Circles are not read differently from squares.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
Throws a ContractError when `values` is not an array of rows (each row an array). An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.
llmNotes: Pass `values` as rows × columns; use null for missing cells (zero is also drawn as empty).
Provide `rowLabels`/`colLabels` so the table is understandable to screen readers.

Use `shape="circle"` for sparse matrices and `gap="lg"` to separate cells further; keep squares for dense calendars. `levels` already sets the number of intensity steps (1 to 5), so there is no separate `scale` prop.
Use `colLabelStep` for wide calendars instead of removing labels.
Pick one `tone`; do not mix colours. Use `min`/`max` to compare several heatmaps on one scale.

components.name: LineChart
components.summary: Dependency-free SVG line chart with multiple series, nice y ticks, linear, smooth or step curves, optional area fill and markers, grid styles, gaps for missing values and tooltips on dots.
components.description: Use `LineChart` for trends over an ordered axis (time, steps). Pass `labels` (x categories) and `series` (`{ name, data, tone? }`). The y domain is the nice-tick extent of the data. NaN / Infinity values break the line into separate segments; a point with no neighbours is drawn as a dot even when `showDots` is false. `curve` joins points with straight segments, a smooth curve that never overshoots the data, or steps that hold each value until the next point. Dots are on automatically up to 60 points (`showDots="auto"`); each dot has a native `<title>` tooltip. Crowded x labels are thinned. Renders 10,000 points quickly (dots stay off by default). Use `Sparkline` for tiny inline trends and `BarChart` for category comparison. Size with `class`; `width`/`height` set the viewBox proportions.

props.name: labels
props.description: X-axis labels, one per point.

props.name: series
props.description: One line per entry. More than 5 series cycle through chart-1..5.

props.name: variant
props.description: Lines only, or lines with a soft fill under each. When omitted, the `area` boolean decides.

props.name: area
props.description: Soft fill under each line. Same as `variant="area"`; `variant` wins when both are set.

props.name: curve
props.description: How points are joined. `smooth` is a monotone curve (it never dips below the lowest or above the highest neighbour); `step` holds each value until the next point. Gaps still break the line. The area follows the curve.

props.name: size
props.description: Chart height when `height` is not set: 160 / 240 / 320 viewBox units.

props.name: showDots
props.description: `auto` draws dots when there are at most 60 points.

props.name: markerShape
props.description: Shape of the point markers. `series` gives each series its own shape (circle, square, diamond, triangle), which the legend repeats, so series differ by shape and dash pattern as well as colour. Markers still follow `showDots`.

props.name: grid
props.description: Gridline style: `horizontal` solid lines at each y tick, `dashed` dashed ones, `full` horizontal lines plus a vertical line at each labelled x position, `none` no lines. When omitted, `showGrid` decides (`horizontal` when on).

props.name: showGrid
props.description: Horizontal gridlines at each y tick.

props.name: showAxis
props.description: Y tick labels and x labels.

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Legend of series swatches; `auto` shows it for more than one series.

props.name: valueFormatter
props.description: Formats y ticks and tooltips.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the chart image. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`); an auto-generated summary ("Line chart: 12 points per series, 2 series, values from 1 to 9") is only the fallback when strict mode is off.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown (as role="img") when there is nothing to plot.

props.name: width
props.description: ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px), so axis text keeps its real size at 320px.

props.name: height
props.description: ViewBox height. Overrides `size` (default height 240).

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

a11y: The chart is `<svg role="img">` with an automatic `aria-label` (points, series, value range); override with `label`.
Dots carry native `<title>` tooltips: "Label, Series: value". Isolated points are always drawn so no data is invisible.
A visually hidden data table (caption, one row per point, one column per series) follows the chart, so every value is readable as text. It is cut at 200 rows.

Series differ by dash pattern as well as colour (solid, dashed, dotted, dash-dot); the legend draws the same line sample. Axis text is 12px with tabular figures and the SVG is sized to its container, so labels stay legible at 320px.
The empty state is a `role="img"` element labelled with `emptyText`.
The HTML legend names every series so colour is not the only identifier.

Variants change only the drawing: `curve`, `variant`, `grid` and `size` leave the image name, the tooltips and the hidden data table identical. `markerShape="series"` adds a third cue (shape) next to colour and dash pattern, and the legend repeats it.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
Throws a ContractError when `labels` is not an array, `series` is not an array, or a series has no `data` array. Empty arrays are valid and show `emptyText`.
llmNotes: Use `labels` for the x axis and `series[].data` for y values (same index).
Use NaN (or a non-finite number) for missing points: the line breaks instead of interpolating.
Provide `valueFormatter` for units and a `label` that states the takeaway.
Large series: leave `showDots` on `auto` (off above 60 points).
Use Sparkline, not LineChart, for tiny inline trends.
Use `curve="step"` for values that hold between readings and `curve="smooth"` only for continuous measurements; never smooth counts that jump.
Prefer `variant="area"` over the `area` boolean in new code. Use `markerShape="series"` when several series share a chart and must be told apart without colour.

components.name: NetworkGraph
components.summary: Dependency-free node-link diagram with four deterministic layouts, group colours with marker shapes, arrowheads, hulls and a text alternative.
components.description: Use `NetworkGraph` to show how things connect: services that call each other, sites on a route, people in a team. Pass `nodes` (`{ id, label?, group?, size? }`) and `edges` (`{ from, to, weight?, directed?, label? }`). `layout` places the nodes: `force` (a spring simulation with a fixed number of steps and no randomness, so the same data always gives the same picture), `circular`, `grid` or `layered` (left to right along the edge direction; cycles are broken deterministically). `variant` sets how much is drawn: `plain`, `labelled` (node and connection labels, up to 120 nodes) or `grouped` (a dashed hull around every group). Nodes grow with their weighted degree (the sum of the weights of their connections) unless `size` is set, so mix `size` on all nodes or on none. Group is told by colour and by marker shape (circle, square, diamond, triangle), and listed in a legend. Hover or focus a node to keep it and its neighbours at full strength and dim the rest. Bad data is handled in place: duplicate ids are ignored, connections to unknown ids are skipped, more than `maxNodes` nodes (default 300) are cut, and a short message under the graph says what happened. Do not use it for more than a few hundred nodes or for a tree; use `Tree` for hierarchies.

props.name: nodes
props.type: { id: string; label?: string; group?: string; size?: number }[]
props.description: The nodes. `id` is unique and required; a repeated id is ignored. `label` defaults to the id. `group` sets colour, marker shape and hull. `size` is a relative size (positive number).

props.name: edges
props.type: { from: string; to: string; weight?: number; directed?: boolean; label?: string }[]
props.description: Connections between node ids. `weight` (positive) widens the line and enlarges both nodes; `directed` draws an arrowhead at `to`; `label` shows on the line in the `labelled` variant. Unknown ids are skipped and counted; `from` equal to `to` draws a loop.

props.name: layout
props.description: Placement. `force` is a spring simulation with fixed steps, `circular` puts the nodes on a ring grouped by group, `grid` fills rows, `layered` stacks columns along the edge direction.

props.name: variant
props.description: `plain` draws nodes and lines; `labelled` adds node labels (cut at 12 characters) and connection labels, up to 120 nodes; `grouped` outlines every group with a dashed hull.

props.name: size
props.description: Drawing height when `height` is not set: 200 / 300 / 420 viewBox units. Also the gap between title, drawing, legend and messages.

props.name: edgeStyle
props.description: `curved` bends every line to one side of its direction, so a connection A to B and one B to A no longer overlap.

props.name: directed
props.description: Draw an arrowhead on every connection that does not set its own `directed`.

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Legend of groups with their colour and marker. `auto` shows it when any node has a group; `false` hides it.

props.name: maxNodes
props.description: Most nodes drawn, 1 to 5000. The first nodes are kept; a message says how many were left out. Connections to left-out nodes are skipped.

props.name: title
props.description: Visible title above the drawing (plain text, not a heading). Also names the graph when `label` is not set.

props.name: description
props.description: Visible description under the title.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the graph. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set; an automatic summary ("Network graph: 6 nodes, 7 connections, 3 groups") is only the fallback when strict mode is off.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown (as role="img") when there is nothing to draw.

props.name: width
props.description: ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The graph then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px), so text keeps its size at 320px.

props.name: height
props.description: ViewBox height. Overrides `size`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

a11y: The drawing is a `role="group"` named by `label` (or `title`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`). Every node is a focusable `role="img"` named with its label, group, number of connections and up to five neighbours.

Keyboard: Tab enters the graph on one node (a roving tab stop); Arrow Right and Down move to the next node, Arrow Left and Up to the previous one, Home and End jump to the first and last. The order follows the layout (grouped for circular and grid, by column for layered). Tab leaves the graph. Hover and focus highlight the node, its neighbours and their lines; the rest dims. Focus also draws a ring.

Group is never colour alone: each group has a marker shape (circle, square, diamond, triangle), the legend shows both, and the node name includes the group. Direction is an arrowhead, not a colour. Nodes keep an outline in forced-colors mode.

A visually hidden text alternative follows the drawing: a table of nodes (name, group, connections written as "A to B (weight 3)") and a table of connections (pair, weight, label), each cut at 200 rows with the cut stated in the caption.
Messages about cut or skipped data are plain text under the graph. The empty state is a `role="img"` with `emptyText`.
The drawing scales to the container (1 unit = 1 CSS px) and reflows at 320px. Highlight changes use opacity only, with a transition under `motion-safe`; nothing moves on its own.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `label`, `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
Throws a ContractError when `nodes` is not an array. An empty array is valid and shows the empty state.
Throws a ContractError when a node has no `id` (a non-empty string).
Throws a ContractError when `edges` is given and is not an array.
Throws a ContractError when a connection has no `from` or no `to`.
llmNotes: Always pass `label` or `title`; give every node a unique `id` and use those ids in `edges`.
Use `group` for categories: it sets colour, marker shape, the legend and the `grouped` hulls. Do not add a second colour prop.
Pick `layout="layered"` with `directed` for flows and dependencies, `circular` for small symmetric sets, `grid` for lists, `force` (the default) for general networks.
Use `variant="labelled"` for fewer than about 30 nodes; larger graphs stay `plain` and rely on hover, focus and the legend.
Do not pass random or time-based data to force a different picture: the layout is deterministic by design.
Raise `maxNodes` only when you must; the default of 300 keeps the drawing readable and fast.
replaces: hand-rolled SVG node-link diagrams
force-graph libraries for small and medium networks

components.name: RadarChart
components.summary: Dependency-free SVG radar (spider) chart with three or more axes, several series, line, area or dots variants, polygon or circular rings, 3 to 6 levels and a configurable scale.
components.description: Use `RadarChart` to compare a few profiles over the same 3 to about 10 measures (a skills matrix, a product comparison). Pass `axes` (names, clockwise from the top) and `series` (`{ name, data, tone? }`, one value per axis). `variant` draws each series as an outline (`line`), an outline with a soft fill (`area`) or only markers (`dots`); every series has its own dash pattern and marker shape, so series differ by more than colour. `shape` sets the rings: straight segments (`polygon`) or circles; `levels` sets how many rings, 3 to 6. The scale starts at 0 (or the lowest value when negative) and ends at a round number that covers the data; set `min` and `max` to compare charts on the same scale. The radius is chosen so every axis label stays inside the chart, also at 320px; long names are shortened (the full name is in a tooltip). Missing or non-finite values sit at the centre and read "n/a" in the table. At most 40 axes are drawn. Use `BarChart` when there are fewer than 3 measures or when exact comparison matters: areas and angles are hard to read precisely.

props.name: axes
props.description: Axis names, at least 3, clockwise from the top. An empty array shows `emptyText`; 1 or 2 names are an error (and show `emptyText` outside strict mode).

props.name: series
props.description: One shape per entry; `data` has one value per axis in the order of `axes`. More than 5 series cycle through chart-1..5, dash patterns and marker shapes.

props.name: variant
props.description: `line` outlines each series, `area` adds a soft fill under the outline, `dots` draws only the markers (a larger marker per axis).

props.name: shape
props.description: Shape of the rings: straight segments between the axes, or circles. The series outline is always a polygon.

props.name: levels
props.description: Number of rings. Other numbers are rounded and clamped to 3..6.

props.name: size
props.description: Chart height 220 / 300 / 380 viewBox units (the radar is as large as the width and the axis labels allow) and the spacing of the figure.

props.name: min
props.description: Value at the centre. Defaults to 0, or the lowest value when that is negative. A `min` above `max` is swapped.

props.name: max
props.description: Value at the outer ring. Defaults to a round number (1, 2, 2.5, 5 times a power of ten per ring) that covers the data. Values above it sit on the rim.

props.name: showValues
props.description: Print the value of each point outside it. Values that would overlap or leave the chart are left out; none are drawn beyond 48 points.

props.name: showScale
props.description: Print the value of each ring along the first axis (thinned when the rings are close together).

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Legend with the dash pattern and marker of each series; `auto` shows it for more than one series.

props.name: valueFormatter
props.description: Formats ring labels, values and tooltips. Defaults to compact (rings) / grouped (tooltip) numbers.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the chart image. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` names it.

props.name: title
props.description: Visible heading above the chart. It also names the chart when `label` is not set.

props.name: description
props.description: Visible description under the title. The image points to it with `aria-describedby`, next to the generated summary.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown (as role="img") when there is nothing to plot.

props.name: loading
props.description: Show a busy placeholder (`role="status"`, `aria-busy`) with `loadingText` instead of the chart.

props.name: loadingText
props.description: Message of the loading placeholder.

props.name: width
props.description: ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px).

props.name: height
props.description: ViewBox height. Overrides `size` (default height 300).

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element (`<figure>`).

examples.description: Nothing to plot, a loading placeholder, and a series with a missing value (it sits at the centre and reads "n/a" in the table).

a11y: The chart is one `<svg role="img">` named by `label` (or `title`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`) and described by the visible `description` and a generated text summary (axis and series counts, value range and scale).
A visually hidden data table (axes as rows, one column per series) follows the chart, so every value is readable as text; missing values read "n/a".

Series are told apart by dash pattern and marker shape (and by the legend), not by colour alone; `dots` uses marker shapes only. Each marker has a native `<title>` tooltip with the axis, series and value.

The radius is computed so that every axis label stays inside the viewBox. The SVG is sized to its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px), so text keeps its size and nothing overflows at 320px. Long names are shortened and keep their full text in a tooltip.

In forced-colors mode lines and markers use the system text colour; dash patterns and marker shapes carry the series, and the area fill is dropped. The loading placeholder is a polite `role="status"` region marked busy; it does not animate.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
Throws a ContractError when `axes` is not an array or has 1 or 2 names, `series` is not an array, or a series has no `data` array. Empty arrays are valid and show `emptyText`.
llmNotes: Use at least 3 axes and keep it to about 10; give each series one value per axis, in the order of `axes`.
Set `label` (or `title`) to say what is compared. Name the unit in `valueFormatter` and set `min` / `max` when several charts must share a scale.
Limit the chart to 2 or 3 series; with `variant="area"` the fills overlap.
Use `shape="circle"` for a softer look and `levels` for the number of rings; neither changes the data.
Do not use a radar chart to read exact values; show `showValues` or use `BarChart`.
Size with `class` and `size`, not `width` / `height`.

components.name: Sankey
components.summary: Flow diagram: nodes in layers joined by ribbons whose width is the amount that flows, with a table of flows as the text alternative.
components.description: Use `Sankey` to show how a quantity moves and splits across stages (orders to outcomes, budget to spending lines, traffic to pages), when the paths matter as much as the totals. Pass `links` of `{ source, target, value }`; nodes are created from the ids, and an optional `nodes` list sets labels. The layout is layered and deterministic: a node sits one layer after its latest source, nodes that nothing leaves line up on the right edge, and a fixed number of relaxation passes places nodes near the nodes they exchange flow with. Repeated source and target pairs are added up. Flows with a value that is not above zero, flows from a node to itself and flows that close a loop are left out and reported in a message. `variant` chooses solid nodes with tinted ribbons or outlined nodes with hairline-edged ribbons; ribbon opacity comes from tokens (`linkOpacity`), never a gradient. Do not use it for a few categories without stages (use `DonutChart` or `BarChart`), for flows that loop back, or for more than a few dozen nodes.

props.name: links
props.description: `{ source, target, value }` flows between node ids. Repeated pairs are added up. An empty array shows `emptyText`.

props.name: nodes
props.description: `{ id, label? }` entries to set labels. Ids that only appear in `links` become nodes labelled with the id; nodes that no flow touches are left out.

props.name: variant
props.description: `flat` solid nodes and tinted ribbons; `outline` empty nodes with a tone coloured edge and ribbons with a hairline edge.

props.name: size
props.description: Height of the drawing: 220, 320 or 440 (an explicit `height` wins).

props.name: gap
props.description: Vertical space between the nodes of one layer: 6, 12 or 22 px.

props.name: tone
props.description: `auto` gives each node the next chart colour and colours a ribbon like its source; any other value paints the whole diagram in that token.

props.name: linkOpacity
props.description: Ribbon opacity: 15, 30 or 45 percent of the tone. Labels stay readable over all three.

props.name: showValues
props.description: Print the node value after its label.

props.name: valueFormatter
props.description: Formats values in labels, tooltips and the table. Default: grouped number with up to two decimals.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the diagram. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.

props.name: title
props.description: Visible heading above the diagram; also the name when there is no `label`.

props.name: description
props.description: Visible sentence under the title.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown when there is no flow to draw.

props.name: width
props.description: ViewBox width until the container is measured. The diagram then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS pixel).

props.name: height
props.description: ViewBox height. Overrides `size`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

a11y: The drawing is one SVG `role="img"` named by `label` (or `title`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`) and described by an automatic summary (nodes, flows, layers).
A visually hidden table lists every flow as From, To and Value (first 200 rows). It is the text alternative; the nodes and ribbons also carry native tooltips ("Shipped to Lost: 10").

Colour is never the only signal: every node that has room is labelled with its name and value, ribbons are matched to their ends by position and tooltip, and the table names every flow. Ribbon tints stay at 45 percent or less so labels over them keep their contrast in light and dark.
The `outline` variant adds a hairline edge to ribbons and an edge to nodes, so shapes remain visible in forced-colors mode.
The diagram is not interactive and has no motion. It scales to its container (1 unit = 1 CSS pixel), so text keeps its real size and nothing overflows at 320px.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `label`, `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
Throws a ContractError when `links` is not an array of flows. An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.
llmNotes: Pass `links` as `{ source, target, value }` with ids that name the nodes; add `nodes` only to set labels.
Values must be numbers above zero. Do not pass flows that loop back (A to B to A); they are dropped.
Always set `label` or `title`; use `valueFormatter` for units.
Use `variant="outline"` for dense pages, `tone` for one-colour diagrams, `linkOpacity` to tune ribbon weight. Never add gradients.
Do not use a Sankey for categories without stages, or for more than a few dozen nodes. Use BarChart, DonutChart or Treemap.

components.name: ScatterChart
components.summary: Dependency-free SVG scatter, bubble and connected-scatter chart with several series, marker shapes per series, nice numeric axes, grid styles, axis titles and an optional linear trend line.
components.description: Use `ScatterChart` to show how two numbers relate across many items (price against rating, load against latency). Pass `points` as `{ x, y, size?, label?, series? }`; points with the same `series` name form one series. `variant` picks the mark: `scatter` plots markers, `bubble` scales the area of each marker with `size`, `connected` also joins the points of a series in the order given (a path over time). Series differ by marker shape as well as colour (`markerShape="series"`, the default), so the chart never relies on colour alone. Both axes are numeric with nice ticks, negative values draw a zero line, and the plot never leaves the container: the chart fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px) and thins tick labels instead of overflowing at 320px. `trend` adds the least squares line of each series (dotted) and states its equation in the text summary. Points with a non-finite x or y are skipped and counted in the summary. Every point is available to assistive technology through the hidden data table (cut at 200 rows); each marker also has a native tooltip. Use `LineChart` when x is an ordered category, `Heatmap` for dense two-dimensional counts and `Sparkline` for a tiny inline trend.

props.name: points
props.type: { x: number; y: number; size?: number; label?: string; series?: string }[]
props.description: The data. `series` groups points (points without one form the series `Points`), `label` names a point in the tooltip, the table and `showValues`, `size` is the bubble area. Non-finite coordinates are skipped; an empty array shows `emptyText`.

props.name: variant
props.description: `scatter` markers of one size, `bubble` markers whose area follows `size` (points without a size get the smallest), `connected` also draws a line per series in data order.

props.name: markerShape
props.description: Marker shape. `series` gives each series its own shape (circle, square, diamond, triangle), which the legend repeats; a single series is drawn with circles. A fixed shape applies to every series.

props.name: size
props.description: Plot height 200 / 280 / 360 viewBox units, marker radius 3.5 / 4.5 / 6 (bubbles 3 to 12, 4 to 18, 5 to 24) and the spacing of the figure.

props.name: grid
props.description: `horizontal` a line at each y tick, `vertical` at each x tick, `full` both, `dashed` both dashed, `none` no lines.

props.name: xTitle
props.description: Title of the x axis, printed under the plot (cut to the plot width, the full text is in a tooltip).

props.name: yTitle
props.description: Title of the y axis, printed rotated at the start edge (cut to the plot height).

props.name: trend
props.description: Draw the least squares line of each series as a dotted line across its x range, cut where it leaves the plot. A series needs two points with different x. The equation and R squared are in the text summary and the tooltip.

props.name: showValues
props.description: Print the label of each point (or `x, y`) next to it. Labels that would overlap, or fall outside the chart, are left out; none are drawn beyond 60 points.

props.name: showAxis
props.description: Tick labels and the two axis lines.

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Legend of series with their marker shape; `auto` shows it for more than one series. A trend adds a "Linear trend" entry.

props.name: tones
props.description: Tone per series name, e.g. `{ Errors: "danger" }`. Series without an entry cycle through chart-1..5.

props.name: valueFormatter
props.description: Formats y ticks, sizes and tooltips (and x when `xFormatter` is not set).

props.name: xFormatter
props.description: Formats x ticks, x values in tooltips and in the data table.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the chart image. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` names it; an auto-generated summary is only the fallback when strict mode is off.

props.name: title
props.description: Visible heading above the plot. It also names the chart when `label` is not set.

props.name: description
props.description: Visible description under the title. The image points to it with `aria-describedby`, next to the generated summary.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown (as role="img") when there is no valid point.

props.name: loading
props.description: Show a busy placeholder (`role="status"`, `aria-busy`) with `loadingText` instead of the chart.

props.name: loadingText
props.description: Message of the loading placeholder.

props.name: width
props.description: ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px).

props.name: height
props.description: ViewBox height. Overrides `size` (default height 280).

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element (`<figure>`).

a11y: The plot is one `<svg role="img">` named by `label` (or `title`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`) and described by the visible `description` and a generated text summary (point and series counts, x and y ranges, trend equations, skipped points).
A visually hidden data table follows the chart with one row per point (label, x, y and size), so every value is readable as text; it is cut at 200 rows and says so in its caption.
Series are told apart by marker shape (and by dash pattern when connected), not by colour alone; the HTML legend repeats the shapes. A trend line is dotted and listed in the legend.
Each marker has a native `<title>` tooltip with the series, label, x, y and size. Individual points are not tab stops: the data table is the keyboard and screen reader alternative.

Axis text is 12px with tabular figures and the SVG is sized to its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px), so labels keep their size and thin out instead of overflowing at 320px. Tick labels are kept inside the viewBox.

In forced-colors mode markers, lines and trend lines use the system text colour; shapes and dash patterns carry the series. The loading placeholder is a polite `role="status"` region marked busy; it does not animate.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
Throws a ContractError when `points` is not an array or an entry has a non-numeric `x` or `y`. An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.
llmNotes: Pass `points` as flat `{ x, y }` objects and group them with `series`, never as nested arrays per series.
Always set `label` (or `title`) to say what the chart shows, and `xTitle` / `yTitle` with the units.
Use `variant="bubble"` only when a third number matters and give every point a `size`; use `connected` only for points that have an order.
Leave `markerShape` on `series` when there is more than one series, so series do not differ by colour alone.
Use `trend` for a straight-line relation; it needs at least two different x values per series.
Provide `valueFormatter` and `xFormatter` for units and currency. Size with `class` and `size`, not `width` / `height`.

components.name: Sparkline
components.summary: Tiny inline trend (pure SVG) as a line, area, bar or win/loss strip, for tables, KPI tiles and lists.
components.description: Use `Sparkline` to show the shape of a short series next to a number. It has no axes, grid or tooltips: use `LineChart` when readers need values. The rendered size is controlled with `class` (default `w-24`, height follows the viewBox aspect ratio); `width`/`height` only set the viewBox proportions. `variant` picks the form: `line`, `area`, `bar` (one bar per value from a zero baseline) or `winloss` (equal squares above the centre line for positive values, below it for negative ones; a short tick on the line for zero). NaN, Infinity and null values become gaps, a single point is drawn as a dot and a flat series is a horizontal line.

props.name: data
props.description: Series values. Non-finite entries are skipped (gap in the line).

props.name: tone
props.description: Colour token of the line, area and dots. Unknown values fall back to chart-1.

props.name: variant
props.description: Form of the sparkline. `line` and `area` join the points (see `curve`); `bar` draws a bar per value from a zero baseline; `winloss` draws equal squares above (positive) or below (negative) a centre line. When omitted, `area` decides between `line` and `area`.

props.name: area
props.description: Soft fill under the line. Same as `variant="area"`; `variant` wins when both are set.

props.name: curve
props.description: How `line` and `area` join points: straight, a monotone smooth curve that never overshoots the data, or steps. Ignored by `bar` and `winloss`.

props.name: size
props.description: Rendered width: `w-16`, `w-24` or `w-32`. `class` overrides it.

props.name: negativeTone
props.description: Colour token of negative values in `bar` and `winloss`. Position below the baseline is the primary cue; colour only repeats it.

props.name: strokeWidth
props.description: Line width in viewBox units. Invalid values fall back to the default.

props.name: width
props.description: ViewBox width (aspect ratio only; size the element with `class`).

props.name: height
props.description: ViewBox height.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label of the image. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`); an auto-generated summary of the numbers is only the fallback when strict mode is off.

props.name: showLast
props.description: Emphasise the last value with a dot (`line` and `area` only).

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; use it to set the rendered size (`w-32`).

a11y: Renders `<svg role="img">` with an automatic `aria-label` summary (point count, first/last value, min and max); override with `label`.

Empty data is announced as "No data". The `winloss` variant is announced as "Wins and losses: N wins, N losses, N even" and shows the sign by position (above or below the centre line), not by colour; `bar` negatives sit below a visible baseline.
It is a small inline image (default `w-24`) that never widens its container; put several in a `flex-wrap` row so a phone does not scroll sideways. The trend is always paired with the number in text.
Purely visual: never rely on the sparkline alone to convey a value: show the number next to it.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
Throws a ContractError when `data` is not an array. An empty array draws nothing.
llmNotes: Use Sparkline for inline trends only; use LineChart when axes or tooltips are needed.
Set the rendered size with `class` (`w-32 h-auto`), not with `width`/`height` (those are viewBox units).
Always pair it with the actual number; pass a descriptive `label` when the trend matters.
Use `variant="winloss"` for outcomes per period (pass/fail, up/down), `bar` for discrete counts and `line` or `area` for continuous trends.
Choose `tone` semantically (success for good, danger for bad) rather than decoratively.

components.name: Treemap
components.summary: Hierarchical tile chart: area follows value, tiles are squarified, groups can be shown as nested containers, and every tile is keyboard reachable.
components.description: Use `Treemap` to show how a total splits into parts and parts of parts (disk use by folder, stock by category, spend by team), when the share matters more than the exact value. Tile area is proportional to the value; the layout is squarified so tiles stay close to square, and it is deterministic (same data, same picture). A node with `children` takes the sum of them as its value, a node without children needs a positive number. `variant` chooses flat tinted tiles, nested containers with a header per group, or soft outlined tiles. `colorBy="depth"` paints everything in one `tone` and makes deeper levels denser; `colorBy="series"` gives every top-level group its own chart colour (with a legend). Labels are written only into tiles that are big enough (`labels="auto"`); every tile keeps its full name in `aria-label` and a native tooltip. Do not use it for exact comparison of many values (use `BarChart`), for time series, or for more than a few hundred visible tiles; tiles smaller than 2px are skipped and counted in a message. No drill-down: it is a static picture with a text alternative.

props.name: data
props.description: `{ label, value?, children? }` nodes. A node with children takes the sum of them; a leaf needs a number above zero. Other entries are left out and counted in a message. An empty array shows `emptyText`.

props.name: variant
props.description: `flat` tinted tiles with a seam, `nested` draws every group as a container with a header and puts its tiles inside, `outline` soft tiles with a tone coloured edge.

props.name: size
props.description: Height of the drawing: 200, 300 or 420 (an explicit `height` wins).

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between tiles: 0, 1, 2 or 4 px.

props.name: tone
props.description: Colour token of the tiles with `colorBy="depth"`. Tiles are a 15 to 45 percent tint so the label keeps its contrast.

props.name: colorBy
props.description: `depth` uses `tone` for everything and makes deeper levels denser; `series` gives each top-level group its own chart colour (cycling chart-1 to chart-5, in input order).

props.name: labels
props.description: `auto` writes the label into every tile that is wide and tall enough (long labels are cut with an ellipsis); `none` leaves tiles unlabelled. Names and tooltips are always there.

props.name: showValues
props.description: Print the value under the label when the tile is tall enough and the value fits.

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Legend of the top-level groups. `auto` shows it with `colorBy="series"` and two or more groups.

props.name: maxDepth
props.description: Levels that are drawn, 1 to 8. Deeper nodes are folded into the node at this level, so totals stay right.

props.name: valueFormatter
props.description: Formats values in labels, names, tooltips and the table. Default: grouped number with up to two decimals.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the chart. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.

props.name: title
props.description: Visible heading above the chart; also the name when there is no `label`.

props.name: description
props.description: Visible sentence under the title.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown when there is nothing to draw.

props.name: width
props.description: ViewBox width until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS pixel).

props.name: height
props.description: ViewBox height. Overrides `size`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

a11y: The drawing is an SVG `role="group"` named by `label` (or `title`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`) and described by an automatic summary (item count, top-level groups, total). It is a group, not an image, because its tiles are focusable.
Every tile is `role="img"` with an `aria-label` of its full path, value and share of the total ("Cables / Fibre: 20 (20% of total)"), even when its text label is hidden or cut.

Keyboard: one tile is in the tab order (roving tabindex). Arrow Right/Down move to the next tile, Arrow Left/Up to the previous, Home and End to the first and last, in layout order (largest first). Focus shows a thick ring in the `ring` token, also in forced-colors mode.
The full name of the focused or hovered tile is written below the chart (hidden from assistive technology, which reads the tile name itself). Tiles also carry a native tooltip.
A visually hidden data table lists every group and leaf with its value (first 200 rows). It is the text alternative for the whole chart.

Colour is never the only signal: tiles are labelled, groups have header text, and the table names every item. Tints stay at 45 percent or less so the foreground label keeps its contrast in light and dark.
There is no motion. The SVG scales to its container (1 unit = 1 CSS pixel) so labels keep their real size and nothing overflows at 320px.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `label`, `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
Throws a ContractError when `data` is not an array of nodes. An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.
llmNotes: Pass `data` as `{ label, value?, children? }`; give leaves a positive number, never give a group a `value` (it is the sum of its children).
Always set `label` or `title`; label values and units with `valueFormatter`.
Use `variant="nested"` when groups matter, `flat` for a plain share picture, `outline` on dense pages. Use `colorBy="series"` only when the top-level groups are the story; otherwise keep one tone.
Use `maxDepth` to cut deep trees. Tiny tiles are skipped automatically; do not pre-filter just to keep the picture clean, tell readers where the rest is.
Do not use a treemap for exact comparison, negative values or time series. Use BarChart, LineChart or DonutChart.

components.name: WaterfallChart
components.summary: Dependency-free SVG waterfall chart: a start value, increases and decreases, subtotals and a total, as bars, steps or lollipops, vertical or horizontal, with connectors and a pattern or marker for decreases.
components.description: Use `WaterfallChart` to show how a value gets from one total to another through a series of changes (a budget, a revenue bridge, a stock movement). Pass `items` as `{ label, value?, type? }`: the first item is the `start` by default, the others are `delta`s, and `subtotal` / `total` items show the running total at that point (their `value` is not used). `variant` picks the drawing: `bars` floats a bar between the old and the new level, `steps` draws a staircase of the running total, `lollipop` a stem with a head at the new level. Increases and decreases never differ by colour alone: decreases are hatched (`bars`), dashed (`steps`) or hollow (`lollipop`), values carry a sign (`+30`, `−12` with a real minus sign) and the data table names each bar. `connectors` draws a thin line from the end of one bar to the start of the next at the running total. A running total below zero is drawn below the baseline. Items without a finite value read "n/a" and change nothing. Use `BarChart` for independent categories and `LineChart` for a trend over time.

props.name: items
props.type: { label: string; value?: number | null; type?: 'start' | 'delta' | 'subtotal' | 'total' }[]
props.description: Bars in order. `start` sets the running total (default for the first item), `delta` changes it (default for the others), `subtotal` and `total` show it (their `value` is ignored). A start or delta without a finite value reads "n/a". An empty array shows `emptyText`.

props.name: variant
props.description: `bars` floating bars (decreases hatched), `steps` a staircase of treads and risers (decreases dashed), `lollipop` stems with a head at the new level (increase filled, decrease hollow, total square).

props.name: orientation
props.description: `vertical` puts the bars side by side along the x axis; `horizontal` stacks them as rows with the labels at the start.

props.name: connectors
props.description: Thin dotted lines from the end of each bar to the start of the next, at the running total.

props.name: size
props.description: Chart height 160 / 240 / 320 when vertical, height of a row 24 / 32 / 40 when horizontal (at most 960 in total).

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between neighbouring bars: `sm` is wide bars, `lg` is narrow bars.

props.name: showValues
props.description: Print the change (`+80`, `−25`) or the total at the end of each bar. Labels that do not fit are left out; they are also in the table.

props.name: showGrid
props.description: Gridlines at each tick of the value axis.

props.name: showAxis
props.description: Tick labels, category labels and the zero line.

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Legend of increase, decrease and total with the marking of the variant; `auto` shows it when more than one kind of bar is present.

props.name: positiveTone
props.description: Tone of increases.

props.name: negativeTone
props.description: Tone of decreases.

props.name: totalTone
props.description: Tone of the start, subtotal and total bars.

props.name: valueFormatter
props.description: Formats axis ticks, values and tooltips. Defaults to compact (axis) / grouped (tooltip) numbers.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the chart image. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` names it.

props.name: title
props.description: Visible heading above the chart. It also names the chart when `label` is not set.

props.name: description
props.description: Visible description under the title. The image points to it with `aria-describedby`, next to the generated summary.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown (as role="img") when there are no items.

props.name: loading
props.description: Show a busy placeholder (`role="status"`, `aria-busy`) with `loadingText` instead of the chart.

props.name: loadingText
props.description: Message of the loading placeholder.

props.name: width
props.description: ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px).

props.name: height
props.description: ViewBox height. Overrides `size`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element (`<figure>`).

a11y: The chart is one `<svg role="img">` named by `label` (or `title`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`) and described by the visible `description` and a generated text summary (bar count, start and end level, number of increases and decreases).
A visually hidden data table lists every bar as a row named with its kind ("Refunds (decrease)") with the signed change and the running total, so no number depends on the picture.

Increase and decrease are never told apart by colour alone: decreases are hatched (bars), dashed (steps) or hollow (lollipop), values carry a plus or minus sign, and the legend repeats the markings. Each mark has a native `<title>` tooltip.

The SVG is sized to its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px): category labels are shortened (full text in a tooltip) and thinned when crowded, value labels that do not fit are left out, so nothing overflows at 320px.

In forced-colors mode marks and the hatch use the system text colour; the hatch, dashes and shapes carry the meaning. The loading placeholder is a polite `role="status"` region marked busy; it does not animate.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
Throws a ContractError when `items` is not an array, an item has no `label`, an unknown `type`, or a `start` / `delta` has no numeric `value`. An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.
llmNotes: Pass `items` in order: the opening value first, then the changes (negative numbers for decreases), then `{ label, type: "total" }`; do not compute running totals yourself.
Use `type: "subtotal"` for an intermediate sum and `type: "total"` for the closing bar; their `value` is ignored.
Set `label` (or `title`) to say what the bridge shows and use `valueFormatter` for currency or units; `showValues` prints signed changes.
Use `variant="steps"` or `"lollipop"` for many items, `orientation="horizontal"` for long labels.
Keep the default tones (increase `success`, decrease `danger`, total `primary`) unless the data has a different meaning; the hatch, dash and hollow head carry the sign regardless of tone.
Size with `class`, `size` and `gap`, not `width` / `height`.
