components.name: ChatMessage
components.summary: One chat message with a role, a bubble, plain or card surface, an avatar, a header, a status written as text and hover or focus actions.
components.description:
Use `ChatMessage` for each turn in a conversation: a person writing, a reply, a system notice or a tool result. It knows nothing about who the participants are (no vendor or model is baked in) and renders whatever you put in the default slot, or a `markdown` string through the library `Markdown` component. Put messages in a `ChatThread` for the scrolling log, follow behaviour and announcements.

**Role** (`user`, `assistant`, `system`, `tool`) picks the colours and the default side (`user` sits at the end, the rest at the start). Role is also spoken: a visually hidden phrase ("You said", "Assistant said", "System message", "Tool result") is placed before the content, so it is not carried by alignment or colour alone. Set `role-label` to name the speaker ("Ada said").

**Status** is text with an icon where one fits: `sending`, `sent`, `error` (failed to send) and `streaming` (responding). The text is not a live region by default, because a thread of fifty messages would announce all of them; let `ChatThread` summarise, or set `live` for a single stand-alone message.

**Actions** (copy, retry) sit in the `actions` slot. They fade in on hover and when anything inside the message has focus, they are always visible on touch screens and in forced-colors mode, and they stay in the tab order and the accessibility tree while faded, so a keyboard or screen reader user never loses them.

**Markdown** goes through the same sanitising renderer as `Markdown`: raw HTML is never parsed, `javascript:` links and unsafe image sources are dropped, external links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Remote images are shown as links, not loaded, unless you set `show-images`. Inline `data:` pictures are shown.

props.name: role
props.description: Author kind. Sets the surface colours, the default side and the hidden speaker phrase. Unknown values fall back to `assistant`.

props.name: variant
props.description: `bubble` is a tinted box, `plain` has no box (transcripts, wide text), `card` is a bordered panel. Unknown values fall back to `bubble`.

props.name: align
props.description: Side of the thread. Defaults to `end` for `user` and `start` otherwise; sets `data-align`. The row uses logical direction, so it mirrors in right-to-left. Unknown values use the default.

props.name: name
props.description: Participant or tool name shown in the header.

props.name: datetime
props.description: When the message was sent. A valid value renders `<time datetime>` with the ISO string; an invalid value is ignored.

props.name: timeLabel
props.description: Visible time text that replaces the formatted time ("Just now"). Shown as plain text when `datetime` is missing or invalid.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale for the formatted time. A bad value falls back to the runtime default.

props.name: timeZone
props.description: IANA time zone for the formatted time, for example `UTC`. Set it when the page is server-rendered so both renders print the same text. A bad value falls back to local time.

props.name: roleLabel
props.description: Visually hidden speaker phrase read before the content ("Ada said"). A trailing colon is added for you. Defaults to a phrase for the role.

props.name: status
props.description: Delivery or generation state, written as text ("Sending", "Sent", "Failed to send", "Responding"). `sending` and `streaming` set `aria-busy` on the message. Unknown values show nothing.

props.name: statusLabel
props.description: Status text that replaces the default, for translation or a more specific message ("Could not reach the server").

props.name: live
props.description: Make the status text a polite `role="status"` region. Leave off inside a `ChatThread`.

props.name: markdown
props.description: Markdown source rendered with `Markdown` (size sm, streaming-aware while `status="streaming"`). Wins over the default slot, an empty string renders an empty body.

props.name: showImages
props.description: Load http(s) images found in `markdown`. Off by default: they become links.

props.name: as
props.description: Root element, for example `li` inside a list or `article`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: default
slots.description: Message content. Ignored when `markdown` is set.

slots.name: avatar
slots.description: Avatar or icon beside the message. Decorative unless it carries text; the hidden role phrase already names the speaker.

slots.name: header
slots.description: Replaces the default header (name and time).

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Copy, retry or other buttons. Every control needs an accessible name.

a11y: The speaker is named in text, not by side or colour: a visually hidden phrase ("You said", "Assistant said", "System message", "Tool result", or `role-label`) comes first in the content.
A valid `datetime` renders a native `<time datetime>`; the visible text can be changed with `time-label`.

Status is visible text (plus an icon for `error` and `sent`). It is not a live region unless `live` is set, so a thread does not announce every message; `ChatThread` owns one polite summary region. `sending` and `streaming` set `aria-busy`.

Actions are ordinary buttons that fade in on `:hover` and `:focus-within`. They are never `display: none` or `visibility: hidden`, so they keep their place in the tab order and the accessibility tree; touch (coarse pointer) and forced-colors modes show them all the time. Every control needs an accessible name.

Markdown output uses real lists, headings, links and code; external links announce that they open in a new tab. Long words and URLs wrap; code scrolls inside its own region, so the message reflows at 320px.

The row uses logical properties and a reversed flex direction, so `dir="rtl"` mirrors it. Bubble surfaces get a transparent border that forced-colors mode draws. Colour pairs are the ones the contrast test covers.
requires: Throws a ContractError when a button, link or `role="button"` element in the `actions` slot has no accessible name (give icon-only buttons an `aria-label`).
llmNotes: Use `role` for who wrote it and keep the default `role-label` unless a name reads better ("Ada said"); never rely on alignment or colour to say who spoke.
Give every icon-only control in the `actions` slot an `aria-label`; use `IconButton` with `label`.
Pass streamed Markdown through `markdown` with `status="streaming"`; do not build HTML strings and never use `v-html`.
Leave `live` off inside a `ChatThread`; the thread announces a short summary instead of each status.
Set `time-zone` (and `locale`) when the page is server-rendered; a `time` element needs a valid `datetime`.
Do not name a vendor or a model in the component; pass names through `name` and `role-label`.

components.name: ChatThread
components.summary: Scrolling conversation log that follows the latest message, with day separators, a typing indicator, a jump button, older-message loading and one polite announcement region.
components.description:
Use `ChatThread` around `ChatMessage` items. It is a labelled, focusable `role="log"` scroll region. Give the root a height (`class="h-96"`, or let a flex parent size it); the log fills it and scrolls.

**Two ways to fill it.** Pass `messages` and draw each one in the `message` slot (day separators, unread count and announcements need the data), or put `ChatMessage` elements in the default slot for a short, static transcript.

**Follow.** While the reader is at the bottom, new and growing messages keep the view at the bottom. Scrolling up stops following and shows a "Jump to latest" button (with the number of messages that arrived meanwhile). The button is a normal focusable button; using it scrolls down, resumes following and moves focus back to the log. `follow-change` reports the state.

**Announcements.** The log is `aria-live="off"`, so assistive technology never reads a streamed reply token by token. A single sibling `role="status"` region carries a short summary ("2 new messages", or the typing label when it appears), collected for one second so a burst is one sentence, and cleared after a few seconds. Set `announcement` to supply your own text. Nothing is announced for the first render or for older messages added at the top.

**Days.** `item-date` (a property name or a function) groups messages by calendar day in `time-zone`; labels use `Intl` in `locale` and say "Today" and "Yesterday" once mounted. All rows are rendered, which is fine for thousands of simple messages; for very large histories load older pages with `load-older` instead of rendering everything.

Attributes you pass (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `id`, `data-*`) land on the log element; `class` and `style` land on the root.

props.name: messages
props.description: Messages as data, each drawn by the `message` slot. `null` counts as empty. Omit it to use the default slot.

props.name: itemKey
props.type: string | ((item: T, index: number) => string | number)
props.description: Stable key per message (property name or function). Needed to tell appended from prepended messages and for stable DOM. Defaults to the index.

props.name: itemDate
props.type: string | ((item: T, index: number) => string | number | Date)
props.description: When a message was sent, for day separators (property name or function). Items without a valid date join the day before them. Without it there are no separators.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the log. Required: set `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: follow
props.description: Stay at the bottom while the reader is at the bottom; scrolling up stops it and shows the jump button. Off makes a plain scrolling list with no button.

props.name: typing
props.description: Show the typing or streaming indicator (text plus a dot that pulses only without reduced motion). Sets `aria-busy` and announces once when it appears.

props.name: density
props.description: Spacing between messages and around the thread. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: canLoadOlder
props.description: More history exists: shows the load-older control above the first message.

props.name: loadingOlder
props.description: A load is running: disables the control and blocks repeated requests.

props.name: autoLoadOlder
props.description: Also emit `load-older` once when the reader scrolls to the top. It fires again only after `loadingOlder` ends or `canLoadOlder` changes, so it cannot loop.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale for day labels. A bad value falls back to the runtime default.

props.name: timeZone
props.description: IANA time zone that decides which day a message belongs to (local when omitted or invalid).

props.name: now
props.description: The current time, for "Today" and "Yesterday". Defaults to the clock after mount (so a server render prints plain dates); pass it for tests or server rendering.

props.name: announcement
props.description: Text to announce politely (collected for one second) instead of the automatic "N new messages". Use it with the default slot, which cannot be counted.

props.name: labels
props.description: Replace any built-in text: `jump`, `unread(count)`, `loadOlder`, `loadingOlder`, `typing`, `empty`, `newMessages(count)`. Use it to translate.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge on the root; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: default
slots.description: Static `ChatMessage` elements, used when `messages` is not set.

slots.name: message
slots.props: { message: T; index: number; id: string | number }
slots.description: Draws one message from `messages`. Required when `messages` is set.

slots.name: empty
slots.description: Shown when there are no messages (default "No messages yet").

slots.name: typing
slots.description: Replaces the typing indicator content.

slots.name: load-older
slots.description: Replaces the load-older button. Call `load` to emit `load-older`.

slots.name: day
slots.description: Replaces the text of a day separator. `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`.

emits.name: load-older
emits.description: More history is wanted: the button was pressed, or the top was reached with `autoLoadOlder`.

emits.name: follow-change
emits.description: The reader started or stopped following the latest message.

a11y: The log is one element with `role="log"`, `tabindex="0"` and a required accessible name, so keyboard users can scroll it: arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down scroll natively; Home and End jump to the first and last message (and End resumes following).

`aria-live="off"` keeps screen readers from reading the log as it grows. One sibling `role="status"` region announces a short summary at most once per second ("2 new messages", the typing label, or `announcement`), is cleared after a few seconds, and never contains message text.

The jump button is an ordinary focusable button after the log. Pressing it scrolls to the latest message, resumes following and returns focus to the log, so focus is never lost when the button disappears.

Day separators are text (`<time datetime>` with a localised label) between two rules drawn as borders, so they survive forced-colors mode. The typing indicator is text; its dot pulses only under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` and only while the indicator is shown.
Scrolling is instant, with no smooth-scroll animation. The thread is `min-w-0` and wraps, so it reflows at 320px; spacing uses logical properties and mirrors in right-to-left.
Message actions inside the log are ordinary buttons in the tab order; the log does not trap focus.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the log has no accessible name (`label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
Throws a ContractError when `messages` is set but there is no `message` slot to draw each item.
llmNotes: Always name the thread with `label` and give the root a height (`class="h-96"`), otherwise nothing scrolls.
Use `messages` with a `message` slot and set `item-key` to a stable id, so appended and prepended messages are told apart; set `item-date` for day separators.
Do not add your own live region and never put streamed text in `announcement`; the thread announces counts only.
Use `follow-change` to show your own state; do not scroll the log by hand (call the exposed `scrollToBottom()` if you must).
Emit-driven history: set `can-load-older`, handle `load-older`, toggle `loading-older`, then prepend items with keys that are not reused.
Pass `time-zone` and `now` when server rendering, so the first client render matches the server render.

components.name: CodeBlock
components.summary: Monospace code panel with copy button, line numbers, titled header and terminal frames, filename header and tabs, diff marks and line highlighting.
components.description: Use `CodeBlock` to show snippets, commands and config. It is plain monospace text: there is NO syntax highlighting and no dependency on a highlighter. Pass the source via `code` (preferred: exact whitespace) or as plain slot text (the Vue template compiler condenses whitespace in templates, so multi-line slot text loses indentation). Variations: `variant="default"` plain panel for docs; `variant="window"` plain panel that always shows the titled header bar; `variant="terminal"` the same header on an inverted console surface for shell sessions (neither draws window dots); `filename` shows the file name in the header (use it for config/source files); `tabs` (+ `v-model:activeTab`) shows several files in one block (install per package manager, multi-file examples); `diff` renders unified-diff lines (`+` added, `-` removed, `@@` hunk) with coloured backgrounds and a gutter marker; `highlight-lines` emphasises chosen lines (`[2, 4]` or `"1,3-5"`). All combine with `line-numbers`, `wrap`, `max-height`. Add `language` for the header label, `line-numbers` for a gutter, `wrap` to wrap long lines and `max-height` to cap tall blocks (the block scrolls). For a short inline value with a copy button use `DescriptionItem copyable`; for inline code in prose use the typography `Code` component.

props.name: code
props.description: Source text. When omitted the default slot text is used.

props.name: language
props.description: Header label and `data-language`. No highlighting is applied.

props.name: variant
props.description: Frame: plain panel, `window` (always shows the titled header bar with the file name), `terminal` (the same header on an inverted console surface), `plain` (no frame or fill, for use inside another surface) or `flush` (full-bleed, top and bottom rules only). No variant draws window dots. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size: `sm` 12px, `md` 14px, `lg` 16px. The line-number gutter, diff markers and header follow. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: filename
props.description: File name in the header, left-aligned. In `window`/`terminal` it replaces the language label; in `default` it is shown before the language label. Also the default accessible name of the code region.

props.name: tabs
props.description: `{ label: string; code: string; id?: string; language?: string }[]`. Renders a tablist and shows the active tab code; overrides `code`/slot. Invalid entries are ignored.

props.name: activeTab
props.description: `v-model:activeTab`. Id (or label) of the active tab; defaults to the first tab. Unknown ids fall back to the first tab.

props.name: diff
props.description: Unified-diff styling: `+` lines green, `-` lines red (the marker char moves to an aria-hidden gutter and screen readers get "Added:/Removed:"), `@@` lines muted. Copy keeps the original text including `+`/`-`.

props.name: highlightLines
props.description: 1-based lines to emphasise: `[2, 4]` or `"1,3-5"`. Invalid tokens are ignored, ranges are clamped to the line count.

props.name: lineNumbers
props.description: Show a line-number gutter (excluded from copy and selection).

props.name: wrap
props.description: Wrap long lines instead of scrolling horizontally.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: CSS length (e.g. `16rem`). Content scrolls vertically beyond it.

props.name: copyable
props.description: Show the copy button.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the scrollable code region. Defaults to `filename`, else `"<language> code"`, else `"Code"`. Give blocks on one page distinct names so the regions are distinguishable.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: default
slots.description: Plain text source used when `code` is not set.

emits.name: copy
emits.description: Emitted after the code was copied to the clipboard.

emits.name: update:activeTab
emits.description: The active tab changed (`v-model:activeTab`).

a11y: The scrollable `pre` is focusable (`tabindex=0`, shared focus ring) and is a `role="region"` named by `label`, the file name or `"<language> code"`, so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys. Give blocks on one page distinct names.
Line numbers are `aria-hidden` and `select-none`, so they are neither read out nor copied.
The copy button is named "Copy code" and keeps that name; the result ("Code copied" or "Copy failed") is announced by a sibling `role="status"` element. It is a 24px target.
Tabs follow the ARIA tabs pattern: `tablist`/`tab`/`tabpanel`, roving tabindex, Arrow/Home/End keys; the panel is labelled by the active tab.

Diff markers are `aria-hidden`; added/removed lines get an sr-only "Added:"/"Removed:" prefix and highlighted lines an sr-only "Highlighted:" prefix, so neither relies on colour. Highlight is a background tint, never an edge stripe.

`plain` and `flush` change only the surface (`window` and `terminal` additionally force the header bar); `size` changes text size only, so the contrast pairs stay the same as the default. The `flush` rules and the focus ring stay visible in forced-colors mode.
The header is plain text on a bar: no window dots. Header text is 12px at full contrast. Long lines scroll inside the region (or wrap with `wrap`), so the page never scrolls sideways.
llmNotes: Pass code via the `code` prop (not slot) when it contains indentation or blank lines.
Do not expect syntax highlighting; do not add a highlighter dependency.
Use `max-height` for long listings instead of overflow classes on a wrapper.
Content is rendered as text, never as HTML.
Use `variant="window"|"terminal"` for showcase/shell snippets, `filename` for files, `tabs` for multi-file or per-package-manager snippets.
Use `diff` only with unified-diff text (+/-/@@ prefixes); use `highlight-lines` to point at lines in normal code.
Tabs: pass `code` inside each tab; give tabs stable `id`s when using `v-model:activeTab`.
replaces: hand-rolled CodeBlock markup in app code

components.name: CodeViewer
components.summary: Read-only code viewer with built-in tokenizers for JSON, YAML, Go, TOML and shell, foldable regions, line numbers, line highlighting and a copy button.
components.description:
Use `CodeViewer` to display code or config that people read, scan and copy: config files, API payloads, scripts. It is the engine behind `YamlViewer` and `GoViewer`. Highlighting is done by small pure-TypeScript tokenizers (no highlighter dependency) and uses only semantic tokens: keywords and keys `text-primary`, strings `text-success`, numbers and types `text-info`, comments `text-muted-foreground`, functions and constants `text-foreground font-medium`.

Folding regions are computed per language: indentation for YAML, tables and brackets for TOML, brackets for JSON and Go (functions, structs, `import (...)`, `const (...)`, switch blocks), brackets plus `if/fi`, `do/done`, `case/esac` for shell, and multi-line block comments. Folded lines are not rendered at all, so folding a large file is cheap; sources above 400 visible lines also use `content-visibility: auto` per row.

Use `CodeBlock` instead for short snippets in prose (tabs, diff marks, terminal frame, no folding), `JsonViewer` to explore a live JS value as a tree, and `YamlViewer` / `GoViewer` when you want to pass a JS value rather than text. This is not an editor: there is no cursor, selection model or editing.

Parts (all carry `data-slot`): `code-viewer`, `code-viewer-header`, `code-viewer-title`, `code-viewer-scroll`, `code-viewer-code`, `code-viewer-line`, `code-viewer-gutter`, `code-viewer-fold-cell`, `code-viewer-fold`, `code-viewer-line-number`, `code-viewer-text`, `code-viewer-token`, `code-viewer-placeholder`, plus the shared `copy-button` and `copy-button-status`. Exposed methods: `expandAll()` and `collapseAll()`.

props.name: source
props.description: The text to show; required, but an empty string is valid. LF, CRLF and lone CR line endings are accepted; one trailing newline is ignored. The copy button copies this exact string.

props.name: language
props.description: Tokenizer and folding rules. Unknown values render as `plain` (no colours, no folds).

props.name: filename
props.description: Shown in the header and used as the accessible name of the code region. Set `filename` or `label`: one of them is required, so viewers on one page have distinct names.

props.name: lineNumbers
props.description: Show a line-number gutter. It is `aria-hidden`, not selectable and uses `tabular-nums`, so copying selects clean code.

props.name: foldable
props.description: Show fold toggles for the regions the language defines.

props.name: defaultFoldDepth
props.description: Regions nested this deep (0 = outermost) or deeper start folded. Unset starts fully expanded. Changing `source` or `language` resets the folds.

props.name: highlightLines
props.description: Lines to mark, by displayed number: `[2, 5]` or `"3-5,9"`. Reversed ranges are swapped, ranges are clamped to the visible lines and invalid parts are ignored. Marked lines get a bar on the start edge, a tint and visually hidden text "Highlighted line".

props.name: startLine
props.description: Number shown for the first line, for excerpts. Fold names and `highlightLines` use the displayed numbers. Values below 1 or non-numbers fall back to 1.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Wrap long lines (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) instead of scrolling sideways.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: CSS length such as `20rem`. The code scrolls vertically beyond it.

props.name: copy
props.description: Show the copy button with a status live region.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size: 12px, 14px or 16px. Rows stay at least 24px tall (28px for `lg`) so fold toggles keep a 24px target. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: variant
props.description: `bordered` is a bordered card surface; `plain` has no frame so the viewer can sit inside another surface; `flush` is full-bleed with top and bottom rules only. Unknown values fall back to `bordered`.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the code region. Required unless `filename` is set; give viewers on the same page distinct names.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

emits.name: copy
emits.description: The source was copied to the clipboard.

emits.name: fold
emits.payload: [event: { start: number; end: number; collapsed: boolean }]
emits.description: A region was folded or unfolded. `start` and `end` are the displayed line numbers of the region.

a11y: The code is a scroll region: `role="region"`, `tabindex="0"` and an `aria-label` from `label`, else `filename`, else "<Language> source". Keyboard users reach it with Tab and scroll with the arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down; it reflows at 320px with scrolling only inside the region.

Fold toggles are real `<button>` elements with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` (the code list) and a name such as "Fold lines 3 to 9". Tab to reach them, Enter or Space to toggle. Targets are 24px, 44px on coarse pointers.
A folded region shows a "… N lines" button (plain text, with an accessible name such as "6 lines hidden. Unfold lines 3 to 9"). Activating it unfolds and returns focus to the fold toggle.

Line numbers are `aria-hidden` and `user-select: none`, so selecting and copying yields clean code. The copy button has a fixed name ("Copy code") and a sibling `role="status"` announces "Code copied" or "Copy failed".
`size` changes text size only; rows keep a 24px minimum height so fold toggles stay 24px targets (44px on coarse pointers). `flush` keeps its top and bottom rules in forced-colors mode.

Highlighted lines use a start-edge bar and visually hidden "Highlighted line" text in addition to the tint. Borders are kept for forced-colors mode; fold buttons keep a transparent border that becomes visible there. No animation is used, so reduced motion needs no special handling.
requires: Throws a ContractError when neither `filename` nor `label` is set, so the code region has a distinct name.
Throws a ContractError when `source` is not passed as a string. An empty string is valid content.
llmNotes: Use CodeViewer for read-only display of JSON, YAML, Go, TOML or shell text with folding and highlighting. It is not an editor.
Use CodeBlock for short snippets inside prose, tabs, diffs and terminal sessions; use JsonViewer to explore a JS value as a tree.
Pass the exact text in `source` (a prop, not slot text) so whitespace survives. For a JS value use YamlViewer or GoViewer.
Always set `filename` or `label` so the scroll region has a distinct accessible name when a page shows several viewers.
Do not hard-code colours around it: token colours come from semantic tokens. Override layout with `class` only.
Use `default-fold-depth` to open long files collapsed; use `start-line` for excerpts and `highlight-lines` with displayed numbers.
Unknown `language` falls back to plain text. Tokenizers are line oriented and approximate: they do not validate the syntax.

components.name: DiffViewer
components.summary: Read-only diff of two texts or a unified diff string, in unified, split or inline layout, with word highlights, folded unchanged lines and change-to-change navigation.
components.description: Use `DiffViewer` to show what changed between two versions of a text: a config file, a document, generated output, a pull request excerpt. Pass `oldText` and `newText` (the viewer computes the diff in the browser with a Myers line diff and a word diff inside changed lines) or a `patch` string in unified diff format. `variant` is `unified` (default, one column), `split` (old and new side by side; below `splitMinWidth` of the viewer's own width it renders as unified) or `inline` (a changed line is one row with removed and added words marked in place). Added and removed lines carry a "+" or "-" marker, a distinct edge and hidden text, and changed words use underline and strike-through as well as a tint, so colour is never the only signal. Unchanged lines between changes fold behind "N unchanged lines" buttons. Long diffs render only the rows in view. All text is rendered as text, never as HTML. It is not an editor and does not merge or apply changes.

props.name: oldText
props.description: The original text. A missing side counts as an empty text.

props.name: newText
props.description: The changed text.

props.name: patch
props.description: A unified diff (`git diff` output, one or several files). When it is not blank it is shown instead of `oldText` and `newText`. Lines between hunks are not in a patch, so they cannot be revealed. A "\ No newline at end of file" line is ignored. Text that is not a diff shows a message instead.

props.name: label

props.name: variant

props.name: size

props.name: wrap
props.description: Wrap long lines inside the viewer instead of scrolling sideways.

props.name: lineNumbers
props.description: Show the line number columns (old and new in unified and inline, one per side in split).

props.name: collapse
props.description: Fold unchanged lines between changes. `false` shows them all.

props.name: context
props.description: Unchanged lines kept around each change. Changes closer than twice this value share one hunk. Ignored for `patch`.

props.name: copy
props.description: Show the copy button. It copies the diff as unified text (the `patch` itself when one is given).

props.name: oldLabel

props.name: newLabel
props.description: Heading of the new side.

props.name: splitMinWidth
props.description: Width of the viewer in px under which `split` renders as `unified`. It is measured on the viewer, not on the viewport, so a narrow column on a wide screen falls back too.

props.name: height
props.description: Fixed height of the scrolling area (px or any CSS length).

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Largest height of the scrolling area. Without `height` or `maxHeight` the area stops at 24rem.

props.name: maxCost
props.description: Largest edit distance the line diff searches. Beyond it the viewer settles for an approximate result and says so in a visible note.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: empty
slots.description: Shown when there is nothing to show (identical texts or an unreadable patch). Defaults to "No differences." or a message about the patch.

emits.name: hunk

a11y: The diff is a `<table>` with a visually hidden caption (the `label`) inside a scroll region (`role="region"`, `tabindex="0"`, named by `label`), so keyboard users reach it with Tab and scroll with the arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down. It reflows at 320px: wide lines scroll inside the region, or wrap with `wrap`.

Added, removed and changed lines have a "+", "-" or "~" marker plus visually hidden "Added", "Removed", "Changed" or "Unchanged" text, and a distinct start edge (solid for added, dashed for removed) that survives forced-colors mode. Changed words are also underlined (added) or struck through (removed), so tint is never the only signal. Line numbers and marker glyphs are `aria-hidden` and not selectable, so copying yields clean text.

Press n for the next change and p for the previous one while the diff area has focus (also the "Next change" and "Previous change" buttons). Focus moves to the hunk header, the current one is highlighted, and a polite `role="status"` says "Change 2 of 5". Navigation wraps around.

Each fold is a button with the visible text "N unchanged lines" and the name "Expand N unchanged lines" (`aria-expanded="false"`). It reveals up to 100 lines and keeps focus on the next fold button, or on the diff area when nothing is left to reveal. Targets are 24px or more, 44px on coarse pointers.

Long diffs (over 400 rows) render only the rows near the viewport with `aria-rowcount` and `aria-rowindex`; the spacer rows are `aria-hidden`. `split` falls back to unified from the width of the viewer itself, not the viewport. No animation is used, so reduced motion needs no special handling.
requires: Throws a ContractError when no accessible name is given (`label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`), so the diff region has a distinct name.
Throws a ContractError when none of `oldText`, `newText` or `patch` is passed as a string. An empty string is valid.
llmNotes: Use DiffViewer to compare two versions of a text. Use CodeViewer to show one text, and do not use it as an editor or merge tool.
Pass the exact texts as props (`old-text`, `new-text`) so whitespace survives, or a `patch` string for ready-made unified diffs.
Always set `label` so the diff region has a distinct accessible name when a page shows several diffs.
Choose `variant="split"` for wide containers and `unified` for narrow ones; `split` already falls back by itself below `split-min-width`.
Keep `collapse` on for long files. The line diff is approximate beyond `max-cost` and the viewer says so; do not raise the cost for very different 10k-line files.
Never pass HTML: all content is rendered as text. Override layout with `class`, not colours.
replaces: hand-rolled diff table markup in app code

components.name: GoViewer
components.summary: Read-only Go viewer: show Go source with highlighting and folds, or render a JS value as a Go composite literal.
components.description:
Use `GoViewer` to display Go code that people read and copy: handlers, type definitions, examples in docs, or a JS value as a ready-to-paste `map[string]any{...}` literal. Pass `source` for Go text (it wins) or `value` for a JS value rendered by the built-in `goLiteral`. It is a `CodeViewer` with the Go tokenizer, so every `CodeViewer` prop works except `language`.

Highlighted: keywords, predeclared types (`string`, `int64`, `error`, `any`, `byte`, `rune`...), builtins when called (`make`, `len`, `append`, `panic`...), constants (`nil`, `true`, `false`, `iota`), interpreted and raw strings (also across lines), runes, `//` and `/* */` comments including `//go:build` and `//nolint` directives, every number form (hex, octal, binary, underscores, floats, hex floats, imaginary), operators (`:=`, `<-`, `...`, `&^` and the compound forms), function names (after `func` and before `(`), type names (after `type` and in `type (...)` blocks), the package name and import paths, and struct tags in backticks. Folding covers functions, `type` and `struct` and `interface` blocks, `import (...)`, `const (...)` and `var (...)`, `switch` and `select` blocks, composite literals and multi-line comments.

Rendering a `value`: objects and Maps become `map[string]any{...}`, arrays and Sets `[]any{...}`, `null` and `undefined` `nil`, strings are quoted with Go escapes (multi-line text without backticks becomes a raw literal), dates become their ISO 8601 string, bigint becomes `int64(n)`, `NaN` and infinities become `math.NaN()` and `math.Inf(...)`. Output follows gofmt style: tabs, trailing commas and aligned map values. Numbers are written naturally (`42` is an `int`, `3.5` a `float64` once stored in `any`); `numbers="float64"` writes `float64(42)` the way `encoding/json` decodes. `package="name"` wraps the literal in `package name`, an `import "math"` when needed and `var data = ...`. Circular values show a `// Cannot render ...` comment line in the component; calling `goLiteral` directly throws a `TypeError` that names the path.

This is a viewer, not an editor, and it does not parse Go: highlighting is line oriented and does not validate. Use `CodeViewer` for other languages and `JsonViewer` to explore a live value as a tree.

props.name: source
props.description: Go source text. Takes precedence over `value`, including when it is an empty string.

props.name: value
props.description: Any JS value, rendered as a Go composite literal. Replace it (do not mutate) to update the view. Ignored when `source` is a string. With neither prop the view shows `nil`.

props.name: package
props.description: With `value`: wrap the literal in `package <name>` and `var data = ...`. Invalid identifiers fall back to `main`. No effect with `source`.

props.name: numbers
props.description: With `value`: `natural` writes `42` and `3.5`; `float64` writes `float64(42)` for every number.

props.name: filename
props.description: Header title and accessible name of the code region. Set `filename` or `label`: one of them is required.

props.name: lineNumbers
props.description: Show a non-selectable, `aria-hidden` line-number gutter.

props.name: foldable
props.description: Show fold toggles for functions, types, import and const groups, switch blocks and comments.

props.name: defaultFoldDepth
props.description: Regions nested this deep (0 = outermost) or deeper start folded. Unset starts expanded.

props.name: highlightLines
props.description: Displayed line numbers to mark: `[2, 5]` or `"3-5,9"`. Invalid parts are ignored; ranges are clamped.

props.name: startLine
props.description: Number shown for the first line, for excerpts.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Wrap long lines instead of scrolling sideways.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: CSS length such as `24rem`; the code scrolls vertically beyond it.

props.name: copy
props.description: Show the copy button. It copies the full text, including folded lines.

props.name: variant
props.description: Framed card surface, no frame (`plain`) or full-bleed with top and bottom rules (`flush`). Unknown values fall back to `bordered`.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size: 12px, 14px or 16px. Rows keep a 24px minimum so fold toggles stay 24px targets. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the code region. Required unless `filename` is set.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

a11y: The Go code is a scroll region: `role="region"`, `tabindex="0"`, labelled by `label`, else `filename`, else "Go source". Tab reaches it; arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down scroll it. At 320px width only the region scrolls, never the page.

Fold toggles are `<button>` elements with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and names like "Fold lines 12 to 20". Tab to focus, Enter or Space to toggle. A folded region shows a "… N lines" button that unfolds it and returns focus to the toggle.
Line numbers are `aria-hidden` and `user-select: none`, so selection and copy give clean Go code. Copy has a constant name ("Copy code") and a `role="status"` region announces the result.

Highlighted lines have a start-edge bar and hidden "Highlighted line" text as well as a tint. Targets are at least 24px (44px on coarse pointers); borders keep controls visible in forced-colors mode; nothing animates. Tabs render 4 columns wide.
requires: Throws a ContractError when neither `filename` nor `label` is set.
Throws a ContractError when neither `source` (a string, empty is fine) nor `value` is passed. `value` may be any value, including `null`.
llmNotes: Use GoViewer for read-only Go display, not an editor. It does not parse or compile Go.
Pass Go text in `source` exactly as written (tabs included); pass `value` to show a JS value as a `map[string]any{...}` literal. `source` wins when both are set.
Use `package="name"` only with `value`; it adds `import "math"` automatically when NaN or an infinity appears.
Set `filename` (or `label`) so the scroll region has a distinct accessible name.
Use `default-fold-depth` to open long files as an outline of declarations; use `start-line` for excerpts.
Circular values render a `// Cannot render ...` comment instead of throwing; `goLiteral` itself throws a TypeError.

components.name: YamlViewer
components.summary: Read-only YAML viewer: show raw YAML text or serialise a JS value to YAML, with highlighting, indentation folds, line numbers and copy.
components.description:
Use `YamlViewer` to display YAML that people read and copy: Kubernetes manifests, compose files, CI configs, or a JS value shown as YAML. Pass `source` for raw text (it wins) or `value` for a JS value that is serialised by the built-in `yamlStringify`. It is a `CodeViewer` with the YAML tokenizer, so every `CodeViewer` prop works except `language`.

Highlighted: keys, scalars, numbers, `true`/`false`/`null`/`~`, comments, anchors `&a` and aliases `*a`, merge keys `<<`, tags `!!str`, block scalars `|` and `>` with chomping and indentation indicators, flow collections `[a, b]` and `{k: v}`, quoted strings with escapes (also across lines), multi-document streams (`---`, `...`) and `%YAML` directives. Folding is by indentation, so every mapping or sequence item with children folds, and each document is folded separately.

Serialising a `value`: block style, two or four spaces (`indent`), key order as in the object, strings quoted only when plain text would change meaning (`yes`, `null`, `12`, `a: b`, a leading `-` or `#`), multi-line strings as `|` blocks with the right chomping indicator, empty containers as `{}` and `[]`, `NaN` as `.nan`, infinities as `.inf`, dates as ISO 8601, `undefined`, functions and symbols skipped in maps and written as `null` in lists. Circular values do not throw in the component: it shows a `# Cannot render this value as YAML: ...` comment line. Calling `yamlStringify` directly throws a `TypeError` that names the path of the cycle.

This is a viewer, not an editor, and it does not parse YAML: highlighting is line oriented and does not validate. Use `JsonViewer` to explore a live value as a tree and `CodeViewer` for other languages.

components.description: Use `JsonViewer` to inspect API responses, config objects, logs and debug state. components.description: Use `Card` to frame a self-contained chunk of information (a stat, a form section, a list item with actions). a11y: `selectable` cards expose `role="checkbox"` with `aria-checked`; give them an accessible name (heading text or `aria-label`). Space and Enter toggle, `disabled` sets `aria-disabled` and drops the card from the tab order.
Plain card is a presentational div; add `role="region"` + `aria-labelledby` if it must be a landmark.
`CardMedia` is a plain div: `aria-label` is only valid on it with a role, so a decorative placeholder gets `role="img"` plus a label (or `aria-hidden`), and a real image carries its own `alt`.
No variant uses a gradient, glow, edge stripe or hover movement: a card is a bordered surface; `elevated` and `interactive` only change the shadow and border colour.
A checked `selectable` card keeps a visible keyboard focus indicator: besides the focus ring it draws a 2px solid outline, because its primary ring and border would otherwise hide the ring.
`interactive` only styles the card: render it as `a`/`button` (`as`) so it is focusable and announced correctly.
CardTitle renders an h3; set `as` to match the page heading hierarchy.

llmNotes: Compose Card from its parts; do not hand-roll padding.
Use `variant="interactive"` together with `as="a"` or `as-child`, never on a bare div with @click only.
Use `selectable` (with v-model) for pick-one/pick-many cards instead of wrapping a Card in a checkbox label; do not put `variant="interactive"` and `selectable` together.
For an image on top use `variant="with-image-header"` + `CardMedia` as the first child; for side-by-side use `layout="horizontal"` with `CardMedia` + `CardBody`.
Do not nest Card inside Card; use `variant="outline"` sections or DescriptionList inside CardContent.
Put the single header action in CardAction, not inside CardTitle.

components.name: FlowCanvas
components.summary: Interactive node and edge canvas: drag nodes, connect ports with the pointer or the keyboard, pan, zoom, undo, auto layout and a text alternative, drawn as one SVG with no extra dependency.
components.description:
Use `FlowCanvas` when people build or edit a graph: a workflow, a pipeline, a routing table. For a picture of a graph nobody edits, use `MermaidDiagram` or `NetworkGraph`. Bind `v-model:nodes` (`{ id, label?, x, y, width?, height?, shape?, tone?, ports? }`) and `v-model:edges` (`{ id, from, to, label?, fromPort?, toPort?, style? }`); without a binding the canvas keeps its own copy.

**Interaction.** Drag the background to pan (touch: one finger; two fingers pinch). Zoom with Ctrl or Command plus the wheel, the toolbar or the keys. Drag a node to move it (`grid` snaps). Drag from a port to another node to connect, or click a port and then a node. Shift plus drag, or the "Select area" toggle, draws a selection box. Every one of these has a keyboard path, see the accessibility notes. Undo and redo keep up to `historyLimit` steps.

**Exposed methods** (template ref): `autoLayout()` arranges the nodes with the layered layout of `MermaidDiagram` in `direction`, `fit()`, `zoomIn()`, `zoomOut()`, `zoomTo(n)`, `undo()`, `redo()`, `deleteSelected()`, `selectAll()`, `clearSelection()`, `getViewport()` and `setViewport()`. They also work when `readonly` (the caller asked for them); `readonly` blocks the user only.

**Limits.** No nested groups. Custom nodes go through the `node` slot, which draws SVG in the node's own coordinates (no HTML inside the canvas). Undo works on the data this component changed; edits you make elsewhere are not tracked. With more than 120 nodes only the nodes and connections near the visible area are drawn (300 nodes stay interactive). The canvas keeps left to right coordinates in right to left pages; the toolbar and labels follow the page direction. The canvas captures touch gestures, so scroll the page from outside it.

props.name: nodes
props.description: `v-model:nodes`. `{ id, label?, x, y, width?, height?, shape?, tone?, ports? }`. `x` and `y` are the top-left corner in canvas units; size defaults to 148 by 52; `shape` is any Mermaid node shape; `tone` is neutral, primary, success, info, warning or danger; `ports` defaults to one port per side and `[]` makes the node impossible to connect.

props.name: edges
props.description: `v-model:edges`. `{ id, from, to, label?, fromPort?, toPort?, style? }`. `from` and `to` are node ids, `style` is `solid`, `dashed` or `dotted`. A connection to an unknown node is not drawn and a note says so.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the canvas. Required unless `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.

props.name: readonly
props.description: No editing by the user: nodes cannot be moved, connected, deleted or laid out, ports are hidden, undo and redo are off. Selecting, panning and zooming still work.

props.name: grid
props.description: Snap positions to this many canvas units while dragging and moving by keyboard. `true` is 20. It also sets the spacing of the `dots` and `grid` backgrounds.

props.name: variant
props.description: Background: a flat surface, a dot grid or grid lines. Both patterns move and scale with the canvas and fade out when they would be denser than 6 pixels.

props.name: size
props.description: Height of the canvas: 288, 384 or 512 px (and the gap to the toolbar and list).

props.name: edgeStyle
props.description: Shape of connections: a line, a smooth curve that leaves each port outward, or right angles with rounded corners.

props.name: direction
props.description: Direction of `autoLayout()` and the toolbar button: top to bottom, left to right, bottom to top or right to left.

props.name: toolbar
props.description: Show the toolbar above the canvas (zoom, fit, auto layout, undo, redo, delete, select area). The `toolbar` slot replaces its content.

props.name: minimap
props.description: Show a small overview in the bottom corner with the visible area; press or drag on it to move there. It is a pointer shortcut and hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: minZoom
props.description: Lowest zoom factor, at most 1.

props.name: maxZoom
props.description: Highest zoom factor, at least 1.

props.name: historyLimit
props.description: Most undo steps kept, 1 to 500. Keyboard moves of the same nodes within one second count as one step.

props.name: autoFit
props.description: Fit all nodes into view once, when the canvas first has a size and nodes. Turn it off to keep the canvas origin at the top-left corner.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Text shown while there are no nodes.

slots.name: node
slots.props: { node, selected, active, connecting, width, height }
slots.description: Replaces the label of a node. SVG content in the node's own coordinates (0,0 is its top-left corner); the outline, selection ring and ports stay. Text is rendered as text, never as markup.

slots.name: toolbar
slots.props: { zoom, readonly, canUndo, canRedo, hasSelection, zoomIn, zoomOut, fit, autoLayout, undo, redo, deleteSelected }
slots.description: Replaces the default toolbar content. Use the scoped functions so your buttons share the canvas history.

emits.name: update:nodes
emits.description: The node array changed (move, delete, layout, undo, redo).

emits.name: update:edges
emits.description: The connection array changed (connect, delete, undo, redo).

emits.name: node-move
emits.description: Nodes were moved by drag, keyboard or auto layout. Fires once per gesture with every moved node.

emits.name: connect
emits.description: A connection was made by the pointer or the keyboard.

emits.name: disconnect
emits.description: A connection was removed, including those removed with their node.

emits.name: select
emits.description: The selection changed.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The data changed, with the new arrays.

a11y: The canvas is a `role="application"` element named by `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`) and described by a visually hidden paragraph that states the keyboard model. It is focusable (Tab) and the page keeps its own scrolling outside it.

Keyboard on the canvas: arrow keys pan (Shift for larger steps), + and - zoom, 0 fits the view, Ctrl or Command plus A selects everything, Delete removes the selection, Ctrl or Command plus Z undoes and Shift plus Ctrl or Command plus Z (or Ctrl plus Y) redoes, Escape clears the selection or abandons a drag.

Nodes are `role="button"` elements named by their label with `aria-pressed` for the selection; one node is the tab stop (roving). Arrow keys move focus to the nearest node in that direction, Home and End jump to the first and last in reading order, Enter or Space selects, Shift plus Enter adds to the selection. Alt plus an arrow key moves the selection (by `grid` or 10 units, Shift for 5 times as far); each move is announced.

Connections by keyboard: focus a node and press C. Focus moves to the nearest other node; arrow keys choose a target in that direction, Tab and Shift plus Tab cycle through all targets, Enter or Space confirms, Escape cancels. Every step is announced. With the pointer, a click on a port followed by a click on a node works without dragging.

Connections are `role="button"` elements named "Edge A to B" (plus the label), also one tab stop; arrow keys move between them, Enter selects and Delete removes. A selected node has a dashed outline ring and a selected connection a thicker line, never colour alone; forced-colors mode uses system colours.
One polite `role="status"` region announces moves, connections, deletions, undo, redo, layout and selection counts. Delete reports how many nodes and connections went; Undo and Redo name the step.

A visually hidden list of every node (with its connection count) and every connection ("Edge A to B") is always in the page; "Show as list" reveals it in a focusable, labelled, scrollable region. Lists are cut at 500 entries with a note.

Touch: the canvas sets `touch-action: none` so one finger pans and two fingers pinch; ports have a 24 pixel hit area. Pointer dragging always has a keyboard or click alternative. The page can be scrolled from outside the canvas.

No motion except the user's own pan and zoom. Colours come from tokens; outlines are system colours in forced-colors mode. The toolbar, list and messages follow the page direction (right to left); the canvas itself stays left to right so coordinates and arrow keys keep their meaning.
Labels are text only (never markup) and long labels are wrapped and cut with the full text in a tooltip and in the accessible name.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
Throws a ContractError when `nodes` is not an array. An empty array is valid and shows the empty state.
Throws a ContractError when a node has no `id` (a non-empty string).
Throws a ContractError when two nodes share an `id`.
Throws a ContractError when a node has no numeric `x` and `y`.
Throws a ContractError when `edges` is not an array.
Throws a ContractError when a connection has no `id`, `from` or `to`.
Throws a ContractError when two connections share an `id`.
llmNotes: Always pass `label`, give every node a unique `id` and numeric `x` and `y`, and every connection a unique `id` with `from` and `to` node ids.
Use `v-model:nodes` and `v-model:edges`; handle `connect` or `change` only to react (save, validate), not to re-add what the model already holds.
Do not put HTML or components inside nodes: use the `node` slot with SVG elements, in the node's own coordinates.
Use `readonly` for display. Use `grid` (or `grid="20"`) when tidy alignment matters; use `autoLayout()` on a template ref to arrange imported data with no positions.
Pick `edge-style="orthogonal"` for flowcharts, `curved` for graphs, `straight` for dense maps. Pick `direction` for auto layout, not for display.
Keep `ports` omitted unless the data has named inputs and outputs; then give each port an `id` and reference it with `fromPort` and `toPort`.
For a static picture of a graph use `MermaidDiagram` or `NetworkGraph`; do not use FlowCanvas for charts.
Give the canvas room: it needs a width, and `size` sets its height. Do not wrap it in another scroll container.
replaces: hand-rolled SVG node editors
node-editor libraries for small and medium graphs

components.name: MermaidDiagram
components.summary: Draws Mermaid text (flowchart, sequence, pie, state, entity relationship, class, gantt, mindmap, timeline, journey) as an accessible SVG, with its own parser and layout and no extra dependency.
components.description:
Use `MermaidDiagram` when a diagram lives as text next to the code or content it explains. Pass the Mermaid source in `source`; the component parses it, lays it out (layered layout for graphs, custom layouts for the rest) and draws SVG with design tokens, so light, dark and accent presets work. Everything is drawn by Vue templates: the source is never inserted as HTML, so hostile text stays inert text. A source that cannot be drawn never throws and never leaves a blank area. A syntax error shows an inline alert with the line, the column, the offending source line and what to write instead; an unsupported diagram type shows a message that names the type. Both emit `error`. A diagram that is larger than `maxNodes` or `maxEdges` shows a size message instead of hanging the page. **Supported syntax** - `flowchart` / `graph` (TB TD BT LR RL): shapes rectangle, rounded, stadium, subroutine, cylinder, circle, double circle, rhombus, hexagon, parallelograms, trapezoids and the asymmetric flag (`A[text]`, `A(text)`, `A([text])`, `A[[text]]`, `A[(text)]`, `A((text))`, `A(((text)))`, `A{text}`, `A{{text}}`, `A[/text/]`, `A[\text\]`, `A[/text\]`, `A[\text/]`, `A>text]`, plus `A@{ shape: cyl, label: "text" }` for the common shapes); edges `-->` `---` `-.->` `==>` `--o` `--x` `<-->` `o--o` `x--x` `~~~`, longer arrows (`---->`), labels `-->|text|` and `-- text -->`; chains (`A --> B --> C`) and groups (`A & B --> C & D`); nested `subgraph ... end` with `direction`; `classDef`, `class`, `:::class`, `style`, `linkStyle`; edge ids (`e1@-->`, with `e1@{ animate: true }` lines) are read and ignored; `click` lines are accepted and ignored. - `sequenceDiagram`: `participant` and `actor` with `as` aliases, messages `->>` `-->>` `->` `-->` `-x` `--x` `-)` `--)`, activation (`+` `-`, `activate`, `deactivate`), self messages, `Note left of|right of|over`, `loop` `alt`/`else` `opt` `par`/`and` `critical`/`option` `break` blocks, `autonumber`, `title`. - `pie`: `title`, `showData`, `"Label" : value` lines. - `stateDiagram` / `stateDiagram-v2`: states, `state "text" as id`, `id : description`, transitions with labels, `[*]` start and end, composite states (nested), concurrent regions separated by `--` (side by side with a dashed divider), `<>` `<>` `<>`, `note left of|right of`, `direction`. - `erDiagram`: entities with attributes (type, name, PK FK UK, comment), aliases, relationships with all cardinality marks (`||` `|o` `o|` `}o` `o{` `}|` `|{`) and the word forms, identifying `--` and non-identifying `..` lines, labels. - `classDiagram`: classes with attributes and methods, visibility `+ - # ~`, annotations (`<>`), generics (`Name~T~`), inheritance, composition, aggregation, association, link, dependency, realisation, cardinalities, labels, namespaces, notes. - `gantt`: `title`, `dateFormat`, sections, tasks with ids, `after`, `until`, durations in ms s m h d w (calendar months `M` and years `y` as whole numbers), tags `done` `active` `crit` `milestone`. - `mindmap`: indentation tree with node shapes (square, rounded, circle, bang, cloud, hexagon). - `timeline`: `title`, sections, periods with several events. - `journey`: `title`, sections, tasks with a 1 to 5 score and actors. - `sequenceDiagram`, `stateDiagram`, `erDiagram` and `classDiagram` accept `;` between statements on one line (write `#59;` for a literal semicolon in text). In flowcharts `;` already works outside brackets and quotes. - All types: `%%` comment lines and `%%` comments after a statement (not inside quotes or brackets), `accTitle` and `accDescr` (one line or a `{ }` block), `---` front matter with `title:`, and `%%{init: ...}%%` directives (read and ignored: configure the look with props instead). **Not supported** (it draws what it can, or shows an error that says so): other Mermaid diagram types (git graph, quadrant, xy chart, sankey, block, packet, architecture, kanban, C4, requirement, radar, treemap), icons, images and markdown strings in nodes (`
` breaks a line, other HTML tags are dropped and their text is kept), interactive `click` handlers, themes and custom CSS from the source, `:::` styling beyond tones. **Colour.** The source cannot set arbitrary colours. A `classDef` or `style` fill or stroke colour is mapped to the nearest tone of the design system by hue (red to danger, green to success, blue to info, yellow and orange to warning, teal to primary, greys to neutral); a class named like a tone (`success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `primary`) picks that tone; `tone:success` in a declaration sets it explicitly; `stroke-dasharray` makes the outline dashed and a `stroke-width` of 3px or more makes it thick. Dashes and weight carry meaning, so state is never shown by colour alone. **Size and reflow.** With `fit="width"` (default) the SVG scales down to its container, so on a 320px screen a wide diagram gets small text. `fit="scroll"` keeps the natural size inside a focusable, named, scrollable region. `fit="auto"` measures the container and behaves like `width` until the scale would drop below 0.6 (text of 14px would be under about 8px), then switches to `scroll`; the choice is made after mount, so the server render is always `width`. Use `auto` for content you do not control and `width` for small, known diagrams. Use `Markdown` for prose with code fences, `CodeViewer` to show plain source, and a chart component (`LineChart`, `DonutChart`, `BarChart`) when the data is numeric and should be formatted and interactive.

props.name: source
props.description: Mermaid source text. Required: a blank value throws a ContractError in strict mode (and shows a "Nothing to draw" message otherwise).

props.name: variant
props.description: `outline` bordered nodes on a card, `filled` tinted nodes, `soft` borderless nodes on a muted panel, `mono` single-colour ink with a heavier border (tones are ignored). Unknown values fall back to `outline`.

props.name: size
props.description: Text and spacing scale: 12, 14 and 16 px base text inside the drawing, and the caption and control text around it.

props.name: density
props.description: Space between nodes and ranks, node padding, and the padding of the frame.

props.name: edgeStyle
props.description: How graph edges are drawn: S-curves, straight segments, or right angles with rounded corners. Applies to flowchart, state, class, ER and mindmap.

props.name: direction
props.description: Overrides the direction of graph diagrams (flowchart, state, class, ER). Without it the direction written in the source is used.

props.name: rounded
props.description: Corner radius of rectangular nodes and boxes. `full` makes pills. Shapes that are round by definition (stadium, circle) are not affected.

props.name: tone
props.description: Accent of nodes that the source does not style itself: the outline colour (outline), the tint (filled, soft). Ignored by `mono`. Pie slices use the categorical chart colours.

props.name: fit
props.description: `width` scales the SVG down to the container (viewBox); `scroll` keeps the natural size inside a focusable, named scroll region; `auto` is `width` until the scale would fall below 0.6 (`MERMAID_AUTO_MIN_SCALE`), then `scroll`. The resolved value is on the root as `data-fit`.

props.name: showSource
props.description: Show the Mermaid source below the diagram (read-only, with a copy button). Readers can also toggle it with the "Show source" button.

props.name: showCode
props.description: Alias of `showSource`.

props.name: showTable
props.description: Show the text version (nodes and connections, participants and messages, slices with values) as visible content. It is always in the page for screen readers; this makes it visible too. Readers can toggle it with the "Show as text" button.

props.name: title
props.description: Caption above the diagram and the accessible name. Wins over `accTitle`, the front matter `title` and the title written in the diagram.

props.name: description
props.description: Longer accessible description. Wins over `accDescr`. Without either, an automatic summary such as "Flowchart with 6 nodes and 7 connections, top to bottom" describes the image.

props.name: maxNodes
props.description: Largest diagram that is drawn, counted in nodes (states, classes, entities, tasks, participants, slices...). Above it an inline error is shown instead of laying out the graph.

props.name: maxEdges
props.description: Largest number of connections (edges, messages, relations) that is drawn.

props.name: as
props.description: Root element. With `figure` the title is a `figcaption`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

emits.name: error
emits.payload: [event: { message: string; line: number; column: number }]
emits.description: The source could not be drawn (syntax error, unsupported type, empty input, size limit). Line and column are 1-based; they are 1 for errors without a position.

emits.name: rendered
emits.payload: [event: { type: string; nodes: number; edges: number }]
emits.description: The diagram was drawn, on mount and after every change of the source or the options. `type` is `flowchart`, `sequence`, `pie`, `state`, `er`, `class`, `gantt`, `mindmap`, `timeline` or `journey`.

a11y: The drawing is one `<svg role="img">` named by `aria-labelledby` (a `<title>` and a `<desc>`): the `title` prop, then `accTitle`, then the title written in the diagram, then an automatic summary such as "Flowchart with 6 nodes and 7 connections, top to bottom". The description comes from `description`, `accDescr` or the summary.

A text version is always in the page: an ordered list of nodes (in reading order) and a list of connections "A to B: label" for graphs, participants and messages in order for sequence diagrams, slices with values for pie charts, tasks with dates for gantt charts. It is visually hidden until `showTable` or the "Show as text" button reveals it (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`).
A syntax error is a `role="alert"` panel naming the line and column, with the offending line; "unsupported" and "nothing to draw" are `role="status"`. Nothing is announced on every redraw.
With `fit="scroll"` the viewport is `role="region"`, focusable (`tabindex="0"`, visible focus ring) and named "<title>, scrollable diagram", so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys.

State is not shown by colour alone: dotted and thick edges differ by pattern and weight, shapes differ by outline, gantt status is written as text and drawn as outline, check or diamond, journey scores are printed, actors differ by marker shape, pie slices list value and percentage in the legend.

Text inside the drawing is at least 12px at natural size (`size="md"` is 14px); with `fit="width"` it shrinks with the container, so use `fit="auto"` (scrolls below a 0.6 scale) or `fit="scroll"` for wide diagrams on narrow screens. Colours are tokens only (ink, muted ink, tones) so dark mode, accent presets and forced-colors mode (system colours replace the tokens) keep working. The component has no animation.

The source is only ever rendered as Vue text nodes inside SVG `<text>` elements. Markup, `<script>`, event handlers and `javascript:` text in the source can never be executed or inserted as HTML: tags inside labels are dropped (their text stays), and the title, description and the source panel show the text literally. `click` lines are ignored, so no link or handler is ever created.
requires: Throws a ContractError when `source` is missing or blank (a non-empty string of Mermaid text is required).
llmNotes: Pass Mermaid text in `source`; build it with a template literal or a constant, never by concatenating untrusted markup (the component is safe, but the text must be valid Mermaid).
Always set `title` (or `accTitle` in the source) so the diagram has a meaningful accessible name; add `description` for the takeaway.
Pick the diagram type with the first line: `flowchart TD`, `sequenceDiagram`, `pie`, `stateDiagram-v2`, `erDiagram`, `classDiagram`, `gantt`, `mindmap`, `timeline`, `journey`.
Do not put colours in the source: use `classDef name tone:success` or a class named `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `primary`; fills and strokes are mapped to tones.

Use `fit="auto"` when the diagram size is not known (user content): it scrolls instead of shrinking text below 60%. Use `fit="scroll"` for wide or dense diagrams and `fit="width"` (default) for small ones. Prefer `direction="TB"` for wide diagrams in narrow columns.
Use `variant="mono"` for print-like output and `variant="soft"` inside cards that already have a border.
Handle `@error` when the source comes from users; read `line` and `column` to point at the mistake.
Import `parseMermaid` and `renderModel` to validate or inspect a source without mounting the component.
Keep diagrams under the default 300 nodes; raise `maxNodes` deliberately.
replaces: mermaid.js client-side rendering
hand-drawn SVG diagrams
pre-rendered diagram images

components.name: Tree
components.summary: Keyboard-navigable expandable tree with single selection, sizes, compact density, checkboxes, connector lines and a boxed variant.
components.description: Use `Tree` for hierarchical data such as file explorers, category pickers and nested navigation inside a page. Items are `{ id, label, children?, icon?, disabled? }`. Expansion (`v-model:expanded`, array of ids) and selection (`v-model:selected`, one id or null) both work controlled and uncontrolled. Clicking a branch row selects and toggles it; clicking its chevron only toggles. Customise rows with the `item` slot. Variations: `density="compact"` for dense sidebars and file explorers; `checkboxes` (+ `v-model:checked`, ids of checked leaves) for pickers where several nodes are chosen: branches show checked / indeterminate derived from their leaves and toggling a branch toggles all its enabled leaves; `lines` draws connector lines (vertical rules with elbows) to make deep hierarchies easier to scan. `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets the type scale, toggle and checkbox size and indentation, while `density` sets the vertical rhythm; `compact` alone still means the small scale. `variant` is `default`, `lines` (the same as the `lines` prop) or `boxed` (a bordered card surface; the selected row is also set in a heavier weight). They combine. For site navigation use the navigation components; for tabular data use `Table`.

props.name: items
props.description: Root nodes: `{ id: string; label: string; children?: TreeItem[]; icon?: IconDefinition; disabled?: boolean }`. Ids must be non-empty and unique across the whole tree; a missing or repeated id throws a ContractError (rendering drops later duplicates when strict mode is off).

props.name: expanded
props.description: `v-model:expanded`. Ids of expanded branches; unknown ids are ignored.

props.name: selected
props.description: `v-model:selected`. Id of the selected node.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height, indentation, toggle size and font size. Unknown values fall back to default.

props.name: size
props.description: Type scale (12px, 14px, 16px), toggle and checkbox size and indentation step. Defaults to `md`, or `sm` when `density="compact"`. An explicit value wins. Unknown values behave as unset.

props.name: variant
props.description: `lines` draws connector lines (same as the `lines` prop); `boxed` frames the tree in a bordered card surface and sets the selected row in a heavier weight. Combine `boxed` with `lines`. Unknown values fall back to default.

props.name: checkboxes
props.description: Show a visual checkbox per node (aria-hidden; the treeitem exposes `aria-checked` true/false/mixed). Space toggles the focused node; Enter still selects/expands.

props.name: checked
props.description: `v-model:checked`. Ids of checked LEAF nodes (branches derive their state). Unknown ids are ignored. Only used with `checkboxes`.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the tree (`aria-label`). Required: set `label`, or pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` as an attribute.

props.name: lines
props.description: Draw connector lines (also set by `variant="lines"`): a vertical rule per ancestor level that ends in an elbow at the last child.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: item
slots.props: { item: TreeItem; level: number; expanded: boolean; selected: boolean }
slots.description: Replace the icon + label inside a row.

emits.name: update:expanded
emits.description: Expanded ids changed.

emits.name: update:selected
emits.description: Selection changed.

emits.name: update:checked
emits.description: Checked leaf ids changed (`checkboxes` only).

emits.name: select
emits.description: A node was activated (click / Enter / Space).

a11y: Follows the ARIA tree pattern: `role="tree"` with flat `treeitem`s carrying `aria-level`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-expanded` (branches only) and `aria-selected`.
Roving tabindex: one tab stop; Up/Down move, Home/End jump, Right expands or enters, Left collapses or goes to the parent, Enter/Space select.
With `checkboxes` every treeitem has `aria-checked` (`mixed` for partially checked branches); the visual box and the connector lines are `aria-hidden`.
Give the tree a name with `label` or `aria-label` (falls through to the root). The selected node also gets an outline in forced-colors mode, and the chevron rotation respects reduced motion.
Rows use logical padding, so RTL mirrors the indentation. Long labels truncate inside the row instead of widening the page.
Disabled nodes stay focusable but cannot be selected or toggled.

`size`, `variant` and `density` change only appearance: the roles, `aria-*` attributes, roving tabindex and the key map are the same in every combination. In `boxed` the selected row keeps `aria-selected` and the forced-colors outline and is also set in a heavier weight, so selection is not shown by tint alone.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the tree has no name (`label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
Throws a ContractError when a node has no non-empty string `id`, or two nodes anywhere in the tree (collapsed branches included) share an `id`.
llmNotes: Always give nodes stable unique string ids; v-model values are ids, not objects.
Always set `aria-label` on Tree.
Use `checkboxes` + `v-model:checked` for multi-pick trees; checked values are leaf ids only, branch state is derived.
Use `size` for the type scale and `variant="boxed"` for a framed tree; `variant="lines"` is the same as `lines`.
Use `density="compact"` for sidebars and `lines` for deep hierarchies; they combine with checkboxes.
Use the `item` slot for badges/actions, not extra buttons that steal keyboard focus.
replaces: hand-rolled Tree markup in app code

components.name: ActivityFeed
components.summary: Chronological list of who did what to which thing and when, with relative times, day groups, expandable details and a load more button.
components.description: Use `ActivityFeed` for audit trails, deploy history and "what changed" panels where each event has an actor, an action, an optional target and a time. `variant` sets the layout: `list` (default, ruled rows with initials avatars), `timeline` (round markers joined by a line), `compact` (one tight line per event, no avatars) and `grouped` (the list under a heading per calendar day, or per `group` you set). `size` sets the text size and `density` the row spacing. Times render with `Intl`: relative ("2 hours ago") up to a week old, absolute after that, with the full date in the `title`. Pass `now` for output that is identical on the server and the client; without it the first render shows absolute times and the relative text appears after mount. Events with `details` get a "Show details" button (controlled with `v-model:expanded` or left uncontrolled). All text is rendered as text, never as HTML. For a single process log use `LogViewer`; for a plain sequence of steps use `Timeline`.

props.name: events
props.description: The events in display order. Each has `id`, `action` and `time`; `actor`, `target`, `icon`, `tone`, `group` and `details` are optional. `null` is treated as empty.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the feed. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).

props.name: variant
props.description: `list` ruled rows with avatars, `timeline` markers joined by a line, `compact` one tight line per event, `grouped` list under a heading per day or `group`. Unknown values fall back to `list`.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size, marker and avatar size. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: density
props.description: Row spacing. Unknown values fall back to `comfortable`.

props.name: showAvatars
props.description: Initials avatar for events with an `actor` in `list` and `grouped`. Other variants always use the marker.

props.name: now
props.description: Reference time for relative text. Set it for server-safe output; without it the current time is read after mount and refreshed every minute.

props.name: relative
props.description: Show relative text for events up to a week from `now`. Off: always the absolute date and time.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale for dates and relative text. Unknown values fall back to the runtime default.

props.name: timeZone
props.description: IANA time zone for dates and day groups, for example `UTC`. Unknown values fall back to the runtime zone.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level of the group headings in `grouped`.

props.name: hasMore
props.description: More events exist: shows the load more button or the `load-more` slot.

props.name: loading
props.description: The next page is loading: the button is disabled, the feed is `aria-busy` and a polite status says so.

props.name: loadMoreLabel
props.description: Text of the load more button.

props.name: expanded
props.description: Ids of the events whose details are open (`v-model:expanded`). Leave it unset for uncontrolled use.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: empty
slots.description: Shown instead of the list when there are no events. Default: "No activity yet."

slots.name: load-more
slots.description: Replaces the load more button. Shown while `hasMore` is true.

slots.name: details
slots.description: Content of the details panel. With this slot every event gets a "Show details" button.

emits.name: load-more
emits.description: The load more button was pressed.

emits.name: toggle
emits.description: An event's details were opened or closed.

emits.name: update:expanded
emits.description: New list of open ids, for `v-model:expanded`.
