a11y: The root is `role="group"` named by `label` (required). Events are one ordered list (`ol` / `li`); in `grouped` each day is a `role="group"` named by its heading, and the heading level is `headingLevel`.
Times use `<time datetime>` with the ISO value; relative text carries the full absolute date and time in `title`. A value that is not a date is shown as given, without `datetime`.
Tone is never colour alone: non-neutral tones add an icon and a visually hidden word ("Success.", "Warning.", "Error.", "Info.") before the text.
Avatars are decorative (`alt=""`) because the actor is named in the text. Initials are derived from the generic actor name.

Details: a real `button` ("Show details" / "Hide details" plus the event as hidden text) with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` while open. Enter and Space toggle it. 24px minimum height, 44px on coarse pointers, shared focus ring.

`loading` sets `aria-busy` and a polite `role="status"` says "Loading more activity." The feed never announces new items by itself. Layout uses logical properties and wraps at 320px, so RTL mirrors it.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the feed has no accessible name (`label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
Throws a ContractError when an event has no `id` (a non-empty string or a number) or two events share an id.
Throws a ContractError when an event has a blank `action`.
llmNotes: Always set `label`; give every event a unique, stable `id` and a non-blank `action`.
Pass `now` (and `time-zone`) for server-rendered pages so the output matches on the client.
Use generic actors ("Deploy bot", "Reviewer 1"); never invent real people. Put the outcome in `action` or `tone`, not only in colour.
Use `variant="grouped"` for long histories, `compact` for side panels, `timeline` when order is the point. Use `hasMore` with `@load-more` for paging.
Details and `empty` text are plain text. Use the `details` slot for richer content you have already made safe.

components.name: DescriptionList
components.summary: Semantic term/definition pairs (`dl`) for showing record details, with optional copy buttons.
components.description: Use `DescriptionList` with `DescriptionItem` children to show key/value details of one record (a user, a deployment, an API key). Pick a `variant`: `stacked` (default) for narrow detail panels, `inline` for compact key-on-left/value-on-right rows (settings summaries, receipts), `grid` for wide overview sections that show many short facts in 1-4 responsive columns, `striped` for long lists of facts that need row tracking (framed, alternate rows tinted). `orientation` (stacked/horizontal) applies inside `stacked`, `grid` and `striped`: `stacked` (default) puts the term above the value and `horizontal` aligns them in two columns from the `sm` breakpoint. Set `copyable` on an item to show a copy button for IDs, URLs and tokens. `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets the type scale and `density` (`compact`, `default`, `comfortable`) the space between items (row gaps, and the padding of divided or striped items). For a single standalone pair use `DetailField` (it takes `size` too). For tabular comparisons of many records use `Table`.

props.name: variant
props.description: Layout: `stacked` default; `inline` term left / value right on one row; `grid` responsive columns; `striped` framed list with alternate row tint. Unknown values fall back to `stacked`.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column count for `variant="grid"` (always 1 on mobile, 2 from `sm`, N from `lg`). Ignored by other variants.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Term above value (stacked) or side by side (horizontal, from `sm`).

props.name: size
props.description: Type scale of terms and values: 12px, 14px or 16px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: density
props.description: Space between items: row gaps (6px, 12px, 20px; grid row gaps 8px, 16px, 24px) and the vertical padding of divided and striped items. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: divided
props.description: Draw a divider between items instead of a gap. Ignored by `grid`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: default
slots.description: `DescriptionItem` children.

parts.name: DescriptionItem
parts.description: One term + definition pair rendered as `div > dt + dd` (valid inside `dl`).

props.name: term
props.description: Term text. Required: set `term` or use the `term` slot for rich content.

props.name: copyable
props.description: Show a copy button next to the definition.

props.name: copyText
props.description: Text to copy; defaults to the rendered text of the definition.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

parts.name: DetailField
parts.description: A single standalone label/value pair (its own `dl`).

props.name: label
props.description: Label text.

props.name: value
props.description: Value; the default slot wins when given.

props.name: copyable
props.description: Show a copy button (hidden when the value is empty).

props.name: size
props.description: Type scale of the label and value. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.description: Placeholder for empty values.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

a11y: Renders native `dl`/`dt`/`dd` so screen readers announce term/definition relationships.

The copy button is named after what it copies ("Copy Region"; "Copy value" without a term) and keeps that name. The result ("Copied" or "Copy failed") is announced by a sibling `role="status"` element, not inside the button. It is a 24px target.
`size` and `density` change type scale and spacing only; the `dl`, `dt`, `dd` structure and copy buttons are the same in every combination. The copy button stays a 24px target at every size.
Inline values align to the end edge (logical), so RTL mirrors the layout. Items stack on narrow screens; `horizontal` orientation only applies from the `sm` breakpoint.
requires: Throws a ContractError when a `DescriptionItem` has no `term` text (prop or `term` slot).
Throws a ContractError when a `DescriptionItem` is rendered outside a `DescriptionList`.
Throws a ContractError when a `DetailField` has a blank `label`.
llmNotes: Put only `DescriptionItem` elements directly inside `DescriptionList`.
Use `copyable` for IDs, URLs, tokens; copyText for masked values.
Use horizontal orientation inside wide cards, stacked in narrow columns.
Use DetailField, not DescriptionList, for a lone label/value pair.
Choose `variant`: stacked for narrow panels, inline for compact key/value rows, grid for wide overviews with many short facts, striped for long fact lists.
`columns` only applies to `variant="grid"`; `divided` is ignored by grid.
Use `size` for text and `density` for spacing on DescriptionList (not per item); `density` has an effect on gaps, `divided` and `striped` rows.
Items adapt to the list `variant` automatically; do not style DescriptionItem per variant yourself.

components.name: List
components.summary: Vertical list of rows with leading/trailing slots, dividers and optional interactivity.
components.description: Use `List` + `ListItem` for simple vertical collections: files, members, recent activity, settings rows. Each item has `leading` (icon/avatar), default (title), `description` and `trailing` (badge, button, meta) slots. Set `interactive` on items that are clickable; for navigation render the item as a link (`as="a"`) or put a link inside. Variants: `plain` (no dividers; for short lists inside another surface), `divided` (hairline dividers; the default), `card` (each row is its own bordered card, for selectable/sortable entries), `interactive` (divided rows that are all hoverable, focusable and keyboard-activatable), `with-avatar` (roomier rows with an unmuted leading slot for an `Avatar`, medium-weight title). `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets row padding and text size for every row; `gap` (`none`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`) spaces rows in `plain` and `card` lists (divided variants are separated by their rule and ignore it). For tabular data with columns use `Table`/`DataTable`; for chronological events use `Timeline`.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render (`ol` for ordered).

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper.

props.name: variant
props.description: Row presentation, shared with every `ListItem` inside. When omitted the `divided` prop decides (dividers by default); unknown values behave as omitted.

props.name: size
props.description: Row padding and text size, shared with every `ListItem`: `sm` 12px text, `md` 14px, `lg` 16px with roomier rows. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between rows (0, 4px, 8px, 16px). Only `plain` and `card` lists use it; `card` rows keep 8px when it is not set. Divided variants ignore it. Unknown values behave as unset.

props.name: divided
props.description: Dividers between items. Only used when `variant` is not set.

props.name: bordered
props.description: Rounded border around the list.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: default
slots.description: `ListItem` children.

parts.name: ListItem
parts.description: One row. Slots: `leading`, default, `description`, `trailing`.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render the slot child; leading/trailing layout is skipped.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Hover/focus styles, tabindex=0 and Enter/Space activation (non-native elements). Defaults to true inside `<List variant="interactive">`; `:interactive="false"` opts a row out.

props.name: selected
props.description: Highlight and set aria-current.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dim and block clicks/keys.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

a11y: Explicit `role="list"` is set so lists keep list semantics in Safari even with list-style removed.
Interactive non-native items get `tabindex=0` and respond to Enter/Space; prefer `as="a"`/`as="button"` for real navigation/actions.
`selected` sets `aria-current`; `disabled` sets `aria-disabled`.

Rows are flat: no accent stripe or hover movement. Selection is a background plus `aria-current`, not colour alone. Slot text inherits a muted colour: give a Button inside `trailing` its own `text-foreground` on selected rows.
`size` and `gap` change spacing and text only. Interactive rows keep at least a 28px height at `sm`, above the 24px minimum target.
Keyboard: Tab reaches interactive rows (and links or buttons inside them); Enter or Space activates a non-native row. Dividers and rows reflow at any width.
requires: Throws a ContractError when a `ListItem` is rendered outside a `List` (a plain `ul`, `ol` or `role="list"` parent also counts).
llmNotes: Use `leading`/`trailing` slots instead of custom flex wrappers inside ListItem.
Choose the look with `variant` on List (not per row): `card` for separated entries, `with-avatar` for people lists, `interactive` when every row is clickable.
Set `size` and `gap` on List, not per row; `gap` only affects `plain` and `card`.
Make an item interactive only if it does something; navigation should be a link.
Do not place block-level layout (cards) inside ListItem; use Card grid instead.

components.name: Timeline
components.summary: Vertical sequence of events with status-toned markers, times and a connector line.
components.description: Use `Timeline` + `TimelineItem` for chronological activity: deploy history, audit trails, order status. Each item has a marker (status tone, optional FontAwesome icon), title, time and free-form body. The connector line is drawn between items and hidden after the last. Layouts: `vertical` (default; activity feeds, audit logs), `horizontal` (a few steps in a row, e.g. order progress; scrolls when it overflows), `alternating` (events left and right of a centre line from `md` up, plain vertical below; for history/roadmap pages). `size` is `compact` (smaller markers and spacing for dense side panels), `default` or `large` (bigger markers, spacing and text). `variant` styles the markers: `default` (tinted), `outline` (a ring in the status tone, plain centre) or `solid` (filled with the tone); the status is also spoken in every variant. For non-chronological rows use `List`.

props.name: layout
props.description: Orientation / arrangement of the events, shared with every `TimelineItem`. Unknown values fall back to `vertical`.

props.name: size
props.description: `compact` = smaller marker (16px), tighter spacing, xs body text; `large` = 32px marker, roomier spacing, larger text. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: variant
props.description: Marker look shared with every item: `default` tinted bubble, `outline` ring in the status tone with a plain centre, `solid` marker filled with the status tone. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the list (`aria-label`). Required for `horizontal` (a focusable scroll region); recommended otherwise.

props.name: as
props.description: List element; `ol` when order matters.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: default
slots.description: `TimelineItem` children.

parts.name: TimelineItem
parts.description: One event. Slots: `icon`, `title`, `time`, default (body).

props.name: status
props.description: Marker tone.

props.name: title
props.description: Event title. An item needs a `title` or a `time` (or the matching slot).

props.name: time
props.description: Human-readable time text.

props.name: datetime
props.description: Machine-readable value for `<time datetime>`.

props.name: icon
props.description: FontAwesome icon inside the marker; a dot is used when omitted.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Times use `<time>` with tabular figures; pass `datetime` for machine-readable values.
Status is spoken as well as coloured: non-neutral statuses add a visually hidden "Success.", "Warning.", "Error." or "Info." before the title.

`variant` and `size` change markers and spacing only. Every variant keeps the visually hidden status word, so `outline` and `solid` markers do not rely on tone alone; the marker glyph is foreground on the ring and on-tone text on the solid fill (the pairs the contrast tests cover). The `outline` ring uses stroke tokens that are at least 3:1 against the page and card backgrounds in every theme, light and dark (WCAG 1.4.11; `warning` uses `warning-foreground` in light mode and `warning` in dark mode), and `contrast.test.ts` pins every status.

The `horizontal` layout becomes a focusable scroll region (`tabindex="0"`, shared focus ring) so keyboard users can scroll it. Spacing and placement use logical properties, so RTL mirrors them. `alternating` is a plain vertical list below `md`.

Put status words in the title/body too, colour alone is not enough.
Pick the layout on Timeline (children adapt): `horizontal` for 3-5 short steps, `alternating` for history pages, `compact` for sidebars.

Use `datetime` whenever `time` is relative text.

components.name: VirtualList
components.summary: Fixed-row-height windowed list that renders only the visible rows, for 10 000+ items.
components.description: Use `VirtualList` when a plain `v-for` would create thousands of DOM nodes (logs, long pickers, big result sets). Every row must have the same `itemHeight` (px); rows are absolutely positioned inside a spacer of the full height, so scrolling stays native. Give the list a height with `height` or a class (`h-96`). `overscan` rows are rendered beyond the viewport to avoid blank flashes. Scroll handling is throttled to one update per animation frame. For variable row heights or table semantics use `DataTable`; for short lists use `List`. Browsers cap element height (about 33 million px, less in Firefox), which limits very tall lists.

props.name: overscan

Give the list an accessible name with `label` or `aria-labelledby`.
Interactive rows (buttons, links) only exist while rendered; keep roving focus logic outside the list or call `scrollToIndex` before focusing.

Always give the list a height (`height` prop or a `h-*` class); without one it grows to full size and nothing is windowed.

Pass `item-key` when items can be reordered or filtered so row state is preserved.

components.name: Carousel
components.summary: Scroll-snap carousel with previous / next buttons, dots, keyboard control, optional loop and accessible autoplay.
components.description: Use `Carousel` for a small set of equal-weight slides (image galleries, feature tours, testimonials). It is built on native CSS scroll-snap: touch and trackpad swiping, momentum and snapping come from the browser, the component adds an index (`v-model`), buttons, dots, keyboard keys and autoplay. Compose `CarouselContent` (the scroller) with `CarouselItem` slides, and optionally `CarouselPrevious`, `CarouselNext`, `CarouselDots` and `CarouselCounter`. Slides are `basis-full` by default; override with a class (`basis-1/3`) to show several at once. Autoplay is off by default, pauses while the pointer is over the carousel or focus is inside, shows a pause/play button (WCAG 2.2.2) and is disabled entirely under `prefers-reduced-motion`. `loop` wraps around (rewind), it does not clone slides. Do not use a carousel for critical content or long lists: prefer a grid or `VirtualList`.

a11y: Root is `role="region"` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"` and an `aria-label` (set `label`). The track is a focusable `role="group"` named "Slides"; each slide is `role="group"` with `aria-roledescription="slide"` and an "n of N" label.

Keyboard: Tab reaches the track, buttons and dots. On the track ArrowLeft / ArrowRight (ArrowUp / ArrowDown when vertical) move one slide and Home / End jump to the first / last. Arrow keys typed on links, buttons and form fields inside a slide keep their own behaviour. The focused track also scrolls natively and snaps to a slide.

Dots are real buttons: 24px targets (44px on touch), `aria-current="true"` on the active one, and the active dot differs by fill, not only by colour. Previous and next sit at the logical start and end, so they mirror in RTL.

The track is `aria-live="off"` while autoplay runs and `polite` otherwise (`live` overrides), so slide changes are announced only when the user caused them. `CarouselCounter` shows the position with tabular figures.

Autoplay never runs under prefers-reduced-motion (scrolling is then instant instead of smooth), stops while the pointer is over the carousel or focus is inside, and always comes with a pause / start button (WCAG 2.2.2) that is the first control in tab order.
Previous and next disable at the ends unless `loop`.

Throws a ContractError when `Carousel` has no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`); there is no generic default name.
llmNotes: Always compose Carousel > CarouselContent > CarouselItem; add CarouselPrevious / CarouselNext / CarouselDots as siblings of CarouselContent.
Set `label` so the region has a meaningful accessible name.
Use `basis-1/2`, `basis-1/3` on CarouselItem for multiple slides per view; vertical carousels need a fixed height class on CarouselContent.
Keep autoplay off unless content is non-essential; never rely on it to reveal important information. Autoplay always renders a pause button: do not hide it.
Slides register in DOM order; keep CarouselItem keys stable when reordering.

components.summary: Label + value + proportional bar for usage vs limit (quota, disk, budget).

Use `tone="auto"` to turn the bar warning/danger as it fills. Ratios are clamped to 0..100% so overflowing values never break layout; show the real numbers via `valueText`. For task progress (something completing over time) use a Progress component instead.

components.name: Leaderboard
components.summary: Ranked entries as a list, a table or a podium, with ties, deltas, proportional bars and a highlighted entry.
components.description:
Use `Leaderboard` to show who or what is ahead on one number: sales by region, tickets closed by team, tests passed by suite. Each entry is `{ id, label, value, rank?, delta?, avatar? }`. Entries are sorted (`sort`), ranked (`ties`) and formatted (`valueFormat`, `locale`) for you.

`variant="list"` is an ordered list of ruled rows. `variant="table"` is a real table (rank, name, value, change) inside a focusable, named scroll region. `variant="podium"` shows the top three as steps in the visual order 2-1-3 while the DOM stays in rank order, with the remaining entries in a list below.

Ranks: `competition` (default) gives equal values the same rank and skips the next (1, 2, 2, 4); `dense` does not skip (1, 2, 2, 3); `none` ranks by position. An entry `rank` always wins. Values that are not finite numbers render the fallback text, sort last and have no rank. `sort="asc"` makes the lowest value rank 1 (times, costs); `sort="none"` keeps the order you pass.

A delta is shown as an arrow icon and a signed number, never as colour alone. `highlight` marks one entry with `aria-current`, a tinted surface and the visible text from `highlightLabel`. Bars are decorative: the number is always the text. For a single quota against a limit use StatBar; for a full data grid use DataTable.

props.name: entries
props.description: The entries: `{ id, label, value, rank?, delta?, avatar? }`. `id` is a unique non-empty string or number. `avatar` is an image source string (an inline data URI works) or `{ src?, fallback? }`; without an image the initials of the label (or `fallback`) are shown. An empty or missing array shows the empty state.

props.description: Accessible name of the leaderboard and the hidden table caption. Required, or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: variant
props.description: `list` ruled rows, `table` a real table in a scroll region, `podium` the top three as 2-1-3 steps and the rest in a list. Unknown values fall back to `list`.

props.name: size

props.name: density

props.name: showRank

props.name: highlight

props.name: highlightLabel
props.description: Visible text on the highlighted entry. Change it to match the meaning, for example "Your team".

props.name: bars
props.description: Draw a bar under each entry, proportional to the largest value (negative values draw an empty bar). Decorative: hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: valueFormat

a11y: The list variant is an ordered list (`ol` and `li`); the table variant is a real `table` with a hidden caption, `th scope="col"` headers and `th scope="row"` names inside a focusable region with the same name, so it scrolls by keyboard at 320px; the podium is an ordered list of the top three in rank order (CSS only reorders them visually to 2-1-3) followed by a list of the rest.

Each rank is text, with a visually hidden "Rank" before it. The highlighted entry has `aria-current="true"` and visible text from `highlightLabel`, so it never relies on colour. A delta is an arrow icon plus a signed number.

Bars and avatars are decorative (`aria-hidden`); the label and the number are always text. Long labels truncate with a `title` and `min-w-0`, hostile text is rendered as text, and logical properties make it work right-to-left.

llmNotes: Always pass `label` (or `aria-label`) and give every entry a unique `id`.
Pass raw numbers in `value` and set `valueFormat` (and `locale`) instead of pre-formatting strings.
Use `highlight` plus `highlightLabel` to mark the current user or team; never mark it with colour only.
Use `ties="dense"` when the next rank must not skip; use `sort="asc"` when lower is better.
Do not use Leaderboard for one value against a limit (StatBar) or for sortable, filterable data (DataTable).
replaces: hand-rolled ranking lists and top-N tables

components.name: Gauge
components.summary: SVG gauge (semicircle, three-quarter arc or linear bar) for a value within a range, with threshold tones, a label and role=meter semantics.
components.description: Use `Gauge` to show one measurement against a known range (CPU load, disk usage, score). `thresholds` map value bands to tones (`success`, `warning`, `danger`, ...): the highest threshold whose `value` is <= the current value wins. Values are clamped to the range, reversed `min` / `max` are swapped and `null` / `NaN` render an empty gauge reading `–`. The arc sweeps in on mount and on change unless the user prefers reduced motion. `variant` picks the shape: `semicircle` (default half-dial), `arc` (three-quarter dial with the value inside) or `linear` (a horizontal bar with caption and value on one line); all three keep the same meter semantics, name and value text. Use `StatBar` for linear usage bars and `Progress` for task completion; a gauge is for a live reading, not progress.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value. null / NaN / Infinity mean "no data".

props.name: min
props.description: Range start. Non-finite values fall back to 0.

props.name: max
props.description: Range end. Non-finite values fall back to 100.

props.name: thresholds
props.description: Tone bands: `{ value, tone }`, applied when the value is >= `value`.

props.name: tone
props.description: Tone below all thresholds (or when there are none).

props.name: size
props.description: Rendered width (w-24, w-40, w-56) and text size.

props.name: variant
props.description: `semicircle` half-dial with the value at its foot, `arc` a three-quarter dial with the value centred, `linear` a horizontal bar (caption left, value right, same width as the dial). Same `role="meter"`, name and `aria-valuetext` in all three.

props.name: label
props.description: Caption under the value; also the accessible name. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).

props.name: valueText
props.description: Replaces the formatted value inside the gauge and `aria-valuetext` (e.g. "3.2 of 4 GB").

props.name: animated
props.description: Animate the arc; always off under prefers-reduced-motion.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; use it to set the size (`w-64`).

slots.name: default
slots.props: { value: number; percent: number; tone: GaugeTone; text: string }
slots.description: Replace the centre value (e.g. add a unit).

slots.name: label
slots.description: Replace the caption under the value.

a11y: Root has `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`; the label becomes `aria-label` (falls back to "Gauge"; pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` when there is no visible label).
With no data the root switches to `role="img"` with the label "<label>: No data", because `role="meter"` requires `aria-valuenow`. Min, max and valuetext are omitted then.

`variant` does not change the semantics: every shape is `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow` / `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` and the same name; without data all three are `role="img"` labelled "<label>: No data". The arc, the bar and their track are `aria-hidden`; the value and caption stay real text.
The value uses `tabular-nums`; the caption is 12px text. The width follows `size` or `class` and never exceeds the container needs at 320px (`w-56` is the widest).
The arc animation is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion; the SVG itself is aria-hidden.
Tone is also exposed as `data-tone`; do not rely on colour alone: add `valueText` such as "Critical: 96%" when the state matters.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
llmNotes: Always give a Gauge a `label` or aria-label.
List thresholds ascending, starting at the range minimum, so the tone below the first band is explicit.
Use `variant="linear"` where a row or card needs a gauge to line up with text (give it `class="w-full"`); use `arc` when the value is the focus and `semicircle` for the compact dial.
Use `valueText` for units; the default text is just the rounded number.
Use the tone `danger` (not `destructive`) for the red state.

components.name: KpiTile
components.summary: Headline metric tile: label, value, trend delta with good/bad colouring, hint, icon and loading skeleton.
components.description: Use `KpiTile` for dashboard headline numbers. `trend` (`up`/`down`/`flat`) picks the arrow; `goodWhen` says which direction is desirable so colour reflects meaning (error rate going down is good). Group tiles with `StatGroup`. Numbers are formatted for you (`12345.6` shows `12,345.6`); pass a string for pre-formatted values such as `99.9%` or `1.2 MB`. Values, deltas and the sparkline use tabular figures so columns of tiles line up. Variations: `size="compact"` for dense dashboards; `variant="inverted"` for one high-contrast hero tile; `sparkline` (array of numbers, or the `sparkline` slot) for a mini trend line; `progress` (0-100) for a bar showing usage against a target. All still accept the Card surfaces (`outline`, `elevated`, `interactive`, `ghost`, ...). For usage against a hard limit with labels use `StatBar`.

props.name: label
props.description: Metric name.

props.name: value
props.description: Headline value; numbers are formatted, null / NaN / Infinity show `–`.

props.name: delta
props.description: Change text; numbers get a sign and formatting.

props.name: trend
props.description: Direction of the change (arrow icon).

props.name: goodWhen
props.description: Which direction is good. `none` always uses the neutral colour.

props.name: hint
props.description: Supporting text, e.g. "vs last 7 days".

props.name: icon
props.description: FontAwesome icon shown top-right.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a skeleton instead of value/delta and sets aria-busy.

props.name: variant
props.description: Card surface, or `inverted` = foreground background with light text. The old `accent` edge stripe was removed; a stale `accent` value renders the plain default tile.

props.name: size
props.description: `compact` = `p-3 gap-1`, smaller label and value; `lg` = `p-6 gap-3` with a 36px value. Unknown values behave like `default`.

props.name: layout
props.description: `stacked` is the default column. `split` puts the label at the start and the value at the end of one row (delta, sparkline and progress span the full width below). `centered` centres every row. Unknown values behave like `stacked`.

props.name: tone
props.description: Colour of the progress bar and sparkline. Unknown values fall back to `primary`.

props.name: sparkline
props.description: Values for a mini area sparkline under the delta (non-finite entries become gaps). Hidden while `loading` or when empty.

props.name: progress
props.description: Percentage 0-100 (clamped) rendered as `role="progressbar"`; null / NaN / Infinity hide it.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render (e.g. `a` for a linking tile).

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: value
slots.description: Replace the value text.

slots.name: delta
slots.description: Replace the delta text (arrow and colour remain).

slots.name: hint
slots.description: Replace the hint (e.g. with a Sparkline).

slots.name: icon
slots.description: Custom icon content.

slots.name: sparkline
slots.description: Replace the built-in sparkline (e.g. a custom chart); rendered below the delta row.

a11y: The delta includes visually-hidden text ("Increase:", "Decrease:", "No change:") so direction is not conveyed by colour/arrow alone.
`progress` renders `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow` and the label "<label> progress"; the sparkline has an `aria-label` ("<label> trend"). Neither replaces the textual value.
Colour is never the only signal: tone and sentiment colours accompany an arrow icon and hidden text. Numbers use `tabular-nums`.

`layout` and `size` only rearrange and rescale the same elements in the same reading order (label, value, delta, sparkline, progress); the colour pairs are unchanged. `split` is a two-column grid whose label column shrinks and wraps, so a long label never overflows at 320px.
Loading sets `aria-busy` and announces "Loading" via a status region.
Render with `as="a"` (or `as-child`) when the tile navigates; a plain tile is not interactive.
requires: Throws a ContractError when `label` is blank.
llmNotes: Set `good-when="down"` for cost, latency, error rate metrics so decreases are green.
Wrap tiles in StatGroup, not a hand-written grid.
Pass pre-formatted strings for currency/percent; numbers only get generic grouping.
Use `size="compact"` in dense grids and `variant="inverted"` for at most one hero tile per view. There is no accent stripe or gradient variant.
Pass `sparkline` / `progress` props rather than custom children; use the `sparkline` slot only for a different chart.
Use `loading` instead of rendering a zero while data is fetching.
replaces: hand-rolled KpiTile markup in app code

components.name: StatGroup
components.summary: Responsive grid wrapper for KpiTile (or any tile) rows.
components.description: Use `StatGroup` to lay out a row of `KpiTile`s. The default `auto` mode fits as many tiles of at least 12rem per row as the container allows; pass `columns` for a fixed number at the `lg` breakpoint (collapsing to 2 then 1 column on small screens). Layouts: `grid` (default; separate tiles with gaps, best for card-style `KpiTile`s), `inline` (wrapping flex row, tiles grow from 10rem; best for a handful of compact tiles in a toolbar/header, `columns` is ignored), `divided` (one bordered surface with hairline dividers; the tiles lose their own border, radius and shadow; choose `columns` that divide the tile count evenly so no empty divider-coloured cell shows).

props.name: layout
props.description: Arrangement of the tiles; unknown values fall back to `grid`.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between tiles of the `grid` and `inline` layouts: 0, 0.5rem, 1rem, 1.5rem. `divided` ignores it (its rules are hairlines). Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column count at the largest breakpoint; invalid values fall back to `auto`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

components.name: TrendBadge
components.summary: Compact up / down / flat change indicator with good-or-bad colouring, Intl formatting and screen-reader text.
components.description: Use `TrendBadge` next to a metric to show how it moved. `direction` picks the arrow (or is derived from the sign of `value`); `goodWhen` (or `inverse`) says which direction is desirable, so a drop in latency is green and a drop in revenue is red. The magnitude is printed without sign because the arrow carries the direction. Formatting goes through `Intl.NumberFormat` (`number`, `percent`, `compact`, `currency`). `null`, `NaN` and `Infinity` render an en dash and announce "No data". Use `KpiTile` when you need the whole tile; use this badge inside tables, lists and headings.

props.name: direction
props.description: Arrow direction. Derived from the sign of `value` when omitted; invalid values are ignored.

props.name: value
props.description: Magnitude of the change (sign is not printed). Omit for an arrow-only badge; null / NaN / Infinity show `–`.

props.name: goodWhen
props.description: Which direction is good. `none` always uses the neutral colour.

props.name: inverse
props.description: Shorthand for `goodWhen="down"` (cost, latency, error rate).

props.name: format
props.description: `percent` appends % to the value as-is (12 becomes 12%).

props.name: currency
props.description: ISO 4217 code for `format="currency"`; invalid codes fall back to a plain number.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale; invalid values fall back to the runtime default.

props.name: fractionDigits
props.description: Maximum fraction digits (clamped to 0-20).

props.name: variant
props.description: Tinted background, solid fill, text only, or bordered text. Unknown values fall back to `soft`.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corner radius: 6px, fully round, or none. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.

props.name: size
props.description: Badge size. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: default
slots.description: Replace the visible value text (the screen-reader text keeps the formatted value).

a11y: The arrow is decorative (aria-hidden); a visually-hidden text states the change: "Increase of 12.4", "Decrease of 3.2", "No change" or "No data".
Colour is never the only signal: direction is conveyed by the arrow and the hidden text, meaning by the text.
`outline` keeps the 1px border in forced-colors mode and uses the same text tokens as `ghost`; `shape` changes only the radius.
Colours come from theme tokens (success / destructive / muted) and keep contrast in light and dark mode. The number uses `tabular-nums`, and the badge never wraps (`whitespace-nowrap`).
llmNotes: Pass the absolute magnitude or a signed number; the sign is never printed, the arrow is.
Set `inverse` (or good-when="down") for cost, latency and error-rate metrics.
Use `format="percent"` with percentage points (12 means 12%), not fractions.
Do not pass pre-formatted strings as `value`; use the default slot for custom text.

components.name: DataGrid
components.summary: Spreadsheet-like data grid: keyboard navigation over cells, inline editing with validation, sorting, resizable and pinned columns, row selection, copy as TSV and a windowed render for 10,000 rows.
components.description:
Use `DataGrid` when people work in the cells: move with the arrow keys, press Enter or F2 to edit, copy a block into a spreadsheet. Use `DataTable` for read-only tables with paging and `Table` for static markup. The grid follows the ARIA grid pattern: `role="grid"` with one tab stop (roving tabindex), so Tab enters and leaves it. Give `columns` (`{ key, label, type, editable, width, pinned, sortable, align }`) and `rows`; bind `v-model:rows` to receive edits (the grid never mutates the array it was given, it emits a new array with a new row object). `v-model:sort` and `v-model:selected` work controlled or uncontrolled.

Rows have a fixed height (set by `density`), cell text is truncated with an ellipsis, and above 200 rows (or with `virtual`) only the visible window is mounted, so 10,000 rows cost about 30 rows of DOM. The row with the focus stays mounted when it scrolls out of view. Cell values are always rendered as text, never as HTML.

Known limits: no merged cells, no column reorder or grouping, no row grouping or tree rows, no fill handle, no undo or redo, no paste, no type-to-edit (press Enter or F2 first), no mouse drag selection of cells (use Shift+Arrow or Shift+click), no horizontal virtualization (every column is rendered), no variable row height, no server paging (use the `rows` you have). After you edit a sorted column the row keeps its place until the next sort. Column widths are in pixels and the grid does not stretch to fill a wider container. Change the data by replacing `rows` with a new array; mutating a row in place is not detected. Text direction is read when the grid mounts and when `dir` changes.

props.name: columns
props.description: `{ key, label, type?, editable?, width?, minWidth?, maxWidth?, pinned?, sortable?, resizable?, align?, options?, formatter? }`. `type` is `text` (default), `number` or `select` and picks the editor. `pinned` is `start` or `end`: pinned columns stick to that edge while the grid scrolls sideways and are moved to the edges in the order given. `width` is in px (default 160, resize limits 48 to 1000). `align` is `start`, `center` or `end` (numbers default to `end`). `options` are values or `{ value, label }` for a `select` column. `formatter(value, row)` returns the text shown and copied.

props.name: rows
props.description: v-model:rows. Plain objects. An edit emits a new array holding a new object for the edited row; the input is never mutated. Replace the array to change the data.

props.name: rowKey
props.type: keyof T | ((row: T, index: number) => string | number)
props.description: Row property or function giving a unique id, used for selection. A row without a string or number id falls back to its index; with `selectable` a missing or repeated id throws a ContractError.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the grid. Required unless `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.

props.name: sort
props.description: v-model:sort. Header click, Enter or Space cycles ascending, descending, none. Stable; numbers compare as numbers, text naturally; empty values go last in both directions.

props.name: selectable
props.description: Adds a pinned checkbox column, `aria-selected` on rows and Space (Shift+Space for a range) on any cell to toggle the row.

props.name: selected
props.description: v-model:selected: ids of the selected rows. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: validate
props.type: (value: unknown, context: DataGridValidateContext<T>) => string | null | undefined | void
props.description: Called before an edit is applied with the parsed value (a number for `number`, the option value for `select`). Return error text to reject it: the editor stays open with `aria-invalid`, the text is shown next to the cell, linked with `aria-describedby`, and announced. Escape cancels.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the scroll area: px number or any CSS length. Virtual grids default to 480px; other grids grow with their rows unless you set it (the header and pinned columns stay in view only inside a bounded height).

props.name: virtual
props.description: `auto` windows the rows above 200; `true` always, `false` never.

props.name: overscan
props.description: Rows mounted above and below the visible window.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height (28px, 36px, 48px) and cell padding. Touch devices get at least 44px rows. Unknown values fall back to default.

props.name: variant
props.description: `bordered` frames the grid and rules the columns; `striped` frames it and tints every second row; `borderless` drops the frame and column rules. Unknown values fall back to bordered.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size: 12px, 14px, 16px. Editors are 16px below the `md` breakpoint so phones do not zoom.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows placeholder rows, sets `aria-busy` and announces the change once.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Message when there are no rows (use the `empty` slot for rich content).

props.name: nullText
props.description: Shown for null and undefined cells (copied as empty).

props.name: dir
props.description: Text direction. `auto` reads the nearest `dir` attribute or the computed direction when the grid mounts. Arrow keys, sticky edges, resize and alignment follow it.

props.name: neutralizeFormulas
props.description: In copied text, prefix text cells that start with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or carriage return with an apostrophe so a spreadsheet shows them as text instead of running them. Numbers are left alone. Turn off only when the clipboard must hold the exact text.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the root (`data-slot="data-grid"`). `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` go to the grid element; every other attribute goes to the root.

slots.name: cell-<key>
slots.props: { row: T, value: unknown, column: DataGridColumn<T>, rowIndex: number }
slots.description: Custom (display) content for the cells of that column; `rowIndex` is the index in the source `rows`. The editor still opens on Enter. Keep the content short: rows have a fixed height.

slots.name: header-<key>
slots.description: Custom header label for that column. The visible text must still contain the column label.

slots.name: empty
slots.description: Replaces the empty-state message.

emits.name: update:rows
emits.description: A new array after a committed edit.

emits.name: update:sort
emits.description: Sort changed from a header.

emits.name: update:selected
emits.description: Row selection changed.

emits.name: cell-edit
emits.payload: [edit: { row, rowKey, rowIndex, column, value, previousValue }]
emits.description: A value was committed and changed. `rowIndex` is the index in the source rows.

emits.name: column-resize

a11y: ARIA grid pattern: `role="grid"` with rowgroups, rows, `columnheader` and `gridcell`, `aria-rowcount` and `aria-colcount` for the whole data set and `aria-rowindex` on every mounted row, so a windowed grid still reports the true position (the header is row 1).

One tab stop (roving tabindex): Tab enters the grid on its current cell and the next Tab leaves it. Arrow keys move one cell (they swap in right-to-left), Home and End go to the first and last column, Ctrl or Cmd+Home and +End to the first and last cell, PageUp and PageDown move by the visible rows. The header is row 0 of the navigation.

Editing: Enter or F2 (or double click) opens the editor, Enter saves and returns focus to the cell, Escape cancels, Tab saves and continues to the next tab stop. Enter and Escape are ignored while an IME composition is open. A rejected value keeps the editor open with `aria-invalid="true"`, the error text visible next to the cell and referenced by `aria-describedby`, and announced in the status region.
Sorting: the sorted header carries `aria-sort`; Enter or Space on a header cell, or a click on its button, cycles the direction. The change is announced ("Sorted by Name, ascending").

Resizing: each header has a visible 24px `role="separator"` handle with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`. Drag it, or Tab from the header cell onto it: ArrowRight and ArrowLeft change the width by 10px (Shift: 50px, reversed in right-to-left), Home and End jump to the limits, Escape returns to the header cell. The handle is a tab stop only while its header cell is the current cell.

Selection: rows carry `aria-selected`, the header checkbox is named "Select all rows" and is indeterminate for a partial selection, each row checkbox is "Select row n". Space toggles the row from any cell, Shift+Space or Shift+click selects a range. Cells in a Shift+Arrow block carry `aria-selected="true"`.
One polite `role="status"` region announces sorting, edits, validation errors, resizing, loading and copying. It is never used for every keystroke or scroll.

Focus is a visible 2px outline inside the cell (kept in forced-colors mode). Rows are at least 28px (44px on touch devices) and the resize handle is 24px wide. State is never colour only: errors have an icon and text, sorting has an arrow icon plus `aria-sort`, selection has a checkbox.
Cell values are text only. Hostile or very long text is truncated inside its fixed-height cell; the full value is in the editor and the copied text.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the grid has no accessible name (`label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
Throws a ContractError when `columns` is empty, when a column has no non-empty `key`, when two columns share a `key`, or when a column has no `label`.
Throws a ContractError when a `select` column has no `options`.
Throws a ContractError when `selectable` is set and a row has no string or number id, or two rows have the same id (they would be selected together).
llmNotes: Always set `label` and give every column a unique `key` and a `label`.
Bind `v-model:rows`; the grid never mutates the rows you pass, it emits a new array. React to `cell-edit` for saving, and use `validate` (return error text) instead of validating in the event.
Mark columns `editable: true` to edit them (default is read-only); use `type: "number"` or `type: "select"` with `options` for typed editors.
For many rows set a `height` and leave `virtual` on auto; rows have a fixed height and text is truncated, so do not put tall content in cells.
With `selectable`, every row needs a unique string or number `id` (or pass `rowKey`).
Cell values render as text; format with `formatter` or a `cell-<key>` slot, never with HTML strings.
Do not use it for read-only report tables: use `DataTable` (paging, cards on phones) or `Table`.
replaces: hand-rolled spreadsheet-like grid with inline editing

components.name: DataTable
components.summary: Data-array table with client-side sorting, row selection, pagination, loading and empty states.
components.description: Give `columns` and `rows`; the table renders them with `Table` parts. Sorting cycles none → asc → desc → none (stable; null/NaN/Invalid Date always last), selection is per page (header checkbox selects the visible page and keeps other pages), pagination is a built-in simple pager. `v-model:sort`, `v-model:selected` and `v-model:page` work controlled or uncontrolled. All work is client-side: for server-side paging/sorting use `Table` parts or pass pre-sorted rows without `sortable`. Without `selectable`, duplicate or missing row keys are tolerated (rendering uses a unique internal key). With `selectable`, selection stores the id from `rowKey`, so every row needs a unique string or number id: a missing or repeated one throws a ContractError, because those rows would be selected together. Name the table with `caption` or `label`. Look props (all combinable): `density`, `size`, `variant`, `striped`, `bordered`, `stickyHeader`; `layout="cards"` turns rows into cards on narrow screens. The header row is hidden visually there, so below 640px a visible control bar appears above the cards: a "Sort by" select with a direction button for the sortable columns, and a "Select all" checkbox when `selectable` is set. It writes the same `v-model:sort` and `v-model:selected` values as the header (one source of truth). Relabel it with `sortByLabel`, `sortDirectionLabel`, `sortDefaultLabel`, `sortAscendingLabel`, `sortDescendingLabel` and `selectAllLabel`, or hide it with `:card-controls="false"`.

props.name: columns
props.description: `{ key, header, sortable?, align?, numeric?, rowHeader?, width?, accessor?, class? }`. `accessor(row)` defaults to `row[key]`; `width` is an inline CSS width; `numeric` right-aligns with tabular figures; `rowHeader` renders the column as `<th scope="row">` and names the row checkbox.

props.name: rows
props.description: Source rows (never mutated).

props.name: rowKey
props.type: keyof T | ((row: T, index: number) => string | number)
props.description: Row property name or function giving a unique string or number id, used for selection. Required to resolve for every row when `selectable` is set; otherwise missing ids fall back to the row index.

props.name: sort
props.description: v-model:sort. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: selectable
props.description: Adds a leading checkbox column.

props.name: selected
props.description: v-model:selected: selected row ids. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: page
props.description: v-model:page (1-based). Out-of-range values are clamped and `update:page` is emitted with the clamped value.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: Rows per page. Undefined, 0, negative, NaN or Infinity disable pagination; fractions are floored.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows skeleton rows, sets aria-busy and hides data rows and the pager.

props.name: loadingRows
props.description: Number of skeleton rows. Defaults to the page size, else 5.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Message when there are no rows (use the `empty` slot for rich content).

props.name: nullText
props.description: Shown for null/undefined (and Invalid Date) cells.

props.name: rowClickable
props.description: Rows get tabindex=0, a pointer cursor and emit `row-click` on click / Enter / Space. Clicks from links, buttons, inputs, selects, textareas, labels and `[data-no-row-click]` are ignored.

props.name: density
props.description: Cell padding scale: `compact` (8px cells), `default` (12px) or `comfortable` (16px). Unknown values fall back to default.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size of headers and cells: `sm` 12px, `md` 14px, `lg` 16px. Independent of `density`.

props.name: variant
props.description: `default` has a rule under every row; `borderless` drops the body row rules; `filled` gives the header a muted band. Combines with `striped` and `bordered`. Unknown values fall back to default.

props.name: striped
props.description: Tint every second body row. Hover and selected styling still win.

props.name: bordered
props.description: Outer frame plus column rules.

props.name: layout
props.description: `cards`: below the `sm` breakpoint (640px) each row becomes a stacked card of label and value pairs (the labels are the column headers) and the header row is hidden visually. Sorting, selection, paging, loading and empty states keep working.

props.name: stickyHeader
props.description: Pin the header; set a height on `containerClass` (e.g. `max-h-96`).

props.name: cardControls
props.description: With `layout="cards"`, show the sort select, direction button and "Select all" checkbox below 640px (where the header row is hidden). It appears only when a column is `sortable` or `selectable` is set. Set `false` to hide it and offer your own.

props.name: sortByLabel
props.description: Visible label of the cards-layout sort select.

props.name: sortDirectionLabel
props.description: Start of the accessible name of the direction button ("Sort direction: Ascending"); its visible text is the current direction.

props.name: sortDefaultLabel
props.description: Select option that clears the sort.

props.name: sortAscendingLabel
props.description: Text for the ascending direction.

props.name: sortDescendingLabel
props.description: Text for the descending direction.

props.name: selectAllLabel
props.description: Visible label of the cards-layout "Select all" checkbox.

props.name: containerClass
props.description: Classes for the scroll container.

props.name: tableClass
props.description: Classes for the inner <table>.

props.name: caption
props.description: Visually hidden <caption> for assistive tech. Set `caption` or `label`: one of them is required.

props.name: label
props.description: aria-label for the <table>; also names the scroll region. Set `caption` or `label`: one of them is required.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the root wrapper (`data-slot="data-table"`). Other attributes also fall through to it.

slots.name: cell-<key>
slots.props: { row: T, value: unknown, column: DataTableColumn<T>, index: number }
slots.description: Custom cell content for the column with that key. `index` is the position in the source `rows`.

slots.name: cell
slots.description: Fallback custom cell content for every column without a `cell-<key>` slot.

slots.name: header-<key>
slots.description: Custom header label (rendered inside the sort button for sortable columns).

slots.name: empty
slots.description: Replaces the empty-state message.

slots.name: footer
slots.description: Content of ; provide your own ….

a11y: Native table semantics; sortable headers are buttons inside <th scope="col">. Only the sorted column carries `aria-sort` (ascending or descending); unsorted columns have no `aria-sort`. Focus stays on the header button after a sort, and a visually hidden `role="status"` announces "Sorted by Name, ascending".
Mark the identifying column `rowHeader: true` so its cells are `<th scope="row">`.
Loading sets aria-busy on the table.

Selection checkboxes are labelled "Select all rows" (header, indeterminate when partially selected) and "Select <row header text>" (or "Select row n" without a row header column). They are 20px targets with 12px cell padding around them.
The scroll container is a focusable `role="region"` named by `label` or `caption`, so a wide table scrolls with the arrow keys; `stickyHeader` pins the header inside a height-bounded container.
The pager is a <nav aria-label="Pagination">; Previous/Next are disabled at the ends and the "Page n of m" text is a polite live region with tabular figures.
Clickable rows are focusable (tabindex=0) and activate on Enter/Space.

`layout="cards"` keeps the table markup: below `sm` the elements get explicit `table`, `rowgroup`, `row`, `columnheader`, `rowheader` and `cell` roles so `display` changes do not drop table semantics, and the visual column labels are `aria-hidden` (the column header names each cell). The header row is hidden visually below `sm`; its sort buttons and select-all checkbox stay in the accessibility tree and appear when a keyboard user focuses them.

Cards layout control bar (`data-slot="table-card-controls"`, visible only below `sm`, so touch users can sort and select all without the header row): the sort select is a native `<select>` wrapped in a visible "Sort by" `<label>` (16px text, 44px high on coarse pointers); the direction button shows the current direction as text plus an arrow icon (never colour alone), is named "Sort direction: Ascending", and is disabled while no column is sorted; "Select all" is a native checkbox inside its label (a 44px target on coarse pointers) with the same indeterminate state as the header box. Everything is keyboard operable (Tab, arrow keys on the select, Space on the checkbox, Enter or Space on the button). The bar writes the same `sort` and `selected` values as the header, so `aria-sort` on the sorted `<th>` and the polite "Sorted by Name, ascending" announcement are identical whichever control sorted. Without sortable columns and without `selectable` the bar is not rendered; `:card-controls="false"` removes it.
Numeric and right-aligned columns use `tabular-nums`. Pass `caption` or `label` so the table has an accessible name.
requires: Throws a ContractError when neither `caption` nor `label` names the table.
Throws a ContractError when `columns` is empty, when a column has no non-empty `key`, when two columns share a `key`, or when a column has neither a `header` text nor a `header-<key>` slot.
Throws a ContractError when `rowKey` is neither a property name nor a function.

Throws a ContractError when `selectable` is set and a row has no string or number id, or two rows have the same id (they would be selected together). Without `selectable`, duplicate or missing ids are tolerated.
llmNotes: Give `columns` stable unique `key`s and rows a unique `id` (or pass rowKey) when using selectable.
Use v-model:sort / v-model:selected / v-model:page; do not mutate props.
Use `cell-<key>` slots for badges/actions; put buttons inside cells (clicks on them do not trigger row-click).
Always set `caption` or `label`.

Look props: `density` padding, `size` text, `variant` rules and header band, `striped`, `bordered`; `layout="cards"` for phones: below 640px it shows its own "Sort by" select, direction button and "Select all" checkbox (same `v-model:sort` / `v-model:selected` state as the header; relabel with `sortByLabel`, `sortDirectionLabel`, `sortDefaultLabel`, `sortAscendingLabel`, `sortDescendingLabel`, `selectAllLabel`; hide with `:card-controls="false"`).
Sorting and paging are client-side only; for server data, handle sorting yourself and omit `sortable`.

components.name: Table
components.summary: Styled, responsive native <table> with compound parts for hand-written tabular markup.
components.description: Use `Table` + parts when you write the rows yourself (static data, custom layouts, footers with totals). The wrapper scrolls horizontally on small screens. For data arrays with sorting, selection or pagination use `DataTable`. Do not use tables for layout. Variations (all props on `Table`, combinable): `density` (`compact`, `default`, `comfortable`) for padding; `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) for the type scale; `variant` (`default`, `borderless`, `filled`) for the row rules and header band; `layout="cards"` to turn rows into stacked cards on narrow screens (the header row is hidden there; place `TableCardControls` above the table to give touch users a visible "Sort by" select, direction button and "Select all" checkbox that drive your own sort and selection state; `DataTable` does this for you); `stickyHeader` for long scrolling tables; `striped` zebra rows to track long rows across wide tables; `bordered` outer frame + column rules for spreadsheet-like data; `:hoverable="false"` for read-only/report tables where rows are not interactive; `selectedTone="accent"` for a stronger selected-row look (primary tint + leading bar) next to `TableRow selected`. `density`, `size`, `variant`, `layout` and `stickyHeader` reach cells through `group/table` data attributes and provide/inject; `striped`, `hoverable` and `selectedTone` reach `TableRow` the same way, so rows and cells must be inside a `Table`. On cells, `valign` sets the vertical alignment and `label` names the cell in the cards layout.

props.name: size

props.name: variant
props.description: `default` has a rule under every row; `borderless` drops the body row rules (the header keeps its rule; forced-colors mode still draws them); `filled` gives the header row a muted band. Combines with `striped` and `bordered`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

a11y: Native table semantics (caption, thead/tbody/tfoot, th scope). Use `<TableHead scope="row">` for the cell that names a row.

The scroll container is `tabindex="0"` so keyboard users can scroll a wide table with the arrow keys, and is a `role="region"` named by `label`, the table `aria-label` or the caption when one exists. It shows the shared focus ring.
Stripes, borders and selection tint are visual only: selection must also be exposed non-visually (a checkbox or aria-selected on grid rows).
Give every table a caption (use `hidden` for sr-only) or an aria-label.
Put aria-sort on the sortable TableHead that is currently sorted; do not set `aria-sort="none"` on the others.
Numeric cells use `tabular-nums` and align to the end edge. `left` and `right` alignment are logical, so RTL mirrors them.

`layout="cards"` keeps real table markup: below `sm` the table, row groups, rows and cells get explicit `table`, `rowgroup`, `row`, `columnheader`, `rowheader` and `cell` roles so screen readers still announce a table after `display` changes. The cell `label` is `aria-hidden` (the column header already names the cell). The header row is hidden visually below `sm` (it stays in the accessibility tree and appears when a keyboard user tabs into it), so touch users cannot reach sort buttons or a select-all checkbox in it: render `TableCardControls` (visible only below `sm`) above the table, bind its `v-model:sort`, and apply the same state to your rows and your `aria-sort`, so the bar and the header stay one source of truth. It is a labelled native select, a direction button with text and an icon, and a "Select all" checkbox, with 44px targets on coarse pointers.
`variant="borderless"` keeps row rules in forced-colors mode (they are transparent borders); `filled` is a header band, not a state.
Responsive: the table keeps its natural width and scrolls inside its region instead of widening the page; `stickyHeader` keeps the header visible inside a height-bounded container.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the table has no accessible name: add a `TableCaption`, or set `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

Throws a ContractError when a `TableHead` is not inside a `TableRow`, or when a `scope="col"` (or `colgroup`) `TableHead` is not inside `TableHeader`. Row headers use `scope="row"` and may sit in `TableBody`.
Throws a ContractError when a `TableRow` is rendered outside a `Table`.
llmNotes: Use Table parts for static markup; use DataTable for arrays of rows.
Always render TableHead cells inside TableHeader > TableRow.
Use `numeric` on TableCell for numbers so columns align.

Use `density` for padding, `size` for text, `variant` for rules and header band; do not set `class` to change them. Use `layout="cards"` with a `label` on every TableCell when the table must work on phones, and add `TableCardControls` above it when phones need sorting or select-all.
Choose Table props by need: `striped` for wide tables, `bordered` for spreadsheet-like data, `density="compact"` for dense views, `:hoverable="false"` for read-only tables.
Use `selected` on TableRow for selected rows and `selectedTone="accent"` on Table for a stronger look; add aria-selected yourself only for grid tables.
TableRow striping, hover and selection tone only apply inside a Table (provide/inject).
Sticky header requires a bounded container height (containerClass="max-h-96").
Do not use tables for layout.

components.name: BlogCard
components.summary: Article teaser card: cover image, category badge, title link, excerpt and author/date/read-time meta.
components.description: Use in blog indexes, "latest posts" strips and related-article lists. Renders a semantic `<article>`; the title is a link stretched over the whole card (the card is one tab stop and one click target), so do not nest other links in it. A valid ISO `date` renders `<time datetime>`; any other string is shown as plain text. `vertical` stacks image over text, `horizontal` places a fixed-width image beside the text from `sm`, `featured` is a large hero card (image 60% from `lg`, bigger title). For several cards use `BlogGrid`.

props.name: title
props.description: Post title; becomes the link text when `href` is set. Must not be empty.

props.name: excerpt
props.description: Short summary (the default slot overrides it).

props.name: href
props.description: Post URL. When set the title is a link stretched over the whole card; otherwise the title is plain text.

props.name: image
props.description: Cover image URL. A missing or broken image leaves a neutral placeholder (or no image block when unset).

props.name: imageAlt
props.description: Alt text of the cover. Required with `image`; an empty string marks it decorative (the title is adjacent text).

props.name: category
props.description: Category shown as a Badge.

props.name: author
props.description: Author name in the meta line.

props.name: date
props.description: ISO 8601 date (`2024-03-01`, `2024-03-01T10:00:00Z`). Valid: `<time datetime>` with a formatted label. Invalid (`"Last Tuesday"`, `2024-02-31`): shown as plain text in a span, no `datetime`.

props.name: readTime
props.description: A number means minutes (`5` -> "5 min read"; zero, negative and non-finite render nothing); a string is shown as given.

props.name: variant
props.description: Layout; unknown values fall back to `vertical`.

props.name: size
props.description: Padding, gaps, title and text scale. `sm` is compact (16px padding, `text-base` title), `md` is the original, `lg` is roomy (24px padding, `text-xl` title, 16px excerpt). The featured layout scales the same way. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corners: `rounded` is the original 8px radius, `square` has none (the cover image is clipped to the same shape). Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.

props.name: appearance
props.description: `card` is the original bordered surface. `plain` has no fill and a transparent border (the content sits straight on the page; the border appears in forced-colors mode). `filled` uses the secondary surface with secondary-foreground text and no visible border. Unknown values fall back to `card`.

props.name: level
props.description: Heading element level of the title; invalid values fall back to 3.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale used to format a valid `date` (always in UTC, so server and client agree). Unsupported locales fall back to `en-US`.

a11y: Root is an `<article>`; the title is a heading (`level`, default 3: set it to fit the page outline) containing the only link, stretched over the card with a pseudo-element so the whole card is one focus target (well above 24px, and the card is one tab stop).
Keyboard: Tab focuses the title link, Enter follows it. The focus ring surrounds the whole card; in forced-colors mode an outline replaces the ring.
The cover image is decorative by default (`imageAlt=""`); give it alt text only when it carries information.
Valid dates use `<time datetime>`; the visible text is formatted for the `locale`. Separator dots in the meta line are aria-hidden.

`size`, `shape` and `appearance` change padding, corners and surface only; the title link, heading level and focus handling are the same in every combination. `plain` and `filled` keep a transparent 1px border, so the focus ring (and the forced-colors outline) still surrounds the whole card, and the box does not shift between appearances. Text colours use token pairs checked for contrast: foreground on background (plain), card-foreground on card, secondary-foreground on secondary (filled).
Layouts reflow to one column on a 320px screen (`horizontal` and `featured` only go side by side from `sm` / `lg`); long words wrap (`overflow-wrap:anywhere`). Nothing animates on hover.

Set `level` to fit the page outline (default 3 under an h2 section heading).
Use `appearance="plain"` for dense indexes on a page background and `filled` for related-post strips on a card surface; keep `card` for general use. Keep one `size` per list.

props.name: label

props.description: Merged last; wins over internal classes. Pass `static` to render the strip in the page flow, as the galleries below do.

requires: Throws a ContractError when the progress bar has no accessible name (`label` emptied and no `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
a11y: role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin/max (0-100), aria-valuenow, aria-valuetext ("42%") and an aria-label (`label`, default "Reading progress"). It is not focusable, has no keyboard map and never takes pointer events.
`size`, `tone` and `variant` change looks only: the role, name and value text are the same in every combination. `tone` is colour only, so the percentage in `aria-valuetext` stays the signal.
The bar is smoothed with `motion-safe:transition-transform`, so reduced-motion users get position updates without animation. Nothing flashes or loops.
In forced-colors mode the fill is drawn as a 4px bottom border in the text colour, because background colours are overridden there.
The bar fills from the start edge, so it mirrors in right-to-left pages (`rtl:origin-right`).

It is a 4px bar fixed to the viewport edge (2px to 6px with `size`; `inset` sits 0.5rem from the edge), so it never affects reflow at 320px and does not cover content that scrolls into view (it is thinner than any focus indicator).
llmNotes: Mount once per page, not per section.
Do not use for form or upload progress; use Progress from feedback.
It tracks the whole document, not an inner scroll container.

components.name: ContactLink
components.summary: mailto: or tel: link with a leading icon, as an inline link, a button (filled, outline or ghost) or a card.
components.description: Use for email addresses and phone numbers in headers, footers and contact sections. For `tel` the display text keeps your formatting while the href is reduced to dialable characters. A missing value renders plain text instead of a dead link. `variant` picks the look: `inline` (text link), `button` (filled button), `outline` (bordered button), `ghost` (borderless button with a fill on hover) or `card` (bordered block with a bare icon, the `label` as headline and the raw `value` beneath it); `size` scales text, icon and padding; `tone` picks the colour (primary, neutral or muted) and `shape` the corners (rounded, pill or square). Tone and shape never change the accessible name or the `mailto:` / `tel:` target.

props.name: type
props.description: Link scheme. Unknown values behave as email.

props.name: value
props.description: Address or number. Empty renders a non-link span.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible text; defaults to `value`. In the `card` variant it is the headline and `value` is shown as the secondary line when they differ.

props.name: subject
props.description: mailto subject (email only), URL-encoded automatically.

props.name: icon
props.description: Override the default envelope/phone icon.

props.name: noIcon
props.description: Hide the icon (and the icon tile in `card`).

props.name: variant
props.description: Look. `button` is filled, `outline` has a border and a hover fill, `ghost` has no border and a hover fill (a border appears in forced-colors mode). Unknown values fall back to `inline`. Reflected as `data-variant`.

props.name: tone
props.description: Colour. `inline` and `ghost`: text in primary, foreground or muted-foreground. `button`: primary fill, foreground fill with background text, or secondary fill. `outline`: border and text in primary, foreground (input border) or muted-foreground. `card`: icon colour. Neutral and muted inline links are underlined so colour is not the only cue. Applies to real links only; a non-link span keeps the surrounding colour. Unknown values fall back to `primary`. Reflected as `data-tone`.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corners: the original radius of the variant (`rounded-sm` inline, `rounded-md` buttons, `rounded-lg` card), `rounded-full`, or none. Also shapes the focus ring. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Reflected as `data-shape`.

props.name: size
props.description: Text, icon and padding scale (button minimum heights 2 / 2.25 / 2.75rem). Unknown values fall back to `md`. Reflected as `data-size`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the root; wins over internal classes.

slots.description: Replaces the visible text (the headline in the `card` variant).

a11y: A real anchor (`mailto:` or `tel:`) whose name is its visible text; the icon is decorative (aria-hidden). Use `label` when the raw value is not meaningful to read aloud; keep the visible text inside the accessible name.

`variant`, `tone` and `shape` change the look only: the element, the `href`, the visible text (the accessible name) and the aria-hidden icon are identical in every combination. Text colours use checked pairs: primary, foreground and muted-foreground on the page background, primary-foreground on primary, background on foreground, secondary-foreground on secondary, accent-foreground on the hover fill. `ghost` and `outline` keep a border in forced-colors mode so the target stays visible.
Keyboard: Tab to focus, Enter to follow. Visible focus ring. A missing value renders a plain span, not a dead link.

Targets are at least 24px tall (button and card more) and 44px on coarse pointers; the button grows with its text instead of clipping at 200% zoom, and long labels wrap (`break-words`) so the card reflows at 320px.
requires: Throws a ContractError when the link has no text: no `value`, no `label` and no default slot content.
llmNotes: Choose `variant`: inline inside text or footers, button for a primary contact call to action, outline or ghost for a secondary one next to it, card for a contact section with several channels (give each a `label` such as "Email us").
Keep `tone="primary"` unless the page already has a stronger accent; `neutral` and `muted` suit footers. Use `shape="pill"` only when the neighbouring buttons are pills too.
Use ContactLink instead of hand-writing mailto:/tel: anchors.
Never embed unvalidated user input as `value`.
Use only addresses and numbers that exist; the docs samples are placeholders.
Do not set `href` yourself; it is derived from `value`.
replaces: hand-rolled ContactLink markup in app code

components.name: ContactSection
components.summary: Contact page section: heading plus a `form` slot and a `details` slot in split, centered, card or inline layouts.
components.description: Layout shell for contact pages. It owns the heading and arrangement only; put your own form (Field/Input/Textarea/Button) in the `form` slot and addresses, phone numbers or ContactLinks in the `details` slot. It does no validation and no network access. `split` shows heading and details beside the form on large screens, `centered` stacks heading, form and details in one column, `card` is `split` inside a bordered surface, `inline` is a compact one-row strip (heading and description left, form and details right) for a short form such as a single question. `size` scales gaps and surface padding, `tone="muted"` gives the section a secondary surface and `align="center"` centres the text of `split` and `card`. Works with any subset of slots.

props.name: variant
props.description: Layout. `inline` is compact: heading and description on the left, form and details in one block on the right from `lg` (one column below). Unknown values fall back to `split`.

props.name: size
props.description: Gaps, padding of a surface (`card` or a muted tone), heading scale and details text. `md` is the original. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: tone
props.description: `default` has no fill (`card` keeps `bg-card`). `muted` gives every layout a bordered secondary surface with secondary-foreground text. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: align
props.description: `center` centres the heading and details of `split` and `card`. `centered` is always centred and `inline` always start-aligned. Unknown values fall back to `start`. Reflected as `data-align`.

props.name: eyebrow
props.description: Short label above the title. Plain text; use only when it adds information the title lacks.

props.name: title
props.description: Section title. State what the section is for ("Ask about the library"), not a generic "Contact".

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting paragraph under the title.

props.name: level
props.description: Heading element level of the title; invalid values fall back to 2.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: form
slots.description: The contact form (any content).

slots.name: details
slots.description: Contact details: addresses, phone, email, hours, ContactLink/SocialLinks. Sits under the heading (split, card) or below the form (centered).

<ContactSection variant="split" title="Ask about the library" description="Write to the maintainers with a question about a component.">
  <template #details>
    <ContactLink type="email" value="name@example.com" />
    <ContactLink type="tel" value="+15550100" label="+1 555 0100" />
  </template>
  <template #form>
    <form class="space-y-4" @submit.prevent="onSubmit">
      <Field label="Name"><Input name="name" autocomplete="name" /></Field>
      <Field label="Email"><Input name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" /></Field>
      <Field label="Message"><Textarea name="message" /></Field>
      <Button type="submit">Send message</Button>
    </form>
  </template>
</ContactSection>

        <Button type="submit">Send the question</Button>

    <ContactLink type="email" value="name@example.com" />
  </template>
  <template #form>
    <form class="space-y-3" @submit.prevent="onSubmit">
        <Field label="Email"><Input name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" /></Field>
        <Button type="submit">Send the question</Button>
      </form>
