a11y: Renders a plain `<section>` with no landmark name: labelling every section would make each a `region` landmark, which dilutes navigation and fails landmark-unique when repeated. Add your own `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` only if the section deserves to be a landmark.
The title renders at `level` (default h2); keep heading levels sequential on the page.

The form is yours: give every field a visible label (use `Field`), `autocomplete` tokens, `aria-invalid` plus a described error, and a live status for the result. The component does no validation and no network access.

Every layout, `size`, `tone` and `align` keeps the same DOM order (heading, form, details) so the reading order and tab order do not change; `inline` only places the form and the details in one block on the right. A muted surface carries a border so it is still outlined in forced-colors mode. Text on it uses secondary-foreground (and muted-foreground for the description) on the secondary surface.
Reflows at 320px: the grid is one column below `lg`, content uses `min-w-0`, and the layouts use no left/right offsets, so RTL mirrors.
requires: Throws a ContractError when a `<form>` inside the component has no submit handler (`@submit` / `@submit.prevent`) and no `action`, because it would submit nowhere.
llmNotes: Put the form in the `form` slot and contact info in the `details` slot; this component does not validate or submit.
Use `split` by default, `centered` for short forms, `card` when the page background is plain and the block needs a surface.
Use `inline` for a one-question strip, `tone="muted"` when the section needs to stand out from the page, `size="sm"` in dense pages and `align="center"` only for short headings with few details.
Use NewsletterSignup, not this, for a single email field.
A form with no `@submit` handler submits nowhere; always wire one or remove the form.
Wrap form fields in `Field`.

components.name: InstallTabs
components.summary: Tabbed install/code snippets with a copy button.

The tablist has an accessible name (`label`), the selected tab has aria-selected="true" and a roving tabindex (only it is in the Tab order), and the panel is named by its tab with aria-labelledby. There is no aria-controls, because the inactive panels are not rendered.

Keyboard: ArrowRight / ArrowLeft move to the next / previous tab and wrap (the arrows swap in a right-to-left page), Home and End jump to the first and last tab, selection follows focus, and Tab moves on to the panel and then the copy button.

The panel is `tabindex="0"` and scrolls horizontally (`overflow-x-auto`), so long commands are reachable by keyboard; its focus outline is drawn inset (2px, `outline-solid`, using the shared `insetFocus` helper) so the frame never clips it.

The copy button is a real button with the visible name "Copy" (WCAG 2.5.3: the visible text is the name). Its result, "Copied" or "Copy failed", replaces the button text and is announced through a persistent `role="status"` region outside the button.
Tabs and the copy button are at least 24px tall and 44px on coarse pointers. In forced-colors mode the active tab is underlined because backgrounds and rings are overridden.
llmNotes: Choose `variant`: default inside content sections, minimal inside docs prose or a hero, contained over images or tinted backgrounds. Use `size="lg"` for hero commands and `sm` for sidebars.
Keep snippets short (one command per tab).
Listen to `copy-error` if you need a fallback UI; copying needs a secure context (HTTPS).
Use unique tab labels.

components.name: NumberedSteps
components.summary: Numbered steps for how-it-works and onboarding sequences: cards, timeline, horizontal, minimal or with media.
components.description: Use to explain a short ordered process (3-6 steps). Renders a semantic `<ol>` in every variant. Numbers are kept because the steps are an ordered sequence; do not use it for lists that have no order. `variant` picks the layout: `default` (bordered card with the number beside the text), `cards` (number above the text), `timeline` (single column with a vertical connector line), `horizontal` (one row from `sm` upward with a connector between numbers), `minimal` (no boxes, large bare numbers and divider lines) and `with-media` (text next to an image per step, alternating sides on `md`+). `columns` applies to `default`, `cards` and `minimal`; the other variants are single-column or flow by step count. Show the real steps in the real product where you can (`with-media`). For feature lists without order use `FeatureGrid`; for interactive wizards use a stepper from the navigation group.

props.name: steps
props.description: `{ title: string, description?: string, media?: string, mediaAlt?: string }`. `media`/`mediaAlt` are used by the `with-media` variant only.

props.name: variant
props.description: Layout. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Reflected as `data-variant`.

props.name: size
props.description: Marker size (32, 40 or 48px), title and description scale, item padding and gaps. Timeline and horizontal connector lines move with the marker. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: tone
props.description: Marker colour. Filled markers use `primary` / `primary-foreground`, `foreground` / `background` (neutral), `success` / `success-foreground` or `info` / `info-foreground`. The outlined timeline marker and the bare `minimal` number use the tone colour on the page background. Unknown values fall back to `primary`. Use `success` and `info` only when the colour means something; the number carries the order.

props.name: shape
props.description: Marker shape: `circle` (the original), `rounded` (6px radius) or `square`. The bare number of `minimal` has no box and ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `circle`.

props.name: align
props.description: `center` centres the marker against the text in row layouts (`default`, `minimal`, `with-media`) and centres the whole step in `cards`. `timeline` and `horizontal` always start-align because their connector lines begin at the marker. Unknown values fall back to `start`. Reflected as `data-align`.

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns on large screens for `default`, `cards` and `minimal`; ignored by `timeline`, `horizontal` and `with-media`. Invalid falls back to 3.

props.name: pad
props.description: Two-digit numbers (01, 02...).

props.name: level
props.description: Heading level of step titles; invalid falls back to 3.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the root `<ol>`; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: step
slots.description: Replaces a whole step's content (number, text and media) inside the `<li>`; the variant's item styling stays.

slots.name: media
slots.description: Custom media for the `with-media` variant (video, illustration, component). Takes precedence over `step.media`; ignored by other variants.

requires: Throws a ContractError when a step has an empty `title` and the `step` slot is not used (the first one is named by index).
a11y: Ordered list semantics in every variant; the visual number is aria-hidden and the title includes a screen-reader-only "N." prefix.

`size`, `tone`, `shape` and `align` change the look only: the order, the screen-reader numbers and the aria-hidden marker are identical in every combination. `tone` never replaces the number, so colour is not the only carrier of order. Marker colours use checked token pairs (primary-foreground on primary, background on foreground, success-foreground on success, info-foreground on info; tone text on the page background for the outlined and bare markers). Marker sizes are decorative (the sequence is announced by the list), so the 24px target rule does not apply.
Connector lines and marker circles are purely decorative (CSS only). They are positioned with logical offsets (`start`/`end`), so RTL mirrors them.
Columns collapse to one on phones; every variant reflows at 320px. Item surfaces use a border, not a shadow.
Give `mediaAlt` a real description when the image carries information; it is empty (decorative) when omitted. Custom `media` slot content owns its own accessibility.
llmNotes: Use only for a real ordered sequence. Keep to 3-6 steps with short titles, and prefer showing the actual steps with `with-media`.

Choose `variant`: default or cards for 3-4 equal steps, timeline for long or detailed sequences, horizontal for 3-5 very short steps on wide layouts, minimal for editorial pages, with-media when each step has a screenshot.
Use `columns` equal to the step count up to 4 (default, cards, minimal only).
Keep `tone` as `primary` unless the colour carries meaning (for example `success` for finished steps); use `neutral` on pages that already have a strong accent. Use one `size` per list.
Use the `step` slot only when you need custom markup; you then own accessibility of the number.
Prefer `step.media` for images and the `media` slot only for non-image media.

components.name: FeatureCard
components.summary: Card that presents one feature: icon, title, description and optional link, in eight variants.
components.description: Use inside `FeatureGrid` (or any grid) to describe a feature. Pick the look with `variant`, scale it with `size`, paint it with `tone` and choose corners with `shape`. Variants: `card` (default: border, no shadow, bare accent icon), `bordered` (heavier outline), `flat` (muted surface, no border), `icon-left` (row layout), `icon-top` (icon above the text), `icon-badge` (borderless with a tinted icon tile; opt-in, because a tinted square above every title is a stock look), `minimal` (no box) and `highlight` (primary border for the one feature that matters). `align="center"` centres the content. The card has no hover effect because it is not interactive; only its link is. Icons are optional: leave them out unless they depict the specific feature. For numbered processes use `NumberedSteps`.

props.name: icon
props.description: FontAwesome-shaped icon definition, drawn in the accent colour. Choose one that depicts the feature; omit it otherwise.

props.name: title
props.description: Feature name and card heading. Required unless the `title` slot is used.

props.name: description
props.description: Short explanation.

props.name: href
props.description: Renders a link at the bottom when set.

props.name: linkLabel
props.description: Link text. Defaults to `Read about <title>` (or `Read more` without a title). Name what happens, not a generic invitation.

props.name: external
props.description: Open link in a new tab with rel="noopener noreferrer"; adds an external-link icon and a screen reader note.

props.name: level
props.description: Heading level of the title; invalid falls back to 3. Keep it one level below the section heading.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style. Unknown values fall back to `card`. Exposed as `data-variant`.

props.name: align
props.description: Content alignment. With `icon-left` the icon stays beside the text and the text stays at the start. Unknown values fall back to `left`. Exposed as `data-align`.

props.name: size
props.description: Padding and type scale: `sm` = p-4 with a 16px title, `md` = p-6 with an 18px title (the original look), `lg` = p-8 with a 20px title and 16px description. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Exposed as `data-size`.

props.name: tone
props.description: Surface colour. `default` keeps the variant's own surface; `muted` paints the muted surface, `primary` the primary colour and `inverted` the foreground colour, with matching text, icon and link colours. `minimal` and `icon-badge` get padding and rounded corners when a tone is set. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Exposed as `data-tone`.

props.name: shape
props.description: `square` removes the corner radius of the card and of the `icon-badge` tile. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Exposed as `data-shape`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: icon
slots.description: Replaces the icon (any element); still wrapped in the variant icon wrapper.

slots.name: title
slots.description: Replaces the title text.

slots.name: default

a11y: Icons are decorative (aria-hidden). The title is a heading chosen by `level` (default h3); keep the heading order valid under the section heading.

The DOM order (icon, title, description, link) is the same in every variant. Cards are not interactive; only the link is focusable, with a visible focus ring and a 24px minimum height (44px on coarse pointers).
Link text is descriptive (`Read about <title>` by default). External links add an icon and a screen-reader note that they open in a new tab.
Text wraps and the card uses `min-w-0`, so it reflows at 320px; alignment uses logical values so RTL works.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is neither a non-empty `title` nor a `title` slot.
llmNotes: Always give `title`; keep descriptions under about 140 characters.
Pass FontAwesome IconDefinition objects, not names, and only icons that depict the feature. Skip the icon when none fits.
Name the link action in `linkLabel` ("Open the data table docs"). Never a generic invitation.
Use `external` for off-site links.

Choose `card` as the safe default, `flat` or `minimal` for dense sections, `bordered` on tinted backgrounds, `icon-left` for stacked lists and `highlight` for one key feature. `icon-badge` is available but is a stock look: use it sparingly.
Use `align="center"` for short centred sections; do not centre long descriptions.

Use `size` for density (`sm` in dense grids, `lg` for a lone feature), `tone="primary"` or `"inverted"` on one card per section, and `shape="square"` only when the surrounding layout has square corners.
Inside FeatureGrid prefer its `variant` prop over styling each card.

components.name: FeatureGrid
components.summary: Feature section in six layouts (grid, list, alternating, bento, centered, with-heading) built from an items array or slot content.
components.description: Use to show 3-12 product features. Pass `items` for the common case, or place your own `FeatureCard`s (or any element) in the default slot. `layout` chooses the arrangement: `grid` (default, 1 column on mobile, 2 from `sm`, then `columns` from `lg`), `list` (stacked icon-left rows), `alternating` (text next to an image, flipping sides every row), `bento` (tiles of mixed width via `span`), `centered` (centred, unboxed cards) and `with-heading` (a built-in SectionHeading above a grid; any of `eyebrow`/`title`/`description` also adds the heading in other layouts). `variant` is passed to every generated card; without it each layout picks a default (`grid`: card, `list`: icon-left, `alternating`: minimal, `bento`: card, `centered`: minimal). Generated items render as a real `ul` with `li` children. When a heading is present the root is a wrapper and the list is the inner `feature-grid-items`. Content placed in the default slot renders in a plain grid `div` without list semantics, so any element is valid there. Give the feature that matters more extra weight (`span`, `variant: "highlight"`) instead of repeating identical cards.

props.name: layout
props.description: Arrangement of the items. Unknown values fall back to `grid`. Exposed as `data-layout`.

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns on large screens for `grid`, `bento`, `centered` and `with-heading`; invalid falls back to 3. Ignored by `list` and `alternating`.

props.name: items
props.description: Cards to render: `{ icon?, title, description?, href?, linkLabel?, external?, span?, image?, imageAlt?, variant? }`. `span` (1-4, clamped to `columns`) is used by `bento`; `image`/`imageAlt` by `alternating`; `variant` overrides the grid variant for that item.

props.name: level
props.description: Heading level for generated cards.

props.name: variant
props.description: FeatureCard variant for generated cards. Omitted = the layout default. Unknown values fall back to `card`. The resolved value is exposed as `data-variant` on the root, also when the cards come from the slot.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of card content and of the built-in heading. `centered` layout always centres.

props.name: gap
props.description: Spacing between items. `md` keeps each layout's own spacing; `sm` tightens and `lg` loosens it. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Exposed as `data-gap`.

props.name: size
props.description: FeatureCard `size` for generated cards (padding and type scale). Cards placed in the slot keep their own props. Exposed as `data-size`.

props.name: tone
props.description: FeatureCard `tone` for generated cards. Exposed as `data-tone`.

props.name: shape
props.description: FeatureCard `shape` for generated cards. Exposed as `data-shape`.

props.name: eyebrow
props.description: Built-in SectionHeading eyebrow.

props.name: title
props.description: Built-in SectionHeading title.

props.name: description
props.description: Built-in SectionHeading description.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Element level of the built-in heading title (cards use `level`).

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last; lands on the root (the wrapper when a heading is shown).

slots.name: default
slots.description: Custom cards; replaces `items` rendering (in every layout).

slots.name: heading
slots.description: Replaces the built-in SectionHeading and forces the heading wrapper.

slots.name: media
slots.description: `alternating` layout: media for each row instead of `item.image`.

a11y: Generated items are a native `ul` with `li` children (cards, or rows in `alternating`), so axe `aria-required-children` and `aria-allowed-role` pass. Slot content is a plain grid `div` with no list role; wrap items in your own list element if you need list semantics.
Alternating images need a meaningful `imageAlt`; an empty alt marks the image decorative. Text comes first in DOM order, so reading order does not change when rows flip.

Layout is 1 column on phones, 2 from `sm` and `columns` from `lg`, so it reflows at 320px. Cards use `min-w-0` and logical alignment for RTL. Heading levels are configurable: `headingLevel` for the section heading and `level` for the cards.
requires: Throws a ContractError when an entry of `items` has no non-empty `title` (the message names the first failing index).
Throws a ContractError when, in the `alternating` layout, an entry of `items` has an `image` but no `imageAlt` string and there is no `media` slot. An empty string marks the image decorative.
llmNotes: Use `items` unless cards need custom content.
Give the feature that matters more extra room with `span` or `variant: "highlight"` instead of repeating identical cards, or use the `list` layout.
Give `alternating` images an `imageAlt` that describes the real screenshot.
Pick `columns` 3 for 3/6/9 items, 4 for 4/8, 2 for 2/4.
Use `layout="with-heading"` (or just set `title`) instead of stacking SectionHeading + FeatureGrid by hand.

Choose `grid` for 3-12 equal features, `list` for narrow columns, `alternating` for 2-4 features that deserve a screenshot each, `bento` for one or two hero features among small ones (give those `span: 2`), `centered` for short icon+title+text rows.
Pass `variant` on the grid, not on each item, unless one item must stand out (`variant: "highlight"`).
Do not set `span`/`image` outside `bento`/`alternating`; they are ignored.

components.name: NewsletterSignup
components.summary: Single-field email signup with validation; the parent performs the request and drives `status`.
components.description: Presentational newsletter form. It validates the address (simple pattern), emits `subscribe` with the trimmed email and renders whatever `status` the parent sets: `loading` disables the button (aria-busy) and ignores further submits, `success` shows `successMessage`, `error` shows `errorMessage`. It never makes a network call itself: the form submits nowhere until you handle `subscribe`, so always wire the event or remove the component. `inline` puts input and button in a row from `sm`, `stacked` is a centred narrow column, `card` is a stacked form on a bordered surface, `split` puts the copy on the left and the form on the right from `lg` (one column below). `size` scales the controls, title and spacing, and `shape` rounds the field and the button as rounded, pill or square. For multi-field forms use `ContactSection` with your own form.

props.name: variant
props.description: Layout. `split` places the title and description on the left and the form and its messages on the right from `lg`; below `lg` it is one column in reading order. Without a title or description the form is not pushed to the right column. Unknown values fall back to `inline`.

props.name: size
props.description: Controls, title, description and spacing. `sm`: 36px controls, `md`: the original 44px, `lg`: 48px controls and a larger title. Touch pointers keep a 44px minimum height and the field keeps 16px text on small screens at every size. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corners of the email field and the button: 6px (the original), fully round (the field gets extra inline padding) or none. The field keeps its border and focus ring. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.

props.name: status
props.description: Controlled by the parent after handling `subscribe`; unknown values fall back to `idle`.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: Email value for `v-model`. Optional: without it the component keeps its own value.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading text (or use the `title` slot).

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting text under the title (or use the `description` slot).

props.name: level
props.description: Heading element level of the title; invalid values fall back to 2.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Input placeholder.

props.name: buttonLabel
props.description: Submit button text.

props.name: label
props.description: Visually hidden label of the input (accessible name).

props.name: successMessage
props.description: Shown (role="status") while `status` is `success`.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Shown (role="alert") while `status` is `error`.

props.name: invalidMessage
props.description: Shown (role="alert") when the typed email fails validation; also sets aria-invalid on the input and moves focus to it.

props.name: resetOnSuccess
props.description: Clear the input (and emit `update:modelValue` with `""`) when `status` becomes `success`.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last; wins over internal classes. Attributes fall through to the root element.

slots.name: title
slots.description: Rich title content; replaces the `title` prop.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Rich description content; replaces the `description` prop.

emits.name: subscribe
emits.description: Fired on a valid submit with the trimmed email. Not fired for invalid emails, nor while `status` is `loading`.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Fired on every input and on reset after success.

a11y: The input has a visually hidden `<label>` (`label` prop) and `type="email"` with `autocomplete="email"`. Keyboard: Tab to the input and the button, Enter submits. The row stacks below `sm`, so it reflows at 320px, and the input text uses `text-start` for RTL.

Invalid input sets `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby` pointing at the error message (`role="alert"`), and moves focus to the input (native validation is off with `novalidate`, so the component does it). The input shows the invalid state with a border, not colour alone, and clears it as soon as the value becomes valid.
A server error (`status="error"`) is announced via `role="alert"` and linked with `aria-describedby`; success uses a persistent `role="status"` live region.
While loading the button is disabled with `aria-busy="true"`, the form has `aria-busy`, and the input is read-only so typing is not lost.

`variant`, `size` and `shape` change layout, scale and corners only. The label, the `type="email"` field, the submit button, the alert and status regions and the `aria-busy` handling are identical in every combination. Controls keep a 44px minimum on touch pointers and 16px text below `md`; the pill field gets extra inline padding so the text stays off the curve, and the border and focus ring follow the shape (a `Highlight` outline replaces the ring in forced-colors mode).

The form is named by the title (`aria-labelledby`) when one is set, which makes it a form landmark: give every newsletter form on a page a different title (or none). Native browser validation is disabled (`novalidate`) so messages are consistent.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no `@subscribe` listener: the form only emits `subscribe`, so without one it submits nowhere.
Throws a ContractError when `label` or `buttonLabel` is an empty string (the input and the button need accessible names).
llmNotes: The form submits nowhere on its own: always handle `@subscribe`.
Handle `@subscribe`, set `status="loading"` immediately, then `success` or `error` when your request finishes; the component does no network I/O.
Never set `status` to `loading` without a pending request; the button stays disabled until you change it.

Use `split` for a wide band with a heading and the form side by side; give it a title or description so the form sits in the right column. Keep one `size` and one `shape` per page, matching the neighbouring buttons.
Choose `inline` for wide bands, `stacked` for footers/narrow columns, `card` for sidebars or plain backgrounds.
Use `v-model` plus `reset-on-success` to clear the field after success.
The `subscribe` payload is the trimmed email string, already validated.

components.name: BeforeAfter
components.summary: Image comparison slider, horizontal or vertical: drag or use the keyboard to reveal the before and after images.
components.description: Use to compare two images with identical framing (renovations, retouching, UI redesigns). `orientation="horizontal"` (default) splits left/right; `orientation="vertical"` stacks before on top of after and the divider moves up/down. The divider is a real ARIA slider: pointer drag on either axis, arrow keys (step, Shift = 5x), PageUp/PageDown, Home/End. Position is a percentage of the width (height when vertical) showing "before" (0 = all "after", 100 = all "before") and is clamped; non-numeric values fall back to 50. Supports `v-model` or uncontrolled via `start`.

props.name: before
props.description: Image URL on the left (top when vertical). Missing = neutral placeholder.

props.name: after
props.description: Image URL on the right (bottom when vertical). Missing = accent placeholder.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Divider axis. Unknown values fall back to `horizontal`. Reflected as `data-orientation` and `aria-orientation`.

props.name: showLabels
props.description: Show the decorative labels. `false` is the same as `variant="none"`. The slider's `aria-valuetext` always names both sides.

props.name: variant
props.description: Label placement. `overlay` puts a chip in the corner of each image, `bar` docks one opaque caption strip along the bottom edge, `none` shows no labels. Unknown values fall back to `overlay`. Reflected as `data-variant`.

props.name: size
props.description: Handle and label size. Hit area 2rem, 2.5rem or 3rem wide; knob 1.75rem, 2.25rem or 2.75rem. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Reflected as `data-size`.

props.name: shape
props.description: Frame corners (and label chips): `rounded-lg` or none. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Reflected as `data-shape`.

props.name: tone
props.description: Colour of the divider line and grip: the background colour, the primary colour (grip text uses primary-foreground) or the foreground colour (grip text uses background). Unknown values fall back to `default`. Reflected as `data-tone`.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Handle style. `knob` is a line with a round grip and two arrows, `bar` a line with a short rounded grip, `line` a thicker line only. Unknown values fall back to `knob`. Reflected as `data-appearance`.

props.name: beforeAlt
props.description: Alt text for the before image. Required with `before`; an empty string marks it decorative.

props.name: afterAlt
props.description: Alt text for the after image. Required with `after`; an empty string marks it decorative.

props.name: beforeLabel
props.description: Corner label and slider text.

props.name: afterLabel
props.description: Corner label and slider text.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: Divider position 0-100 (v-model): % of the width (height when vertical) showing "before". Clamped.

props.name: start
props.description: Initial position when uncontrolled.

props.name: step
props.description: Keyboard step in percent; invalid falls back to 2.

props.name: aspect
props.description: CSS aspect ratio "w / h"; invalid falls back to 16 / 9.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the slider.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the root; wins over internal classes.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Position changed by pointer or keyboard.

a11y: The divider handle is role="slider" (tabindex 0) with aria-valuemin 0, aria-valuemax 100, aria-valuenow, aria-valuetext ("40% Before, 60% After") and an aria-label (`label`).

Keyboard map: ArrowRight/ArrowUp/PageUp add "before" and ArrowLeft/ArrowDown/PageDown remove it (horizontal); vertical follows the arrow (Down/Right/PageDown move the divider down). Shift multiplies the step by 5; PageUp/PageDown always move 5 steps; Home = 0, End = 100.

Focus is shown as an inset outline around the whole handle and as a ring on the round knob (and, in forced-colors mode, an outline). The handle hit area is 40px wide (a 36px knob) so it exceeds the 24px target size; the page can still scroll over the image on the cross axis (`touch-pan-y` / `touch-pan-x`).

`size`, `shape`, `tone`, `appearance` and `variant` change looks only. The role, name, value text, keyboard map and alt contract are identical in every combination. In every appearance, focus is an inset 2px outline in the ring colour around the whole handle hit area (also visible in forced-colors mode), plus the ring on the grip when there is one; `appearance="line"` has no grip, so the outline is its only indicator. With `tone` primary or neutral the grip border follows the tone.

`variant="bar"` is an opaque caption strip (no blur, no translucency) docked along the bottom edge with the labels in physical order (before left, after right) in right-to-left pages too; it is aria-hidden like the chips.
`aria-orientation` follows `orientation`. Corner labels are decorative (aria-hidden), opaque, and can be hidden with `showLabels`; the slider text always names both sides.

Provide meaningful beforeAlt/afterAlt: both images stay in the accessibility tree. The divider axis is physical (left/right or top/bottom) and is not mirrored in RTL because the images are not mirrored either. Nothing animates, so reduced motion needs no special handling.
requires: Throws a ContractError when `before` is set without a `beforeAlt` string, or `after` without an `afterAlt` string. An empty string marks the image decorative.
Throws a ContractError when `label` is an empty string: the slider needs an accessible name.
llmNotes: Use `orientation="vertical"` for portrait/tall images or narrow columns; keep horizontal for landscape images.
Both images must share the same crop/aspect ratio.
Always set beforeAlt/afterAlt describing the content.
Do not rely on drag only; the slider is keyboard operable by design.

components.name: ImageGrid
components.summary: Image gallery as a uniform grid, masonry or featured layout that opens a Lightbox on click.
components.description: Use for galleries and screenshot collections. `variant` selects the layout: `grid` (uniform tiles, default), `masonry` (CSS columns with natural image heights, so mixed portrait/landscape photos pack tightly) and `featured` (the first image spans 2x2 beside smaller tiles). `gap` sets the spacing, `aspect` the tile ratio (`ratio` still works as a legacy alias) and `shape` the tile corners. Each thumbnail is a button labelled "View image: <alt>" that opens the built-in `Lightbox` at that image (state is internal; listen to `open` if you need to know). Set `lightbox=false` for a static grid. Broken thumbnails fall back to their alt text.

props.name: images
props.description: `{ src, alt, caption?, thumb? }`. `alt` is required (an empty string marks the image decorative; with `lightbox` a `caption` also counts). `thumb` is a smaller image for the grid.

props.name: variant
props.description: Layout. Unknown values fall back to `grid`. Reflected as `data-variant`.

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns from `sm` upward; invalid falls back to 3. Always 2 on mobile.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between tiles (0 / 0.375rem / 0.75rem / 1.5rem); invalid falls back to `md`.

props.name: shape
props.description: Tile corners: `rounded-lg` or none. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Reflected as `data-shape`. There is no circle: tiles are photos with their own aspect ratio, and a circle would crop them into ovals (use `Avatar` for round images).

props.name: aspect
props.description: Tile shape (1:1, 16:9, 3:4, 4:3, natural height). Wins over `ratio`; invalid values are ignored. Default `square`, or `auto` for masonry.

props.name: ratio
props.description: Legacy alias of `aspect` kept for compatibility; used when `aspect` is not set. Default `square` (`auto` for masonry).

props.name: lightbox
props.description: Open a Lightbox on click.

props.name: viewLabel
props.description: Prefix of each button's accessible name (localise here).

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the root; wins over internal classes.

emits.name: open
emits.description: A thumbnail was activated.

a11y: The root is a native `<ul>` and each tile an `<li>`. With the lightbox on, a tile is a `<button type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog">` named "View image: <alt>" (the alt text, else the caption, else the position); its image is decorative so the name is not announced twice. Tiles are at least 44px tall (`min-h-11`) even before the image loads, which keeps lazy images above the 24px target size.

Keyboard: Tab moves through the thumbnails, Enter or Space opens the Lightbox (see Lightbox: Esc closes, Left/Right arrows and Home/End navigate, focus returns to the thumbnail). With `lightbox=false` the tiles are plain images with their `alt`.
Masonry fills column by column, so the visual order differs from the DOM and tab order across columns; use it for galleries whose order does not matter.
`shape` changes the corners only: the tile is still a bordered, named button, so `square` tiles stay visible in forced-colors mode and keep the focus ring.
Two columns on a 320px screen, `columns` from `sm`; there is no hover zoom, so nothing moves under reduced motion. Tiles have a border (visible in forced-colors mode).
requires: Throws a ContractError when an entry of `images` has no `alt` string (with `lightbox` on, a non-empty `caption` also satisfies it). The message names the first failing index. The internal Lightbox is bound to `open`, so its own contract holds.
llmNotes: Always provide meaningful `alt` (it becomes the button label); never remote placeholder URLs in examples.
Provide `thumb` for large originals.
Choose `variant`: grid for uniform screenshots, masonry for mixed-orientation photography, featured to spotlight one hero image among 4-7 others.
Use `aspect` (not `ratio`) in new code; use `aspect="auto"` only with masonry or when images share a shape.
Use `shape="square"` for flush galleries; do not try to make tiles circular (use Avatar for round images).
Do not nest ImageGrid inside a link.

components.name: Lightbox
components.summary: Full-screen image viewer dialog with previous/next, Esc, focus containment and scroll lock.
components.description: Use to enlarge images from a gallery or screenshot. Controlled with `v-model:open` (and optionally `v-model:index`); it is teleported to `<body>`. Opening moves focus to the close button, Tab stays inside, Escape closes, arrow keys navigate, and focus returns to the opener on close. `ImageGrid` wires this up for you. For arbitrary modal content use the overlays Dialog instead.

props.name: open
props.description: v-model:open. Required: the viewer never opens itself, so bind it (`false` is fine). Renders nothing when false or when `images` is empty.

props.name: index
props.description: v-model:index, the visible image; clamped to the valid range.

props.name: images
props.description: `{ src, alt, caption? }`. `alt` is required (an empty string marks the image decorative); a non-empty `caption` also satisfies it.

props.name: loop
props.description: Wrap around at the ends; false disables prev/next at the ends.

props.name: closeOnBackdrop
props.description: Close on backdrop click.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the dialog.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: aria-label of the close button.

props.name: prevLabel
props.description: aria-label of the previous button.

props.name: nextLabel
props.description: aria-label of the next button.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last onto the overlay; wins over internal classes.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Requested open state change.

emits.name: update:index

emits.name: close

a11y: role="dialog" aria-modal="true" with an aria-label (`label`); focus moves to Close on open and is restored to the opener on close.

Keyboard map: Tab/Shift+Tab stay inside the dialog (no trap escape); Escape closes; ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move to the previous/next image (swapped in RTL); Home/End jump to the first/last image. Close, previous and next are real buttons with accessible names (`closeLabel`, `prevLabel`, `nextLabel`). At the ends with `loop=false` they use aria-disabled so a focused button keeps focus.
The counter ("2 / 5") is a polite live region. Body scroll is locked while open and restored afterwards (including on unmount).

Layout: the overlay is `h-dvh`, controls sit in header and footer bars (never over the picture), the image shrinks to the space left, so nothing is clipped at 320px or behind mobile browser bars. Controls are 40px (48px on coarse pointers) and the chevrons mirror in RTL. Nothing animates, so reduced motion needs no special handling.
Give every image meaningful `alt` (it falls back to the caption).
requires: Throws a ContractError when the `open` prop is not provided (undefined). `false` is fine: bind `v-model:open`.
Throws a ContractError when an entry of `images` has no `alt` string and no non-empty `caption`. The message names the first failing index.
llmNotes: Always bind `v-model:open`; the component never opens itself.
Supply `alt` for each image.
Prefer ImageGrid unless you need a custom trigger.

components.name: Marquee
components.summary: Infinite CSS ticker (horizontal or vertical) for logos or short text, paused on hover and focus.
components.description: Use for decorative, repeating strips: partner names, tech stack, announcements. Content is duplicated once (the copy is aria-hidden) and translated with a pure CSS animation. `direction` is `left`, `right` (horizontal) or `up`, `down` (vertical, needs a height: `h-64` by default, override with `class`). A visible pause/resume button (`pausable`, on by default) lets anyone stop it (WCAG 2.2.2); it also pauses on hover and focus-within and fades at the edges (`fade`). For users who prefer reduced motion it stops animating, hides the duplicate and the button, and becomes a focusable, named, manually scrollable row. Do not use for important content that must be read; a moving target fails many users, so use `LogoCloud` for static display.

props.name: items
props.description: Simple text items (ignored when the default slot is used).

props.name: duration
props.description: Seconds per loop; invalid or <= 0 is ignored (then `speed` applies, else 30); clamped to 0.1-86400. Wins over `speed`.

props.name: speed
props.description: Preset for `duration`: slow = 60s, normal = 30s, fast = 15s per loop. Alias for quick tuning; an explicit valid `duration` always wins. Unknown values are ignored.

props.name: direction
props.description: Scroll direction. `up`/`down` make a vertical strip (set its height via `class`, default `h-64`). Unknown values fall back to `left`.

props.name: pauseOnHover
props.description: Pause while hovered or focused within.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between items (0 / 1 / 2 / 3 rem); unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: fade
props.description: Fade both ends of the strip with a CSS mask (horizontal or vertical to match the axis).

props.name: size
props.description: Text size of `items` (text-sm / text-lg / text-2xl). Slot content is not affected. Unknown values fall back to `md`. The resolved value is exposed as `data-size` on the root, also when slot content replaces `items`.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional accessible name; sets role="group".

props.name: pausable
props.description: Render the pause/resume button below the strip. Keep it on: moving content that lasts longer than 5 seconds needs a pause mechanism (WCAG 2.2.2).

props.name: paused
props.description: `v-model:paused`. Leave undefined for uncontrolled use.

props.name: pauseLabel
props.description: Button text while the strip moves (localise here).

props.name: playLabel
props.description: Button text while the strip is paused.

props.name: scrollLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the strip when it becomes a scrollable row under prefers-reduced-motion.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last on the root; wins over internal classes (e.g. `h-96` for vertical strips).

emits.name: update:paused
emits.description: The pause button was used.

slots.description: Rich items (logos, badges). Rendered twice; do not attach unique ids inside.

requires: Throws a ContractError when `pausable` is false while the strip moves (no reduced-motion preference, items present) and `paused` is not bound to your own control (WCAG 2.2.2).
a11y: Pause mechanism (WCAG 2.2.2): a real "Pause scrolling" / "Resume scrolling" button (Tab to it, Enter or Space) stops and restarts the animation; the label changes with the state. It is at least 24px tall and 44px on coarse pointers, sits outside the faded edges and has the shared focus ring. The strip also pauses on hover and while focus is inside it.

prefers-reduced-motion: the animation never runs, the duplicate and the button are hidden, and the strip becomes a scrollable row (or column) that is focusable (`tabindex="0"`), named (`scrollLabel`) and operable with the arrow keys.
The duplicate copy is aria-hidden so content is announced once; `label` names the group.
Treat as decorative: do not place the only copy of critical information here. Gaps use logical padding so RTL works; the strip clips inside its own box, so 320px screens never scroll sideways.
llmNotes: Use only for decorative strips.
Prefer `speed` (slow/normal/fast) for tuning; use `duration` only for an exact loop time.
Use `direction="up"`/`"down"` only in a container with a fixed height (set `class="h-48"` etc.). Horizontal is the default for logo and tech-stack rows.
Set `:fade="false"` when the strip sits edge-to-edge or on a tinted section.
No interactive elements with unique ids in the slot (it renders twice).
Give a `label` if the strip carries meaning.
Keep `pausable` on; WCAG 2.2.2 requires a way to stop moving content.

components.name: SectionReveal
components.summary: Opt-in wrapper that fades its content in (rising, dropping or sliding sideways) when scrolled into view. Does nothing unless `enabled`.
components.description: Off by default: without `enabled` it renders a plain element, with no classes, no observer and no hidden state. Turn it on for at most one orchestrated moment on a page (for example the first below-the-fold section), never on every section, because the same fade-up on every block is a stock look. When enabled it uses IntersectionObserver. Content is visible by default for server rendering, no-JS and browsers without IntersectionObserver; it is hidden only after mount, and only when it starts below the viewport. Users who prefer reduced motion never see the hidden state. Use `delay` to stagger siblings. Do not wrap above-the-fold content. `effect`, `distance` and `speed` only change the hidden state and the transition length: only `opacity` and `translate` animate, so the box never moves in the layout. A sideways effect moves the wrapper itself, so put it inside a container that clips horizontally (`overflow-x-clip`, or a `Container` with side padding at least as large as `distance`) when it spans the full viewport width, otherwise the hidden state can add a horizontal scrollbar.

props.name: enabled
props.description: Turn the reveal on. When false the component is a plain wrapper (no-op).

props.name: as
props.description: Element or component to render.

props.name: once
props.description: Reveal once; false re-hides when scrolled out.

props.name: threshold
props.description: Visible fraction (0-1) that triggers the reveal; invalid falls back to 0.15.

props.name: rootMargin
props.description: IntersectionObserver rootMargin.

props.name: delay
props.description: transition-delay in ms for staggering; invalid falls back to 0.

props.name: effect
props.description: `fade-up` fades in while rising, `fade-down` while dropping, `fade` only fades, `slide-left` and `slide-right` fade in from the left or right. The sides are physical and are not mirrored in right-to-left pages. Unknown values fall back to `fade-up`. Reflected as `data-effect` while enabled.

props.name: distance
props.description: How far the hidden state is offset: 0.5rem, 1rem or 2rem. Ignored by `fade`. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Reflected as `data-distance` while enabled.

props.name: speed
props.description: Transition length: 300ms, 700ms or 1000ms. Unknown values fall back to `normal`. Reflected as `data-speed` while enabled.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last; wins over internal classes.

slots.name: default
slots.description: Content to reveal.

emits.name: reveal
emits.description: Content became visible (each time when `once` is false). Never emitted while `enabled` is false.

a11y: The new effects change only `opacity` and `translate`; text is never scaled or rotated, so it stays readable at 200% zoom, and nothing moves in the layout. Sideways effects can extend past the right edge while hidden: wrap them in `overflow-x-clip` so no horizontal scrollbar appears at 320px.

Content is never removed from the accessibility tree or `display`-hidden, only made transparent, so assistive technology reads it in order. Without JavaScript or IntersectionObserver it stays fully visible.
prefers-reduced-motion: content is shown immediately and no observer is created; transitions also carry `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
No focusable element is moved or hidden by the transition, and the wrapper adds no role or tab stop.
llmNotes: Default is a no-op. Add `enabled` for one orchestrated moment, not on every section.
Never wrap the Hero or other above-the-fold content.
Keep the whole moment short: `duration-150` to `duration-300` via `class`, and `delay` steps of 40 to 100ms, not long chains.
Prefer `effect="fade"` for large containers to avoid layout-looking jumps.
Put `slide-left` and `slide-right` inside an `overflow-x-clip` container; keep `distance` at `sm` or `md` and `speed` at `fast` or `normal` for a calm page.

components.name: CookieConsent
components.summary: Cookie notice with per-category toggles and equally prominent accept and reject buttons; it stores nothing and emits `change`.
components.description: Presentational consent notice. It shows a title, an explanation, a policy link (`policy` slot) and one toggle per category. Necessary categories are on, locked and labelled "Always on"; every optional category starts off. "Reject all" and "Accept all" are the same button: same variant, size, weight and width, rejecting comes first in the reading order, and neither needs a second step. "Save choices" sends the toggles as they are. The component remembers nothing: handle `change`, store the result yourself (the optional `readConsent` / `writeConsent` / `clearConsent` helpers do that in `localStorage` and are safe on the server) and load scripts only for categories that are `true`. `banner` is a full-width bar (categories sit behind "Choose categories"; place it with `class`, for example `fixed inset-x-0 bottom-0`), `inline` is a card with the categories always visible, and `modal` is a dialog with a focus trap. In the modal, Escape and the close button hide it and emit `dismiss` without a choice, and a click outside does nothing. Wording is plain: no guilt copy, no pre-ticked boxes, no hidden reject.

props.name: variant
props.description: Look. `banner`: full-width bar with the categories behind a button. `inline`: bordered card with all categories shown. `modal`: dialog with a focus trap and a close button. Unknown values fall back to `banner`.

props.name: categories
props.description: Entries `{ id, label, description?, necessary? }`. Entries without a non-blank string `id` and repeated ids are dropped; a missing label falls back to the id. With no categories only the three-choice notice is shown (no toggles, no "Save choices").

props.name: modelValue
props.description: Toggle state by id (`v-model`). Only `true` turns an optional category on. A necessary category stays on whatever this holds. Unknown keys are ignored.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the notice is shown (`v-model:open`). Omit it and the component hides itself after a choice or a dismissal.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading text and accessible name of the region or dialog. Required: an empty title needs `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The `title` slot replaces it.

props.name: level
props.description: Heading level of the title. Invalid values fall back to 2.

props.name: description
props.default: 'We use cookies to run this site. Optional categories stay off until you turn them on.'
props.description: Explanation under the title. The `description` slot replaces it.

props.name: acceptLabel
props.description: Text of the accept button.

props.name: rejectLabel
props.description: Text of the reject button.

props.name: saveLabel
props.description: Text of the button that sends the current toggles. Shown only while the categories are visible.

props.name: manageLabel
props.description: Text of the button that shows and hides the categories in the `banner` variant (aria-expanded).

props.name: alwaysOnLabel
props.description: Text added to the description of a necessary category, so the locked state is not only a dimmed switch.

props.name: categoriesLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the list of categories.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last; wins over internal classes. Attributes fall through to the root (the section, or the dialog content in `modal`).

slots.name: title
slots.description: Rich title content; replaces the `title` prop.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Rich explanation; replaces the `description` prop.

slots.name: policy
slots.description: Link to the cookie or privacy policy, shown under the explanation. The component renders no link of its own.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The user pressed Accept all, Reject all or Save choices. `categories` has one boolean per id and necessary ones are always `true`. Never emitted by Escape or the close button.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: A toggle moved, or a button set the state.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Emitted with `false` after a choice or a dismissal.

emits.name: dismiss
emits.description: `modal` only: closed with Escape or the close button, without a choice.

a11y: The banner and the inline card are a `section` named by the title (`aria-labelledby`), so they are a region landmark: give each one on a page a different title (or `aria-label`). The modal is a reka Dialog: focus moves in, Tab stays inside, Escape closes it and focus returns to what had it before. The dialog title is required (the Dialog contract).

Every toggle is a switch with a visible label and a description linked with `aria-describedby`. A necessary category is a disabled switch that is on; the words "Always on" in its description carry the locked state, so it is not conveyed by dimming alone.

Accept all and Reject all share one variant, size and class set, so they look and behave the same. Both are reachable with Tab in a fixed order (reject, accept, save, choose categories). The categories button has `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.

Buttons are at least 36px high and 44px on touch pointers, stack to full width below `sm` and wrap, so the notice reflows at 320px. Long labels and descriptions wrap (`break-words`). Logical properties keep it correct in right-to-left layouts.
The modal does not close on an outside click, so a stray tap is never treated as a decision; Escape and the close button emit `dismiss` and never `change`.
requires: Throws a ContractError when there is no accessible name: an empty `title` (and no `title` slot) without `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. In `modal` the Dialog also throws when no title is rendered.
llmNotes: The component stores nothing: handle `@change`, persist the result (`writeConsent` helps) and only load scripts for categories whose value is `true`.
Never pre-tick an optional category, never style accept and reject differently, never hide reject behind a second screen, and never write guilt copy; the defaults already avoid all four.
Show it again only when no saved choice exists, or when the user opens a "Cookie settings" link (use `v-model:open`).
Mark categories `necessary: true` only for cookies the site cannot work without; those cannot be switched off.
Give a policy link through the `policy` slot; the component does not know your URL.
Use `banner` with a fixed-position `class` for the first visit, `inline` on a settings page and `modal` when the choice must interrupt.

components.name: ComparisonTable
components.summary: Generic feature matrix: a real table of columns x features with check, cross, text and empty cells, grouping, a highlighted column and sticky options.
components.description: Use to compare plans, products or editions feature by feature. `columns` define the headers (one may be `highlighted`), `rows` are features (`{ label, description?, values[] }`) or `{ group }` headings that open a new section. Cell values: `true` = check, `false` = cross, text/number = shown as-is, `null`/`undefined`/missing/empty = dash. Every check and cross carries screen-reader text. The table scrolls horizontally inside a focusable region on small screens (`stickyFirstColumn` is on by default, so feature names stay visible; pass `false` to let the whole table scroll). `stickyHeader` keeps the header visible while the region scrolls vertically, so give the root a max height (`class="max-h-96"`). For plan headers with prices and CTAs use `PricingTable` (built on this component). For a handful of plans with long feature lists use `PricingGrid` instead.

props.name: columns
props.description: Headers: `{ key?, title, subtitle?, badge?, highlighted? }`. Malformed entries are skipped.

props.name: rows
props.description: Feature rows `{ label, description?, values: (boolean | string | number | null | undefined)[] }` and group headings `{ group: string }`. Malformed entries are skipped; `values` may be shorter than `columns`.

props.name: variant
props.description: `default` framed, `striped` alternating row shading, `bordered` borders on every cell, `minimal` no outer frame. Unknown values fall back to `default`.

props.name: size
props.description: Cell density. Unknown values fall back to `md`.

props.name: caption
props.description: Required (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`). Accessible name: used for the sr-only `<caption>` and the `aria-label` of the scroll region. Give each table on a page a different caption: identical region names fail the landmark-unique rule.

props.name: stickyHeader
props.description: Pin the header row while the region scrolls vertically (needs a max height on the root).

props.name: stickyFirstColumn
props.description: Pin the feature-name column while the region scrolls horizontally. On by default so row labels never scroll out of view; pass `false` to let the whole table scroll.

props.name: cornerLabel
props.description: Text of the top-left header cell.

props.name: includedLabel
props.description: Screen-reader text for a check.

props.name: excludedLabel
props.description: Screen-reader text for a cross.

props.name: unavailableLabel
props.description: Screen-reader text for an empty cell.

props.name: class
props.description: Merged last onto the scroll region (root).

slots.name: corner
slots.description: Replaces the top-left header cell content.

slots.name: column-header
slots.description: Replaces the content of a column header.

slots.name: column-footer
slots.description: Adds a footer row; one cell per column (e.g. CTA buttons).

slots.name: cell
slots.description: Replaces the default check/cross/text rendering of a cell.

slots.name: row-label
slots.description: Replaces the feature name cell content.

requires: Throws a ContractError when the table has no name: set `caption` (also the sr-only `<caption>`), `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
Throws a ContractError when a column has an empty `title` and no `column-header` slot replaces the header (the first one is named by index).
a11y: A real `<table>` with `<caption>` (sr-only), `scope="col"` column headers, `scope="row"` feature headers and `scope="rowgroup"` group headings (each group is its own `<tbody>`).
Checks, crosses and dashes are icons with screen-reader text ("Included", "Not included", "Not available"); localise with the label props.

The scroll region has `role="region"`, an accessible name (`caption`, make it unique per page) and `tabindex="0"` so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys; focus shows a ring (an outline in forced-colors mode).
The highlighted column is marked with `data-highlighted` and an opaque tinted header; add a `badge` so the emphasis is not colour-only.

Reflow: the table keeps a 36rem minimum width and scrolls horizontally inside its own region at 320px, so the page never scrolls sideways; `stickyFirstColumn` (on by default) keeps feature names visible. Alignment uses logical properties (`text-start`, `start-0`) so RTL works.
llmNotes: One value per column, in column order; use `true`/`false` for yes/no and strings for specifics ("10 GB").
Mark at most one column `highlighted`, and give it a `badge`.
Use `{ group: "..." }` rows to section long matrices instead of several tables.
Use `stickyHeader` only with a max-height class on the root; `stickyFirstColumn` is on by default, turn it off only for two- or three-column tables with short labels.
Pick `striped` for long tables, `bordered` for spec sheets, `minimal` on plain pages, `default` otherwise.
For priced plans with CTAs use PricingTable; do not rebuild headers by hand.

components.name: PricingCard
components.summary: Single pricing plan: name, monthly/yearly price, feature checklist, badge and CTA slot, in five variants.
components.description: Use one card per plan, usually inside `PricingGrid`. `variant` picks the look: `default`, `highlighted` (recommended plan; same as `highlighted`), `outline` (transparent, 2px border), `minimal` (no frame, for plan lists on plain backgrounds) and `compact` (smaller padding and type, for sidebars or 4+ plans). Features are strings or `{ label, included }`; excluded features get an X icon, strike-through and a screen-reader "Not included" note. Provide prices already formatted ("Free", "Custom" or your own currency format). For yearly billing give `yearlyPrice` (+ optional `yearlyPeriod`, `yearlyNote`) and set `billing="yearly"`; PricingGrid and PricingTable do that from their billing toggle. Plans without `yearlyPrice` (Free, Custom) keep `price` in both modes.

a11y: Rendered as an `<article>` with a heading (`level`, default 3: set it to follow the section heading, e.g. `:level="2"` under an h1); features are a `<ul>`; excluded items are announced as "Not included" and the check/cross icons are decorative.

Highlighting is not conveyed by colour alone: it uses a solid border (kept in forced-colors mode) and you should add `badge` text for the recommended plan. Text on the card uses card tokens, so contrast holds in light and dark mode.

The card has no interactive parts of its own; Tab reaches the buttons you put in `cta`. Inside PricingGrid the card is wrapped in an `<li>`; do not put `role="listitem"` on it (an article cannot take that role).
Variants only change styling, never the DOM order or semantics. The card stacks to one column at 320px and nothing animates.
llmNotes: Provide pre-formatted price strings.
One `highlighted` plan per grid.
Put exactly one Button per card in the `cta` slot; use the default variant only on the highlighted plan.
For monthly/yearly pricing set `price` + `yearlyPrice` on each plan and let PricingGrid/PricingTable own the `billing` state; do not set `billing` on cards inside a grid.
Use `outline` on coloured backgrounds, `compact` for 4+ plans or narrow columns, `minimal` only on plain backgrounds.
Free/Custom plans: omit `yearlyPrice` so they stay unchanged.

components.name: PricingGrid
components.summary: Responsive grid of PricingCards from a plans array, with a per-plan CTA slot and an optional monthly/yearly billing toggle.
components.description: Use to lay out 1-4 plans side by side. Pass `plans` (PricingCard props) and a scoped `cta` slot, or put your own `PricingCard`s in the default slot. When at least one plan has a `yearlyPrice` a billing toggle appears above the grid (force it with `showToggle`); the selected `billing` is passed to every generated card so prices switch together. `v-model:billing` controls the state; without it the grid keeps its own state (`defaultBilling` sets the start value). `variant` is passed to generated cards (a plan's own `variant` wins). When the toggle is visible the root is a wrapper (`pricing-grid`) and the list element is the inner `pricing-grid-items`. For a feature-by-plan matrix use `PricingTable`.

components.name: PricingTable
components.summary: Pricing comparison table: plans as columns (price, badge, CTA), features as rows with check/cross/text cells and an optional billing toggle.
components.description: Use when visitors need to compare many features across plans; for a short card-per-plan layout use `PricingGrid`. `plans` define the columns (price, optional `yearlyPrice`, `badge`, `highlighted`), `rows` the features and `{ group }` headings (same shape as `ComparisonTable`). Cell values: `true` check, `false` cross, text/number as-is, `null`/missing dash. A monthly/yearly toggle appears when a plan has a `yearlyPrice` (`v-model:billing`, or uncontrolled with `defaultBilling`). Put CTA buttons in the `cta` slot (under each price; `repeatCta` repeats them in a footer row). The table is a real `<table>`; table-level options (`variant`, `size`, `stickyHeader`, `stickyFirstColumn`) match `ComparisonTable`, which this component wraps.

Checks and crosses are icons with screen-reader text; localise with `includedLabel`, `excludedLabel` and `unavailableLabel`.

components.name: CtaBand
components.summary: Call-to-action section in 5 layouts (band, card, split, inline, newsletter) and 3 flat tones.
components.description:
Use near the end of a landing page, or between sections, to push one action. Pick a `variant` for the layout and a `tone` for the colour. Keep to one clear action and label it with what happens; do not stack several CtaBands. Unknown `variant` falls back to `card`; unknown `tone` falls back to `primary`.

Variants and when to use them:
- `card` (default): rounded centred block inside the page container. The closing CTA.
- `band`: full-width square band with centred copy. Use when the CTA spans edge to edge between full-width sections.
- `split`: copy on one side, `media` or `form` on the other. Use when a real screenshot or a sign-up form supports the pitch.
- `inline`: compact one-liner (headline, optional subtext, buttons at the end). Use mid-page or inside articles and docs.
- `newsletter`: centred copy with an email `form` slot. Use for subscriptions.

Tones: `primary` (brand fill with `primary-foreground`), `muted` (quiet panel) and `inverted` (`foreground` fill with `background` text). All are flat fills; the gradient tone was removed, and text is never faded with opacity so contrast is the tested token pair.

props.name: subtext
props.description: Supporting sentence.

props.name: tone
props.description: Flat colour treatment. Unknown values (including the removed `gradient`) fall back to `primary`.

props.name: size
props.description: Padding and headline scale of every layout; `md` is the original spacing. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Exposed as `data-size`.

props.name: shape
props.description: `square` removes the corner radius of the boxed layouts (`band` has none). Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Exposed as `data-shape`.

props.name: level
props.description: Heading level; invalid falls back to 2.

props.name: as
props.description: Root element.

slots.description: `newsletter`: email form under the subtext. `split`: form shown beside the copy. Ignored by other variants.

components.name: Hero
components.summary: Page-top hero with 14 layouts, 4 backgrounds, 3 sizes, media frames, stats, logos, a form slot and bento tiles.
components.description:
Use once at the top of a landing, docs or product page. Pick a `variant`, a `size` and optionally a `background`; everything else is slots. The default `variant` is `left`: left-aligned text with a headline that says what the product does. The title is an h1 by default; raise `level` to 2 when the page already has an h1. Unknown `variant`, `size` and `background` values fall back to `left`, `md` and none. Entrance fades use `motion-safe:` so they stop under prefers-reduced-motion.

Variants and when to use them:
- `left` (default): left-aligned text, optional media below. Docs, product and editorial pages.
- `centered`: short display line, centred. Use only when the headline is a few words; centred long text is hard to read.
- `split`: text on one side, media on the other. Use when one real screenshot carries the argument.
- `split-reverse`: media first on large screens.
- `minimal`: compact heading. Inner pages and changelogs.
- `stacked-media`: large media below the text in a browser frame. For a real dashboard screenshot.
- `announcement`: a bordered notice above the title. Only for real news with a link; leave it out otherwise.
- `with-stats`: stat row below the text (`stats` prop or slot). Only numbers you can source.
- `with-logos`: logo strip below the text. Only logos you have permission to show.
- `with-form`: `form` slot under the subtitle, for example an email field.
- `terminal`: text beside a window frame with command output (`code` prop or media slot).
- `code`: text beside a window frame with source code.
- `full-bleed`: cover `image` behind a solid text panel, so contrast never depends on the picture. Without an image it falls back to the primary colour with `primary-foreground` text.
- `bento`: text plus a grid of tiles in the `bento` slot. Only when tile sizes reflect importance.

Backgrounds: `none` (default), `grid` and `dots` (aria-hidden SVG patterns, hidden in forced-colors mode) and `image` (cover photo, needs `image`). `gradient`, `glow` and `spotlight` were removed and now render nothing. `decoration` is the old name of `background` and still works.

Actions: put one primary action in `actions`, labelled with what happens ("Open the catalogue"), not a generic invitation.

components.description: Wrap real screenshots of the product, or a code block, in a frame. Do not use it to draw a fake dashboard: the content must be an actual capture or actual code. Variants: `browser` (three dots and an address pill; web screenshots), `window` (dots and a centred file name; terminal and code), `phone` (rounded bezel with a notch; mobile screenshots) and `plain` (bordered panel, no chrome). components.name: SectionHeading
components.summary: Optional eyebrow, title, description and actions that introduce a page section, in 3 alignments, 4 sizes and 2 eyebrow styles.
components.description:
Use at the top of a landing or docs section so headings, spacing and alignment stay consistent. The title should state the section's claim, not label it ("Every part has a keyboard map", not "Features"). `level` controls the heading element for a correct outline; `size` scales the type and the max width. Not for page titles inside a Hero (Hero has its own title). Unknown `align`/`size`/`eyebrowStyle` values fall back to `left` / `md` / `text`.

Options and when to use them:
- `align="left"` (default): section titles above left-aligned content such as feature lists or docs.
- `align="center"`: classic landing sections above centred grids (features, pricing, testimonials).
- `align="right"`: end-aligned block (follows the writing direction); rare.
- `size="sm"` compact subsection or sidebar heading; `md` default; `lg` hero-like section opener; `full` removes the width limit (use with a side-by-side layout).
- `eyebrowStyle="text"` plain accent label in sentence case; `eyebrowStyle="pill"` bordered badge. Use an eyebrow only when it adds information the title lacks; most sections need none.
- `divider` adds a short accent rule between title and description, good on text-heavy pages.
- `actions` slot (or the default slot) adds buttons or links below the description.

components.name: SiteFooter
components.summary: Marketing footer in 7 variants (columns, simple, centered, minimal, newsletter, mega, split) with sizes, alignment and default, muted or dark tones.
components.description:
Use at the bottom of marketing and docs sites. Columns are `{ title, links }` groups rendered as a labelled navigation landmark with one heading and list per column. The bottom row combines legal text and legal links. Put social icon links (see `SocialLinks`) in the `social` slot. Unknown `variant` falls back to `columns`; unknown `tone` to `default`.

Variants and when to use them:
- `columns` (default): brand block left, 2-4 link columns right. Most marketing sites.
- `simple`: one row with brand, a flat list of links and social icons, then the legal row. Small sites with 4-8 links. Flat links come from `links` or, by default, every link in `columns`.
- `centered`: everything stacked and centred. Personal, portfolio and brand-led sites.
- `minimal`: only the legal row (optionally brand and social inline). Apps, checkout and focused landing pages.
- `newsletter`: brand, link columns and an extra newsletter column (`newsletterTitle`, `newsletterDescription`, `newsletter` slot for the form). Content and community sites that grow a mailing list.
- `mega`: large brand block plus four link columns and a spaced legal row. Big sites with many pages.
- `split`: brand block on one half, link columns (up to three per row) on the other, then the legal row. Sites with a longer tagline and a few link groups.

Link only pages that exist; a four-column footer of dead links is a stock look. Compute the copyright year (`new Date().getFullYear()`) instead of hard-coding it.

Tone: `tone="dark"` inverts the footer (`bg-foreground` with `text-background`) and works with every variant. Use it to anchor a light page or to contrast with a light CtaBand above. `tone="muted"` uses the muted surface with the usual text colours: a quieter separation from the page than the border alone.

Size: `size` sets vertical padding (`sm`, `md`, `lg`; `md` is the original) and the text size of links, titles, descriptions and legal text (`lg` is 16px, `sm` and `md` stay at 14px).

Align: `align` (`start`, `center`, `end`) sets text and item alignment in every variant. Unset keeps the variant default (`centered` centres, the others start). On `simple`, centred or end-aligned content stacks instead of spreading across one row.

components.name: SiteHeader
components.summary: Marketing header in 7 variants (default, centered, minimal, transparent, floating, with-announcement, stacked) with sizes, tones, borders, link groups and a mobile menu.
components.description:
Use at the top of marketing, docs and product sites. Links are plain anchors (`href`) so it works with any router: listen to `navigate` or place RouterLinks in the `links` slot. Below `md` the links collapse behind a menu button; Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the button. The active link gets `aria-current="page"` and an underline, so the state is not colour alone. This is not the app shell top bar; use navigation components for in-app chrome. Unknown `variant` values fall back to `default`.

All surfaces are opaque: no backdrop blur, no translucent fills, no shadows. The bar is separated from the page by a border.

Variants and when to use them:
- `default`: logo left, links, actions right, sticky bar. Works everywhere.
- `centered`: logo in the middle, links left, actions right. Brand-led sites with few links.
- `minimal`: slim bar, links always behind the menu button. Landing pages and checkout flows with few distractions.
- `transparent`: overlays the top of the page (fixed, or absolute when `sticky` is false) with no fill, and becomes opaque after scrolling more than 8px or when the menu opens. Only place it over a hero whose surface keeps the link text at 4.5:1 (the default Hero surface does); over a photo use `default` instead.
- `floating`: a bordered `rounded-lg` panel inset from the edges (`w-11/12`, `max-w-5xl`). Product sites that want a detached bar.
- `with-announcement`: default bar plus a primary-colour top bar (`announcement` + optional `announcementHref`, or the `announcement` slot). Only for real news.
- `stacked`: brand and actions on the first row, the navigation on a second row under a rule (links from `md`; below that the menu button opens the usual panel). Sites with many links.

Look dimensions, all independent of the variant:
- `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`): minimum bar height 3rem, 4rem or 5rem (`minimal` and `floating` are one step slimmer), brand text and link text. Targets stay at least 24px (44px on coarse pointers).
- `tone` (`default`, `muted`, `inverted`): page surface, muted surface, or the ink surface with page-coloured text. The `transparent` variant stays transparent over the page until it turns solid, then takes the tone.
- `appearance` (`bordered`, `flat`, `elevated`): the original hairline, no border, or a 2px stronger border. Nothing casts a shadow.

Simple link groups: pass `linkGroups` (`{ title, links }[]`) for sectioned navigation without dropdowns. Groups sit inline on desktop (separated by a rule, labelled for assistive tech) and appear as headed sections in the mobile menu.

Sticky behaviour: while `sticky`, the component keeps the page `scroll-padding-top` equal to the header height (restored on unmount) so a focused element is never scrolled underneath it (WCAG 2.4.11). Link only pages that exist; a generic Features/Pricing/Blog row with dead targets is a stock look.

props.name: tone
props.description: Surface: the page, the muted surface, or the foreground colour with page-coloured text. `transparent` applies it only once solid. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Reflected as `data-tone`.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Edge: hairline border (default), no border, or a stronger 2px border. No shadow in any value. Unknown values fall back to `bordered`. Reflected as `data-appearance`.

props.description: Brand text link, used when the `logo` slot is empty.

props.description: Brand link target.

requires: Throws a ContractError when a link has an empty `label` or `href`, or a link group has an empty `title` (the first one is named by location).
Throws a ContractError when the navigation is shown and `navLabel` is empty.
Throws a ContractError when the navigation is shown and the menu button has no name (`menuLabel` emptied; not checked while `openLabel` / `closeLabel` are in use).
a11y: The root is a `header` (banner) with a labelled `nav` (`navLabel`). Several headers on one page need distinct `navLabel`s, or axe reports landmark-unique.

The menu button is a real button with a constant name (`menuLabel`, default "Menu"), `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the panel. Focus stays on the button when the panel opens, so the next Tab enters the panel. Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the button.
Keyboard: Tab / Shift+Tab move through links and actions in DOM order; Enter activates links; there is no arrow-key menu model because this is site navigation, not an application menu.
The current page uses `aria-current="page"` and an underline (not colour alone, and visible in forced-colors mode). External links use `target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
Link groups are `role="group"` named by the group title (desktop) with a visible heading (mobile).
Sticky header: `scroll-padding-top` follows the header height so focus is not obscured (WCAG 2.4.11).

Targets are at least 24px (44px on coarse pointers). The bar has a minimum, not fixed, height and the desktop nav wraps, so it reflows at 320px and with 200% text. Logical properties (`ms-`, `ps-`, `border-s`) keep RTL correct.

`size`, `tone`, `appearance` and the `stacked` variant change looks and layout only: landmark, names, keyboard map, `aria-expanded` and Escape behave the same. The inverted tone draws focus as a 2px outline in the page colour (the shared ring colour is too close to the ink surface); the current page stays underlined in every tone. `stacked` keeps DOM order brand, links, actions, so Tab order is unchanged.

All surfaces are opaque (no blur), so text contrast is the tested token pair. The only scroll listener is passive and toggles a colour; nothing animates beyond a short colour transition that stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
llmNotes: Use one SiteHeader per page. If a page shows several (docs, demos), give each a distinct `nav-label`.

Pick by need: default for most sites, centered for brand-led, minimal for focused flows, transparent over a plain Hero, floating for a detached bar, with-announcement for real news, stacked for many links.
Use `size` for density, `tone="inverted"` for a dark bar on a light page, `appearance="flat"` only with a tone that differs from the page surface.
Use `transparent` only directly above full-width hero content with a solid surface; keep `sticky` true in real pages (fixed) and add top padding to the Hero. There is no blur variant.
Link only pages that exist.
Pass router paths as `href` and set `active-href` from the current route.
Put at most one primary Button in `cta`.
Use the `links` slot with RouterLink when client-side routing is required; use `linkGroups` for sectioned links instead of building dropdowns.
The announcement props/slot only render in `with-announcement`.
